description: Large Xenomorph! The time if finally here to post a project I have been working on over the last month. After the recent set of my smaller Xenomorph models, I got peer-pressured into making one that was lifesized (ish). This model model stands 5ft tall from floor to tip of tail, measures almost 6ft long diagonally from the back foot to the tip of the head, and is almost 4 foot wide! In order to get it to fit through my doorways I ended up leaving the Head, Right Arm, and half othe tail removable and not fully glued in place. This project is not for everyone and requires quite a bit of dedication and printing resouces to make. At the time of the upload I only sliced the model to fit the H series and A2L printers (to maximize the the size of pieces I could print). Please note that if you are changing your printer from the current H2D that is seleted in the profile you may need to move some pieces around to make sure they fully fit within the build volume. Most are OK, but some have next to no wiggle room for placement. Please also note that the current profile is set to be printed with a .6mm nozzle. This helps speed up print time and the use the .3x layer heights* I printed my model with a very low infill amount (3-4% for most of the print) with the exception of some of the support/critical stress pieces where I increased the infill. This allowed to print quick and not use too much filament. I printed my model in MATTE PLA from Bambu, but due to the low infill amount, and the size/geometry of the model I REALLY wish I did it PETG so that I could display it outside and not worry about the tail melting/bending in the sun (still a risk with PETG I guess, but not as much). The assembly requires and advaced level of skill, this is not for first time large model printers. I did my best to make hexagonal pegs to help align everything, but you will likely need to sand all of the surfaces to ensure a good fit. I used CA glue on the pegs, with a 2-part expoxy to hold the flat surfaces together. To fill the joints I useda 2-part epoxy putty that I found on Amazon. Please note that the Base Tail section and the main body has an interference that I didn't catch until after the model was fully sliced and will need to be manually trimmed/sanded when doing the test fitting. I just used my scraper and knife to snip away bits of the main body until the tail section could fully fit. Please be careful test fitting pieces, due to the low infill amount it can be easy to break*** After the resin cured and the gaps were filled I sanded the joints using 320 grit sand paper before applying a bit of primer, and I used a Gloss Black spray paint to the the entire model. I ended up using a total of 6 spray paint cans* so plan accordingly. The Drool was accomplished using a 2-part epoxy resin (for fiberglass in my particular case) and I used some 2" brushes to coat the entire model and make it appear more wet than the gloss paint achieved by itself. To get the drool effect, I waited until the resin was just about dried, and kept applying over the mouth area until it didn't fully run off. A good/easier way to do this may be with some UV activated epoxy that cures in 5-10 seconds, but I have not tried this route. The teeth were painted in steps between the epoxy using an air brush.

description: 👽 THEM 1947 Disclosure Alien Greys – THE OBSERVER (3 Foot Edition) Some things are better left unseen... unfortunately, THE OBSERVER didn't get that memo. Standing an impressive 3 feet tall , THE OBSERVER is the largest member of the THEM 1947 Disclosure Alien Greys collection. Towering over the rest of the series, this life-sized display piece is guaranteed to turn heads, start conversations, and make your neighbors question whether they should be checking the skies a little more often. Designed with the classic Grey alien appearance in mind, THE OBSERVER features an oversized cranium, deep black eyes, an unnaturally slender body, and a slow, unsettling stance that makes it feel like it's quietly studying everyone around it. Whether displayed indoors, on your porch for Halloween, in a haunted house, or standing watch over your yard, this alien has an uncanny ability to make people stop and stare. Now... before anyone points it out... yes, he only has three toes on one foot. That's because aliens can get diabetes too. We don't judge around here. 😄 🛸 Model Information Approximately 3 feet (36") tall when assembled 7 build plates for the complete alien Optional display stand: 4 additional build plates for extra stability if you plan to display him outdoors or in high-traffic areas 1122.29g of Grey Filament for the Alien 29.83g of Black Filament for the Alien 420.91g of Black Filament for the Base 🖨️ Print Recommendations (MAKE SURE SUPPORTS ARE TURNED ON) While the prototype was successfully tested using KINGROON filament , I strongly recommend printing this model with Bambu Lab filament on a Bambu Grey Cool Plate . During testing, the Bambu filament consistently produced: Cleaner surface finish Better dimensional accuracy Less noticeable seams on glued joints More forgiving connector tolerances during assembly During testing, PLA KINGROON filament was printed using the standard textured build plate , while PLA Bambu filament was printed on the Bambu Grey Cool Plate . The Bambu combination consistently produced better print quality, smoother mating surfaces, and less noticeable seams after assembly. I also found that the Bambu parts were much more forgiving during test fitting. With the KINGROON prints, the connector tolerances were noticeably tighter, making assembly more difficult. If a part needed to be disassembled for adjustment, the connectors were much more susceptible to breaking. In many cases, you only had one chance to get the fit right before risking damage to the connector. The Bambu filament provided a better balance of strength and fit, making assembly considerably easier and more reliable. I also printed these with a Bambu P2S and the heads using a H2C and X2D 🔧 Assembly Assembly is straightforward using the keyed connectors. Dry-fitting each section before gluing is highly recommended to ensure proper alignment. Taking your time during assembly will reward you with an impressive display piece that looks like it walked straight out of a 1947 government file. 👽 Complete Your THEM 1947 Disclosure Alien Greys Collection Explore the rest of the series and bring the entire THEM 1947 Disclosure Alien Greys universe to life! 🛸 ROSWELL GREY 🔬 THE EXPERIMENTER 🚜 K.A.R.L. Android 21 (Evil) Realistic Multi-Color Parted Statue 1. Concept & Design This statue reimagines Android 21 (Majin form) with a realistic anatomical style while preserving her iconic dangerous aura and allure. The physique is intentionally stylized—finely detailed abdominal muscles, tense dynamic limbs, and a confident forward-leaning battle stance—amplifying the intimidating elegance behind her character. Engineered as a fully multi-color parted model, every major visual element is physically separated: her volumetric silver-gray hair, black tube top, gold arm rings, gloves, boots, belt, baggy pants, face features, and even her long pink tail. Each color exists as an individual printed part, meaning no AMS, no filament swapping required , yet the final assembly achieves a near-collectible finish straight off the print bed. 2. Engineering & Recommended Assembly Order The model is engineered to significantly reduce print time and failure risk. All parts are intentionally designed with forgiving tolerances. Since printers often vary slightly in dimensional accuracy, each part is meant to be joined securely using CA glue (super glue) . Gently heating joint areas with a heat gun before applying glue helps the adhesive cure faster and bond stronger. ⚠️ CRITICAL ASSEMBLY STEPS & PRO TIPS: To avoid top-heavy balance issues during gluing, please follow this precise assembly sequence : Upper Torso (Important Note): Assemble the upper chest and shoulders first , and then attach the black tube top clothing piece . This ensures a smooth fit and seamless alignment. Head & Hair Module: Combine the main volumetric hair and face piece first . Next, attach the neck and front bangs , and finally mount the complete head assembly onto the upper torso. Lower Body & Tail: Pre-assemble the pants, boots, and belt completely, then attach the pink tail . Final Upper-to-Lower Merge (Pro Tip): Complete the lower body group (pants + boots + belt + tail) first before joining it with the upper body. Installing top parts too early creates heavy top-weight from the massive hair, making lower joint gluing extremely difficult and forcing awkward holding angles while waiting for glue to set! 3. Display & Customization Although fully colored through part separation alone, painters may optionally enhance shadows on the black top, gold trims, or skin folds to further elevate realism. Her fierce stance and striking silhouette make this statue ideal as a standalone centerpiece or as part of a paired display alongside Majin Buu. The clean part boundaries also make it enjoyable for hobbyists who prefer hybrid finishing—mixing raw printed colors with light airbrush detailing. 4. Conclusion Following the release of Majin Buu, this Android 21 statue marks another exciting milestone in multi-color parted sculpture design. It delivers an accessible printing experience while maintaining professional visual depth. Your support and patience made this milestone possible, and more multi-color parted designs are actively in development. Quick Tips: For complex prints, avoid photography mode: It increases carriage travel and print failure risks. Calibrate your machine and use dry, stable filament to maximize printing reliability. Filament preference: Bambu’s gray remains my personal favorite. Cleanup tools: Needle-nose pliers and Bambu’s FAC002-N scraper make support removal significantly easier.

description: St. Michael the Archangel - Classical Sculpture Lleva una pieza de arte clásico atemporal a tu hogar con esta escultura altamente detallada del Arcángel San Miguel. description: In Book Five of the Odyssey , Odysseus is finally within sight of home when the sea itself turns against him. Poseidon, the Earth-Shaker, the dark-maned lord of the deep has not forgotten that this man blinded his son, the Cyclops Polyphemus. So he gathers the clouds, takes up his trident, and calls every wind down onto a single raft. This is that moment made solid. Not a calm sea-king on a throne, but the god rising out of his own storm: the wave curling into a fist beneath him, the trident already lifted, the grudge that will keep a hero wandering for ten more years. Homer never lets us forget that the sea has a memory, and a temper. I wanted the base to carry that: the water isn't scenery, it's Poseidon's will taking shape. Sculpted as a single figure rising from a sculptural mass of sea, so the wave does the storytelling instead of a second character competing for the eye.

description: “Big Chap” (Alien) Ultra Detailed Sculpture Staying on the recent Xenomorph Theme, here is another absoutley awesome, and highly detailed, “Big Chap” Xenomorph Sculpture! There are 2 size profiles being made available at the time of the model upload - 18" tall version as well as a 10" tall version. Please note that the 19" tall version is printed in pieces, and is maximized in size to fit the P/X series printer beds. The 10" tall version is printed a simplified one-piece print. I should know that I have printed 6 different size variants and will note that you can easily scale this between 10" and 19" tall models. **Please be aware that the print times are lengthy. I had 4 machines running test prints none stop. I promise though, it is worth it at the end. **Please also be aware that the model images you see are 100% real, with 0 use of AI, but they have been post-process colored using some Rub'n Buff waxes, 2-part epoxy resin, and then some gloss clear coat layer application at the end. ASSEMBLY REQUIRED ** Discard the small round cylinder that prints on the 2nd plate with the arms and foot. It is an uneeded part that was a result of slicing the model in the studio* The 19" tall, multipiece print will require some glue. I have used both super glue, as well as hot glue. Hot glue was my preference. With all the parts printed, and supports cleaned up (TAKE YOUR TIME REMOVING THE SUPPORTS AS THE PARTS ARE HIGHLY DETAILED AND FRAGILE ) do a dry-fit of all the parts to ensure proper fitment. You may need to file down some pieces if they do not fit. All 4 of my models went together with no issues, but different printers/filaments may have some tolerance issues. With the Dry fitting completed, if you are satisfied with the fitment you can take the piees apart and proceed to glue them together. As with the above test-fit process. If you are planning to paint/apply color to the model I highly advise doing so with Xenomorph OFF of the base. For final assembly, apply some glue to the foot mounting pegs and firmly place the model on to the base. COLOR APPLICATION I used a very straightforward process for my coloring via application of some Rub'n Buff Antique Gold wax for the Xenomorph, and Brass color for the base. Wear gloves and apply the wax to a towel and gently go over the details. Avoid pressing really hard so that the void remain black/dark, this helps with final contrast of the model. As you can tell from these two photos the difference between the plain model and the colored one is pretty phenomenal and I HIGHLY recommend going through the effort!

This project is a highly customizable 3D Car Profile Desk Sign. Create the perfect personalized gift for any car enthusiast by blending their name directly into the silhouette of a sleek car model. Fully parametric in OpenSCAD. ⚠️ BETA VERSION - COMMUNITY FEEDBACK NEEDED!⚠️ This is the beta release of our Car Sign generator. Due to the high level of customization, there are still several challenges regarding part positioning, support generation, and overall print optimization. We want to build this project together with the community and are actively looking for your feedback on: * Best printing orientation(laying flat vs standing up) * Support settings** (if needed for overhanging letters) * General optimizations to make printing easier Please leave a comment with your tips, pictures, and suggestions to help us improve the final version! --- CUSTOMIZATION --- Choose from 5 distinct car models and adjust sizes, thickness, and text spacing to create a completely unique desk piece. --- PARAMETER GUIDE --- 1. Size Selection - Médio (Medium): 97x20x35 mm - The perfect balanced size for shelves and desk displays. - Grande (Large): 145x30x50 mm - A striking centerpiece for a desk or garage. 2. Car Settings & Base - Car Model: Choose between Sedan, Hatchback (Default), Retro Muscle, Supercar, or Original Sports Car. - Solid Base (Use_Solid_Base): **Enabled by default!** Adds a solid backing plate behind the letters in the exact shape of the car profile. This greatly improves structural rigidity, prevents fragile letters from snapping, and makes the side-profile look stunning. You can adjust the base thickness. - Flip Car (Flip_Car_Horizontally): Mirrors the car horizontally so the front points the other way, ensuring it flows perfectly with your chosen name. 3. Text Customization - Name / Text: Type any name or word (Default: "TESLA"). - Font Style: Currently locked to a robust, bold font (*Courier New Bold*) that works exceptionally well for 3D printing and Boolean intersections. - Letter Spacing & Thickness: Adjust how close the letters sit (Default: 0.85) and add extra boldness (Default: 1.2) if needed for better fusion. --- TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS --- - Flawless Geometry: The model uses an advanced OpenSCAD boolean intersection technique to guarantee a 100% solid, gap-free model (manifold) that imports perfectly into your slicer without errors. - Smooth Vector Curves: The car profiles have been algorithmically smoothed to completely eliminate jagged pixel-stepped edges. --- RECOMMENDED PRINT SETTINGS (Bambu Studio / OrcaSlicer) --- Depending on your chosen car model and specific letter combination, you might need to adapt your slicing approach. Here are some potential strategies you can use to reduce supports and improve print quality: - Orientation: Rotate the part in the X and Y axes on your build plate. Finding the perfect angle depending on your specific car model and letter combination can drastically reduce overhangs! - Supports: Enable supports only for critical areas. - Layer Height: Use Variable Layer Height. This keeps print times low while creating perfectly smooth curves on the car's roof and hood. - Top Surface Pattern: Rectilinear. - Ironing: Test Enabled (Topmost surface only) for a perfectly smooth finish on the front face of the letters. - Wall Generator: Arachne (Crucial for sharp letter details). - Outer Wall Speed: Reduce the speed of the outer walls to ensure a flawless, premium surface finish. - Infill: 10% Gyroid.

Debe estar instalada en tu sistema o soportada en línea. fuente_texto : Tipo de fuente para el nombre superpuesto (puedes incluir variantes como :style=Bold). 📏 [Dimensiones y Alturas] tamano_letra_base : Tamaño (en mm) de la letra inicial. tamano_texto : Tamaño (en mm) del nombre superpuesto. altura_base : Grosor o altura del cuerpo principal del llavero (Eje Z). altura_offset : Altura extra que sobresale la silueta/borde del texto por encima de la base. Si la pones en 0, el fondo del texto quedará a ras de la base. altura_texto : Grosor o altura de relieve que sobresale el nombre superpuesto por encima de su fondo/offset. 📍 [Posición y Rotación del Texto] offset_x : Desplaza el nombre superpuesto de izquierda a derecha en el plano horizontal. offset_y : Desplaza el nombre superpuesto de arriba a abajo en el plano vertical. rotacion_texto : Grados de rotación del nombre (ej. 0 para horizontal, 90 para vertical). 🎨 [Colores] (Visualización en Render) Nota: Estos colores ayudan a previsualizar la separación de materiales en el diseñador antes de enviar el archivo .3mf o .stl a tu laminador. color_letra_base : Color asignado a la inicial gigante. color_extension_offset : Color del relleno interno del fondo del texto si se incrusta dentro de la base. color_offset : Color del borde o silueta en relieve alrededor del texto. color_extension_texto : Color de la estructura interna del texto si atraviesa la base. color_texto : Color de las letras del nombre superior. 🛡️ [Opciones de Offset / Soporte] activar_offset : true: Añade una silueta/soporte detrás del texto para que no quede flotando si las letras no están unidas. false: Muestra únicamente las letras flotantes del nombre. offset_hasta_base : true: El bloque del fondo atraviesa toda la base hasta tocar el suelo (Z=0), ideal para cambios de color por purga directa en la primera capa. false: El fondo del texto descansa sobre la superficie de la inicial. ancho_offset : Grosor (en mm) del contorno que rodea al nombre superpuesto. ✏️ [Opciones de Texto] texto_hasta_base : true: El texto incrustado atraviesa la pieza por completo desde el suelo (Z=0), permitiendo incrustaciones de color de texto completo en la base. false: El texto solo existe en las capas superiores. 🔑 [Configuración del Enganche / Llavero] tipo_enganche : "anilla": Añade una orejeta o anilla redonda exterior a la base. “The Odyssey - Achilles” I have wanted to recreate and color my take on Achilles from The Odyssey for quite some time.. and figured what better time than when the contest is ongoing? This is a 20" tall, highly detailed, multi-piece print. Please note that the print profile is SINGLE COLOR ONLY. The coloring of the model was achieved in post-process application of coloring wax, as well as acrylic paints applied via air brush. This is not your typical AI colored model, this is truly what this could look like! I only spent 30 minutes on mine! The model prints in several pieces in order to maximize the build volumes of the P and X series machines. Some gluing is required. ASSEMBLY Assembly of the model is very straightfoward - first glue the upper torso to the lower body, and then test fit the arms. The arms stay in place pretty good, and I highly recommend waiting to glue the arms/shield on until after you're doing with painting just so you can have better access. Once the modle is painted, just add a drop of glue on each joing and press them into place. Wait to glue the arrows into their respective holes until the end of the process. COLOR APPLICATION I used a very straightforward process for my coloring via application of some Rub'n Buff waxes - Antique Gold, Copper, Brass, etc. Below is an example of this application process on my Alien model I posted earlier. I simply use a microfiber towel, wear gloves, dab a bit of the Rub'n Buff (I buy mine on amazon) and lightly spread it on the model. For this particular model I could have stopped at the first Bronze look.. but I decided to try out some acrylic paints and see what I can do to really bring it to life. After about 20 minutes of spraying this was the end result! I use really cheap, hobby store acrylic paints that are water based. I dilute them with distilled water to make them sprayable. Clean up is a breeze, and so far I have been loving the color effects. As a finishing step, I applied to Matte Clear Coat to the model. The Before and After really give you a good idea of just a little added effort can REALLY make for an awesome print!

Fine-tune the result with each pattern's dedicated controls. 3. Shape and Blend Adjust the pattern height, soften the perimeter with a fade, or blend in a second pattern globally, across a feathered split, or through a radial transition. 4. Prepare the Print Use a coarse Resolution while designing and a lower value for the final mesh. Export flat for maximum bed contact, or enable Print Upright for smoother relief slopes (recommended). Diese Meerjungfrau sitzt gemütlich in ihrer Muschel und verwandelt deinen Brunnen in ein echtes Highlight. Die Figur ist extra so dimensioniert, dass die Funktion der Solarzellen nicht beeinträchtigt wird. Das Modell besteht aus zwei Teilen. description: F1 - Redbull Racing RB20 - 1/12 Scale model! Next on my list is this my take on Redbull's RB20 F1 Car done in 1/12 scale! The main idea behind this model was to try and (finally) make a model with some spinning wheels. I had a bunch of 608 bearings from an old project and models this size/wheels around it. The car body is split into 3 pieces to fit the X/P series machines. The wheels and wheel covers print separately. Gluing is required. Size This is a 1/12th scale model Assembly Assembly is straightfoward. The body of the car has hex pegs and needs to be glued. I use Contact Adhesive but any glue will work. The only thing to watchout for is to make sure that your body is perfectly aligned, or your wheels won't sit square across all 4 corners. While the body is drying, take your 608 bearings and press them into the wheel/tire. With that done, install the wheels onto the body (paying attention to which is the front and rear) by pressing the bearing onto the stub shaft. The fit should be somewhat snug, but not too tight. If you are having issues sliding the wheel on, I recommed sanding the wheel stud around just a bit to smooth it out. With the wheels pressed onto the body, proceed to install the retainer washer by pressing it onto the shaft. Don't press it too tight against the wheel or it will prevent free wheel spin. If you want added assurance that this stays in place, you can add a dab of glue to the washer/stubshaft, but it will make it impossible to remove later. With the wheel retainers installed, proceed to press in the covers (again paying attention to the front/rear as they are different). You're done! Only thing left is to paint it you want to go an extra step!

description: Hades & Persephone – Between Two Worlds ( 3 part sculpture, no AMS needed ) A story of light drawn toward darkness, and darkness softened by light. Inspired by the ancient Homeric Hymn to Demeter , this dual sculpture captures the fateful moment when Persephone is offered the pomegranate—the fruit that will forever connect her to the Underworld. As the old tale tells it, Hades gave her the sweet pomegranate seed, quietly binding her to his realm and dividing her life between the darkness below and the blooming world above. Persephone can be displayed in two different positions , allowing you to change the meaning of the scene: Place her slightly farther back, with her hand only reaching toward the pomegranate—a moment of hesitation, temptation, and choice. Move her forward so her hand is touching the pomegranate , capturing the instant when her fate becomes intertwined with Hades and the Underworld. The bright floral details and flowing dress of Persephone contrast with Hades’ dark crown, powerful form, and gothic Underworld base. Display them together as one dramatic scene or separately to emphasize the distance between their two worlds. A striking mythological statement piece about love, longing, temptation, and the eternal balance between darkness and spring. Printing Use a clean print plate with some glue (unless you are using a super tack plate) Use dried out filament (Different filament and printers impacts the print differently, please adjust your settings accordingly.) Keep the models in the provided positions Support Removal Instructions Allow the print to cool completely before removing it from the build plate. Use small flush cutters, needle-nose pliers, and tweezers to remove the support branches in smaller pieces. Patience and careful handling are important for protecting the hands and the leaves. Be especially careful around the hands and leaves. Gently pull/wiggle the support downwards. Break the branches into smaller sections and alternate around each supported section as needed. I needed to alternate between the front and backside around the leaves on the Persephone sculpture. After removing the supports, clean up potential rough contact points with a precision knife, small file, or fine-grit sandpaper if needed. Light sanding and gentle, controlled heat may be needed to clean up areas where the supports were attached. I used a handheld mini torch, but apply heat carefully to avoid warping or damaging the print. Wood PLA is very sensitive to heat! description: 💀 The Reaper - Undead Skeletal Champion (32mm Base) "The grave cannot hold those whose vengeance still hungers for blood." Expand your undead horde with The Reaper , a high-fidelity skeletal warrior designed for classic tabletop RPGs (D&D, Pathfinder) and skirmish wargames. Designed as a thematic spiritual successor and companion model to the popular The Undead Marauder , this miniature features an agile, aggressive undead champion wielding a massive, rune-engraved scythe over its head. Standing upon a detailed 32mm scenic bone-and-rock base , the figure showcases intricate skeletal anatomy, including a fully hollowed ribcage, spinal column, spiked pauldrons, and a tattered battle skirt. 📐 Print Specs & Slicing Architecture Base Diameter: 32mm integrated scenic base. Nozzle Diameter: 0.4mm standard nozzle. Layer Height: 0.08mm (Highly Recommended) . Because of the delicate skeletal frame, spinal vertebrae, and fine scythe engravings, a 0.08mm layer height is necessary to maintain structural integrity and resin-like detail resolution. 🛠️ Chirurgical Support Extraction Guide (Step-by-Step Order) ⚠️ CRUCIAL POST-PROCESSING WARNING: Skeletal geometry features thin, vulnerable stress points (especially the central spine and waist). Proceed with extreme patience and follow this exact extraction sequence to prevent accidental breakage. 🚫 Golden Rule: Always snip contact tips with fine flush cutters and pull support branches DOWNWARD , never outward or toward yourself, to avoid applying snapping leverage against the thin bone connections. 🌾 Step 1 - The Scythe & Blade: Begin by freeing the top rune-engraved scythe blade and the upper hand grip. Snip the small tree contact tips cradling the curved blade first. 🦾 Step 2 - The Arms & Shoulder Spikes: Move down to the arm joints and spiked pauldrons. Isolate and clip the tree interface tips around the elbows before pulling the outer supports away. 👗 Step 3 - The Tattered Skirt: Gently disengage the support columns surrounding the lower tattered loincloth/skirt. Gently pull these branches straight down toward the base . 🦴 Step 4 - The Spine & Torso (SAVE FOR LAST!): The central spine and ribcage cavity are the most delicate parts of the entire mesh. Do not touch the torso supports until steps 1-3 are fully completed. Once the outer limbs are free, carefully clip the remaining support roots behind the vertebrae and gently pop the core column out without applying lateral force to the waist. 🔥 BUILD THE ULTIMATE UNDEAD ARMY! This is part of a complete set. description: "Internecivus Raptus" (Alien) - Ultra Detailed Sculpture Staying on the recent Xenomorph Theme, here is another absoutley awesome, and highly detailed “Internecivus Raptus” - Xenomorph Sculpture! There are 2 size profiles being made available at the time of the model upload - 20" tall version as well as a 10" tall version. Please note that the 20" tall version is printed in pieces, and is maximized in size to fit the P/X series printer beds. The 10" tall version is printed a simplified one-piece print. I should know that I have printed 6 different size variants and will note that you can easily scale this between 10" and 20" tall models. **Please be aware that the print times are lengthy. I had 4 machines running test prints none stop. I promise though, it is worth it at the end. **Please also be aware that the model images you see are 100% real, with 0 use of AI, but they have been post-process colored using some Rub'n Buff waxes, 2-part epoxy resin, and then some gloss clear coat layer application at the end. ASSEMBLY REQUIRED ** The 20" tall, multipiece print will require some glue. I have used both super glue, as well as hot glue. Hot glue was my preference. With all the parts printed, and supports cleaned up (TAKE YOUR TIME REMOVING THE SUPPORTS AS THE PARTS ARE HIGHLY DETAILED AND FRAGILE ) do a dry-fit of all the parts to ensure proper fitment. You may need to file down some pieces if they do not fit. All 4 of my models went together with no issues, but different printers/filaments may have some tolerance issues. With the Dry fitting completed, if you are satisfied with the fitment you can take the piees apart and proceed to glue them together. As with the above test-fit process. If you are planning to paint/apply color to the model I highly advise doing so with Xenomorph OFF of the base. For final assembly, apply some glue to the foot mounting pegs and firmly place the model on to the base. COLOR APPLICATION I used a very straightforward process for my coloring via application of some Rub'n Buff Antique Gold wax for the Xenomorph, and Brass color for the base. Wear gloves and apply the wax to a towel and gently go over the details. Avoid pressing really hard so that the void remain black/dark, this helps with final contrast of the model. As you can tell from these two photos the difference between the plain model and the colored one is pretty phenomenal and I HIGHLY recommend going through the effort!

Hazards: Bonds skin and eyes in seconds. Causes skin irritation, serious eye irritation, and respiratory irritation. Key Risk: Exothermic polymerization (rapid heat generation) if spilled on clothing, particularly cotton or wool. Before any work begins, ensure the following PPE is worn: Gloves: Nitrile or polyethylene gloves. Do not wear cotton or fabric gloves, as they react violently with cyanoacrylate. Eye Protection: Safety goggles or glasses. Ventilation: Use only in well-ventilated areas to avoid inhaling excessive vapours. Emergency Response & First Aid Skin Bonding: Do not pull the skin apart. Immerse in warm, soapy water or apply acetone to penetrate the bond, then peel gently with a blunt edge. Eye Contact: Do not force eyes open. Flush immediately with warm water or apply a moist gauze patch, and seek immediate medical attention. Spillages: Do not use cloth rags for cleaning. description: FULLY ARTICULATED or FLEXI, Glow In The Dark Anglerfish Detailed Description of the Model Bring the deep ocean trenches right to your desk with this fully articulated, print-in-place Anglerfish model! Designed with intricate textural scales, razor-sharp teeth, and its iconic illuminated lure, this model features zero assembly and requires no supports. It prints entirely as one piece with fluid, snaking articulation across its body segments, allowing it to slither and pose naturally. To achieve that authentic bioluminescent deep-sea look, print it using TECBEARS PLA Glow in The Dark (Luminous) 3D Printer Filament . Because glow-in-the-dark filaments contain abrasive phosphorescent particles, we highly recommend pairing your setup with SUNLU PLA Glow in the Dark Filament or using a hardened steel nozzle to prevent premature wear. Nighttime Display: Charge the filament under a bright light or UV source to watch the deep-sea predator cast an eerie, glowing green light in a dark room. History & Background Anglerfish are famous inhabitants of the aphotic zone of the ocean—the pitch-black depths of the sea where sunlight never reaches. Using a modified fin ray acting as a glowing bioluminescent lure (the esca) to attract unsuspecting prey, these creatures represent some of the most fascinating evolutionary traits in marine biology. This 3D model captures that natural wonder, translating deep-sea mythology into a modern mechanical print-in-place design. description: Chinese Rosewood-inspired Storage Chest – 1:12 Scale A detailed 1:12 scale Chinese rosewood-inspired storage chest designed as a functional miniature furniture piece. This ornate chest features an opening lid with a working captured hinge and two separate functional sliding drawers. It is well suited for dollhouse interiors, historical room scenes, miniature displays, and collector showcases. The model is supplied as three separate STL files: One chest frame with its integrated captured hinged lid Two individual sliding drawers Printing Notes The chest frame and lid print together as a permanently captured assembly. The hinge components capture one another during printing; the lid cannot—and should not—be separated from the chest afterward. Before attempting to open the lid fully, carefully inspect the hinge area. A small amount of adjoining filament may need to be cut away from between the male and female hinge surfaces. Use the tip of a sharp hobby or X-Acto knife carefully, removing only the unwanted filament. Once cleared, gently work the lid through small movements until the hinge operates freely. Do not force the lid open, as excessive pressure may damage the printed hinge. The original model measures: 60 mm W × 65 mm D × 100 mm H Reducing the model size will also reduce the hinge clearances. Smaller prints will require more careful hinge cleanup and release before the lid can move freely. With its decorative detailing, functional drawers, and opening upper compartment, this chest makes an attractive feature piece for miniature bedrooms, studies, period-inspired interiors, and display collections. How I Established the 1:12 Dollhouse Scale The image below shows how I estimated the final 1:12 scale dimensions for this model. I use an image editing application called Pixelmator Pro, but most image editing programs should work. The process is simple: I place the model image into a Victorian room reference image where the back wall has been set to 254 mm high. At 1:12 scale, 254 mm represents a 10-foot ceiling. Once the wall height is set, I resize the model image until it looks correct inside the room. The image editing application then gives me the approximate width and height of the model. I use those measurements as the starting point in my slicer and adjust the 3D model to match. This method helps me scale the model visually, rather than guessing from numbers alone. Important: The wall image must be set to exactly 254 mm high. The width will adjust automatically once the height is set. I have included the wall image near the bottom of this description, after the Buy Me a Coffee notice, so you can download it and use the same method to help scale models for your own 1:12 dollhouse. This is not a precision engineering method, but it is a very useful visual guide for dollhouse room scale. Bambu Settings for this Model For those of you who want the model but in a different scale: Here is the Victorian wall image for you to download and use as a simple 1:12 scale reference. Set the height of this wall image to 254 mm in your image editing application. That represents a 10-foot wall at 1:12 scale. Then import the image of the model you want to scale and place it into the room. Resize the model image until it looks correct visually. Record the model’s height and width from your image application, then use those measurements as a starting point in your slicer. That’s it. This is not a precision engineering method, but it is a very useful visual guide for checking dollhouse scale. 😊

The Legendary Golden Apple🍎✨ A timeless symbol of beauty, temptation, and destiny. The next project is inspired by one of the most iconic stories of Greek mythology . This elegant sculpture features the Legendary Golden Apple , resting upon a classic marble pedestal reminiscent of ancient Greek architecture. Printed in only two colors , the model combines an impressive appearance with an easy printing experience. The complete sculpture finishes in around 4 hours , and although supports are required, they are carefully designed to be easy to remove , leaving behind a beautiful and highly detailed result that truly stands out on display. Whether you're a fan of mythology, classical art, or simply enjoy elegant display pieces, this sculpture brings one of history's greatest legends into your home. 🍎 The Mythology Behind the Golden Apple In Greek mythology , the Golden Apple is one of the most enduring symbols of beauty, pride, and destiny . The story begins when Eris , the goddess of discord, was deliberately excluded from the wedding of Peleus and Thetis . Seeking revenge, she cast a magnificent golden apple among the guests, bearing the famous inscription: "To the Fairest." The simple inscription ignited a bitter rivalry between three powerful goddesses: 👑 Hera , Queen of the Gods ⚔️ Athena , Goddess of Wisdom and War ❤️ Aphrodite , Goddess of Love and Beauty Unable to settle the dispute, Zeus appointed the Trojan prince Paris to choose the rightful owner of the apple. Each goddess attempted to sway his decision with an extraordinary promise. Hera offered limitless power and kingdoms, Athena promised unmatched wisdom and victory in battle, while Aphrodite tempted him with the love of the most beautiful woman in the world— Helen of Sparta . Paris chose Aphrodite. His decision became known as The Judgment of Paris , a single choice that ultimately led to Helen leaving Sparta and ignited the legendary Trojan War . From that day forward, the Golden Apple became far more than a prize for beauty. It evolved into a timeless symbol of temptation, vanity, rivalry, and the unforeseen consequences that can arise from a single decision. 🎨 My Artistic Interpretation This sculpture goes beyond the classical myth. Rather than depicting only the Golden Apple, it merges three powerful symbols into one artistic composition: 🍎 The Golden Apple — beauty, desire, and destiny. 🐍 The Serpent — temptation, persuasion, and hidden consequences. 👤 The Emerging Woman's Face — beauty itself, capable of inspiring both admiration and obsession. Cracks spread across the apple's surface, reminding us that even the most flawless object can hide the seeds of conflict. Together these elements transform an ancient myth into a universal story about human nature—our ambitions, our desires, and the difficult choices that define history. 🍎 Symbolism & Analogy The apple is far more than a fruit—it becomes a vessel for human ambition. Its polished golden surface radiates perfection, yet beneath that beauty lie subtle fractures, reminding us that perfection often comes at a hidden cost. The serpent does not simply guard the apple. It represents temptation itself, quietly whispering that every irresistible desire demands a sacrifice. The woman's face emerging from within the fruit embodies timeless beauty—captivating enough to influence kings, heroes, and entire civilizations. Yet the growing cracks reveal an enduring truth: Beauty can inspire greatness, but when mixed with vanity, envy, and pride, it can divide kingdoms and change the course of history. Like the legendary Golden Apple itself, this sculpture reminds us that a single decision—one moment of temptation or one choice driven by desire—can create consequences that echo for generations.

model_name: Jason Stained Glass Suncatcher — Friday 13th CCL
description: Welcome to Camp Crystal Lake. Jason Voorhees stands full-figure in this tall printed "stained glass" panel — the hockey mask, the work coveralls and gloves, machete in hand — planted on a stone path with the cabin, the pines, and a crescent moon behind him in a green-and-blue night sky. Hang it in the sun and the translucent PETG lights up like a real leaded window, turning the whole Friday the 13th scene into glowing glass. 🔪 Fan tribute: an original stained-glass interpretation of a horror icon, made as a printed window panel. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the rights holders. Features Full-scene panel — not just a portrait: Jason stands on a stone path with the cabin, forest, and crescent moon behind him. Backlit "stained glass" effect — translucent panes glow when light passes through, framed by black "lead came" lines. The full Jason — hockey mask, coveralls, gloves, and machete all rendered in glass. Tall portrait format — an upright panel that fills a vertical window pane. Flat, no-support print — one piece, straight on the plate. No supports, no assembly. Two material paths — translucent/transparent PETG for a true glow, or solid PLA for an opaque mosaic look. Print Settings Setting Value Nozzle 0.4 mm Layer height 0.24 mm Infill 100% Wall generator Arachne Top / bottom / infill pattern Aligned Rectilinear Material Translucent/Transparent PETG (show finish) — solid PLA also works Supports None — flat panel Orientation Flat on the build plate ⚙️ Why these settings: 100% infill with Aligned Rectilinear on top, bottom, and infill fills every pane in one even pass — so backlight diffuses smoothly across the glass instead of looking blotchy. Arachne keeps the fine detail lines — the mask, the coveralls, the cabin logs — crisp and unbroken. The show pieces are translucent PETG so the panes actually glow; solid PLA prints just as cleanly for an opaque mosaic. Color Guide Area Suggested color Notes Frame / leading Black The outline that defines every pane Mask Translucent white / bone The hockey mask Coveralls & gloves Translucent grey + brown Jason's work clothes Machete Translucent silver + red Blade and blood accent Sky & moon Translucent blue + white The night sky behind him Forest & foliage Translucent greens + brown Trees, cabin, and ground Stone path Translucent tan / sand The path he stands on 📏 Scale to fit your window. The tall format suits a vertical pane — keep the full figure and scene in frame when you scale. Tips & Tricks Print flat, no supports — the panel lies on the plate and needs nothing under it. Go translucent for the glow — transparent/translucent PETG is what makes the night scene light up in a sunny window. Keep the aligned rectilinear pattern — it's what gives the even, light-through-glass diffusion. Hang it in a tall window to suit the upright format. Solid PLA is a valid look too — an opaque mosaic version reads great on a wall or shelf. description: Chairs of the Past — 1:12 Miniature Series Chairs of the Past brings unusual, historic, and sometimes wonderfully peculiar chair designs back to life as printable 1:12 miniatures. Each model begins with an old engraving or documented chair from another era, then is carefully interpreted as a three-dimensional object suitable for a dollhouse, miniature room, display, or historical scene. Some chairs are elegant, some practical, and others hide surprising stories—but every one offers a small glimpse into how people once sat, worked, rested, and lived. Tennyson Armchair The Tennyson chair is an elegant cane-seated study armchair with a tall arched back, slender turned uprights, and gracefully scrolling arms. Its light, refined construction gives it a more polished and decorative appearance than many of the heavier historic chairs in the series, while the shaped front rail and small hanging pendant details add a touch of Gothic character. This chair was associated with Alfred, Lord Tennyson, and was described as a modern French-type cane-bottomed study chair. The original was sketched in the poet’s study at Haslemere, where it stood near his writing table. That connection gives the chair a quiet literary presence, while its refined silhouette makes it especially appealing as a miniature furnishing. In 1:12 scale, the Tennyson chair would work especially well in: • a study or writing room • a library • a parlour • a literary interior • any miniature setting needing an elegant antique armchair Its open back, cane seat, and decorative details also make it an appealing piece for painted finishes, wood-toning, and fine miniature display work. How I Established the 1:12 Dollhouse Scale The image below shows how I estimated the final 1:12 scale dimensions for this model. I use an image editing application called Pixelmator Pro, but most image editing programs should work. The process is simple: I place the model image into a Victorian room reference image where the back wall has been set to 254 mm high. At 1:12 scale, 254 mm represents a 10-foot ceiling. Once the wall height is set, I resize the model image until it looks correct inside the room. The image editing application then gives me the approximate width and height of the model. I use those measurements as the starting point in my slicer and adjust the 3D model to match. This method helps me scale the model visually, rather than guessing from numbers alone. Important: The wall image must be set to exactly 254 mm high. The width will adjust automatically once the height is set. I have included the wall image near the bottom of this description, after the Buy Me a Coffee notice, so you can download it and use the same method to help scale models for your own 1:12 dollhouse. This is not a precision engineering method, but it is a very useful visual guide for dollhouse room scale. Bambu Settings for this Model For those of you who want the model but in a different scale: Here is the Victorian wall image for you to download and use as a simple 1:12 scale reference. Set the height of this wall image to 254 mm in your image editing application. That represents a 10-foot wall at 1:12 scale. Then import the image of the model you want to scale and place it into the room. Resize the model image until it looks correct visually. Record the model’s height and width from your image application, then use those measurements as a starting point in your slicer. That’s it. This is not a precision engineering method, but it is a very useful visual guide for checking dollhouse scale. 😊 [End]

description: Great Imperial Jade Seal – Historical Fantasy Display Model This detailed 3D printable model is an artistic interpretation of the legendary Great Imperial Jade Seal of China , also known as the Heirloom Seal of the Realm . The mythical beast features an open mouth, prominent fangs, powerful paws and flowing ornamental details inspired by traditional Chinese jade carvings. The underside contains an intricate seal-face design inspired by ancient Chinese seal script and symbolic motifs. When displayed upright, this detailed base becomes an additional decorative element and emphasizes the object’s historical character. Supports are recommended beneath the creature’s mouth, fangs, whisker-like ornaments and other extended details. Tree supports can help reduce contact marks on the visible surfaces. For a jade-inspired finish, the model works particularly well with muted green, translucent green or stone-effect filament. Light sanding and a satin clear coat can further enhance the appearance. description: 2" Virgin Mary Concrete Casting Mold Create a beautiful, 12-inch tall statue of the Virgin Mary with this custom-designed, multi-part 3D printable mold. This project is designed for those who enjoy the challenge of high-quality concrete casting and want to produce professional-looking results at home. Project Overview This mold is comprised of 8 distinct parts, engineered to lock together to create a seamless casting cavity. The intricate details on the inner faces are designed to capture the delicate features and flowing fabric textures of the statue perfectly. Instructions for Casting The process for using this mold requires patience and attention to detail: Printing: Print all 8 segments of the mold. For the best results, I recommend using SUNLU PLA+ Filament , which provides the durability and surface finish needed for intricate molds. Assembly: Connect the printed parts using clips and rubber bands to ensure they are held tightly in place during the pour. No glue is required for this assembly. Concrete Preparation: Select a high-quality concrete mix. Crucially, you must sift out ALL large rocks from the mix to ensure a smooth, detailed surface. Pouring: Add water according to the manufacturer’s instructions and carefully fill the assembled mold. Setting: Allow the concrete to set for the full recommended time specified by the manufacturer. Removal: Once set, place the mold in an oven at a low temperature to slowly and carefully melt the 3D-printed pieces away, revealing your finished statue. Remixing and Applications This design can be adapted for various purposes beyond religious decor: Garden Art: Scale up or down for custom garden accents. Custom Plaster Casting: Use the same mold with plaster of Paris for indoor display pieces. Abstract Sculpture: The modular nature of the 8-part system allows for creative re-orientation to produce abstract, geometric concrete art. description: You'll float too. Pennywise leers out of this printed "stained glass" panel — the pale domed forehead, the sweep of orange hair, the red nose and grin, and that huge pleated ruff over the yellow costume, all set against a burst of pale-blue rays. Hang it in the sun and the translucent PETG lights up like a real leaded window, the Dancing Clown glowing from your glass. 🎈 Fan tribute: an original stained-glass interpretation of a horror icon, made as a printed window panel. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the rights holders. Features Backlit "stained glass" effect — translucent panes glow when light passes through, framed by a black "lead came" outline. Full-face detail — the domed forehead, arched orange hair, red-lined eyes, red nose and grin, all in glass. The pleated ruff — the big radiating collar rendered as a fan of grey-and-white panes. Radiant background — pale-blue rays burst out behind the head like light off a fairground sign. Flat, no-support print — one piece, straight on the plate. No supports, no assembly. Two material paths — translucent/transparent PETG for a true glow, or solid PLA for an opaque mosaic look. Print Settings Setting Value Nozzle 0.4 mm Layer height 0.24 mm Infill 100% Wall generator Arachne Top / bottom / infill pattern Aligned Rectilinear Material Translucent/Transparent PETG (show finish) — solid PLA also works Supports None — flat panel Orientation Flat on the build plate ⚙️ Why these settings: 100% infill with Aligned Rectilinear on top, bottom, and infill fills every pane in one even pass — so backlight diffuses smoothly across the glass instead of looking blotchy. Arachne keeps the fine face lines and the thin red accents on the costume crisp and unbroken. The show pieces are translucent PETG so the panes actually glow; solid PLA prints just as cleanly for an opaque mosaic. Color Guide Area Suggested color Notes Frame / leading Black The outline that defines every pane Hair Translucent orange The swept-back clown mane Face Translucent white / bone The pale domed forehead Eyes, nose & mouth Translucent red The red-lined eyes, nose, and grin Ruff collar Translucent grey + white The big pleated fan Costume Translucent yellow + red accents The suit and red pom-pom button Background Translucent pale blue / ice The radiating rays 📏 Scale to fit your window. Keep the thin red costume lines in mind if you scale down — very fine leading can get delicate at small sizes. Tips & Tricks Print flat, no supports — the panel lies on the plate and needs nothing under it. Go translucent for the glow — transparent/translucent PETG is what makes the clown light up in a sunny window. Keep the aligned rectilinear pattern — it's what gives the even, light-through-glass diffusion. Hang it where the light moves — an east or west window gives the best changing glow through the day. Solid PLA is a valid look too — an opaque mosaic version reads great on a wall or shelf. What's your favorite scary movie? This one hangs in your window. Ghostface is rebuilt as a printed "stained glass" panel in full cathedral-window style — the robed figure with the screaming mask, knife in hand, standing between gothic columns beneath a soaring arched tracery of red, green, blue, and amber glass. Hang it in the sun and the translucent PETG lights up like a real church window, turning a slasher icon into something that genuinely belongs in stained glass. 🔪 Fan tribute: an original stained-glass interpretation of a horror icon, made as a printed window panel. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the rights holders. Features True cathedral-window styling — a gothic arch, columns, and tracery frame the figure like a real church window. Backlit "stained glass" effect — translucent panes glow when light passes through, framed by black "lead came" lines. The full Ghostface — the robe, mask, and raised knife rendered in glass, standing between two pillars. Rich color spread — red, green, blue, amber, and white panes fill the arch and side lights. Flat, no-support print — one piece, straight on the plate, including the decorative arch and base trim. Two material paths — translucent/transparent PETG for a true glow, or solid PLA for an opaque mosaic look. Print Settings Setting Value Nozzle 0.4 mm Layer height 0.24 mm Infill 100% Wall generator Arachne Top / bottom / infill pattern Aligned Rectilinear Material Translucent/Transparent PETG (show finish) — solid PLA also works Supports None — flat panel Orientation Flat on the build plate ⚙️ Why these settings: 100% infill with Aligned Rectilinear on top, bottom, and infill fills every pane in one even pass — so backlight diffuses smoothly across the glass instead of looking blotchy. Arachne keeps the fine gothic tracery and thin leading lines crisp and unbroken. The show pieces are translucent PETG so the panes actually glow; solid PLA prints just as cleanly for an opaque mosaic. Color Guide Area Suggested color Notes Frame / leading Black The outline that defines every pane Arch, columns & tracery Brown / bronze The gothic "stonework" framing Robe & mask Translucent grey / white The Ghostface figure Arch panes Translucent red, green, blue, amber The tracery glass above Side lights Translucent blue, orange, green, white The panes flanking the figure 📏 Scale to fit your window. The decorative base trim and arch peak are part of the panel — keep the whole silhouette in frame when you scale. Tips & Tricks Print flat, no supports — the arch, columns, and base trim all print on the plate. Go translucent for the glow — transparent/translucent PETG is what makes it read as a real church window. Keep the aligned rectilinear pattern — it's what gives the even, light-through-glass diffusion. Hang it in a tall window — the vertical cathedral shape suits a narrow, upright pane of glass. Solid PLA is a valid look too — an opaque mosaic version reads great on a wall or shelf. model_name: Chucky Stained Glass Suncatcher — Good Guys
description: Wanna play? This is the Good Guy doll himself rebuilt as a printed "stained glass" suncatcher — wild red hair, stitched-up scars, those piercing blue eyes, and the blue "Good Guys" overalls, knife in hand, all ringed by a wheel of red, blue, and yellow glass panes with flames licking up the sides. Hang it in the sun and the translucent PETG lights up like a real leaded window, with a heavy black frame doing the work of the lead came. 🔪 Fan tribute: an original stained-glass interpretation of a horror icon, made as a printed window panel. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the rights holders. Features Backlit "stained glass" effect — translucent panes glow when light passes through, framed by a black "lead came" outline. Loaded with detail — the scarred face, red hair, blue eyes, striped sleeves, raised knife, and the "Good Guys" overalls all rendered in glass panes. Radial glass wheel — a full ring of red, blue, yellow, and orange panes with flame motifs surrounds the figure. Flat, no-support print — one piece, straight on the plate. No supports, no assembly. Multi-color or paint — run it multi-color for the show-piece look, or lay the frame and fill the panes by hand. Two material paths — translucent/transparent PETG for a true glow, or solid PLA for an opaque mosaic look. Print Settings Setting Value Nozzle 0.4 mm Layer height 0.24 mm Infill 100% Wall generator Arachne Top / bottom / infill pattern Aligned Rectilinear Material Translucent/Transparent PETG (show finish) — solid PLA also works Supports None — flat panel Orientation Flat on the build plate ⚙️ Why these settings: 100% infill with Aligned Rectilinear on top, bottom, and infill fills every pane in one even, continuous pass — so backlight diffuses smoothly across the glass instead of looking blotchy. Arachne keeps the many thin black leading lines crisp and unbroken. The show pieces are translucent PETG so the color panes actually glow; solid PLA prints just as cleanly for an opaque mosaic look. Color Guide Area Suggested color Notes Frame / leading Black The outline that defines every pane Hair Translucent red / orange The wild Good Guy mane Face & hands Translucent tan / flesh Scarred doll skin Eyes Translucent blue The piercing stare Overalls Translucent blue The "Good Guys" dungarees Ring panes Translucent red, blue, yellow, orange The radial glass wheel + flames 🎨 No multi-color setup? Print the black frame solid and backfill panes with translucent filament swaps by color, or paint clear panes with glass paint. It reads great either way. 📏 Scale to fit your window. If you scale down, keep an eye on the thin leading lines — they're what hold the piece together. Tips & Tricks Print flat, no supports — the panel lies on the plate and needs nothing under it. Go translucent for the glow — transparent/translucent PETG is what makes it read as real stained glass in a sunny window. Keep the aligned rectilinear pattern — it's what gives the even, light-through-glass diffusion. Hang it where the light moves — an east or west window gives the best changing glow through the day. Solid PLA is a valid look too — an opaque mosaic version reads great on a wall or shelf. Chicago Screw Paramétrico com Rosca Real — OpenSCAD Gerador paramétrico de Chicago Screws (parafuso macho + poste fêmea) desenvolvido em OpenSCAD e otimizado para fabricação por impressão 3D. O modelo utiliza a biblioteca BOSL2 para gerar roscas helicoidais reais, permitindo que as duas peças sejam impressas separadamente e posteriormente rosqueadas entre si. Todas as principais dimensões podem ser ajustadas diretamente nos parâmetros do arquivo, permitindo criar conjuntos personalizados para diferentes espessuras, aplicações e tolerâncias de impressão. Características Conjunto completo com peça macho e peça fêmea. Rosca interna e externa geometricamente modeladas. Dimensões totalmente parametrizáveis. Comprimento do poste configurável. Diâmetro externo do poste configurável. Diâmetros superior e inferior da cabeça configuráveis. Espessura da cabeça configurável. Diâmetro e passo da rosca configuráveis. Fenda para chave de fenda. Controle de tolerância entre as roscas através do $slop. Geometria preparada para impressão 3D. Visualização automática das duas peças lado a lado no OpenSCAD. Dependência Este projeto utiliza a biblioteca BOSL2 — Belfry OpenSCAD Library . BOSL2 deve estar instalada na pasta de bibliotecas do OpenSCAD ou disponível junto ao projeto. Parâmetros principais post_length Define o comprimento útil do poste fêmea. post_outer_d Define o diâmetro externo do poste. head_d_s Define o diâmetro superior da cabeça. head_d_i Define o diâmetro inferior da cabeça. head_thickness Define a espessura da cabeça. thread_d Define o diâmetro nominal da rosca. pitch Define o passo entre os filetes da rosca. slot_width Define a largura da fenda para chave de fenda. slot_depth Define a profundidade da fenda. $slop Controla a folga entre a rosca interna e externa, sendo especialmente útil para compensar as tolerâncias da impressão 3D. Ajuste para impressão 3D O valor de $slop é um dos parâmetros mais importantes para garantir que o parafuso e o poste possam ser rosqueados após a impressão. O valor padrão utilizado no projeto é: $slop = 0.15 Dependendo da impressora, material, diâmetro do bico e calibração de fluxo, pode ser necessário aumentar ou reduzir esse valor. Como referência inicial: menor folga: aproximadamente 0.10 folga padrão: aproximadamente 0.15 maior folga: aproximadamente 0.20 Recomenda-se realizar um pequeno teste de rosca antes de produzir peças maiores ou múltiplas unidades. Configuração padrão do modelo O conjunto fornecido utiliza aproximadamente: Poste fêmea: 14 mm Diâmetro externo do poste: 6 mm Rosca: 3 mm Passo: 0,6 mm Cabeça: aproximadamente 8–10 mm Espessura da cabeça: 0,8 mm O parafuso macho possui comprimento calculado proporcionalmente ao comprimento do poste. Observação O modelo foi projetado principalmente para impressão 3D FDM . Roscas pequenas são bastante sensíveis à calibração da impressora, largura de linha, fluxo, altura de camada e características do filamento. Para roscas próximas de 3 mm, recomenda-se utilizar boa resolução de camada e realizar testes de tolerância antes da produção definitiva.

description: Create a custom print-in-place chain in the length and style you want. ChainMaker is a fully parametric OpenSCAD generator for classic interlocking chains and sculpted Cuban chains. Choose a target length or link count, customize the link geometry, and arrange the chain to suit your build plate. Smart sizing, layout, spacing, and validation systems handle the technical work behind the scenes, so you can focus on designing the chain instead of constructing it. Click Customize to open the generator. 🚀 Quick Start 1. Choose the Chain Select Classic for alternating interlocking links or Cuban for smooth, flattened links. Set a target stretched length, enter a manual link count, and resize the complete design with Link Scale . 2. Choose the Layout Arrange the chain as a Closed Loop , Closed Snake , Straight line, or compact Spiral . Use Print Spacing to control the distance between neighboring links, and adjust the bend or layout-specific settings when needed. 3. Customize the Links Classic links support rounded or chamfered paths, multiple profiles, profile twist, thickness, and interlocking angle. Cuban links provide control over radii, thickness, Bezier shaping, and face flattening. Enable Connector Link to open one end link for attachments or reconnecting the chain. Enable Debug to view calculated chain and layout information. 4. Preview and Export Inspect the complete layout in your slicer and check that all links remain separate. Once satisfied, export your chain at the desired resolution and print. Have fun! ⭐ Features Two Link Families Create two distinct chain families with one shared sizing and layout system. Smart Length Solving Enter a target length or choose the exact number of links yourself. Flexible Print Layouts Use rounded loops, compact closed snakes, straight chains, or spirals. Measured Diagnostics View solved length, link count, pitch, bend, and layout size. Print-Focused Workflow Tune spacing, test clearances, and export clean printable geometry. 🖨️ Printing Advice Print-in-place chains depend heavily on first-layer accuracy and clearance. Use a brim for small chains with limited build-plate contact. Enable variable layer height for smoother steep curves. Inspect the chain carefully in the slicer. Print the Clearance Test before committing to unfamiliar geometry or materials. ChainMaker uses mathematical spacing, envelope, closure, and bend calculations, but extreme custom shapes should still be checked visually before printing. Closed chains have no clasp. For wearable designs, make sure it passes over the hand or head, or use an open chain with your own clasp. Integrated functional clasps may be added in a future update if there is enough interest. ℹ️ Notes For additional guidance and troubleshooting, see the Frequently Asked Questions attached to this post. *** Images are actual photographed Prints. This is a fully 3D-printable eyewear design that you can print, finish, and assemble entirely at home. It requires no screws, hinges, or extra hardware—all you need is some super glue and a bit of post-processing to get a clean, functional pair of glasses. This model is designed to support standard and prescription lenses, making it both a stylish accessory and a practical daily wear option. For ordering lenses in the EU: I found Lens4Glasses to be an affordable option that ships across the EU. Important: Please ask your optician not to heat the frame when fitting the lenses. The frame is designed to fit the lenses without heating—and yes, they will deform your eyewear and send it back! 🙂 Key Features Two Sizes Included: Comes in two different sizes to help ensure a proper fit for different face shapes. Lens-Ready: Designed to accommodate both standard non-prescription lenses and prescription lenses. 100% Hardware-Free: No need to source tiny screws or specialized hinges. Easy Assembly: Simple joint design secured with a small amount of super glue. Recommended Print Settings To ensure the best surface finish and structural strength, the following settings are recommended: Layer Height: 0.10mm to 0.15mm (highly recommended for smoother curves and easier sanding) Infill: 40% – 50% Supports: Required. You will need to enable supports for the curved sections of the temples (the arms that go behind the ears). Material Compatibility This model has been tested with several filaments, and you can print it using almost any standard material: Bambu PLA-CF: Highly recommended. The carbon fiber texture provides a premium matte finish and excellent structural rigidity. Wood PLA: Gives a unique, organic aesthetic. It looks great but will require extra sanding and finishing to get a smooth feel. Standard PLA/PETG: Works well and offers a wide range of color choices. Assembly & Post-Processing Sanding: To achieve a comfortable fit and clean look, thoroughly sand the frames and temples. Start with a coarser grit (like 220) to smooth out print lines, and finish with a wet sand (400 to 1000 grit) for a smooth surface. Dry Fit: Test-fit the temples into the frame joints before applying any glue to ensure they align properly. Gluing: Apply a very small drop of super glue (cyanoacrylate) to the connection points. Hold the pieces firmly in place Lens Installation How to install: Standard scanned or custom-cut lenses can be snapped directly into the frame from the inside. Important Note: Do not apply heat (such as hot water or a hairdryer) to the frame during installation. Heating the plastic can cause the printed frame to warp or lose its shape. The lenses are designed to snap into place easily at room temperature.

description: 骨羁・荒墟（Bone Bond・Desolate Ruin） 骨羁・荒墟白瓷戒指，是暗黑先锋雕塑美学与德化高白瓷烧制工艺碰撞诞生的艺术首饰，打破大众对骷髅配饰冰冷粗粝的固有印象，以温润瓷质重构生死艺术。整件首饰以写实人类颅骨为视觉核心，匠人手工精雕颅骨全部细节，深邃眼窝、立体鼻骨、整齐齿列完整复刻人体骨骼肌理，凹凸起伏精准写实，既还原骨骼原生力量感，又不会带来狰狞压迫感。环绕骷髅的镂空结构由仿生掌骨、指骨交错编织而成，一节节骨节轮廓饱满圆润，骨骼线条纵横交错，层层围合形成牢笼框架，如同肉身羁绊困住灵魂，极具故事氛围感。 主材选用顶级德化羊脂白瓷，历经 1300℃高温多次入窑烧制，瓷胎密度紧实坚硬，抗磕碰、耐磨损，釉面呈现柔和细腻的亮白光泽，没有工业塑料的廉价惨白，触感顺滑温润。镂空是整件作品的灵魂，错落的骨骼缝隙让光线自由穿梭，转动戒指时光影不断流转，骨骼的硬朗线条与白瓷的温润质感形成强烈反差，刚柔平衡恰到好处。戒圈做加厚圆弧打磨，保证结构稳固的同时减轻整体重量，长时间佩戴不会硌压手指，内圈全圆角处理，亲肤顺滑。 设计内核探讨束缚与本我的博弈，交错骨骼象征世俗规则、外界标签层层桎梏，居中骷髅代表最真实的自我，寓意挣脱他人定义，接纳完整的自我，拥有直面本心的勇气。穿搭适配度极强，无论是街头高街、机能工装、哥特暗黑穿搭，还是极简黑白通勤风都可以适配，男女皆可佩戴，风格辨识度独一档。不同于金属骷髅配饰容易氧化发黑、触感冷硬，白瓷性质稳定，防水防汗，常年佩戴依旧莹白干净。全程手工修雕，骨骼缠绕走向没有标准化模板，每一枚纹路都具备独一无二的手工痕迹，兼具穿搭装饰价值与小众收藏属性。它拒绝流水线的千篇一律，把哲学思考藏于指尖方寸，酷感内敛高级，小众不易撞款，既是穿搭点睛配饰，也是承载精神态度的微型雕塑。 Bone Bond · Desolate Ruin white porcelain ring is an artistic jewelry born from the collision of avant-garde dark sculptural aesthetics and Dehua high-white porcelain firing craftsmanship. It subverts people’s stereotype of cold and rough skull accessories, reshaping life-and-death art with tender porcelain texture. Centered on a realistic human skull, the ring is manually carved with exquisite details, including deep eye sockets, three-dimensional nasal bones and neat teeth, perfectly restoring physical bone texture. It retains the primitive power of bones without intimidating ferocity. The hollow frame wrapping the skull is woven by bionic metacarpals and phalanges. description: 浪漫复古花卉/玫瑰戒指（3D 打印款）完整说明 一、项目主要特点 立体层叠花卉一体造型 戒圈上方立体绽放多层花瓣花朵，花瓣自然卷曲舒展，瓣内雕刻细腻放射纹路，复古文艺、国风、轻奢小众风格，造型大气优雅，穿搭辨识度极高。 一体式闭环戒圈结构 整体无缝一体成型，戒圈壁厚均匀，可精准缩放内径适配不同手指尺寸，内侧曲面顺滑贴合指腹，佩戴稳固不易滑动，受力不易断裂。 高精度花瓣肌理细节 完整复刻花瓣卷曲弧度、瓣内放射纹理、花心立体凸起结构，3D 打印层纹自带细腻磨砂雕刻质感，素模可打磨抛光、手工做旧上色，DIY 改造空间充足。 多功能多用设计 主打复古花卉个性戒指，也可作为国风、森系装扮道具、桌面迷你摆件、静物拍摄道具、小众创意礼品，同时可作为金属首饰翻模原型。 低支撑友好打印模型 仅外层花瓣尖端少量悬空，仅需局部简易支撑，环形戒圈主体无大面积悬空，FDM 打印机成型稳定，新手打印不易失败。 两种打印材质可选 PLA 性价比高，适合静态摆件、短期搭配使用；PETG 韧性更强，抗弯折、耐汗水侵蚀，长期贴身佩戴不易脆裂变形。 二、适用场景 & 适配人群 1. 日常穿搭佩戴 立体花卉复古指环，国风、森系、文艺轻奢小众穿搭配饰适配人群：国风穿搭爱好者、文艺女生、手工涂装 DIY 玩家、创意首饰定制人群 2. 道具装饰用途 古风汉服、森系主题装扮道具、桌面小众潮玩摆件、静物摄影拍摄道具、节日送礼成品 3. 二次加工衍生 金属首饰浇筑翻模原型、树脂复刻白模、做旧古银 / 哑光上色创作素材 三、3D 打印设置（0.4mm 标准喷嘴通用参数） 方案 A：PLA（低成本、摆件 / 短期搭配） 层高：0.15mm（完美还原花瓣细密纹路；赶工期快速打印可选 0.2mm 层高） 壁厚 / 周长：3–4 圈（壁厚≥1.2mm，提升戒圈抗弯折强度） 填充率：15% 蜂窝填充，兼顾结构强度，节省耗材 喷嘴温度：200–210℃ 热床温度：首层 65℃，后续 60℃，防止戒圈底部翘边变形 打印速度：外壁 35mm/s，内部填充 55mm/s 支撑：仅外层花瓣边缘开启局部支撑，环形戒圈主体无需支撑 底部厚度 1.2mm，顶部封层 1.0mm 适用局限：不耐长期汗水浸泡，高温环境易软化形变，不适合长期贴身佩戴 方案 B：PETG（长期贴身佩戴推荐款） 层高：0.15mm 壁厚 / 周长：3–4 圈（1.2–1.6mm，韧性更强，弯折不易断裂） 填充率：15%–20% 蜂窝填充 喷嘴温度：240–250℃ 热床温度：全程 70–75℃持续加热 风扇：首层关闭，第 3 层后风扇全开 打印速度：外壁 30mm/s，填充 45mm/s 支撑：仅花瓣尖端添加简易支撑 优化设置：开启熨烫功能，戒圈内壁光滑平整，佩戴不磨手指皮肤 核心优势：防水抗汗、耐摔不易开裂，温差环境不易变形，适合日常长期佩戴 补充打印小贴士 尺寸缩放参考常规戒指内径 18–22mm；加大道具款内径 24–28mm；摆件放大款 90–120mm 后处理优化打印完成后用细砂纸逐层打磨支撑残留毛刺，可喷涂哑光银、复古做旧漆，还原做旧银饰质感；也可手绘上色打造彩色花卉效果 保养说明PETG 款可清水直接擦拭清洁；PLA 款避免长期接触汗液、阳光暴晒、暖气等高温热源

Bring a touch of nature and elegance to your wrist with this Orchid Lace Bracelet . This design combines the precision of 3D printing with a simple and fun post-processing technique (thermoforming) to create a perfectly curved, comfortable piece of wearable art. It features a delicate, lace-like pattern inspired by the beautiful silhouettes of orchids, making it a perfect accessory or a unique gift. 💡 The Concept & Credit This model is designed to be printed completely flat on your print bed and then shaped using hot water. Stop struggling to roll tiny, perfectly uniform spheres by hand! This compact dual-plate roller set is designed to effortlessly form identical mini spheres out of nail art gel, modeling clay, play dough, polymer clay, or fondant. Available in 3 distinct size variants (1 mm, 2 mm, and 3 mm), it is an essential tool for nail tech artists, miniature sculptors, DIY crafters, and cake decorators who need consistent, clean results in seconds. The design features a matching pair of textured plates with parallel semi-circular grooves tailored to your chosen bead size. Simply place your material in small, roughly measured amounts between the two plates, press lightly, and slide them back and forth in a linear motion. The guided channels rapidly shape the soft material into round, smooth spheres with perfectly equal diameters every single time. It serves as a highly reusable, durable, and easy-to-clean alternative to manual hand-rolling, bringing ultimate symmetry and precision to your nail art designs, miniature details, or craft projects. Features: ✔ 3 Size Variants: Choose between 1 mm, 2 mm, or 3 mm versions to match your specific project needs ✔ Parallel groove channels engineered to form perfectly round, uniform spheres instantly ✔ Multi-material utility suitable for solid nail gels, modeling clay, fondant, and resin crafts ✔ Ergonomic textured exterior providing a firm, comfortable grip during rolling motions ✔ Compact two-piece system that stores flat and cleans off effortlessly ✔ Time-saving tool ensuring consistent sizing across multiple decorative beads ✔ A practical, versatile crafting essential and a great novelty gift for nail techs and artists 📋 How to Use (Step-by-Step): Prepare Material - Place a small piece of clay or gel on the flat back side of the roller. Premium sunglasses case. There are a few varieties to choose from. They by default have fuzzy skin turned on for parts of it to make it look more proffesional. This summer, I went on several trips. I like to take sunglasses, because they're convenient for driving, and we were in the sun a lot. However, (I have four pairs that I took on the trips) I had to store them in a zip up pocket that I hoped would protect them. It didn't sadly. I stored them in there with books, chargers, devices - anything you'd take on a vacation. I opened up the pocket and there my fancy pink aviators were, bent all out of shape. I had to try to bend them back into shape, and even then they fit too loosely on my head. This is designed to completely prevent things like that from happening. Looks good in almost any color. Here's a few instructions: Magnets You need 10 8x2mm round magnets for this, linked below in the BOM. If you don't want to use that much, just put 6 in; two pairs in the corners, and one in the hole closest to the center. Works very well either way. The magnets should friction fit pretty well but if any are too loose just put a drop of superglue. TPU padding. You can optionally print a TPU pad for the lenses to not get scratched. You don't need it, but it is recommended. I have also included a DXF file if you want to lasercut it out of something else, like cork (for looks), felt, foam, etc. If you slice it yourself, don't forget to turn off the top and bottom layers so it is directly cushioned by the infill. I simulated the case getting smashed in a suitcase by, say a laptop corner or just something. I know that it simulates solid PLA instead of printed, so I tested it with a 15mm cube pushing with 500 lbf of force to make completely sure. With that force it deformed by 2.5~mm . Should be completely fine with whatever you're taking it in! If you have any suggestions just comment!

description: One customizable OpenSCAD generator for everyday personalized tags: keychains, luggage tags, fridge magnets, screw plates, bin labels, door signs, and desk nameplates. Universal Personalized Tag Generator Pro expands a simple winning keychain label into a broader personal-label generator. Choose a mode, type your text, and generate a practical tag for keys, bags, storage bins, fridge notes, tool panels, doors, desks, and workshop organization. The first build includes seven fast MakerWorld-ready modes: `keychain` , `luggage_tag` , `fridge_magnet` , `screw_plate` , `bin_label` , `door_sign` , and `desk_nameplate` . Each mode has sensible default size, shape, text layout, and mounting, while manual overrides let you tune the width, height, thickness, shape, mount type, and text style. Mounting options include single ring hole, double ring holes, strap slot, blind magnet pockets, screw holes with counterbores, adhesive tape recess, and no-mount plates. The default text style uses raised lettering so color changes near the top layers are easy on a standard FDM printer. Optional text styles include engraved, recessed, and inlay-ready lettering for paint, resin, or filament-fill workflows. The desk nameplate mode prints as a simple support-free wedge with text on the sloped face. Customization Notes - Use `tag_mode` first, then leave `size_preset` , `mount_type` , `text_layout` , and `shape_style` on `mode_default` for a quick printable result. - Leave `color_style` on `raised` for the easiest two-color print with a filament swap near the top layers. - Use `inlay_ready` for deeper lettering pockets that can be filled after printing. - Use `fridge_magnet` or `magnet_pockets` for blind underside magnet pockets; glue magnets in after printing. - Use `screw_plate` or `door_sign` for screw holes with counterbores. - Use `back_side` for simple underside ID text such as phone number, serial number, property label, or emergency info. - Keep very long labels short or reduce the font size for narrow tags.
