description: 3 parametrische Rohrmodelle Dieses Set enthält drei vollständig anpassbare Rohrmodelle für den MakerWorld Parametric Model Maker . Alle Abmessungen werden in Millimetern angegeben und können direkt vor der Erstellung des Modells verändert werden. Enthalten sind: ein gerader Rohradapter zum Vergrößern oder Reduzieren eines Durchmessers ein Rohrwinkel mit frei einstellbarem Winkel eine U-förmige Rohrbefestigung für die Wand Die Modelle eignen sich unter anderem für Werkstattprojekte, Absaugungen, Belüftungen, Kabeldurchführungen, Modellbau und individuelle Rohrinstallationen. 1. Rohradapter / Reduzierstück mit 45°-Übergang Der Rohradapter verbindet zwei unterschiedliche Rohrdurchmesser miteinander. Zwischen den beiden geraden Rohrabschnitten befindet sich ein automatisch berechneter, konischer Übergang mit einer Flankensteigung von 45° . Der Adapter kann sowohl als Reduzierstück als auch als Vergrößerungsstück verwendet werden. Sind beide Durchmesser identisch, entsteht automatisch ein gerades Rohrstück. Einstellbare Parameter diameter_1 – Außendurchmesser der ersten Seite diameter_2 – Außendurchmesser der zweiten Seite thickness – Wandstärke des Adapters length – Länge jedes geraden Rohrabschnitts bis zum 45°-Übergang Die Länge des konischen Übergangs wird automatisch anhand der beiden Durchmesser berechnet. Wichtig diameter_1 und diameter_2 beziehen sich auf die Außendurchmesser des gedruckten Adapters . Die jeweiligen Innendurchmesser ergeben sich aus: Innendurchmesser = Außendurchmesser − 2 × Wandstärke Der Begriff „45°“ beschreibt hier den konischen Übergang zwischen den Durchmessern und nicht eine Richtungsänderung des Rohres. Geeignet für Rohrreduzierungen und Rohrerweiterungen Absaug- und Lüftungsleitungen Schlauch- und Geräteanschlüsse Werkstattadapter individuelle Übergangsstücke 2. Parametrischer Rohrwinkel Das zweite Modell erzeugt ein gebogenes, hohles Rohrstück mit frei einstellbarer Richtungsänderung. Dadurch können beispielsweise 30°-, 45°-, 60°- oder 90°-Winkel erstellt werden. Auf beiden Seiten des Bogens befindet sich ein gerader Rohrabschnitt mit identischer Länge. Einstellbare Parameter diameter – Außendurchmesser des Rohrwinkels thickness – Wandstärke des Rohrwinkels length – gerade Rohrlänge je Seite, gemessen ab dem Bogen angle – gewünschte Richtungsänderung in Grad Der Biegeradius wird automatisch passend zum eingestellten Rohrdurchmesser erzeugt. Wichtig diameter bezeichnet den Außendurchmesser des gedruckten Rohrwinkels . Der Innendurchmesser ergibt sich aus: Innendurchmesser = diameter − 2 × thickness Der Parameter length gilt für beide Seiten einzeln. Bei einer Einstellung von 30 mm besitzt der Winkel daher vor und nach dem Bogen jeweils einen geraden Rohrabschnitt von 30 mm. Geeignet für Rohrleitungen mit individuellen Winkeln Absaug- und Belüftungssysteme Kabel- oder Schlauchführungen Modellbau Prototypen und Sonderlösungen 3. Rohrbefestigung für die Wand Das dritte Modell ist eine U- beziehungsweise Omega-förmige Rohrhalterung. Das Rohr wird vom gebogenen Bereich umschlossen, während die beiden nach außen umgeklappten Enden an einer Wand oder einer anderen ebenen Fläche befestigt werden können. In den beiden Befestigungslaschen befinden sich Schraublöcher. Einstellbare Parameter diameter – Außendurchmesser des zu befestigenden Rohres thickness – Materialstärke der Halterung width – Breite der Halterung entlang des Rohres Die Länge der beiden Befestigungslaschen wird automatisch an den Rohrdurchmesser angepasst. Passung und Schraublöcher Das Modell besitzt standardmäßig ein radiales Spiel von ungefähr 0,4 mm . Dadurch ist der Innendurchmesser der Halterung etwa 0,8 mm größer als der eingestellte Rohrdurchmesser. Beispiel: diameter = 40 mm Innendurchmesser der Halterung ≈ 40,8 mm Die beiden Befestigungslöcher besitzen in der aktuellen Version einen Durchmesser von 4,5 mm und sind damit beispielsweise für M4-Schrauben geeignet. Geeignet für Befestigung von Rohren und Schläuchen Kabel- und Leitungsführung Werkstatt- und Garageninstallationen Absaugrohre leichte Rohrsysteme und Modellbauprojekte Die mögliche Belastung hängt vom verwendeten Filament, der Wandstärke, der Druckausrichtung, den Schrauben und dem jeweiligen Untergrund ab. Hinweise zum 3D-Druck Für normale Anwendungen eignen sich PLA oder PETG. Für wärmere Umgebungen, Werkstätten oder Bereiche mit höherer mechanischer Belastung ist PETG, ASA oder ein vergleichbar widerstandsfähiges Material meist besser geeignet. Als Ausgangspunkt können folgende Einstellungen verwendet werden: Schichthöhe: 0,20 mm Wandlinien: 4–6 Obere/untere Lagen: 4–6 Infill: 25–40 % Der Rohradapter lässt sich durch seinen 45°-Übergang normalerweise ohne Stützmaterial drucken. Die Wandhalterung sollte mit den beiden Befestigungslaschen flach auf dem Druckbett positioniert werden. Beim Rohrwinkel kann abhängig vom gewählten Winkel und der Ausrichtung Stützmaterial erforderlich sein. Für Steck-, Klemm- oder Klebeverbindungen sollte zusätzlich eine passende Drucktoleranz berücksichtigt werden. Diese hängt vom Drucker, Filament und der gewünschten Passung ab. Für eine lose Steckverbindung sind häufig etwa 0,2 bis 0,5 mm Spiel pro Seite sinnvoll. Ein kurzer Testdruck ist bei präzisen Verbindungen empfehlenswert.

model_name: BC-6 Cooler – Ice Pack for the BC-6. 33 and 50cl
description: Update 2026-07-29. updated the model to fit with BC-6 MK2 The BC-6 Cooler is a reusable ice pack designed specifically for the BC-6 can carrier. It sits between the two rows of cans, while the curved sides follow the shape of the cans to provide a large contact area and more effective cooling. The cooler is filled with water through the removable plug and then placed in the freezer. Features Designed specifically for the BC-6 carrier Cools cans on both sides Refillable and reusable Large contact area against the cans Removable plug for easy filling Can be stored ready to use in the freezer Designed for straightforward 3D printing and assembly How to Fill It Carefully remove the filling plug using the correct Allen key (8mm). Make sure the inside is clean. Fill the cooler approximately 80–85% with ordinary water . Leave at least 15% empty space because water expands when it freezes. Reinstall the plug and tighten it gently. Do not overtighten it, as this may damage the threads or printed part. Wipe the cooler dry and check it carefully for leaks. For the first leak test, place it on a paper towel before freezing. Do not fill it completely. A fully filled container may crack or split when the water freezes. How to Use It Freeze the cooler for at least 8–12 hours , preferably overnight. Place the frozen cooler in the centre of the BC-6 carrier. Place three cans on each side of the cooler. After use, wipe it clean and return it to the freezer. For the best cooling performance, both the cans and the cooler should already be cold before being placed in the carrier. Important Information Ordinary water is recommended. Avoid unnecessary additives. Check regularly for cracks, damage or leaks. Do not use the cooler if it is damaged. The contents are not intended for drinking. Wash by hand using lukewarm water. Do not place it in a dishwasher or microwave, and avoid hot water. A watertight print and a properly sealed filling plug are required. PETG is generally more suitable than PLA for repeated freezer use.

Im Code diese Werte anpassen: #define SERPENTINE false #define ORIGIN_TOP_LEFT true #define FLIP_X false #define FLIP_Y false Viele 8×8 LED-Matrizen sind unterschiedlich aufgebaut. Wenn die Anzeige nicht passt, zuerst SERPENTINE ändern. Danach bei Bedarf FLIP_X oder FLIP_Y testen. Zusammenbau Gehäuseteile drucken. ESP32, AMG8833 und LED-Matrix probeweise ins Gehäuse legen. AMG8833 mit 3V3, GND, SDA und SCL verbinden. LED-Matrix mit 5V, GND und GPIO 5 verbinden. Alle GND-Leitungen miteinander verbinden. Firmware auf den ESP32 laden. Vor dem Verschließen testen, ob Sensor und LEDs funktionieren. AMG8833 so einsetzen, dass der Sensor nach vorne zeigt. LED-Matrix hinter die Frontöffnung bzw. den Diffusor setzen. Kabel sauber verlegen und Gehäuse verschließen. Mit dem WLAN ThermalCamera verbinden und http://4.3.2.1 öffnen. Falls nötig, Ausrichtung der Anzeige im Browser anpassen. Fehlerbehebung Problem Mögliche Ursache / Lösung AMG8833 wird nicht gefunden SDA/SCL vertauscht, falsche Spannung, GND fehlt LED-Matrix bleibt dunkel 5V/GND prüfen, DIN prüfen, Richtungspfeil der Matrix beachten ESP32 startet ständig neu Stromversorgung zu schwach, Helligkeit reduzieren Bild ist gespiegelt FLIP_X, FLIP_Y oder Browser-Einstellungen anpassen Bild ist um 90° verdreht Rotation im Browser ändern WLAN erscheint nicht ESP32 neu starten, Code erneut hochladen, seriellen Monitor prüfen Browser zeigt keine Daten Mit dem WLAN ThermalCamera verbinden und http://4.3.2.1 öffnen Hinweise Diese Wärmebildkamera ist ein DIY-Maker-Projekt und kein kalibriertes Messgerät. model_name: FFB-01: A Force Feedback Sim Racing Steering Wheel
description: Recently I wanted to get into sim racing, so I looked up some “good” cheaper racing wheels. Like many others, I found the Logitech G29. However, that wheel goes for $230 (with pedals) and has sloppy feedback and is not very precise. So after seeing Daz Project's video , I decided to go down the large rabbit hole of making my own. I present to you the FFB-01; A precise, premium, and affordable force feedback racing wheel you can make yourself for as little as $144! If you want to get into sim racing without spending hundreds of dollars, this wheel is for you. This is a 3D printable direct drive force feedback steering wheel powered by the FFBeast firmware. It delivers strong, responsive force feedback, and since it uses open source FFBeast firmware, you don't need to do any coding. Just upload the firmware and you're done. The design is based around a hoverboard motor. Because of the design and strength of the hoverboard motor, you get up to 15nm of torque and direct drive precision. It is also completely silent! I made sure this project is as beginner-friendly as possible and goes together with basic tools. For more info about the build prosses, check out the PDF instructions! This wheel is fully printable on the A1 Mini! A1 Mini print profiles can be found above :) I included the STEP file for a blank middle steering wheel cap so that you can put whatever logo you want on it! Want more sim racing gear? Be sure to check out my new 6-speed manual sim racing shifter here! I would love to here your feedback (pun intended) and comments about this project! BOM: - XT60H connectors (1 pair) - Makerbase MKS XRIVE MINI - 24V 15A 360W Power Supply - E6B2CWZ6C Rotary Encoder (2000 P/R) - GT2 Belt (Width 10mm, 198mm) - Aluminum Linear Shaft Support (SK16) - 16 gauge ofc wire - M3x25 (4) - M3x20 (12) - M3x12 (14) - M3x10 (22) - M3 thread inserts (54) - AC Power Cord - 6.5" Hoverboard Motor All of these parts together cost $144 at the time of writing this. This includes everything! From controller board to the 16 gauge wire. Prices may change. I made this racing wheel with inspiration from Daz Projects wheel. Daz Projects has lots of genius creations and designs. Go check his stuff out here!

Fully printed system to make plaster moulds. This produces a 3-part mould to cast a mini cauldron and lid This print has been scaled to 112% to account for clay shrinkage, which should give a final ornament size of 6cm diameter with most casting slips. If you want it smaller/larger than 6cm, scale every piece of the print. This design has a lid at one end and the cauldron at the other. You should be able to cast both at the same time (ish) by casting one end first, then casting the second while the slip is fully draining out the first. Because of the double ended design, this printed model is particularly difficult to demould from the plaster , and I've added several extra slots for extra flexibility (with extra caps to cover them while casting plaster). The more you sand/smooth your print and the better your release agent, the easier the process will be, but I wouldn't recommend this mould as a first project! With any fully 3D printed mould, you’ll benefit from using a release agent on the base plate surface. I use a generic mouldmaker’s soap, but any product designed for plaster release should be fine. It needs around 375ml of plaster, and you can calculate the weight of water and plaster needed with this tool: Plaster Calculator You can get a much better cast surface, even if your plaster mix is full of air bubbles, by using a paintbrush to dislodge any trapped air from the surface. I would suggest that you pour plaster until the ornament surface is covered but it isn’t completely full, then get a relatively small paintbrush and move it around in the plaster so that you’re brushing all of the details on the base plate surface. This will dislodge air bubbles, and once dislodged they’ll float upwards. Once you’ve finished this, pour in the rest of the plaster. If you manage to avoid adding more air as you do it (just brush gently), you’ll eventually remove all the bubbles from the surface and get a perfect cast. description: Looking for a custom adapter, fitting, reducer, or elbow? Look no further. AdapterGenerator is a fully parametric OpenSCAD generator for hollow adapters. Configure End A and End B independently using round or rectangular spigots and sockets, hose barbs, male or female threads, or bolted flanges, then connect them with a straight, offset, reducing, stepped, or bent transition. From vacuum hose adapters and duct transitions to threaded couplers, nozzles, reducers, and custom fittings, it's built for practical real-world connections. A shared transition system keeps the workflow simple, while independent end geometry, fit allowance, taper, bends, seals, wrench flats, and finishing controls let you tailor the result to the connection you need. Click Customize to open the generator. 🚀 Quick Start 1. Choose End A Select the first interface type and enter its size, length, and any interface-specific settings. 2. Choose End B Configure the second end independently. Mix sockets, spigots, hose barbs, threads, flanges, or rectangular fittings as needed. 3. Shape the Transition Set the transition length and optional offset. Use a length of 0 for an abrupt stepped connection. 4. Add a Bend Set the bend angle, radius, and rotation to create straight adapters or custom elbows. 5. Refine and Export Adjust fit, wall thickness, barbs, threads, O-ring grooves, flanges, and finishing details, then choose the desired output and quality. ⭐ Features Mix-and-Match Interfaces Connect round or rectangular sockets and spigots, hose barbs, threads, and flanges. Flexible Transitions Create reducers, enlargers, stepped adapters, and eccentric or offset connections. Custom Elbows Add bends up to 180° with adjustable centerline radius and rotation. Functional Details Add tapers, hose barbs, wrench flats, O-ring grooves, flange bolt patterns, chamfers, and socket lead-ins. Preview & Test Tools Use section views, test pieces, and Debug mode to inspect geometry and dimensions. ℹ️ Notes Some controls apply only to specific interfaces. Rectangular dimensions require rectangular ends, thread settings require threaded ends, and O-ring grooves support round sockets and flange faces. The generator validates many incompatible dimensions and clearances. Still inspect short transitions, large offsets, and tight bends in Section View or your slicer. Use Debug to diagnose geometry. For critical fits, print an End A Test or End B Test first and tune Fit Clearance for your printer and material. Use Print End to choose which end sits on the build plate. description: LUX3: A Minimal Case for the Xteink X3 Credits This design was inspired by the Retro X3 Case and Xteink X4 Full Body Case . Though I designed all geometry from scratch in Fusion 360, I wanted to give credit where it's due, since the overall concept and vibe started with their work. Go check out their cases! About the Case LUX3 is a rounded, minimalist case built specifically for the Xteink X3 e-reader. It intentionally covers several parts of the device (reset button and micro SD card slot) to keep it looking and feeling as clean as possible. The lower back portion has a subtle arch/contour pattern for grip and visual interest without breaking the minimal look. It's a snap-fit case, no adhesives or hardware required, designed to closely hug the X3's body while still being easy to get on and off. What's New in V2 Huge thanks to everyone who printed V1 and sent feedback, it directly shaped these changes: Added an alternate lanyard version (see new print profile) Added alternate flush-mount buttons for a smoother front profile (see new print profile) Fixed a fit issue at the upper corners (front and back weren't sitting flush) by adding small locking notches and adjusting tolerances Reworked tolerances throughout the case for a more consistent fit across different printers Slightly enlarged the chin for a cleaner print on the bottom front face and added extra drop protection Loosened up the front button housings so buttons no longer feel too snug Optimized the print profile for the cleanest results yet More excitingly, I've also created and uploaded two new accessories for the LUX3 V2 case: Stand: Holds the X3 cleanly on a desk or nightstand: https://makerworld.com/en/models/3107171-desk-stand-for-lux3-xteink-x3-case#profileId-3503118 Front Cover: Snaps onto the case to protect the screen: https://makerworld.com/en/models/3107147-snap-on-screen-cover-for-lux3-xteink-x3-case#profileId-3503084 Assembly Guide Insert the front facing buttons into the front case piece. Insert the X3 screen-down, then add the side button with the extended lip facing down (toward the front of the device). Slide the top back half on using the guide rails on the side. Slide on the bottom back half until it snaps into place with the top back half. Admire your now protected X3 :) Misc. Notes Note that the new accessories mentioned above will only work with the new V2 case. If youve printed a V1, you will need to repreint a V2 to use the accessories Photos shown were printed in Bambu Lab PLA Small parts mean a clean print bed matters, make sure to clean yours beforehand! All configuration settings in my 3mf file are recommendations based on my testing, but feel free to alter them. That said, these seemed to matter the most .1mm layer height Concentric bottom surface patter for lower back piece Concentric top surface patter for buttons (this just looks nice) Feedback shaped this whole update, so keep it coming. model_name: Working Telescopic Micro Fishing Rod with reel
description: buymeacoffee.com/Metatronic All your boosts , likes and downloads inspire me to do more , this is also my full time job so any help is so much appricated , love you all :) TL;DR A compact, fully 3D printed telescopic fishing rod inspired by Japanese micro-fishing. It collapses to around 100 mm, extends to roughly 300 mm, includes a working reel, and is designed to print flat on the bed for maximum strength. The Idea Behind It The idea for this rod came after I discovered Japanese micro-fishing, where people target extremely small fish and even hold competitions for the smallest catch. I had never really thought about fishing for tiny fish before, so I started researching the hooks, line and equipment used. My first version was made from wood, but it needed too much assembly and was not very practical. That made me think, I have a 3D printer, so why not design something that does exactly what I want? This rod is the result. It is designed for small fish, from little perch and similar species down to true micro-fishing sizes. Check out the video to see the wee perch I caught with it. Pocket-Sized Design The rod measures around 100 mm when collapsed and approximately 300 mm when fully extended . The goal was to make something small enough to keep in a pocket without it becoming a hassle to carry. It works well as a backup rod, or for those times when the bigger fish are not biting but there are plenty of smaller fish nearby. Designed for Strength This was one of the most important parts of the design. Most telescopic prints are printed vertically, which places force across the weaker layer lines. The square shape of this rod allows every telescopic section to be printed flat, so the layers run along the length of the rod instead. This gives it the strongest possible print orientation for its size. The rod feels surprisingly rigid when extended and can handle much more pressure than the small fish it is intended for. Working Reel The rod includes a clip-in reel with a small finger recess, allowing you to wind the line back in by hand. It can also be operated with your thumb, depending on which direction you spool the line. I kept the reel low-profile so the rod remains smooth and compact when collapsed. I may add an optional reel handle accessory in the future. Print Information The model is split across three print plates , making it easier to customise the colours. I highly recommend using the included print profiles, as a lot of testing went into getting the sliding tolerances working correctly. The full rod can be printed in PLA. Assembly Instructions 1. Assemble the Telescopic Sections The rod sections are tapered, so the correct direction should be visible by eye. Keep every part facing the same way, with the build-plate texture aligned on the same side. Slide the sections through one another, then pass the full assembly through the main body. Fit the butt cap onto the bottom once everything is in place. 2. Fit the Eyelets Press the eyelets onto the rod sections. They are designed to fit snugly, but printer tolerances vary, so I recommend using a very small dab of glue to stop them coming loose when the rod is collapsed. 3. Feed the Line Feed the line through: The top eyelet The second eyelet The third eyelet The body eyelet Pull enough line through to give yourself room to attach it to the reel. 4. Attach the Reel Before pressing the reel into the body, feed the line through the reel from the inside to the outside . Adding a small hook-shaped bend to the end of the line makes this easier. Pass the line through a few times, tie it securely, then carefully press the reel into place using firm, even pressure. Wind on your preferred amount of line. I used a few metres, which was plenty for testing. Hook and Weight Storage Once the rod is collapsed and the line has been reeled in, the hook and weight can be tucked into the butt cap. The cap then closes over the end, keeping the rig secure and stopping the hook from moving around loose in your pocket. Important: Tight Tolerances The telescopic sections use very tight tolerances to keep the rod smooth, secure and free from excessive movement. With some filaments, the sections may feel slightly stiff or may not fully extend at first. Gently work the affected section in and out a few times. The parts will usually wear themselves in and become smoother with use. This can vary depending on filament type, moisture and small differences in printing. If the sections remain unusually tight, make sure your filament is dry or try printing them with a different filament. FAQ How long is it? Around 100 mm collapsed and approximately 300 mm fully extended . What material should I use? PLA works well. Does the reel work? Yes, it can be used to wind the fishing line back in. Why is the rod square? The square shape allows the sections to print flat, placing the layer lines along the rod for better strength. Does it need glue? The main parts are designed to fit together without glue, but a tiny amount is recommended on the eyelets. Can it catch real fish? Yes. I caught a small few perch with it, which you can see in the video. enjoy the test pile :) remember for assembly Feed the line through: The top eyelet The second eyelet The third eyelet The body eyelet Pull enough line through to give yourself room to attach it to the reel. Before pressing the reel into the body, feed the line through the reel from the inside to the outside . Adding a small hook-shaped bend to the end of the line makes this easier. Pass the line through a few times, tie it securely, then carefully press the reel into place using firm, even pressure.

description: I picked up embroidery this year and every hoop I bought had the same problem: a metal screw sticking out of the edge, right where my thread wants to travel. It snagged on every pass. So I went looking for a hoop without one. Amazon, Etsy, the craft store. It does not exist. Spring hoops have fixed tension. Press-fit hoops do not adjust. Every adjustable hoop on earth puts the screw on the edge. So I moved it. On this hoop the entire tension mechanism lives in a small bridge behind the frame. The outside edge is completely smooth. You still tighten it clockwise like any hoop, you still get fine control (about 3 turns per millimeter), but there is nothing for your thread to catch on. Ever. Four oval sizes (60x80 up to 140x200 mm). All the hardware tucks completely inside. Prints without supports. Round sizes coming soon. WHAT YOU NEED PER HOOP (not included, standard hardware-store parts): 1x M4x30 socket head cap screw 2x M4 hex nuts a 3mm allen key (for assembly only) Any brand works, metric sizes are standard. Use socket head cap screws and plain hex nuts, not button-head screws and not nylon lock nuts. Always print knobs two at at least .16 high quality, .12mm is best PRINT: No supports, anywhere. Do not rotate parts. PETG recommended for inner rings (they flex when you mount fabric). 0.2mm rings, 0.12mm knobs. Snap the mouse ears off the knob after printing. description: Gen 5 Glock 17 / 19 Magwell for Talon Grips A low-profile magwell designed for Gen 5 Glock 17 and Gen 5 Glock 19 frames, specifically sized to also fit over sandpaper style grip tape . This magwell was designed to also add a more secure lower grip area while keeping it simple, durable, and easy to print. Customized personally the fuzzy skin profile to be aggressive. The lower swell is intentionally shaped higher where your pinky sits, helping give the hand a firmer purchase on the grip. This works especially well on Glock 19's, since the higher swell helps lock the hand in better. Features Fits Gen 5 Glock 17, Glock 19, Gen 6 17 and 19 with some scaling as well. Hardware Uses an M3 flat-style screw . The best-fitting screws I found were spare Holosun RDS screws , which sat flush and fit the design cleanly. Fitment / Install Notes This is a very tight fit. Before installing, visually and physically confirm the firearm is clear and unloaded, then remove the slide. Start at the back of the magwell where the rear pillar inserts. Squeeze both sides of the magwell inward and make sure they are seated inside the frame channels. Once both sides are in the channels, press down with your thumb on the back of the magwell to keep it in place. Next, squeeze the front of the magwell and do the same thing, making sure the front edges are also inside the channels. Once everything is lined up and sitting inside the channels, push the magwell into place. It should pop in. Again, this is a tight fit. Only use an amount of force you are comfortable with and that you know your firearm can handle. Do not force it if something looks misaligned. Testing / Disclaimer Personally tested with over 500 rounds in a single session to check fit and durability. That said, printed parts can vary. SIMPLE . FLYING . FUN Motte RC is a compact two-channel RC biplane designed for relaxed flying on small fields. Smaller and more agile than Hummel RC , it trades a little speed for improved maneuverability and better stability in light wind. Its lightweight modular construction is durable, quick to print and requires little material, while the adjustable wing position makes CG and pitch tuning simple. The model has no movable control surfaces: altitude is controlled by total motor thrust, and turns are performed through differential thrust between the two wing-mounted motors. Motte RC is part of a growing series of simple 2-channel RC aircraft. Each model shares the same accessible control concept while offering a different configuration, appearance and flight character. Motte RC continues the ideas of WingStar , COMET , Wespe , SkyStar , DragonFly and Hummel RC in a compact, vintage-inspired and practical RC model made to fly often. Key Features Control: 2-channel differential thrust Motors: 2 × brushed motors Battery: 1S LiPo Adjustable wing position for CG and pitch tuning Recommended conditions: calm weather or light breeze Suitable for small outdoor fields Why Motte RC? Quick and material-efficient to print Simple modular assembly Easy, Beginners' friendly, two-channel control Replaceable and easy-to-reprint parts Mix and match selected parts from Hummel RC, WingStar, Wespe and COMET to create your own configurations More compatible parts and modular configurations are planned for future updates. 1 - Model Datasheet Wingspan: 346 mm Length: 293 mm Wing chord: 60 mm RC Transmitter and receiver: 2Channel 2.4G FX803 J3 (or equal), link here Battery: 3.7v, 220 mAh, Molex 51005 connector (or equal), link here Motors and Props: 2x716 Coreless motors with 2 props diam 46 mm (or equal), link here Model mass (with RC receiver, battery and motors): 50 g. 2 – Material, Settings, Printing Model design created and tested using Bambu PLA Basi c. Use this material for best results. Do NOT use PLA Matte, especially for the wing parts. Printed parts may deform after removal from the Plate due to internal material strains after cooling. Use recommended print settings. Note: The print profile for A1 mini use slightly higher material flow coefficient (1.03 instead of 0.98). For reliable printing: Clean the printing Plate before printing. After printing, remove the Plate and let it cool for 3-4 minutes Do not remove parts while the Plate is hot. 3 - Model Assembly The model consists of 18 parts, as shown in the figure. 1 – Nose, 2 – PCB Mount, 3 – A-Beam , 4 – B-Beam, 5 – Strut, 6 – Sting, 7 – Tail, 8 – Fin, 9 – Central Bracket, 10 – Dual-pin, 11 – Right Wing, 12 – Left Wing , 13 – Right Rib, 14 – Left Rib, 15 – Gear Strut (Right and Left), 16 – Wheel (2pcs), 17 – Pin (2pcs), 18 – BHCS Screw M2 x 4 mm (3 pcs). RC Receiver, Engines, props are not shown. The following assembly steps are shown without the electronic components installed. It is recommended to review them before installing the motors and electronics. Use cyanoacrylate glue where specifically indicated. Assemble the tail unit and fuselage as shown. Assemble the wing as shown in the figures. Use Dual-pin to fix wings. After installing and fixing the wing surfaces, install Wing Ribs (13, 14) on both sides. Assemble the landing gear struts as shown in the pictures below. Install landing gear struts in Central Bracket (9). Pay attention on proper positioning of right and left struts. Check correct positioning before application of glue. As final step, mount the fixing screw BHCS Screw M2 x 4 mm (18) in Central Bracket (9). Wing and landing gear assembly completed. To install the wing on the fuselage, pull the fuselage beam through predefined guide points on the wing Central Bracket, as shown in the picture. A slight pushing force may be gently applied if needed. 3.1 – Electronic Components Installation Install RC transmitter on PCB bracket (2). Finally, connect the motors to the receiver board as shown in the illustration. Before final assembly, make sure the motors rotate in opposite directions. For easier assembly and adjustment, the wires should be approximately 130-140 mm long. The wires are preferable to route through the rib. To install the motor in the rib, gently press it into place and slide it slightly forward until there is no gap. To prevent the motor from rotating during operation, secure it with a small piece of adhesive tape, as shown in the illustration. Install the ribs with the motors onto the wing as shown in the illustration. The motors must be positioned on the outer side of each rib. Install the assembled wing onto the fuselage beam, approximately 10 mm from the fuselage forward end. Then route the motor wires behind the lower fuselage beam on each side, then twist the wires together for several turns, as shown in the illustration. Only after routing the wires, install the PCB receiver bracket (2). Install the nose part (1) and secure it with screw (18). Install the battery and hold it in place with a suitable rubber band, as shown on picture. Position the wing so that the distance from the rear edge of the upper central bracket to the tail-boom joint is approximately 42 mm, as shown in the illustration. Fix finally the screw (18) of wing assembly. The model assembly is now complete. 3.2 – Balancing Pre-flight balancing not required when assembled as described above. CG positioned approximately 10 mm from the bottom wing leading edge. 4 - Model Flight Launch the model outdoors in calm weather or slight breeze conditions. Recommended wind speed: up to 5 km/h (≈1.4 m/s, ≈2.7 knots) . Always launch the model directly into the wind . Launch the model applying full throtle with a gentle horizontal push. If the model dives strongly, then: Move the wing slightly forward OR bend the elevator slightly upward If the model pitches up or stalls, first try reducing the flight speed. If flight speed reduction does not help, then: Move the wing slightly backward OR bend the elevator slightly downward Flight tip: For a ground takeoff, apply full throttle. After a takeoff run of about 10–12 meters , make a gentle turn in either direction. This slight bank helps the model lift off. Happy Flights and Smooth Landings!

Microgroove turns the $30 M5Stack Cardputer-ADV into a four-track groovebox: three synth tracks (each switchable between a mono 303-style voice with slide & accent, and 3-voice polyphony for chords), eight drum lanes of 808/909 synthesis or sample playback, live mic sampling, and resampling of its own output. This listing is the shell and keycap label system that makes it playable — the free, open-source firmware lives on GitHub: https://github.com/matoslav/MicroGroove It fits the M5Stack Cardputer- ADV specifically. The screen, USB-C port, and headphone jack all stay fully accessible after the swap. Printing Print with a 0.2 mm nozzle (strongly recommended). A 0.4 mm nozzle works, but the fine label text won't come out clean. The parts: Top + label top — the two-piece face. The label top is multi-color (blue / red / white). Keys — the keycaps, also multi-color. Bottom — optional. Table stand and box with instructions — optional extras. The label top and keys need a multi-color setup (AMS / multi-material or manual filament swaps). If you only print in one color, you'll still get a working shell, just without the colored labels. Assembly Glue the top and the label top together, slide in the keys, and swap the assembly for the original top your Cardputer-ADV came with. Two screws hold it in place — gluing the two face pieces matters because without it the edges lift. What the firmware does Three acid synth voices — saw/square/tri/sine plus 16 wavetables through a resonant 303 filter. Flip any track from mono squelch to 3-voice chords. Eight drum lanes — 808 and 909 synthesis or your own samples, side by side. Tune, decay, and choke each one. Sample the room — hold one key, watch the level meter, release. It's already playing on a lane. Resample yourself — bounce the live mix onto a pad and build the next layer on top. Sequence and arrange — 8 patterns of 16 steps, clone with a hold, chain up to 64 into a full song. Ready to play out of the box — the SD image on GitHub ships a five-pattern demo track and a CC0 sample pack.

The VORTEX 2 Tornado Probe (often referred to as a Tornado Pod) is a rugged, rapidly deployable ground instrument used in the Vortex 2 severe weather project to measure the core flow and structural characteristics of tornadoes at ground level. Key Characteristics: Design: A 1-meter (approx. 3.3 ft) tall instrument tower anchored by a heavy, flat base, allowing it to withstand extreme winds without being easily overturned. Instrumentation: Equipped with specialized anemometers and sensors to measure high-resolution wind speed, wind direction, temperature, and atmospheric pressure. Deployment: Mobile field teams rapidly positioned the probes on the ground in the direct path or immediate vicinity of an advancing tornado to gather data from inside the core flow. Scientific Purpose: The primary goal was to capture "ground truth" atmospheric data in the crucial zone where tornadoes develop to understand why and how tornadogenesis occurs. Probes provided critical near-surface data to correlate storm rotation with temperature, humidity, and wind fields. This model took me lot of time to complete, hope you enjoy it! Fully printed system to make plaster moulds. This produces a 3-part mould to cast round ornaments with a pumpkin design. This print has been scaled to 112% to account for clay shrinkage, which should give a final ornament size of 6.5cm diameter with most casting slips. If you want it smaller/larger than 6.5cm, scale every piece of the print. With any fully 3D printed mould, you’ll benefit from using a release agent on the base plate surface. I use a generic mouldmaker’s soap, but any product designed for plaster release should be fine. It needs around 375ml of plaster, and you can calculate the weight of water and plaster needed with this tool: Plaster Calculator You can get a much better cast surface, even if your plaster mix is full of air bubbles, by using a paintbrush to dislodge any trapped air from the surface. I would suggest that you pour plaster until the ornament surface is covered but it isn’t completely full, then get a relatively small paintbrush and move it around in the plaster so that you’re brushing all of the details on the base plate surface. This will dislodge air bubbles, and once dislodged they’ll float upwards. Once you’ve finished this, pour in the rest of the plaster. If you manage to avoid adding more air as you do it (just brush gently), you’ll eventually remove all the bubbles from the surface and get a perfect cast. This uses the updated 3 part mould design, which is compatible with other updated 3 part moulds but not the original ornament moulds. This new design has slots added to the back to allow the mould to bend slightly when releasing the plaster, making the process much easier. This version has an additional larger slot in the print with a removable insert to stop plaster from leaking during casting. Remove the insert once you're ready to demould the plaster, then the added flexibility will allow the print to pop right off!

Powerful printable foam dart sniper pistol blaster capable of up to 250FPS These are alternative cosmetic parts for the Zinc .50, with a new more tactical design. This listing contains all parts needed for the Zinc .50, including unchanged ones. This listing includes new parts for the following Zinc .50 configurations: 160mm barrel compact front, 160mm barrel BCAR front, and 205mm barrel BCAR front. These parts require no hardware changes and so use the original hardware kit for the Zinc .50. See here for the original Zinc .50 model listing (check out all the amazing makes from everyone!). About the Zinc .50 blaster: Technically all standard Nerf darts are ‘50 caliber’ as the darts have a diameter of half an inch, though the Zinc .50 brings the essence of 50 caliber into foam dart hand-cannon format. The Zinc .50 is a high-powered, mag fed (7-13 dart capacity) foam dart springer pistol blaster capable of up to 250 feet-per-second muzzle velocity for 205mm barrel configurations, and up to 230 FPS for 160mm barrel configurations. If you have no reference for those velocities - don't hit your tv or it may break. It may also leave divots in your drywall. Everything You Need To Build Your Own Purchase a hardware kit: Hardware Kits can be found here. Discounted 'Duel Bundle' (2x Hardware Kits) for this blaster can be found here. Discounted 3-Blaster Hardware kit Bundle pack (Zc Aus, Znc Aus, Zinc .50) can be found here. The hardware kit can make any blaster configuration, just choose your barrel length! Affordable international shipping available, fast and tracked! Please note: Hardware kit sales support me in developing upcoming designs. They include several custom-machined parts, not just off-the-shelf parts. They are priced for an order frequency that I can keep fast dispatch times up with while also remaining competitive with similar kits. Download the print files, or Bambu Studio 3MF with all parts and preset settings (contains one of every part, remove unused parts for your configuration, duplicate parts as desired), from this model listing. Download the print and assembly guide here . Buy some half-length darts if you don't already own any, here are some links: US - Frontline Foam , OutOfDarts EU - Blaster Time AU - Blaster Tech Although the files include some printable tools to make assembly easier, you will also need some basic common tools for assembly, see the assembly guide linked above. Lubricant is included in the hardware kit. Demo Video Warning Note This blaster has a large spring with a somewhat heavy prime weight. Said spring may present danger if the blaster is not assembled, used, or cared for correctly. This is your responsibility. Information on correct assembly, use and care is provided in the assembly guide linked above. If you are looking for a blaster with a lighter prime and less powerful spring: check out the more compact Znc Aus / Znc Aus Cosmetic Part Variants , or even the ultra-compact Zc Aus . IMPORTANT NOTE - PRINT IN BRIGHT COLOURS Due to it's design this blaster must be printed in bright colours and with an orange tip so it is clearly visible as a toy, for your safety and other's. Use responsibly and in responsible settings. Details Textured Grip Note The textured grip shown on the frame part in the images is done with fuzzy skin fill-painting in the slicer. The grip sections are bordered by a small deboss which allows them to be easily fill-painted with the fuzzy skin fill-painting tool. The settings used for fuzzy skin in the blasters in the images are 0.18 thickness and 0.25 point distance. The Bambu Studio 3MF file already has the fuzzy skin set up with these settings. Variants A bearing scar (BCAR) uses rings of flanged bearings with each at a slight angle to impart spin on the dart as it exits the barrel, vastly increasing accuracy with little effect on fps. These new cosmetic parts for the Zinc .50 can make 3 total configurations (all shown in the cover image), two of which include a 9-bearing (3 rings) BCAR. The hardware kit can make any configuration, just choose your desired barrel length (all hardware kits come with 9x BCAR pins and bearings): 160mm barrel with a compact front (no BCAR) Up to 230FPS Not very accurate due to lack of BCAR but fun in that it's super powerful for it's size 160mm barrel with a 9 bearing BCAR Up to 230FPS Good balance of size and accuracy/power 205mm barrel with a 9 bearing BCAR Up to 250FPS Proper sniper pistol configuration, longer barrel for maximum FPS and BCAR for accuracy Zinc .50 Additions and Changes vs Ziiiinc and Zinc The Zinc .50 is based on the Ziiiinc by Misplaced Moose, and is modified and sold with his permission, though it includes many changes and upgrades including a slightly larger diameter plunger tube, a longer barrel, many customisable part options allowing for many different configurations, revised hardware, and modified/remodeled part designs and tolerances in the interest of performance, ease of assembly, and aesthetics. Hardware changes include a tighter-toleranced aluminum plunger tube over the original polycarbonate one, refined closed-end springs for all springs to fix issues of the original Zinc such as the stiff catch and weak mag release, double O-rings on all seals, lubricant oil included, tapping screws replacing machine screws with nuts (caused part splitting or the nuts would turn in place, making removal impossible), and more. See images for further details. Assembly Assembly is relatively straightforward. The assembly guide is detailed and includes troubleshooting steps for common issues. Unlike the original Zinc 2.0, no excessive sanding is required to get parts to fit and function. A dimensionally accurate printer such as a Prusa or Bambu model is recommended for easy assembly. See the print guide for printing tips. Care and Safety Print in bright colours and use in responsible locations/settings. Do not leave the blaster outside under sunlight or in a car that may get hot when not in use. Do not leave the blaster primed when not in use as this will fatigue the main spring and other parts. Use responsibly. Do not aim at eyes or face. Eye protection for skirmishing is essential. Not recommended for use by young children. Note Like the Ziiiinc, the Zinc .50 is an unofficial descendant of the Zinc 2.0 blaster by 118 Design.

description: Say goodbye to a wet back and butt with this Tesla air conditioning kit for ventilated seat covers. (Without cover not tested) I bought ventilated seat covers for my 2022 Model 3, which was great—they keep you dry—but your back and butt still get hot when you get into a car that’s been sitting in the sun for 9 hours, even if it’s been pre-conditioned. So I designed a system that lets the rear AC to circulate cool air across your back and seat through an aftermarket ventilated seat cover—you can easily find these online; they’re the same models everywhere. The cover really helps distribute the cool airflow—the feeling is truly revolutionary. I’m not sure if this works well without the seat cover. I think you’d feel the plastic in your body since there isn’t the thickness of the cover to cushion it, but you can give it a try by You can cut in Bambu Studio the diffuser extensions to match your body, and driving position. Or simply don't fit the diffuser extensions, at least you will feel the AC at the bottom of your back for sure. But the seat cover creates a sort of tunnel that allows air to flow under your body without you blocking the airflow, all that with 10x fans, that's what makes the difference. Compatible with Model 3 and Model Y through 2023 (until the seat design changes). It may be compatible with the new Model 3 and Model Y, but I haven't been able to test it. By the way, if you're sensitive to the cold, you can turn on the heater in the winter in addition to the standard heated seats. Warning : Please note that is a DIY project and each driver have different driving/seat position so you may modify some pieces. Maybe you can use TPU to make flexible extension so that it would be more compatible without any modifications. You can try to heat the parts with heat gun to give it the form you want. The diffuser was designed for my seat adjustment; the angle of the seatback might restrict the diffuser. I'm providing a 2D drawing of the diffuser's profile so you can check if it would fit your setup. Otherwise, perhaps when installing the heater, you could adapt it to your setup—since it's a complex part, I haven't created any other versions. It's recommended to print it in heat resistant material like ABS, ASA, (maybe PETG but my car get 74°C at max), you can just try in PLA if you have the cabin overheat protection (that's how I made my first prototype to see if it worth it and damn it worth it !) Warping can be a bit annoying but doesn't prevent the assembly. I strongly recommend to print at 50% to avoid support at 45°. 60° overhang angle print good and I prefer to be safe and print slowly Assembly : First, You need to unclip the two elastic straps under the seat, at the back, that hold the small piece of leather cover in place. (white piece on my rear photo) Insert the main diffuser in the seat by the front to the rear, clip the diffuser extensions Insert 3x M6 nuts (or only 2) in the rear plenum, connect the rear plenum on the main diffuser with at least 2 screws to lock it Connect the 2x parts of the "Rear AC diffuser 2x Ø50 mm" by gluing them or using 4x plastic screw Put some sticky foam all around the part who goes in the Tesla vent, it make sure the part fits securely in the car, it prevent from moving. Be sure to make foam opening for the flaps like on photos I recommend to put foam around the flat surface to prevent from air leaks, it's a bit of a DIY I know, but it's worth it. Connect Ø50 mm air hoses with zip ties or collar to the plenum and to the the rear AC cover. If you have a ventilated seat cover then try to put the diffuser extensions (for butt and back) in the seat cover opening to really force the air to go in the seat cover, like sealing. For those who test without cover, feel free to share your felling :)

description: This is a 45-degree directional return jet designed for above-ground pools with a 32 mm water outlet, such as compatible Bestway and Intex systems. The original pool outlet sends the filtered water straight ahead. This replacement nozzle redirects the water at approximately 45 degrees, allowing the flow to be aimed downward or sideways to improve water circulation inside the pool. The model consists of two printable parts: Directional outlet nozzle Threaded retaining ring It replaces only the original water outlet nozzle. The remaining original pool fitting, seals and internal components are reused. The nozzle can be rotated before tightening the retaining ring, allowing you to choose the direction of the water flow. Compatibility Tested on a Bestway pool with a 32 mm outlet. It should also be compatible with Intex and other above-ground pools that use the same style of 32 mm return outlet, although small differences may exist between models. Please compare the original fitting and dimensions before printing. Printing Recommended material: PETG PETG is recommended because the part will be exposed to water, sunlight and outdoor temperatures. No supports required Print both parts in the orientation provided Recommended layer height: 0.20 mm Recommended walls: 4 Recommended infill: 25–40% A brim can be used if your printer has adhesion problems Print the threaded ring slowly for better thread quality Assembly Turn off the pool pump. Remove the original directional outlet nozzle. Keep the original pool fitting and rubber seals in place. Insert the printed directional nozzle. Rotate it to the desired position. Tighten it using the printed retaining ring. Turn the pump back on and check for leaks. Do not overtighten the threaded ring. Hand tightening should be enough. Important This model has been tested on my own Bestway 32 mm pool outlet. Always check the connection for leaks after installation. The model is not intended for high-pressure plumbing systems. If you successfully test it on another Bestway or Intex pool model, please leave a comment with the exact model so the compatibility list can be expanded.

description: A fish priest with an actual whack to it. Printed plastic alone is sometimes too light to dispatch a fish cleanly, so this one has a 77 cm3 weight chamber inside the head, sealed by an M33x3.5 threaded plug with a coin slot. Fill it with steel BBs for roughly 370 g of added mass, or dry sand for about 120 g, or you can leave as is without any fill and it should do the job for small fish. Made it for my own tackle box because I can never find a stick when I need it. Specs (default): 300 mm long, 44 mm octagonal head, 30 mm handle with three grip grooves, pommel flare plus a 9 mm lanyard hole so it stays on your wrist over water. Chamber is a 31 mm bore, 92 mm deep with a tapered end. Plug threads are printed in place, no hardware needed. Print settings, and these matter for strength: the file is pre-oriented lying flat (fits a 256 bed diagonally at 238 x 238 mm), no supports, and the layer lines run the length of the bat, which is the strong direction in bending. Do not stand it upright in the slicer or it will snap at the neck on the first hit. PETG or ABS, not PLA (PLA gets brittle in the cold and can shatter on impact). 6 walls minimum, 30% gyroid infill. The plug prints cap-down next to the bat. Wrap the plug threads with PTFE tape, or a drop of CA glue for permanent, so fine sand stays put. Honest note: this is a fish priest, not a demolition tool. Filled with BBs it lands around 550 g total, plenty for trout through salmon. I have not torture-tested it against rocks. Printed one and bonked something? Apache Mod Box Modular Electronics Housing for Apache 2800 Boombox Builds Update — July 30, 2026 This update adds more amplifier options and additional layout flexibility: Added a mirrored ZK-1001U lid for left- or right-side placement inside the Apache case Added ZK-1002T compatibility using inward-facing mounts on either bump out Added TW100U compatibility using an inward-facing mount between the two bump outs Added a protective cover panel for the TW100U Added Lid - No Amp for the ZK-1002T, TW100U, or builds that need a clean top lid Added selectable left- and right-side wire cutouts to Lid - No Amp Overview I designed the Apache Mod Box as an all-in-one housing for the amplifier, battery, wiring, and controls used in an Apache 2800 boombox build. There are several similar designs available, but I wanted something that gave the builder more freedom when planning the layout. Instead of locking the power button, charging port, and Voltmeter/USB Quick Charger into one location, the included 3MF lets you choose which openings to use before printing. The Mod Box currently supports three amplifier configurations: Amplifier Mounting Location Recommended Lid ZK-1001U Mounted on top of the Mod Box Standard or mirrored ZK-1001U lid ZK-1002T Inward-facing on either bump out Lid - No Amp TW100U Inward-facing between the bump outs Lid - No Amp and optional protective cover panel Make sure you choose the correct amplifier mount, lid, wire cutout, and control openings before starting the print. Amplifier Compatibility ZK-1001U The ZK-1001U mounts directly to the top of the Mod Box using an amplifier-specific lid. Two lid orientations are included: Standard ZK-1001U lid Mirrored ZK-1001U lid The mirrored version gives you more freedom to position the Mod Box on either the left or right side of the Apache case and have the amp be near or away from the opening of the case. Because of the available clearance, the amplifier power connection requires a 5.5 × 2.1 mm right-angle DC adapter . A straight connector will not fit properly with this setup. The battery and wiring remain contained underneath the lid, while the amplifier controls stay accessible from the top. ZK-1002T The ZK-1002T mounts inward-facing on one of the two bump outs. There are two available mounting locations: Left bump out Right bump out Choose the mounting objects for the side you want to use and change them to Negative Parts in Bambu Studio. After printing: Remove the washers and nuts from the amplifier knobs. Slide the controls through the openings from inside the Mod Box. Reinstall the washers and nuts from the outside. Install Lid - No Amp for a clean finish on top. The ZK-1002T does not require an amplifier-specific lid. TW100U The TW100U mounts inward-facing in the center area between the two bump outs. Unlike the ZK-1001U, the TW100U does not mount to the lid. Use Lid - No Amp to close the top of the Mod Box. A separate protective cover panel is also included for the TW100U. The panel can be installed over the amplifier to help protect it while keeping the controls accessible from inside the Apache case. This mounting position uses the open area between the bump outs while keeping the top of the Mod Box clean. Make sure the TW100U mounting openings and the appropriate wire cutout are selected before printing. Assembly Required Hardware The Mod Box is assembled using M4 heat-set inserts and M4 × 12 mm screws . You’ll need: 6x M4 heat-set inserts 6x M4 × 12 mm flat head machine screws Install the heat-set inserts into the Mod Box, then secure the lid using the six M4 screws. Tools Soldering Iron Heat Set Insert Tips Parts 5.5mm x 2.1mm Charge Port Jack 5.5mm x 2.1mm Right Angle Adapter Voltmeter/USB Quick Charger or USB-C Model 16mm 12v/24v Latching Power Button 24v 4Ah Battery or 7Ah Battery (same size) Internal Space Main Chamber: 227 mm long × 86 mm deep × 74 mm tall Bump Outs: 46mm wide x 111mm long Make sure your battery and other components fit within that space before printing. Voltmeter/USB Charger The model is designed around a standard 30 mm round Voltmeter/USB Charger with a 30.3 mm modeled opening. There are three possible mounting locations: Inside of the Apache case Outside of the Apache case Top of the Mod Box and accessible from inside the case So whether you want your USB ports accessible without opening the case or would rather keep everything inside, you can set it up either way. Charging Port The charging port is designed for a standard 12 mm round charging port with a 12.3 mm modeled opening . There are four possible mounting locations: Inside – left Inside – right Outside – left Outside – right This gives you the option to keep the charging connection inside the case or make it accessible from the outside. Power Button The Mod Box supports 16 mm, 19 mm, and 22 mm power buttons . Like the charging port, the power button has four possible mounting locations: Inside – left Inside – right Outside – left Outside – right The modeled openings are: Button Size Modeled Opening 16 mm 16.3 mm 19 mm 19.3 mm 22 mm 22.3 mm The power button and charging port do not have to be placed together. For example, you can: Place the power button outside and the charging port inside Put them on opposite sides of the Voltmeter/USB Quick Charger Keep all controls inside Mount all controls outside Setting Up Your Mod Box The different cutouts are already built into the included 3MF, so you don't need to edit anything in CAD . In Bambu Studio, open the Objects tab and expand the Mod Box. You'll see the different cutout options labeled by size and location. Find the openings you want to use and change those objects to Negative Part . When the model is sliced, the negative objects will create the holes in the Mod Box. Leave any locations you aren't using alone. I highly recommend checking the sliced preview before starting the print. It's an easy way to make sure you've opened the right locations before committing to the full box. Important: Power Button Sizes The charging-port and power-button openings are nested together. Because of that, when you choose a larger power button, you also need to make all of the smaller openings at that same location negative . What You're Using Make These Negative 12 mm charging port 12 mm 16 mm power button 12 mm + 16 mm 19 mm power button 12 mm + 16 mm + 19 mm 22 mm power button 12 mm + 16 mm + 19 mm + 22 mm For example, if you're using a 22 mm power button , make the 12 mm, 16 mm, 19 mm, and 22 mm objects at that location Negative Parts. Making only the 22 mm object negative will not create the complete opening. Thanks for checking out the Apache Mod Box! I put a lot of thought into making this as flexible and useful as possible for different Apache boombox builds. If you print one, I’d love to see how you set yours up. And if you have an idea for another amp lid, different port size, mounting option, or anything else that would make the Mod Box better, drop a comment or send a recommendation. I’m always open to improving the design and adding more options for future builds. Ratings and comments help me so much and if you love it, please consider boosting!

Fully printed system to make plaster moulds. This produces a 3-part mould to cast freestanding ornaments with a snowman design. This print has been scaled to 112% to account for clay shrinkage, which should give a final ornament size of 8.5cm height with most casting slips. If you want it smaller/larger than 8.5cm, scale every piece of the print. With any fully 3D printed mould, you’ll benefit from using a release agent on the base plate surface. I use a generic mouldmaker’s soap, but any product designed for plaster release should be fine. It needs around 375ml of plaster, and you can calculate the weight of water and plaster needed with this tool: Plaster Calculator You can get a much better cast surface, even if your plaster mix is full of air bubbles, by using a paintbrush to dislodge any trapped air from the surface. I would suggest that you pour plaster until the ornament surface is covered but it isn’t completely full, then get a relatively small paintbrush and move it around in the plaster so that you’re brushing all of the details on the base plate surface. This will dislodge air bubbles, and once dislodged they’ll float upwards. Once you’ve finished this, pour in the rest of the plaster. If you manage to avoid adding more air as you do it (just brush gently), you’ll eventually remove all the bubbles from the surface and get a perfect cast. This uses the updated 3 part mould design, which is compatible with other updated 3 part moulds but not the original ornament moulds. This new design has slots added to the back to allow the mould to bend slightly when releasing the plaster, making the process much easier. This version has an additional larger slot in the print with a removable insert to stop plaster from leaking during casting. Remove the insert once you're ready to demould the plaster, then the added flexibility will allow the print to pop right off!

description: Shad Fishing Mold – Professional Soft Bait Mold length 66 mm Shad Fishing Mold is a professional, two-piece reusable mold designed for DIY casting of soft plastic fishing baits in a highly effective minnow/shad shape with a paddle tail. The project is optimized for smooth material flow and flawless detail reproduction, giving your DIY lures a professional, store-bought finish. 🎣 Application & Target Species These paddle tail shads are a true staple in any angler's tackle box. The classic fish-like profile paired with high-frequency tail vibrations works wonders across various fishing styles: Perch: An absolute magnet for perch. The realistic action and subtle rolling body mimic small fry perfectly. Trout: Extremely stable in the water – it works brilliantly whether retrieved slowly in search of active pike or cast into fast-flowing rivers for wild trout. Rigging Versatility: Thanks to its sleek and hydrodynamic shape, the lure performs beautifully on a standard jig head, cheburashka rig, or an offset hook for weedless presentations and Carolina/Texas rigs. 🖨️ Recommended Print Settings To ensure the mold is completely sealed and the cast lures come out smooth with a high-gloss finish, use the following settings: Layer Height: Max 0.16 mm (for premium quality, 0.12 mm is highly recommended). A lower layer height ensures a flawless surface finish inside the cavity, resulting in perfect-looking baits without visible layer lines. Infill: Min. 20% ( 25% is recommended for extra durability under clamp pressure). Wall Loops: Min. 3-4 walls to prevent liquid plastic/plastisol from seeping through the printed layers. Material: PET-G, ABS, or ASA is highly recommended due to their superior thermal and chemical resistance when coming into contact with hot casting materials (liquid plastisol is typically poured at 160–180°C / 320–350°F). Note: Standard PLA may deform over time from the intense heat of liquid plastisol. 💡 How to Use Align: Fit both halves of the mold together (the built-in alignment pins ensure a perfect, flush fit). Clamp: Secure the mold tightly using a small hobby clamp, G-clamp, or strong rubber bands to prevent any leaking along the seams. Pour/Inject: Slowly inject or pour heated liquid plastisol (soft bait plastic) into the injection port. De-mold: Allow it to cool down completely (approx. 2-3 minutes), gently open the mold, and enjoy your custom, high-catching homemade shads! If you like this project, please leave a "Like" ❤️ and share photos of your custom baits or catches in the comments!

Before you print: An AMS is required. You must have PETG and PLA, or any two filaments that don't stick together, or soluble support material. This boomerang does indeed work, but boomerang throwing is not easy. If this is your first time throwing this sort of boomerang, expect to take at least 1-2 hours of practice before you have even one successful catch. Printing Make sure you choose the correct file. I have made a different print profile for the left-handed version so that my signature isn't mirrored. Set the green material to whatever PETG you have, and the white material to whatever PLA you have. The bottom of the boomerang is designed to print my signature in a different colour of PETG. If you only have one colour of PETG, use the fill tool under the paint menu to make the whole boomerang one colour. Make sure your buildplate has been cleaned with soap and water, and that bed-levelling is enabled to ensure optimal adhesion. VERY IMPORTANT: While the printer is printing the purge line , start to peel it off before the whole purge line has printed . The boomerang will be printed over the purge line if it is not removed immediately, and you will have to try again. When finished printing, peel off the supports using the little tabs that stick out, and then pop out the chamber supports by poking an object through the hole on the other side with something like a screwdriver. Optional: Sand or scrape the edges and the ‘transitions’ to and from the undercut as they may have a slightly bumpy edge. Safety: This boomerang is not a toy. Treat it as a piece of sporting equipment that has the capacity to injure or even kill very young children or small animals if you throw within the vicinity of others. This boomerang can be thrown without much power, but please keep in mind that it is designed to be thrown in excess of 75mph (120km/h) and is a spinning piece of solid plastic. I do not take any responsibility for any injuries this may cause if thrown carelessly. If you are actually going to use this boomerang for fast-catch (5 consecutive throws and catches, timed), I recommend wearing safety glasses and a thick glove on your non-dominant hand. Restrain any hair that may block your eyesight and wear sunglasses if sunlight hinders your ability to see the boomerang in flight. I would recommend throwing this boomerang during wind speeds of under 10km/h, and never during wind speeds of 15km/h or more. About this Boomerang I am very proud to present this boomerang as I truly believe that it is currently my magnum opus - my best work to date. This current design has taken about 5 iterations to perfect, and is now my go-to for practicing fast-catch and endurance. Previously, I had thought it would be impossible to incorporate chambering and undercut, something that is very common on hand-made boomerangs into 3D printed boomerangs due to the limitations of supports and the very steep angles required. I worked around this by designing custom supports in my CAD software, and had them print in a filament that wouldn't stick to the main boomerang. I print my boomerangs in PETG, so PLA was the obvious choice for the support material, which ended up giving me very clean bottom surfaces. Many people would probably already have these two filaments on hand too, which is a plus. This boomerang also features a stepped airfoil on the trailing edge of each wing which was inspired by Denis Suprana's ‘Turbo’ boomerang. From my testing, I found that it reduced the likelihood of the boomerang swooping up during the end of the flight, but the exact reason for why is still unclear. Range: 19-23 metres (adjustable by twisting wings - angle of attack) Flight time: around 3.4 seconds, calculated from one of my fast-catch rounds Below is a video of the boomerang being tested, thrown by Grant Perry, captain of the Australian Boomerang team. Throwing Guide Pinch grip the boomerang as shown: Throw at shoulder height and straight forward or just very slightly up (as seen in the video). Use your wrist and the whipping motion from your elbow to give the boomerang spin. It is very important to keep the boomerang vertical, i.e. the plane of rotation is perpendicular to the ground when you throw, and never throw sidearm. If you have a weaker throw and/or there is little to no wind, throw with about 5 to 10 degrees of layover (lean the boomerang towards the right rather than releasing it completely vertical). Adjusting throwing direction for better accuracy: Like with most boomerangs, throwing 45 degrees to the right of the wind is a good starting point, but this must still be adjusted most of the time. With a fast-catch in very light wind, you can try throwing directly into the wind, or about 10 degrees to the right of it (a so-called ‘backdoor’ approach). Adjust your throwing direction with the following guide (flip left/right if you are left handed but not front/behind): Lands in front of you or to your right . Turn to the right a little bit. Lands behind you or to your left . Turn to the left a little bit. Simply repeat this until you can catch the boomerang while standing from the same spot or until you are satisfied with the accuracy. You will have to adjust this every time the wind changes direction. Enjoy the boomerang and I wish you many happy returns! Throw safely and responsibly :)

tags: sand anchor|beach anchor|snow anchor|deadman anchor|camping beac|tent stake|ground anchor|sand stake|outdoor|van life|picnic|pack and deploy|portable|desert|snow campin|basecamp|basecamp anywhere|compression anchor|confinement anchor|dual disc|petg|BAMBU LAB|A1 MINI|no supports|flat pack|fdm printable
description: Why this anchor exists: Every traveler knows the frustration: you arrive at the beach, set up your tent or lay down your towel, and the wind turns your stakes into useless plastic sticks. Sand, loose soil, and snow laugh at conventional stakes. They bend. They slip. They fail. I designed this anchor because I was tired of chasing my gear across the sand. The solution came from studying a classic mountaineering technique called a "deadman anchor" — a buried plate that uses the weight and friction of the ground itself to resist extraction. I engineered that principle into a compact, printable design that fits flat in your bag and deploys in under a minute. How it works (the physics): This is not a stake. This is a compression confinement anchor. Two discs (109.2 mm diameter) are separated by 115 mm along a cross-shaped central shaft. When buried and subjected to an upward pull, the lower disc compresses the sand between itself and the upper disc. The sand, trapped and compacted, generates lateral pressure against the surrounding ground, mobilizing its internal friction angle (φ). The result: the anchor must lift an entire confined cylinder of sand — over 1 liter in volume (1.08 L) — to be extracted. Standard stakes rely on surface friction along their shaft. In loose sand, that friction is nearly zero. This anchor converts a weak material into a solid block of resistance. Measured and calculated performance: Loose dry sand (children's sandbox): extraction force of 8–10 kg-f — already 5 to 15 times higher than a plastic beach stake in the same conditions. Compacted beach sand or moist earth: estimated extraction force of 20–30 kg-f, based on load capacity models with friction angles of 30–35°. Visual proof: when extracted from loose sand, the anchor pulls out a massive sand cylinder, demonstrating the confinement mechanism in action. A conventional stake in the same sandbox? Pulls out clean with almost zero resistance. Key features: Pack-and-deploy: assembles from flat-packed plates into a rigid cross-anchor structure. No tools required. 100% printable: no supports, no external hardware. Designed for consumer FDM printers (tested on Bambu Lab A1 Mini). Dual-disc bayonet lock: discs slide over the shaft, rotate 45°, and lock into teeth — secure, fast, and sand-tolerant. PETG recommended: for outdoor durability, UV resistance, and the flexibility needed during assembly. Scenarios: 🏖️ Beach: secure towels, sunshades, beach tents. ❄️ Snow camping: deadman anchor for tent guylines in powder. ⛺ Loose soil: anywhere conventional stakes fail. INSTRUCTIONS FOR USE Standard Setup: Dig: Make a vertical hole about 15 cm deep (remember: greater depth means greater pull-out resistance). Assemble the cross: Slide the two shafts together to form the cross-shaped structure. Place the lower confinement disc: Slide one disc over the shafts, pushing it down until it rests on the lower locking tabs . Rotate it 45° so the bayonet teeth lock it firmly in place. Bury and compact the base: Place the device into the hole and fill it with sand or snow up to the upper crossbars . Compact the material firmly with your hands to ensure proper confinement. Secure the upper disc: Place the second disc with the locking notches facing up, and rotate it 45° onto the upper crossbars to lock it. Finish filling: Cover the entire anchor, leaving only the tie-down holes visible on the surface for passing ropes through. Advanced Method (Deep Anchoring): For extreme wind conditions or deep snow, use the total burial method: Follow steps 1 through 5, but dig significantly deeper. Before finishing the fill, secure your ropes to the tie-down holes. Then cover the anchor completely and compact. The anchor will work at depth, providing maximum resistance. Usage tip: For tents, use 1 anchor per corner or tension point .

description: AI Buddy is an open-source AI companion powered by the DFRobot UNIHIKER K10 and the Xiaozhi Framework. Build your own customizable AI chatbot with interchangeable animal enclosures including Bunny, Cat, Fox, and Giraffe. The project combines 3D printing, electronics, PCB design, and AI into a fun STEM project for makers, students, and educators. Supplies To build AI Buddy, you'll need: Electronics 1× DFRobot UNIHIKER K10 1× Custom BMS PCB 1× 3.7V Li-Po Battery 1× M2 Screw Kit Tools 3D Printer Precision Screwdriver Kit Assembly Assembly is quick and beginner-friendly: 3D print all enclosure parts. Install the two button extensions into the front housing. Insert the DFRobot UNIHIKER K10 into the housing. Mount the custom BMS onto the rear cover using two M2 screws. Connect the Li-Po battery to the BMS. Connect the BMS output to the UNIHIKER battery connector. Place the battery inside the enclosure. Close the enclosure and secure it with four M2 screws. Your AI Buddy hardware is now complete! Easy Flash Firmware No Arduino IDE, PlatformIO, or code compilation is required. Simply: Connect AI Buddy to your computer using a USB Type-C cable. Open the Easy Flash website. Click Connect & Flash . Select your device's serial port. Wait about a minute while the latest firmware is downloaded and installed automatically. After flashing, AI Buddy will boot into Wi-Fi setup mode, where you can connect it to your network and link it to your Xiaozhi account. Easy Flash: https://mukeshsankhla.github.io/EasyFlash/#/project/ai-buddy Custom BMS PCB To make AI Buddy fully portable, I designed a custom IP5306-based Battery Management System (BMS) . I wanted to be able to permanently mount a monitor to my 19" 45U rack. I looked at some options and they were all fairly expensive. I didn't need it to move or articulate .. I just wanted a monitor I could use if I needed to connect directly to any of the servers in my rack. This design uses 4U for the mounting plate, but this is less space than is used by a typical monitor. I used a 4U size plate because it gave me appropriate thickness to mount the monitor and access to more mounting holes and a larger mounting surface area to ensure the mount was secure. I printed this using Siraya Tech's PPA-CF Core (mostly because I wanted to try it out). The mount is actually more sturdy than the aluminum in the rack - the rack bends before the mount does if I apply force. Any material that can handle the temperatures in your server closet will work given that small monitors < 24" are generally fairly light. I would suggest ABS or ASA at a minimum since some PETG formulations and most PLA formulations may deform under load at temperatures commonly found near a network rack.
