Quarter-Turn Compression Latch A compact and robust 3D-printable quarter-turn latch for enclosures, cabinet doors, and DIY projects. The mechanism consists of only four printed parts and operates with a simple 90° rotation between the open and closed positions. The handle naturally rests in the downward position , allowing gravity to keep the latch closed. This makes it well suited for applications exposed to vibration, such as camper cabinets, workshop furniture, or portable equipment. The tapered latch arm provides a slight compression effect when closing, allowing doors or panels to be pulled tightly against the frame if required. Installation & Assembly The latch is designed for a simple installation using only three drilled holes and common hardware. Preparing the Door Drill the main center hole to 20 mm using a step drill. Drill two 3.5 mm clearance holes vertically aligned with the center hole, as shown in the model preview (use 2 parts as a guide for the holes). The mounting holes should be clearance holes only. The screws should not engage the door material. Instead, they thread into the printed retaining part, clamping the complete assembly securely to the door. Installing the Latch Insert the outer body through the 20 mm hole from the outside. Press-fit the inner carrier onto the outer body from the inside. Secure both parts using the two short mounting screws . Place the latch arm onto the shaft. Snap the handle through the carrier and latch until fully seated. Install the long center screw , which secures the handle while allowing smooth 90° rotation. No adhesive is required. Although the parts can be glued together, using screws is strongly recommended. The mechanical connection provides a much stronger assembly and significantly improves rigidity across the layer lines of the printed parts. If required, the center section of the model can be stretched or elongated in your slicer to accommodate thicker doors without affecting the locking mechanism. Recommended Hardware The original design was developed using common flat-head SPAX wood screws , although equivalent metric machine screws work equally well. Short Clamping Screws Original design: Quantity: 2 Length: 8 mm Flat countersunk head Approximately 7.5 mm head diameter Equivalent machine screw: M3 × 8 mm DIN 7991 / ISO 10642 Countersunk Socket Head Screw These screws clamp the outer body and inner carrier together through the door. Center Retaining Screw Original design: Quantity: 1 Length: 20 mm Countersunk head Equivalent machine screw: M3 × 20 mm DIN 7991 / ISO 10642 Countersunk Socket Head Screw The center screw retains the handle and latch assembly while allowing free rotation. If the latch is modified for thicker or thinner panels, simply adjust the screw lengths accordingly. Key Features Four printed parts Simple 90° quarter-turn operation Gravity-assisted closed position Tapered latch for optional compression Press-fit assembly Three-screw construction No springs required No glue required Easily adaptable for different door thicknesses Designed for reliable operation under vibration Technical Specifications Specification Value Rotation 90° Printed Parts 4 Main Bore 20 mm Mounting Holes 2 × 3.5 mm clearance Designed Panel Thickness 2.5 mm acrylic (default) Door Thickness Adjustable by extending the center section in the slicer Original Mounting Screws 2 × M3 × 8 mm countersunk (or trimmed SPAX) Original Retaining Screw 1 × M3 × 20 mm countersunk (or SPAX) Applications Acrylic enclosures 3D printer enclosures Camper cabinets Workshop cabinets Storage compartments Electronics enclosures Access panels DIY furniture Utility doors Why This Exists This latch was originally designed as part of my custom Ender 3 enclosure project. The goal was to create a simple, reliable, and inexpensive latch that could be printed without supports, assembled with common hardware, and withstand everyday use. After extensive testing, the design proved to be strong, easy to assemble, and highly reliable. Its gravity-assisted closing action helps prevent accidental opening due to vibration, while the tapered latch provides slight compression without requiring springs or additional hardware. Since then, the design has been reused for workshop cabinets, acrylic enclosures, camper furniture, and other DIY projects where a compact and dependable quarter-turn latch is needed. The design is intentionally simple, easy to modify for different material thicknesses, and inexpensive to build. If there is enough interest, I may also release the complete Ender 3 enclosure project that inspired this latch. description: Tesla Model Y A-Pillar Gutter (washer fluid deflector) Why I made this At highway speed a lot of the windshield washer fluid gets pushed around the side of the windshield and runs down the driver's side window. You end up cleaning the windshield and dirtying the side glass in the same action. With the window open, some of it comes in. This gutter mounts on the A-pillar and catches that flow before it wraps around the corner, directing it up over the roof instead. Design I kept it as small and low profile as I could while still catching the fluid, since I didn't want a visible accessory stuck to the car. It isn't very noticeable unless you're looking for it. The profile is thin enough to flex, so it conforms to the curve of the A-pillar when you press it down instead of needing to match the contour exactly. I designed and tested this on a Model Y. The Model 3 pillar geometry is close enough that it should fit, but I haven't tried it. If you do, let me know how it goes. Print settings Material: PCTG-CF Anneal it before mounting I used PCTG-CF for the heat stability. A car exterior sitting in direct sun gets well above air temperature, and a part that softens will lose its shape on the first hot day, taking the VHB bond with it. PCTG-CF holds up better than PETG in that environment, and the carbon fill helps it keep its shape. Annealing I annealed it in the printer rather than an oven: Take the part off the build plate after printing. Tape it back down to the plate with blue painter's tape. This holds it flat while it's soft and stops it curling. Heat the chamber to 65C and the plate to 80C. Leave it for 60 minutes. Let everything cool down before removing it. This needs an enclosed printer to hold chamber temperature. Without one, an oven at a similar temperature is the usual alternative, but I haven't tested that myself. Mounting It attaches with VHB tape. Clean the mounting area on the A-pillar with isopropyl alcohol and let it dry fully. Wax or road film left on the paint will cause the tape to release later. Apply the VHB to the part first, then position it on the car. Press firmly along the whole length. VHB needs pressure to bond properly. Do this in warm conditions if you can, as VHB adheres poorly in the cold. Wait a day or two before washing the car or driving in heavy rain. The bond continues gaining strength over the first 24 to 72 hours. To remove it later, work a length of fishing line behind the part to cut through the tape without damaging the paint. If you print one Post a make. I'd like to hear from anyone running it on a Model 3, and from anyone in a hot climate on how it holds up over a summer.

Tilt the boomerang slightly outward, roughly at a 15 to 30-degree angle (like a clock hand pointing at 1 o'clock). The Snap: Throw it forward and slightly upward, aiming just above the horizon. The secret is in the wrist—snap your wrist upon release to give it maximum spin! ⚠️ Safety Warning: Please only throw the Snap-Fly in open outdoor spaces like parks or empty fields. Keep away from roads, windows, and crowds. If you get a great flight and catch, please drop a make, leave a rating, and hit that Rocket to Boost! Happy flying! 🚀

Position the grille over the speaker Carefully place the completed grille assembly over the speaker. Check that the wires and capacitor remain properly positioned and that no wiring is trapped between the grille and speaker frame. Install the speaker and matching spacer Place the speaker into the enclosure with the matching spacer. The tweeter and LED array are firmly secured. The grille sits flat against the speaker and spacer. All wiring is clear of the speaker cone and mounting screws. model_name: Kicker KM8 Apache 2800 Spacer & Reinforcemnt Plate
description: This project contains an inner reinforcement plate and outer speaker spacer ring for attaching a Kicker KM8 speaker to an Apache 2800 rugged box. These parts are each 10mm thick to provide a rigid foundation for the speaker on the flexible face of the box. While polypropylene, as an LSE plastic, is very difficult bond to, successful use of these parts has been performed by using Lexel gel adhesive between the speaker and spacer and between the backing plate and the case lid and finally butyl tape between the spacer and the case face. Add the speaker gill to the outside of the speaker and bind this “sandwich” with 4 M4 hex cap screws (approx 50mm long), an M4 washer on the inside and a nylon lock M4 nut. Gradually tightening all screws evenly in small increments, while crossing over X wise to provide an even compression of the speaker gasket and the butyl tape. Clean excess Lexel with mineral spirits before it cures. Scrap off excess butyl tap with a plastic tool to avoid scratching the face of the case or spacer and then clean the remaining residue with an adhessive remover such as “Goo-Gone”. Slightly pre-heating the butyl with a heat gun before cleaning is helpful. There is no rush to do the butyl as it remains pliable through its life. The mechanical binding provided by the mounting screw/nut passed through the 4 screw holes along with these adhesives, provides a reasonable air-tight, water-resistant seal. This has not been tested long-term. There is also the option to add additional binding of the backing plate to the lid using heat set brass nuts in the stock screw bosses at the corners of the lid and fabricate a bracket to connect the backing plate to the screw boss. This has not proven to be necessary in my testing so far. Recommended print settings PETG filament 6 wall loops for strength, particularly the screw holes 45% Cubic infill for rigidness

description: Ultimate Onion Slicer Update 23/07/2026 : une V2 est désormais disponible ! Elle apporte plusieurs améliorations de conception : structure plus robuste, meilleure durabilité, temps d’impression réduit et emboîtement optimisé entre les deux parties du modèle, nettoyage des supports en quelques secondes. Deux tailles sont proposées : 100 % pour les petits à moyens oignons et 120 % pour les moyens à grands oignons, disponible pour la A1 mini également. Je vous recommande vivement la V2 . Ce modèle est un outil d’aide à la découpe conçu pour maintenir fermement les oignons (peut être utilisé pour les pommes ou d'autres aliment de le même taille/forme), pendant la préparation, tout en garantissant une coupe plus sûre, stable et régulière. Les dents du modèle sont dotées de picots permettant le maintient des oignons en place sans glissement. Les espacements réguliers entre les les dents servent de guide de coupe, permettant de réaliser des tranches ou lamelles homogènes et de taille identique, pour une découpe plus précise et constante. Une poignée ergonomique intégrée améliore la prise en main et le contrôle de l’ensemble pendant l’utilisation. L’outil permet également de sécuriser la découpe, en particulier pour les enfants ou les utilisateurs peu à l’aise avec les couteaux, en réduisant le contact direct avec l’aliment et en limitant les risques de glissade ou de blessure. PS : Je l'ai imprimé en PLA mais je vous recommande d'utiliser du PLA-FS (Food Safe). Je l'ai testé sur des oignon de taille normal. Si vous pensez utiliser des oignon de grand calibre, vous pouvez imprimer le profil à 120%, voir faire une mise à l'échelle si besoin, en fonction de la variété / taille que vous utilisez. Démonstration : Couper un oignon en deux. Poser une moitié sur la partie inférieure 'Poignet" du slicer dans le sens de la découpe. Placez la partie supérieure (« dents ») au-dessus, en respectant le sens d’assemblage, puis exercez une légère pression jusqu’à entendre un « clic », afin que les deux parties s’emboîtent et maintiennent fermement l’oignon. Utiliser un couteau de cuisine de taille normal ( entre 1 et 2mm d'épaisseur max) pour trancher l'oignon. Retirez la partie supérieure à dents en tirant sur l'un des deux côtés, puis récupérez vos lamelles d'oignon. Et voilà !

Are you ready to see the world from a little higher through the eyes of a giraffe? The Giraffe Bookshelf is more than just a cute decorative piece. It is an innovative hybrid project that combines 3D printing with Cricut (or similar cutting plotter) technology to create a truly unique bookshelf. Its integrated Shadow Box transforms the piece into a warm and immersive display when illuminated with a simple LED light, bringing depth and atmosphere to your space after dark. The heart of this design hides a meaningful quote between the layers of the Shadow Box: "Reading books puts you ahead of others." These inspiring words came from the imagination of a 10-year-old child and became the inspiration behind this project. Simply: Print a flat 0.20 mm single-layer PLA sheet directly on your print bed. Carefully remove the flexible sheet. Place it onto your Cricut (or compatible cutting machine). description: A flowing hummingbird sculpture captured at the exact moment its beak reaches into a flower for nectar. Parametric Stackable Soda-Can Dispenser Keep your fridge or pantry organized with this fully customizable, stackable can dispenser. Cans load from the back and roll forward on a gently tilted floor, so a fresh one is always waiting at the front lip. Features 🥤 Auto-feeding tilted tray — load at the back, grab from the front 🧱 Stackable — build a wall of dispensers as tall as you like 🍯 Honeycomb side walls for a light, rigid, great-looking print 🔩 Snap-together assembly — no glue, no screws 🦵 Snap-on legs that hold the base unit at the perfect dispensing angle 🖨️ Auto bed-splitting — large models are tiled into printable pieces that clip back together with Multiboard-style dual-clip keys Fully parametric — tune it to your cans and printer right in the customizer: can height & diameter, tray depth, tilt angle, wall thickness, honeycomb size, number of stacked units, legs, and more. Assembly: Print the wall, floor, and leg parts, then join the tiles with Multiboard dual-clip bowtie keys (printed separately). Snap the legs onto the bottom unit and stack additional units on top. The attached profile is for six EU 0.33l cans. I've printed it with PETG and its sturdy enough to handle four fully loaded levels of cans. 🛠️ How to Use This is a fully parametric model — open it in the MakerWorld customizer (or OpenSCAD) and dial it in to your cans and printer. ⚠️ Important: The model opens in stacked mode so you can preview a full stack. Before exporting for print, set mode → print . Then use part_select to export each piece: wall, floor, and legs (or all to lay everything flat on one plate). Quick start Set your can size — can_diameter and can_height . Set space_depth (how deep the tray is — it rounds down to a whole number of cans). Adjust angle if cans don't roll freely (higher = steeper). Switch mode to print , set part_select , and export STLs. Print the parts, snap them together, and lock the seams with Multiboard dual-clip keys (printed separately). 🎛️ Key Parameters Group Parameter What it does Can can_height, can_diameter Your can's length & diameter Capacity & Tilt space_depth Tray depth / how many cans fit angle Floor tilt so cans roll forward (deg) can_gap Extra clearance for print tolerance Lips start_angle / end_angle Front (low) & back (high) lip curl lip_clearance Gap between can and lip Thickness floor_thickness, wall_width Panel thicknesses stack_gap Free space above the can (stack pitch) Pattern pattern Honeycomb cut-outs on/off hex_cell, hex_rib, border Honeycomb cell size, rib width, frame Legs legs Snap-on braces that stand the base at the tilt leg_length, leg_size, leg_clearance Brace length, thickness, front lift Clips clip_thk Match to your Multiboard clip thickness clip_fit, pocket_deepen Fine-tune snap tightness / flush seams clip_spacing, seam_clip_spacing How often clips are placed Output bed_size Your printer's bed — auto-splits larger models into tiles mode stacked (preview) → switch to print to export part_select all / wall / floor / legs stack_count Units shown in stacked preview

description: Tired of not finding a practical system to make your own roller blinds? This is a complete, robust, and 100% DIY system designed for MakerWorld! This project allows you to create a custom roller blind at a very low cost. It uses a standard 22.5mm cylindrical wooden rod (readily available in any DIY or hardware store) and a smooth cord-pull mechanism. Key Highlights: Cost-Effective & Custom: Make it exactly to the dimensions of your windows without paying a premium. Versatile Mounting: Supports can be screwed directly into either the ceiling or the wall. Easy Maintenance: The clever slider design allows you to easily unhook and remove the brackets to wash the fabric. Smooth Operation: Features a 4-roller system acting as mechanical bearings for a frictionless roll. Bill of Materials (Printed Parts) 2x End Caps (to glue onto the ends of the wooden rod) 4x Rollers (mechanical wheels for smooth rotation) 1x Left Bracket 1x Right Bracket 2x Base Mounts (The sliding brackets to screw into the wall/ceiling) Hardware Required (Non-Printed) 1x Cylindrical wooden rod (22.5mm diameter). 1x Fabric curtain (cut and hemmed to your window size). 2x Screws and wall anchors (adapted to your wall or ceiling material). 1x Cord (approximately twice the total length of your curtain). Tools: Wood glue (to secure the end caps) and, to attach the fabric to the wood I personnally used staples but feel free to propose any alternative ! Step-by-Step Assembly Guide Prepare the fabric: Cut your fabric to your window's width and length, then hem the edges. Glue the 3D-printed end caps to both ends of the wooden rod. Attach the fabric to the wooden rod using staple for example Assemble the brackets (put the 4 rollers into their designated place, they are purposely loose but any proposal to improve that part is highly welcomed !) Mount the little rail to the wall / ceiling using a screw. Do a test to ensure they are properly placed with regard to the wooden rod length with their caps: Measure the exact distance needed, then screw the two Base Mounts into your wall or ceiling. Slide the left and right brackets onto them. Set up the cord: Wind the cord around the wheel (to ensure the cord doesn't slide around the cap I had to make 3 turns around the caps) of the dedicated end cap. Place the wooden rod assembly into the bracket rollers. Test the pull mechanism!

model_name: Letrero de Nombre Cursivo con Corazón
description: ¡Hola! 👋 Este letrero personalizado te permite escribir cualquier nombre (¡o hasta dos nombres juntos! 💑) en una preciosa tipografía cursiva, con la opción de añadir un corazón y unas colas decorativas que le dan un toque súper especial y romántico. Perfecto para regalar, decorar una estantería o sorprender a alguien especial 🎁✨ 🔤 ¿Cómo escribo el nombre? Solo tienes que escribir el texto en el parámetro texto . Puedes usar mayúsculas y minúsculas sin problema para las letras normales 😊 ⚠️ Importante: las colas decorativas (inicio, final y el corazón) solo funcionan con letras en minúscula . Si escribes una letra en mayúscula donde debería ir una cola, esa letra se quedará "normal", sin la colita. Así que, si quieres el efecto completo, ¡escribe el nombre todo en minúscula! (ej: "aurora" en vez de "Aurora") 💕 ¿Cómo pongo el corazón entre dos nombres? ¡Súper fácil! Solo escribe los dos nombres separados por un espacio , por ejemplo: "oscar giu". El sistema detecta automáticamente el espacio y coloca ahí el corazón, uniendo las dos palabras de forma preciosa 🥰 No hace falta escribir ningún símbolo especial, ¡el espacio ya hace toda la magia! 🪢 ¿Qué son las colas de inicio y final? Son dos pequeños adornos decorativos (una especie de rúbrica caligráfica) que se añaden antes de la primera letra y después de la última letra de todo el texto, dándole un acabado mucho más elegante y "hecho a mano" ✍️ activar_adorno_inicio ✅/❌ — activa o desactiva la cola antes de la primera letra activar_adorno_final ✅/❌ — activa o desactiva la cola después de la última letra activar_corazon_espacio ✅/❌ — activa o desactiva el corazón en el espacio entre nombres Recuerda: estas 3 opciones solo se aplican si la letra correspondiente (primera, última, o la de antes del espacio) es minúscula 🔡 ⚙️ Todos los parámetros que puedes personalizar 📏 Tamaño ancho_deseado_letrero — el ancho total del letrero en mm; las letras se ajustan solas para que el texto entero mida justo esto, sea cual sea el nombre 📐 ✏️ Texto texto — el nombre o los nombres que quieres grabar (recuerda: minúsculas para el efecto completo de colas) 🖋️ grosor_texto — el grosor (altura en Z) del relieve de las letras, en mm 🔼 💕 Adornos especiales activar_adorno_inicio — cola decorativa al principio del texto activar_adorno_final — cola decorativa al final del texto activar_corazon_espacio — corazón automático en el espacio entre dos nombres 🧱 Base contorno_base — grosor del borde/marco sólido alrededor de las letras, en mm grosor_base — grosor de la base, en mm (con un valor alto, ej. 50mm, el letrero se sostiene solo de pie sin necesitar agujeros de montaje) 🧍 🕳️ Parches Tapahuecos (por si alguna letra deja huecos sueltos, como en la "o" o la "a") activar_parche_izquierdo / activar_parche_derecho / activar_parche_centro — activa cada parche donde lo necesites parche_izq_x / _y, parche_der_x / _y, parche_cen_x / _y — posición de cada parche (mm) radio_parche_izq / _der / _cen — tamaño (radio) de cada parche, en mm 🎨 Colores color_base — color del cuerpo/base del letrero color_texto — color del relieve de las letras (colores disponibles: Rojo, Amarillo, Rosa, Verde, Azul, Naranja, Morado, Negro, Blanco, Gris) ¡Espero que te encante el resultado! 💖 Si tienes dudas al generar tu nombre personalizado, no dudes en preguntar 😊🖨️ Hi! 👋 This personalized sign lets you write any name (or even two names together! 💑) in a beautiful cursive font, with the option to add a heart and decorative tails for a super special and romantic touch. Perfect for a gift, decorating a shelf, or surprising someone special 🎁✨ 🔤 How do I write the name? Just type the text in the text field. You can use uppercase and lowercase letters without any problem 😊 ⚠️ Important: the decorative tails (start, end, and heart) only work with lowercase letters. If you type a capital letter where a tail should be, that letter will remain "normal," without the tail. So, if you want the full effect, write the name all in lowercase! (e.g., "aurora" instead of "Aurora") 💕 How do I add the heart between two names? Super easy! Just type the two names separated by a space, for example: "oscar giu". The system automatically detects the space and places the heart there, beautifully joining the two words 🥰 No need to type any special symbols, the space does all the magic! 🪢 What are the start and end tails? These are two small decorative flourishes (a kind of calligraphic signature) that are added before the first and last letters of the text, giving it a much more elegant and "handmade" finish ✍️ activate_flourish_beginning ✅/❌ — activates or deactivates the flourish before the first letter activate_flourish_end ✅/❌ — activates or deactivates the flourish after the last letter activate_heart_space ✅/❌ — activates or deactivates the heart in the space between names Remember: these 3 options only apply if the corresponding letter (first, last, or the one before the space) is lowercase 🔡 ⚙️ All the parameters you can customize 📏 Size desired_flag_width — the total width of the flag in mm; The letters automatically adjust so the entire text measures exactly this, whatever the name 📐 ✏️ Text text — the name or names you want engraved (remember: lowercase for the full tail effect) 🖋️ text_thickness — the thickness (Z-height) of the letter relief, in mm 🔼 💕 Special Embellishments activate_embellishment_start — decorative tail at the beginning of the text activate_embellishment_end — decorative tail at the end of the text activate_heart_space — automatic heart in the space between two names 🧱 Base base_outline — thickness of the solid border/frame around the letters, in mm base_thickness — thickness of the base, in mm (with a high value, e.g., 50mm, the sign stands on its own without needing mounting holes) 🧍 🕳️ Patches Filler letters (in case any letters leave gaps, like in the "o" or the "a") activate_left_patch / activate_right_patch / activate_center_patch — activate each patch where you need it left_patch_x / _y, right_patch_x / _y, center_patch_x / _y — position of each patch (mm) left_patch_radius / right_patch_radius / _center_patch — size (radius) of each patch, in mm 🎨 Colors base_color — color of the body/base of the sign text_color — color of the letter relief (Available colors: Red, Yellow, Pink, Green, Blue, Orange, Purple, Black, White, Gray) I hope you love the result! 💖 If you have any questions while creating your personalized name, don't hesitate to ask 😊🖨️

description: 萌系黑龙/夜煞桌面摆件与屏幕挂件（3D 打印款）完整说明 一、项目主要特点 双形态互动设计： 巧妙的重心与姿态设计，使其既能像趴在屏幕边缘的“监工”一样稳稳挂在显示器上，也能作为独立的立体公仔稳固地站立在平坦的桌面上，兼顾实用与趣味。 超精细仿生鳞片： 尽管是 Q 版造型，但模型体表布满了极其精细的微缩龙鳞与皮革般的肌理纹路，极大地提升了手办的精致度与高级感。 分件灵动大眼： 标志性的超大眼睛极其适合分件打印（或多色 AMS 打印）。黑白分明的灵动大眼不仅是整个模型的灵魂，也大大降低了手残党的涂装门槛。 萌系治愈比例： 采用大头小身子、短手短脚的经典 Q 版拟人化比例，配合充满好奇的无辜神态，能瞬间融化打工人的心。 二、适用场景 & 适配人群 适用场景 电脑桌面 Setup： 绝佳的显示器屏幕挂件或机箱内部装饰，为冰冷的数码办公空间增添一丝奇幻与温馨。 车载治愈萌物： 配合无痕胶固定在车载中控台或屏幕上方，陪伴你的每一次出行。 潮玩盲盒展示： 独立站立姿态极其适合摆放在展示柜中，与其他动漫手办或盲盒完美契合。 适配人群 奇幻动画/萌宠爱好者： 对《驯龙高手》等奇幻 IP 中忠诚、可爱的龙形生物毫无抵抗力的玩家。 办公桌“软装”达人： 喜欢用各种治愈系小物件打造个性化工位、缓解工作压力的上班族。 3D 打印手办玩家： 追求高精度皮肤质感表现，喜欢给模型进行眼部点睛涂装的手工爱好者。 三、3D 打印设置（0.4mm 标准喷嘴通用参数） 为了完美还原极其细密的皮肤鳞片，确保这只小黑龙拥有高级的手办质感，建议参考以下切片参数： 层高（Layer Height）： 强烈建议使用 0.12mm - 0.16mm。头顶与背部等平缓的圆弧区域建议开启“动态层高（Adaptive Layers）”，以彻底消除顶部的等高线台阶。 墙数量 / 外轮廓（Walls / Perimeters）： 3 层。多层外墙能让表面的微小鳞片起伏更加立体扎实。 填充率（Infill）： 10% - 15%。推荐使用 聚 Gyroid（陀螺仪） 填充。若打算将其主要作为屏幕挂件，较低的填充率能减轻整体重量，使其挂在屏幕上时重心更稳。 打印速度： 外部可见区域（Outer Wall）建议降速控制在 40-60 mm/s，慢速不仅能大幅提升哑光耗材的表面光泽一致性，还能确保每一片微小的鳞片细节不糊、不拉丝。 四、补充打印 & 组装建议 尺寸缩放参考： 屏幕挂件款（80–100mm）： 专门为显示器定制的最佳尺寸，不挡视线，小巧灵动。 (注：缩放前请先使用卡尺测量您显示器边框的厚度，确保缩放后龙爪与身体的间隙能够刚好卡住您的屏幕边缘) 。 桌面标准款（120–150mm）： 适合作为独立的手办摆件放在鼠标垫旁或书架上，体表的鳞片细节表现力最强。 超大镇宅款（180mm以上）： 适合拥有大尺寸打印机的玩家，极致放大后的鳞片犹如真实的爬行动物皮肤般震撼。 耗材与色彩推荐： 强烈建议使用哑光黑（Matte Black） 或带有极细微闪粉的 星空黑（Galaxy Black）耗材打印主体，能完美过滤掉廉价的塑料反光，复刻出深邃的高级皮革质感。 眼睛涂装/点睛小贴士： 如果是单色打印，眼睛部分可以用丙烯马克笔（白色打底，黑色画瞳孔）轻松涂装。强烈建议在纯黑的瞳孔边缘点上一抹白色的“高光”，这能让整只小龙瞬间注入灵魂，眼神变得极其清澈灵动。 屏幕安全固定技巧： 虽然模型设计有卡住屏幕的物理结构，但为了防止不小心触碰导致其掉落摔坏，建议在挂上屏幕时，在龙的腹部或前爪内侧贴一小粒蓝丁胶（Blu-Tack）或透明无痕纳米胶，既稳固又绝对不会损伤显示器屏幕。

description: PET ARCH – Elevated Pet Bowl Stand with Storage Designed for Easier Handling, Feeding and Storage PET ARCH grew from a simple observation in daily life with my cat. Refilling food, cleaning the bowl, moving the feeder, and organizing nearby essentials often involve several separate actions. This led me to explore how these small inconveniences could be combined into a more intuitive feeding solution. The design centers on ease of handling . Openings around the stand create multiple natural grip points , allowing the feeder to be lifted and repositioned from different sides. The lower arch continues the same idea, serving as an additional handhold while giving the form a practical purpose. A removable Bowl Lift Ring makes the bowl easier to take out for serving, refilling, and cleaning. Beneath it, the Storage Base Tray turns otherwise unused space into convenient storage for food cans, treats, toys, and other pet essentials. Together, the removable parts form a compact modular system that is easy to assemble, clean, carry, and store. Tall and Short options provide two feeding heights, while the customizable Bowl Lift Ring supports different compatible bowls and feeding setups. More than a raised bowl holder, PET ARCH brings handling, mobility, and storage together in one cohesive design: Lift / Move / Reach. Included Components Tall Stand Body – The taller stand option for an elevated feeding setup. Short Stand Body – The lower stand option for a more compact feeding setup. Bowl Lift Ring – Fits around the bowl for easier lifting, serving, and removal. Storage Base Tray – Creates an integrated space below for food cans, treats, toys, or other small pet essentials. Key Features Easy to Lift and Move – Multiple openings and the lower arch provide natural grip points for repositioning the feeder from different sides. Easy Bowl Removal – The removable Bowl Lift Ring simplifies serving, refilling, and cleaning. Integrated Storage – The Storage Base Tray uses the space beneath the bowl for food cans, treats, toys, and other small pet essentials. Customizable Modular System – Tall and Short stand options, removable components, a customizable Bowl Lift Ring, and five ready-to-print ring sizes support different compatible bowls and feeding setups. Support-Free Printing – All components are designed to print without supports, reducing material use and post-processing. Customize Your Bowl Lift Ring Adjust the Bowl Lift Ring to fit your pet bowl before slicing. Click “Objects” to open the object list. Select “Bowl Diameter.” Click “Scale (S)” and enter the desired diameter in either X or Y . The other axis will update automatically. Keep the Z dimension unchanged . Recommended diameter range: 80–125 mm . How to measure: The Bowl Lift Ring can be adjusted within the recommended size range to fit different compatible bowls. Measure the outer diameter of the bowl at the point where it will rest on the Bowl Lift Ring. Add approximately 2 mm to the measured diameter to provide suitable clearance and allow the bowl to sit securely on the ring. The bowl used in the example has a measured diameter of Ø114 mm .

Esta es mi interpretación de cómo pudo haber sido realmente el Caballo de Troya. Al modelarlo, intenté considerar aspectos que suelen pasarse por alto: la resistencia estructural necesaria para soportar su propio peso y el de los guerreros que ocultaba, así como una postura sólida y convincente. También imaginé que, al presentarse como una ofrenda o tributo, su apariencia debía transmitir solemnidad y respeto, más que la de una simple estructura de madera. Otro aspecto importante fue pensar en los recursos disponibles de la época. Asumí que fue construido principalmente por guerreros, con conocimientos prácticos, y no por artesanos especializados. Por eso busqué un diseño robusto, funcional y factible de construir con las herramientas y materiales que probablemente tenían a su alcance. Esta no pretende ser una reconstrucción histórica definitiva, sino una interpretación basada en criterios estructurales, funcionales e históricos.

description: Fan Maker - The Ultimate Parametric Folding Fan Welcome to the Fan Maker! Create your own fully customizable, mechanical folding fan directly in the browser. Colors Pick standard colors for the blades and the text/SVG inlay to preview your multi-color print accurately before exporting. Dimensions Adjust the overall length, top width, and thickness of your fan. The internal dovetail mechanism scales automatically! Personalization Global Here the magic happens. Choose between a single image across the whole fan or individual blades. Adjust text rotation, font, size, and line spacing. Pro Tip: Use the "Text Curve Radius" (e.g., 80) and "Text Letter Spacing" to perfectly bend your text along the fan's arc! SVG Graphic Want to use a logo? Adjust the thread clearance for a buttery smooth nut, or tweak the pin/hole tolerances if your printer needs a little extra room. ⚙️ Assembly Instructions Simply stack the printed blades in the correct order, slip the dovetail V-pins into the corresponding slots with a 90-degree twist to lock them in, insert the bolt through the bottom holes, and gently screw on the nut—done!

description: Bring a warm Halloween glow into your home with the GlowPaws LED Tealight Holder Collection ! Each design features an adorable animal peeking over a classic jack-o’-lantern while the light shines beautifully through the carved pumpkin face. Unlike many traditional tealight holders, the pumpkin is completely enclosed at the top. Because the LED tealight is inserted from underneath, the light is contained inside the pumpkin, creating a much brighter and more dramatic glow through the eyes, nose and mouth—even when the room isn’t completely dark. This allows you to switch the light on and off directly from underneath without removing it from the holder. An additional print profile is also included with a Twist-Lock Bottom featuring an integrated Light Tube . This version uses the same Twist-Lock system but adds a Light Tube that helps keep non-Bambu LED tea lights centered, hides the light from direct view, and creates a softer, warmer, and more atmospheric glow. Both Twist-Lock Bottom versions are fully compatible with the Bambu Lab LED Tea Light . The Light Tube version also accommodates many other LED tea lights up to 48 mm (1.89 in) in diameter and 40 mm (1.57 in) in height. For LED tea lights larger than 48 mm (1.89 in) in diameter, simply leave the Twist-Lock Bottom off and place the holder directly over the light. description: LumaForge – Customizable LED Lamp Generator Version: 1.1.0 LumaForge is a MakerWorld customizer for creating complete layered LED lamps for desks, bedside tables, shelves, ambient room lighting, or pendant installations. Export the housing once, then change only the light source and export the required inserts. Compact source-specific fit produces a smaller lamp intended for one selected light source. For E14 and E27, measure the real holder neck diameter, body diameter, and height before printing. E14/E27 describe the bulb thread, not the outside dimensions of the holder. Preset groups can be overridden independently. You can keep a preset's colors while changing its body, replace only the diffuser pattern, disable its upper window, or manually adjust the lamp dimensions. Patterns are generated within one continuous illuminated band, so the diffuser can be rotated to present a different section without changing its fit. For illuminated patterns, use enough wall loops to fill the diffuser wall and disable sparse infill for that object. Six or seven walls with Arachne are a practical starting point. description: What It Is The ReSpool Bag Tower is a modular storage and dispensing system for reusable plastic bags. Its structure incorporates the cardboard cores found inside filament refill spools, parts that would normally be discarded after the filament has been used. Instead of printing an unnecessarily large container, the design gives these cardboard cores a practical second life. Each core becomes part of the body of the dispenser, reducing the amount of filament required while increasing storage capacity. The system is modular: add or remove sections according to the number of bags you want to store and the space available. A vertical configuration uses very little floor space, while the weighted base keeps the tower stable during everyday use. Upcycling by Design This project was developed around a simple principle: sustainability should be integrated into the design process, not added as an afterthought. By identifying a common piece of waste, the cardboard core from a filament refill spool—and turning it into a structural component, the ReSpool Bag Tower transforms discarded material into a useful resource. The project balances sustainability with: Practical everyday functionality Comfortable and safe interaction Reduced filament consumption Modular capacity Very Simple assembly An experimental approach that can evolve into new configurations The objective was not simply to make something new, but to create an object with a clear purpose while encouraging makers to reconsider the materials they normally throw away. Feel free to experiment with as many colors as you like, it will look fantastic! Embrace the upcycling spirit and use your leftover filament to create a truly unique combination. Key Features Upcycled structure: reuses cardboard cores from filament refill spools. Modular capacity: add as many sections as needed. Space-saving vertical design: provides generous storage without occupying much kitchen floor space. Weighted base: designed with additional mass for improved stability. Soft dispensing outlet: the flexible TPU nozzle protects both your hand and the plastic bags. Non-slip feet: TPU feet improve grip and help protect the supporting surface. Material-efficient construction: the reused cardboard sections replace a large amount of printed material. Easy loading: bags are inserted through the opening at the top and removed from the outlet near the base. Materials Rigid Parts The base, connectors and remaining structural parts can be printed in PLA, PETG or another rigid material of your choice. For the example shown, I used carbon-fibre-filled PLA. Both PLA-CF and PETG-CF can provide an especially clean surface finish, but standard PLA or PETG will also work well. Flexible Parts The feet and dispensing nozzle are designed to be printed in TPU. I used TPU with a Shore hardness of 95A, although another suitable flexible filament may also work, the softer the better. TPU was selected for the outlet because this is the area that comes into contact with your hand and with the bags. I f you don't like TPU or don't have it, drop me a message and I will provide a special part for the outer ring. The flexible surface: Feels more comfortable when reaching for a bag, does not scratch your hand Avoids sharp rigid edges Helps prevent thin plastic bags from tearing during removal Important TPU Preparation Dry the TPU for at least 12 hours before printing, even if the spool is new. TPU can absorb moisture during manufacturing, storage and transport. Printing wet TPU may cause stringing, bubbles, rough surfaces and weak or inconsistent areas. Proper drying makes a significant difference to the quality of the finished part. Printing the TPU outer ring The outer ring is printed in TPU with PLA support material. This combination works particularly well because TPU does not bond strongly to PLA. The PLA supports the flexible part during printing but can be separated afterwards without permanently attaching to it. After printing, flex and twist the TPU part firmly . The rigid PLA support will normally crack and break into smaller sections, while the TPU bends without damage. Remove the broken support material gradually. Be careful: some broken PLA sections may have sharp edges. Wear gloves if necessary and do not direct the part or fragments towards your face while twisting it. Assembly Print the base, modular connectors, TPU feet and TPU outlet nozzle. Remove the PLA supports, be patient... Glue the TPU feet in the base. Fit the flexible outer ring in its position. Place the first cardboard spool core on the base. Use the printed connecting sections to stack additional cardboard cores. Finish the tower with the upper loading section. Add only as many modules as you need. From a practical point of view, approximately six sections already create a tall dispenser with substantial storage capacity. When building a particularly tall configuration, place the dispenser on a level surface and check its stability before filling it completely. How to Use Insert folded or loose plastic bags (works best with folded bags) through the opening at the top. Folded bags should normally fall through the central channel under their own weight. Looser bags may need to be pushed down gently until they reach the lower section. If a bag becomes trapped inside the channel, use a smooth, blunt tool to guide it down. Avoid sharp tools that could puncture or tear the plastic.Remember tat you can alway detach any ring Remove the bags individually through the flexible TPU outlet near the base. As the dispenser fills, you can either add another modular section to increase its capacity, or print another ReSpool Bag Tower Design Notes The vertical configuration was selected because it offers a good balance between capacity and occupied space. The base is intentionally more substantial than the upper components, lowering the centre of gravity and improving stability. The contrast between the reused cardboard cores, rigid printed components and soft TPU interaction points is an important part of the design. Each material is used where its characteristics provide a functional advantage. This project also reflects an experimental design mindset: test an idea, observe how it behaves in everyday use and allow the system to evolve. Feel free to experiment with as many colors as you like, it will look fantastic! Embrace the upcycling spirit and use your leftover filament to create a truly unique combination. Future Plans A horizontal version may be explored in the future. While the current vertical arrangement makes better use of limited floor space, a horizontal configuration could work well inside cabinets, under shelves or in other locations where vertical clearance is limited. Other possible developments include: Alternative base configurations Wall-mounted versions Modules for other cardboard-core dimensions Additional heights and decorative finishes If you have a particular configuration in mind, leave a comment. Community feedback is often the starting point for the next version. Changelog 2026-07-29 — Initial Release Initial modular vertical configuration Upcycled filament-refill cardboard core structure Weighted printed base Flexible TPU dispensing nozzle TPU non-slip feet

description: It’s not uncommon for a stiff breeze to blow through an open patio door, causing doors to slam shut. Meanwhile, a little one might be crawling on the floor, finding the door fascinating—only to quickly get their fingers caught in the hinge or the gap at the bottom. Or perhaps you just want the door to stay open while carrying dishes back and forth between the kitchen and dining room. The stopper is 3 millimeters high, so you need at least that much clearance—plus the thickness of the adhesive—under your door. That’s why I designed this great door stopper. It attaches at the spot where you want the door to stay open (using double-sided tape, hot glue, etc., or two screws; both versions are pre-sliced). When you move the door over the stopper, the raised section prevents it from swinging back. The door can only be closed or moved again once you press that raised part down—either by hand or with your foot. In our case, this ensures safety, as our baby can't simply move the door and get their fingers trapped while exploring the house. While similar solutions exist, I focused on keeping this design simple, ensuring the curves are just right, and making it durable enough not to break—provided it’s used properly and not handled roughly. Please make sure to print the door stopper using PETG so it functions optimally and doesn't break. PLA is too rigid to withstand the constant up-and-down movement or the stress of a door being pulled shut with a bit of force. Enjoy the product—feel free to leave a boost and give me some feedback!

description: Updates : 30/07/2026 : Added new A1 profile : H320xW150xD150 30/07/2026 : Fix compatibility for X1C 📐 Customizable dimensions Standard bookshelves come in standard sizes. This one does not. Parametric Shelf is a modular 3D-printed bookshelf that can be customized directly through the MakerWorld Customizer. Instead of entering the final outside dimensions of the furniture, you enter the usable internal space required for your books : Book_Width Book_Height Book_Depth The surrounding structure, rods, connectors, and side pieces are then generated automatically around that usable space. This makes it possible to create a bookshelf for a specific book format, collection, or available space that may be difficult to match with standard furniture. 📏 Calculating the external dimensions For the current version of the design, you can estimate the external dimensions of the main structure using these formulas: Structure height = Book_Height + 16 mm External width = Book_Width + 30 mm External depth = Book_Depth + 27 mm For example, with the following usable book space: Book_Height: 330 mm Book_Width: 230 mm Book_Depth: 223 mm The external dimensions of the main structure will be: Height: 346 mm Width: 260 mm Depth: 250 mm ⚠️ The height formula does not include the feet or the final top piece. Their height must be added separately when calculating the total height of the fully assembled bookshelf. 🧰 Choose your starting model Three customizable model types are available: Starter Pack – Pattern Circle A complete starter unit using the circular side pattern. Starter Pack – Pattern Square A complete starter unit using the square side pattern. Horizontal Expansion Pack An expansion kit designed to extend an existing structure horizontally. To build your first complete bookshelf, you must begin with one of the two Starter Packs . The Circle and Square patterns can both be seen in the project photos. ↕️ Vertical expansion To add another level vertically, use another Starter Pack , but do not print the duplicated Top and Bottom pieces or their associated rods. I have personally assembled a configuration with two vertically stacked levels , and I currently find it acceptable for my own use. However, stacking increases leverage and side-to-side movement. The result may vary depending on the selected dimensions, the weight of the books, print quality, and the surface on which the bookshelf is placed. ↔️ Horizontal expansion The Horizontal Expansion Pack adds one complete shelf section horizontally, including its top, bottom, and associated rods. When using the Horizontal Expansion Pack to extend an additional vertically stacked level, do not print its Top and Bottom pieces or their associated rods. The system can therefore be expanded both vertically and horizontally , depending on your available space. ⚠️ Important: strength and long-term testing Please read this section before printing. This is an experimental, fully 3D-printed bookshelf , not heavy-duty wooden or metal furniture. The structure is functional, but its strength and rigidity are not extreme. It should therefore be assembled, loaded, and handled with care. I chose PLA for my own test structure, so my current observations are based on a bookshelf printed with this material. At the time of publishing, I have only tested the bookshelf for a few days . It is currently holding books correctly, but I do not yet know how the structure will behave after several weeks or months under continuous load. Long-term durability may vary depending on: The selected dimensions The weight and distribution of the books The filament used The print settings Layer adhesion Room temperature The number of stacked levels I currently find my two-level configuration acceptable for my own use. However, it has not yet been tested over a long period, so please use your own judgment and handle the finished bookshelf carefully. 🛠️ How to use the Customizer Choose one of the Starter Packs for your first bookshelf, or the Horizontal Expansion Pack for an existing structure. Click Customize on the MakerWorld model page. Enter the required values for Book_Width, Book_Height, and Book_Depth. Generate your customized model. Export the generated model as a 3MF file . Open the exported 3MF in Bambu Studio . Reorganize the generated parts across the build plates, using the corresponding print profile as a reference. Before slicing, set the Wall Loops to 3 for the rods and connectors . Check the orientation and arrangement of all parts, then slice and print. The Customizer generates all the required parts using your selected dimensions, but it does not automatically reproduce the optimized build-plate organization from the prepared print profiles. You will therefore need to reorganize the parts manually in Bambu Studio. For a complete Starter Pack, the reference print profile shows how to arrange the bookshelf parts across seven build plates . 🖨️ Important print recommendation The default print settings can be used for most parts. However, for the rods and connectors , I strongly recommend increasing the number of Wall Loops from 2 to 3 . This uses slightly more filament, but it makes a noticeable difference to the rigidity and strength of the assembled structure. Because the design has not yet been tested over a long period, I recommend prioritizing strength over minimum material usage for these structural parts. 🔧 Assembly guide ⚠️ Before starting Inserting the rods requires a significant amount of force. This is intentional and helps create a tight and rigid structure. So far, none of my rods have broken during assembly , even when considerable force was required. However, once a rod has been inserted, I have not found a clean way to remove it again. Before beginning the final assembly, make sure that: The selected dimensions are suitable All parts have been printed correctly You understand where each part needs to go The assembly should be considered mostly permanent. 1️⃣ Assemble the first side Choose one side of substructure A or B . Take its Side Top and Side Bottom pieces and insert the rods into them. 2️⃣ Prepare the opposite side Place the matching side pieces that do not yet contain rods flat on a stable surface. 3️⃣ Connect both sides Align the rods already attached to the first side with the openings in the side pieces placed on the surface. Push the assembly together to engage the rods. With some luck, all the rods may enter at the same time. In my experience, however, they usually need to be inserted one by one . Continuously check the alignment during this step. Do not continue pushing if a rod is not correctly aligned with its opening. 4️⃣ Join the substructures Attach the connectors to the completed side assemblies, then use them to connect all the substructures together. 🧩 The top piece is strongly recommended The top piece is an important part of the structure . It helps prevent the upper front section of the bookshelf from twisting or flexing and noticeably improves the rigidity of the finished assembly. For this reason, I strongly recommend printing and installing the final top piece, especially when the shelf will carry books or when multiple levels are stacked. 👣 Optional feet The feet are optional from a structural point of view. The bookshelf can be assembled without them, but I think they give the model a cleaner and more finished appearance. They also help make the printed object feel more like a complete piece of furniture. Remember that the feet are not included in the height calculation given in the customization section. 🧵 Material usage Material consumption depends on the selected dimensions, filament, and slicer settings, but as a general reference: Approximately 550 g of PLA per shelf level Approximately 150 g of PLA for the feet and top combined I am aware that this is a significant amount of filament. A simple wooden bookshelf will often be more economical and may also be stronger. This model was originally created as a personal design and printing challenge. Its main advantage is its parametric flexibility : it can be adapted to a specific book format, collection, or available space instead of forcing the user to choose from standard furniture dimensions. 💬 Feedback and future updates This project started as a personal design challenge, but the parametric system turned it into something much more flexible: a bookshelf that can adapt to the user instead of forcing the user to adapt to the bookshelf. Because this is still a recent and experimental design, feedback will be especially valuable. Please share your makes, selected dimensions, print settings, book formats, expansion layouts, and how the shelf behaves over time. This feedback will help me improve the structure and decide which configurations should be added next.

description: Modular kit for securely adapting your portable AC to an open tilt-window and adding an intake hose for better cooling efficiency. Holds the window firmly in place while sealing off the opening and providing excellent airflow for both the intake & exhaust vents. For complete sealing, I recommend cutting foam pieces to fill the open space above and below the opened window. The kit includes a 255x230mm to 150mm intake hose adapter for portable AC units, a modular plate with two 150mm vents and adjustable brackets to fit the majority of tilt-windows as shown in the cover image. Printing : Print this in PETG or ABS . The exhaust vent will get too hot for PLA. The file is structured as follows: The kit is made up of multiple 250mm segments and a smaller 105mm segment. In my case, the window was 85.5cm in height, so I needed both adapter segments ( plates 3 and 4 ), as well as the top segment with mounts ( plate 5 ) and the short 105mm fill plate ( plate 7 ), which adds up to 855mm. Perfect fit, almost like I designed it specifically for that window or something :) In your case, measure the height of your window. Then print the plates according to your needs. You can add a blank 250mm segment by printing plate 6, or a blank 105mm segment by printing plate 7. It is likely that you'll need to modify at least one piece to achieve a perfect fit, if you wish to have zero gap. Whether you do that with a hacksaw or by simply shortening the piece in the slicer is up to you. Assembly: Assembly is fairly simple, refer to this image. The only supplies required are some M8x20 Screws, nuts and washers to secure the mounting brackets . The locking pieces to secure the segments together are meant to fit tightly, don't hesitate to tap them into place lightly with a hammer. You can assemble the segments in different orders than shown here, just be sure to have a set of mounting brackets somewhere near the top and another somewhere near the bottom. Test fit everything and then tighten the screws. The brackets can be both slid back and forth within their mounting slots, as well as tilted to fit as tightly as possible. Make sure to place the exhaust vent ABOVE the intake vent! The intake will otherwise ingest hot air directly from the exhaust! While this design should fit most european-style tilt windows as shown in the cover image, there is no way I can guarantee it will fit yours exactly. The modular design and seperate brackets should however make it easy to adapt with minimal effort. Happy printing and enjoy!

model_name: CIRCULAR TESSERA - Modular Parametric Wall Tiles
description: CIRCULAR TESSERA A modular decorative disc that splits itself to fit your build plate — and carries one continuous pattern across every joint. Pick a diameter. Pick a pattern. The model works out how to cut the disc into printable pieces, hides the joints behind bowtie connectors, and flows the design across every seam so the finished piece reads as one object, not a mosaic of tiles. 28 pattern engines. Any size. Multi-colour out of the box. The idea Most large wall pieces are built from tiles, and you can always tell — the grid shows. CIRCULAR TESSERA works the other way round. The pattern is defined once, across the whole disc , as a single continuous field. Each piece simply shows its own window onto that field. Two neighbouring segments aren't drawing their own pattern and hoping it lines up; they're computing the same pattern in different places, so it has to match. The cuts exist for one reason only: build plate size. Everything else in the model is there to make them disappear. What you get Centre disc + concentric rings. Set the centre radius, the ring thickness and how many rings. That's the whole geometry. It cuts itself to fit. Tell it the longest piece your printer can handle and every ring is split accordingly — outer rings automatically get more segments. Seams that don't line up. Radial cuts are staggered on alternate rings, so no cut ever runs straight through the disc. Hidden joinery. Bowtie connectors sit in pockets recessed into the back. Nothing is visible from the front. Two-mesh pieces. Every piece exports as a base and a relief, ready for a colour change with no post-processing. Wall mounting built in. Keyhole hangers recessed into the back, with the exact drill coordinates printed to the console. 28 pattern engines , from geometric tilings to sculpted surfaces. Default settings give a 210 mm disc in 21 pieces. Scale it to a coaster or to something that fills a wall — the model doesn't care. The patterns Polar-grid — built on the disc's own circular grid Truchet arcs · Diagonal maze · True labyrinth Flat geometric — one field across the whole disc Voronoi web · Hexagon honeycomb · Tri-weave · Isometric cubes · Diamond plate · Flowing waves · Concentric ripples · Sunflower (Fibonacci phyllotaxis) · Fish scales · Basket weave · Star lattice · Girih strapwork · Celtic plait · Bubbles · S-wave flames · Scallop interlace · Hicks hexagon Sculpted — the whole surface becomes one continuous curve Radial waves · Silk ridges · Dunes · Interfering waves · Stepped topography True 3D relief — engines that build their own solid geometry Vertex cubes · Hex height field · Overlapping hexagons Each has its own parameter group, so you can tune density, scale and character. seed re-rolls anything random — every seed is a different disc. A few worth trying first: Concentric ripples for something classical, Sunflower to make the most of the circular format, Radial waves for a sculpted splash that peaks at the centre, and Hicks hexagon if you want three colours. Make it yours Everything runs through the Customizer. The order of the panel follows the order you'd actually make decisions in: Pattern — pick the engine, set stroke_width and seed Centre — solid hub, pattern all the way in, or a clean central hole Geometry — center_radius, ring_thickness, ring_count Segmentation — set max_arc to your plate size and let it do the maths Base / Edges — thickness, relief height, optional chamfer on the pattern edges Joints / Wall mounting — connector fit and keyholes Then set part to what you want: assembly for the full preview, exploded to inspect the joints, or the individual parts for printing. Tip: design on part = segment or ring_here. Rendering the full assembly on every change gets slow, especially with Voronoi or the sculpted engines. Printing Print the calibration piece first. Set part = calibration. You get two test plates sharing a socket, plus one connector. Check the fit — snug, but you can push it home by hand. Adjust conn_clearance in 0.05 mm steps until it's right. Five minutes here saves reprinting real pieces later. All tolerance lives on the connector. The sockets in the pieces stay at nominal size, on purpose: if the fit is off you reprint a connector that costs a quarter of a gram, never a whole piece. Everything else: No supports , anywhere, on any piece or any pattern. The sockets are recesses in the underside, so they print against the plate as clean pockets. Print flat, face up , exactly as generated. 0.2 mm layers are fine. Drop to 0.12–0.16 mm for the sculpted patterns — their whole surface is a curve. 3+ walls , 15–20% infill. Print a few spare connectors . They're tiny, and a contrasting colour makes assembly easier to keep track of. Multi-colour Each piece is generated as separate meshes — a base and a relief, plus a third mesh of solid cores on the Hicks hexagon engine. That's what lets you assign a different filament to the pattern without splitting anything by hand. If you're rendering the .scad yourself: turn on Preferences → Features → lazy-union in OpenSCAD before exporting. It's off by default, and with it off everything merges into one mesh — you lose both the colour split and the separation between pieces. Export as 3MF , not STL. In the slicer, group each base with its matching relief, assign your filaments, and slice normally. The relief sits directly on the base, so the colour change lands on a clean layer boundary. Assembly Work outward from the middle : centre disc first, then ring 1, then ring 2. Building inward from the outside means fighting the last ring into place. Complete each ring before moving on — join its segments to each other and close the circle, then connect that finished ring to the one inside it. Push each connector fully home into one piece, then slide the neighbour on. If a connector needs real force, stop and adjust conn_clearance rather than risk splitting a piece. Hanging it Set mount_mode and the model recesses keyhole hangers into the back, then prints the exact screw positions in millimetres from the disc centre. Mark, drill, leave the heads a couple of millimetres proud, slide the disc down onto them. Use two screws, not one. A disc is rotationally symmetric — its weight is the same all the way round — so a single screw leaves nothing to stop it turning. The pattern settles crooked and stays that way. Two keyholes on a horizontal line fix the orientation completely. This is the one thing that's genuinely different from hanging a square tile. Mount in the centre disc for small and medium sizes, or spread the keyholes around a ring for something large or heavy. With a 3 mm base the chamber suits thin and countersunk heads; raise base_thickness to 4 mm for standard pan-head screws. Good to know Why do some ring-to-ring connectors go missing? They're placed only where there's genuinely clear space between the radial cuts of both neighbouring rings, so a socket never lands on a cut. circ_n is a target, not a guarantee — rings with many segments simply offer fewer safe gaps. The disc is still held: nested rings can't fall apart, and the connectors are there to stop them rotating out of pattern alignment. Why does the centre look different on some patterns? The three polar-grid engines have cells that get narrower toward the middle, so they keep a small solid hub by default. Set center_mode = fill to run them all the way in anyway, or empty for a clean central hole. Every other engine reaches the centre on its own. edge_chamfer seems to do nothing. It shapes the top rim of the relief on the flat 2D engines. The sculpted and 3D-relief engines already shape their own surface, so they ignore it. Rendering is slow. Voronoi is by far the heaviest engine, and the sculpted ones scale with sculpt_res. Design on a single segment and render the full assembly only at the end. Included circular_tessera_v1_0.scad — the full parametric model, OpenSCAD 2021.01 compatible User guide (PDF) — 17 pages covering the joint system, every parameter, the pattern catalogue, printing, multi-colour export and troubleshooting A note on the family CIRCULAR TESSERA is the round sibling of TESSERA , my square wall-tile system. Same philosophy — one continuous field, invisible joinery, tolerance on the connector — worked out for polar geometry instead of a grid. The pattern engines are shared, so a disc and a tiled wall can carry the same design. If you make one, post it. The parameter set is the recipe, and I'd genuinely like to see what people do with it. description: Portable air conditioners come with a flimsy fabric window seal that never fits properly, leaks hot air back in, and looks awful. This is a set of printed components that let you build a proper rigid panel for your window, sized to fit exactly, with screw-on hose ports and quick-release clamps that need no adhesive and leave nothing behind on the window. The kit is four parts: a hose connector that screws onto your AC hose, an internal plate that mounts the hose connector to your panel, handles for lifting the panel in and out, and spring clamps that hold the whole thing in the window frame. Before you print — measure your window Print the clamps last, and set their dimensions to your own window casing first. The three that matter: Spring_Clamp_Depth — the measured distance from the rear side of your window frame to the back of your panel. This is the one that decides whether the clamp reaches at all. Spring_Clamp_Hook_Plate_Length — the long leg that sits behind the frame. It needs to clear the frame lip without fouling the rubber seal. Spring_Clamp_Mounting_Plate_Length — the short side that screws to your panel. The ones in the print profile are for 20-22mm gap Everything else in the kit is forgiving. The clamps aren't, so it's worth printing a single test clamp and offering it up to the frame before committing to a full set of nine. Additionally I have provided customisability to panel thickness and screw dimensions. Finally if you use the mobile app, make sure you configure the number of handles and clamps you need, in the print profile I only added 1 copy of each. Assembly Decide on your handle and hose positioning. Drill holes for the spring clamps — I used 4 on top, 3 at the bottom and 1 on each side. The clamp mounts through the hole on its short side, with the long leg pointing outward, so make sure that long edge has room to sit inside the window frame on the external side. Screw on the spring clamps using the head button. Drill holes for the internal connector plate and screw the connector on using the back screw receiver. Cut out the hose holes in your panel, using the connectors as a guide. Screw in the handles wherever is convenient, using the handle backplate to clamp the screw, panel and handle together. Screw the hose connector onto your AC hose. This works equally well for single or dual hose systems — a two-hose setup is just one extra hole. Fitting the panel Tilt the panel so the top clamps reach the back side without tugging on the window rubber seal. Keep all the other clamps rotated around so they don't block insertion. Once the panel is tilted into position, start rotating the clamps into place, using the hose holes as access points. Each clamp is held by a single screw — that's deliberate, and it's the whole trick. One screw lets the clamp swing freely, so you can rotate them all clear on the way in and then swing them home once the panel is seated. You could use double-sided velcro for an easier install, but that leaves the velcro receiver stuck to your window. That's exactly why I designed these clamps. What you'll need Rigid panel — I used 10mm foam PVC, but anything should work 30mm wood screws × 23: 6 for the hose connector plate, 4 per handle (×2), 1 per clamp (I used 9) Self-adhesive weather strip, 1/2 × 1/4 inch — goes on the external face of the panel Hose: mine is 5.9in / ~150mm Print notes PETG, please — not PLA. This panel sits in direct sunlight during exactly the weather you bought the aircon for, and PLA will sag. Default 0.24mm standard profile is fine throughout, but bump the spring clamps to 4 walls . Feel free to drop a comment with any questions or anything you think I should make more clear in the instructions.

description: 📻 AMPER - Retro Radio Toddler Lock Socket Cover Tired of ugly wall outlets, messy power strips, and loose cables spoiling your interior? AMPER transforms exposed wall sockets into a functional piece of mid-century modern decor. Styled after classic vintage tabletop radios, it seamlessly blends into your home while keeping live outlets safely out of reach. Designed for easy single-color or multi-color printing with zero external hardware required for the body assembly . 📸 Overview & Features Covers 23.5x19.5x8.5 cm socket box. Toddler-Proof Cable Protection: Completely covers exposed wall outlets. The front mesh panel uses a tight friction fit to prevent toddlers from pulling it open, while functional, rotatable knobs give little hands a safe, satisfying element to play with. Smart Cable Access: To plug or unplug devices, simply slide the mesh panel up, route your cable through the top groove, adjust through the mesh opening, and slide the panel back down into its tracks. Authentic Vintage Aesthetic: Dual-knob layout, detailed frequency dial face, and a sliding speaker grille pattern. 🖨️ Print Settings & Assembly Tips Setting Recommendation Supports Required on Main Body & Mesh Grooves Mesh Scale 99.6% (Default friction fit) Material PLA / PETG 💡 Support & Finish Notes: Mesh Panel Grooves: Supports inside the sliding grooves require careful removal and light filing/sanding. Do not skip these supports—the printing orientation is essential for structural integrity. Middle Horizontal Bar (Wood Texture Artifact): Depending on your support interface distance, the support interface under the middle bar may leave slight layer-line separation. This is a deliberate feature! It creates an authentic, subtle wood-grain texture that enhances the vintage radio look. Prefer a completely clean line? Simply tune your top support distance / interface layers tighter in your slicer. Friction Fit Tuning: The mesh panel is pre-scaled to 99.6% . If your printer's flow rate or material shrinkage makes it too loose or too tight, adjust the scaling in 0.1% increments (e.g., 99.5% or 99.7%) to achieve your ideal toddler-resistant resistance. 🔩 Mounting Instructions For maximum safety against toddler pulls, AMPER anchors directly to your shelf or media unit: Assemble all internal/body parts ( do not slide the mesh panel in yet ). Position the shell against the wall over your outlet/cables and mark the four leg peg locations on your shelf. Drill pilot holes into the shelf at the marked points. Drive 4 screws down through the internal leg peg guides into the shelf. Plug in your devices, pass the cables through the top groove, and slide the mesh panel down to lock everything securely.

description: 🩻Overview🩻 This high-precision 3D model is a faithful replica of the human knee joint, created through a rigorous anatomical and digital workflow. The skeletal structures were directly extracted and reconstructed from real CT scans to guarantee true-to-life bone morphology. The soft tissues—including ligaments, menisci, and articular cartilage—were then meticulously 3D modeled by hand, based on in-depth studies of MRI scans and anatomical literature. It serves as a premium medical-grade educational tool, perfect for students, orthopedic professionals, physical therapists, or 3D printing enthusiasts. Included Anatomical Structures The model features all critical bony and soft tissue structures necessary to understand the complex biomechanics of the knee: 🦴Skeletal Structure (CT Extracted): Femur, Tibia, Fibula, and Patella (kneecap), featuring accurate reproductions of condyles, epicondyles, and articular surfaces. 🔗Ligamentous Apparatus (MRI Modeled): Cruciate Ligaments (Anterior Cruciate Ligament - ACL & Posterior Cruciate Ligament - PCL). Collateral Ligaments (Medial Collateral Ligament - MCL & Lateral Collateral Ligament - LCL). Patellar System (including the patellar tendon/ligaments). 🦵Cartilage & Cushioning (MRI Modeled): Menisci (Medial and Lateral menisci). Articular Cartilage covering both the femoral and tibial contact surfaces. Overview This kinetic sculpture has linkages that cause the ball to be always centered in the exact same position. Due to each hinge axis passing through the center, no matter how each link is moved, it will cause the entire structure to articulate around a stationary center. It features a print-in-place and thread-together design that requires no glue or additional hardware. It requires no supports and is extremely fascinating and satisfying. The base can also be filled with sand or other materials to provide a more premium feel. I have also created other versions that are completely compatible with all of these parts. You can find the collection here: https://makerworld.com/en/collections/29606948-fixed-center-kinetic-sculptures For printing Standard setting can be used for printing. No AMS is required and no supports are needed. For the print profiles, there is one with all parts on separate plates for different colors for each part and two that have all the parts on a single plate (one includes the funnel and the other does not). All materials should work; however, for the ball to stay more centered, avoid flexible materials like TPU. Features The model prints in three pieces: the ball, the base, and the print-in-place linkages. Additionally, a funnel can be printed to more easily fill the base with sand or another material. The hole for filling the base is the same hole that the linkage structure threads into. The entire structure is about 95 mm in diameter and about 105 mm tall. All parts are compatible with the other versions. Assembly Assembling this model is very simple. Optionally, the funnel can be threaded into the hole in the base and the base filled. After the funnel is removed, the linkage structure can be threaded into that same hole until it stops. The location of where the threads stop should position the linkage structure properly. Lastly, the ball can be threaded onto the rod at the center of the ring. The links may be slightly stiff and not want to move after printing, but with some slight pressure, the links can be broken free. Versions with Themes I currently plan on making more variations of this model with specific themes. Job storage - Your latest generated 3D mesh is always stored in the database under your account, so you can always come back to redownload or modify your model. Interactive 2D map view - Resize, rotate, or drag your choice of shape on a 2D map view. Selective water body removal - You may or may not want to print some of the fetched water bodies. This tool lets you exclude water body segments from being generated. Extension tiles - A single GPX is a single tile by default. You can extend the tiles by adding new tiles in the Interactive 2D Map View. Jigsaw puzzle - Generate up to a 20×20 jigsaw terrain puzzle with full control over the jigsaw shape parameters and randomness. description: The Great Pyramid Cross-Section Explore the secrets of the Great Pyramid of Giza with this detailed cross-section display, revealing the intricate chambers that have fascinated humanity for millennia. What Lies Within? While traditionally understood as a grand tomb for Pharaoh Khufu, the Great Pyramid remains an enigma. Beyond the famous King’s Chamber —home to the enigmatic red granite sarcophagus—and the Queen’s Chamber , the pyramid contains the breathtaking, corbelled-roof Grand Gallery . Hidden shafts, mysterious voids discovered via muon tomography, and an unfinished Subterranean Chamber carved deep into the bedrock all point to a level of engineering sophistication that continues to challenge our understanding of the Old Kingdom. Are these voids hidden burial sites, or part of a larger, lost architectural plan? A New Discovery Beneath the Sands Recent, cutting-edge research using satellite imaging and synthetic aperture radar (SAR) has suggested the existence of an extensive, deeper subterranean complex beneath the Giza Plateau. Reports indicate potential anomalies, including vertical shafts and structured, geometric patterns reaching deep into the bedrock beneath the major pyramids. While these findings have sparked intense debate among archaeologists regarding their nature and origin, they offer a tantalizing glimpse into what may still be hidden beneath our feet. Inspired by these findings, I have designed a model of the subterranean structures that some researchers believe may be part of this deep network, featuring complex pillars with coiled sections and block-like bases.
