About Models: These models are designed to represent real animals as naturally as possible, with focus on accurate size, shapes, proportions, colors, fine details, and natural movement or pose. Some models include articulated, hinge, or flexi parts for motion and flexibility, while others are non-articulated and focus on realistic appearance. Some parts, such as legs, can be carefully adjusted with gentle heat for a more natural pose, but too much heat can damage or deform the model. Print: All settings are pre-configured and optimized for a balance between detail, print time, strength, functionality, and easy support removal. I recommend printing the models at their original scale. Scaling down may cause issues such as fused moving parts, small hinges not working correctly, or fine details not printing properly. Difficulty Guide: The difficulty icon is a general overall guide and may vary depending on your printer, filament, slicer settings, calibration, and experience. It mainly reflects print complexity, filament changes, possible waste, fine details, support use, and support removal. Multicolor prints may create more waste on single-nozzle AMS or AMS Lite systems, such as A1 with AMS Lite, compared to dual-nozzle or lower-waste systems like X2D or H2C. Level 3 / Supports: For higher difficulty models, especially Level 3, I recommend using Support Material for PLA. It can make support removal much easier, cleaner, and safer for delicate parts. This is especially helpful when the model has many supports, thin details, legs, antennas, or other fragile areas. Note / Handling: Some models may have very small hinge parts or delicate thin areas, such as legs, antennas, tails, or other small details. On some models, these parts may disconnect or break more easily if handled roughly. Please handle the models with care. They are not intended for aggressive play, but rather as educational models, display pieces, or gentle collectible toys. Durability may vary from model to model. Some models are stronger and may be suitable for careful play, while others are more delicate and better suited for display on a shelf. Articulated / Hinge Versions: For models with moving parts, hinges, or flexi sections, please open the included 3MF file, ideally in Bambu Studio. Exporting to another slicer may cause hinge problems. My hinges are created and tested by me, usually designed to print without supports, and are added this way so they can be moved, adjusted, customized, or removed when scaling the model down. STL / 3MF Note: STL files are usually provided without moving parts. The prepared articulated or hinge version is inside the 3MF file. This helps avoid problems with small scaled-down models, where moving parts, gaps, or hinges may fuse or fail. If needed, you can remove the hinges and print the model as a solid version. Safety Notice: Some models may have sharp edges or small parts. Avoid printing them too small and do not leave children unattended with them, as there is a choking risk. If you adjust parts with heat, always proceed carefully and use heat gently. Support / Links: I truly appreciate every comment, rating, or photo of your print it really motivates me to keep creating. description: Lemure Swarm Miniature – Tide of Damned Souls This miniature is part of the Monster Manual 2024 Collection , a series of iconic creatures faithfully reimagined as dynamic, tabletop-ready sculpts. The Lemure Swarm represents one of the most horrifying manifestations of infernal corruption—a heaving mass of countless damned souls fused together into a single crawling nightmare. Closely inspired by the uploaded reference and the Monster Manual 2024 depiction, this miniature emphasizes overwhelming organic horror rather than speed or aggression. The miniature is designed on a Large (50 mm) round tabletop base , allowing the sprawling mass of bodies to nearly fill the entire footprint. Instead of depicting individual Lemures standing separately, dozens of infernal bodies have merged into one towering mound of living flesh. The broad contact area gives the model exceptional structural stability while creating an unmistakable silhouette unlike any other fiend in the collection. The lower portion forms a thick pool of liquefied infernal flesh that spreads naturally across the base. From this grotesque foundation, countless humanoid forms emerge as though attempting to free themselves from eternal imprisonment. Bodies are only partially formed before dissolving back into the surrounding mass, creating a seamless transition between individual Lemures and the larger swarm. No figure appears completely separate; every soul remains permanently fused to the collective. Dominating the composition are numerous screaming faces positioned at different heights throughout the mound. Some stretch upward with mouths opened impossibly wide in silent agony, while others twist sideways or emerge only halfway from the flesh. Every expression conveys suffering rather than rage, reinforcing the tragic nature of these damned beings. The faces vary subtly in size and angle, preventing visual repetition while maintaining the impression of an endless sea of tortured souls. Multiple malformed arms reach outward from every direction. Some extend fully toward unseen victims with clawed fingers spread wide, while others appear only halfway formed before disappearing back into the flesh. Thick strands of melting tissue connect every limb directly to the central body, ensuring there are no fragile unsupported parts while enhancing the impression that the swarm itself is continuously shifting and reforming. The surface of the miniature is densely textured with stretched skin, flowing muscle fibers, sagging folds, puckered scars, exposed veins, and merging anatomical forms. Faces dissolve into shoulders, arms vanish into torsos, and bodies blend seamlessly together without clear boundaries. This continuous sculpt creates remarkable visual depth while remaining strong enough for reliable resin printing. Rather than standing upright, the swarm advances slowly as a creeping wall of flesh. The front of the miniature pushes forward with numerous crawling limbs dragging the mass across the ground, while the rear rises into a mound of intertwined bodies that gives the model impressive height despite having no fragile vertical structures. This low center of gravity makes the miniature exceptionally durable for gaming. The scenic base depicts corrupted infernal ground partially submerged beneath pools of viscous flesh. Weathered skulls, broken bones, scattered debris, and patches of cracked earth emerge from beneath the advancing tide, suggesting countless previous victims consumed by the swarm. Every scenic element is sculpted directly into the base to maximize durability and simplify printing. The recommended paint scheme closely follows the uploaded reference. The flesh should be painted using pale ivory, unhealthy pinks, bruised purples, raw crimson, and desaturated flesh tones blended together across the numerous bodies. Deep burgundy washes settle into every fold while lighter ivory highlights emphasize the stretched skin. The mouths benefit from dark crimson interiors with yellowed teeth and pale tongues, creating striking focal points across the model. Thin layers of gloss varnish on selected areas can simulate wet, freshly formed flesh without overwhelming the entire miniature. The infernal ground beneath is best painted using dark earth browns, blackened stone, scattered bone colors, and pools of coagulated crimson. No soul escapes. Every scream becomes another voice. Hell remembers everyone. ✨ Key Features Faithfully inspired by Monster Manual 2024 . Closely matches the uploaded reference miniature. Large swarm composed of countless fused Lemures. Numerous screaming faces emerging organically from the mass. Multiple grasping arms integrated directly into the body. Rich sculpted textures featuring flowing flesh, scars, folds, and merging anatomy. Low, stable composition with exceptional structural integrity. Scenic infernal base with skulls, bones, and corrupted ground. No floating elements or unsupported anatomy. Outstanding centerpiece for infernal encounters, Lower Plane adventures, and complete Monster Manual 2024 collections. 🎨 Great for Painting Prime in grey or black before layering pale flesh tones across the entire swarm. Build variation using ivory, bruised pinks, muted purples, crimson glazes, and sepia washes to distinguish individual bodies without separating them visually. Highlight raised folds using pale ivory while keeping deep recesses saturated with burgundy and violet washes. Paint mouths with dark reds, gums in fleshy pinks, and teeth using aged bone colors. Finish selected areas with controlled gloss varnish to create the appearance of wet infernal flesh. The base works beautifully with blackened stone, dusty earth pigments, scattered skulls, and dark blood effects. 📏 Scale & Compatibility Creature Size: Large Recommended Base: 50 mm round tabletop base Compatible with standard 28 mm and 32 mm heroic-scale fantasy tabletop games. Perfect for infernal invasions, abyssal battlefields, Lower Plane encounters, fiend-themed campaigns, and complete Monster Manual 2024 miniature collections.

description: Bring iconic frozen frontline defenses to your grimdark sci-fi battlefield with this detailed Hoth Defense Gun Emplacement terrain piece. This model is designed as a stationary defensive turret inspired by the fortified battlefields of a frozen ice world, featuring a tall armored support column, a broad circular gun housing, a mounted heavy cannon and an integrated snow-covered base platform. Thargor Eisenfuß – Der Fels in der Brandung Wie aus dem lebendigen Fels der tiefsten Minen gemeißelt, so steht dieser Zwergenkrieger auf dem Schlachtfeld. Seine Rüstung ist ein Meisterwerk zwergischer Schmiedekunst: schwere, quadratische Platten aus dunkel schimmerndem Grollsilber, übersät mit uralten Runen, die im Takt seines heftigen Atems schwach aufleuchten. Ein wilder, zu Zöpfen geflochtener Bart, verziert mit eisernen Ringen, reicht ihm fast bis zum Gürtel. Seine Waffe ist kein bloßes Werkzeug des Krieges, sondern ein Urteilsvollstrecker: Ein massiver, zweihändiger Großhammer , dessen Kopf so groß ist wie der Amboss einer Dorfschmiede. Wenn er diese Waffe schwingt, weicht die Luft mit einem dumpfen Wreschen zurück. Für seine Feinde gibt es kein Schild, das diesem Aufprall standhält, und keine Rüstung, die nicht unter dem schieren Gewicht seiner Schläge zermalmt wird. Wo Thargor steht, weicht kein Zoll Boden – er ist der unaufhaltsame Zorn der Berge. Die Base der Figur hat eine Durchmesser von 40mm. Viel Spaß beim Bemalen und Spielen. ! Achtung ! beim entfernen der Stützen an den empfindlichen stellen.

description: Detailliertes 3D-Modell eines Transportarbeiters mit Holzkiste, geeignet für die LGB-Gartenbahn (Maßstab ca. 1:22,5). „ Wenn euch meine Figuren gefallen und ihr spezielle Wünsche habt, schickt mir gerne eine PN – ich versuche, diese umzusetzen.“ Die Figur zeigt einen Transportarbeiter, der eine rechteckige Holzkiste mit beiden Händen vor dem Körper trägt. Die aufrechte Haltung vermittelt den Eindruck einer realistischen Transportszene. Eine flache Schiebermütze sowie die authentische Arbeitskleidung unterstreichen den Charakter eines Lager- oder Güterarbeiters. Die Figur trägt ein blaues langärmeliges Arbeitshemd mit hochgekrempelten Ärmeln, dunkle Hosenträger, dunkelgrüne Arbeitshosen, braune Schuhe sowie eine braune Schiebermütze. Die rechteckige Holzkiste ist schlicht gestaltet und weist eine realistische Holzstruktur auf. Die Figur eignet sich ideal für Güterbahnhöfe, Lagerhäuser, Fabriken, Laderampen, Speditionen oder andere realistische Alltagsszenen auf der Modellbahnanlage. Kleidung und Holzkiste sind fein modelliert. Die natürlichen Proportionen, realistische Stoffstrukturen sowie die stimmige Körperhaltung sorgen für einen hochwertigen und authentischen Gesamteindruck. Die ruhige Tragehaltung verleiht der Figur eine glaubwürdige und lebendige Präsenz in jeder Transport- oder Verlade-Szene. Gedruckt in neutralen Hautfarben und anschließend individuell nach Wunsch bemalbar. Die Figur kann optional auf eine Scheibe oder einen Sockel geklebt werden. description: Description: Bring your tabletop adventures to life with this Classic Stone 2 Floor Townhouse. Whether your party is exploring a bustling fantasy city, sneaking through a medieval village, or setting up an ambush in a historical wargame, this highly detailed terrain piece is the perfect addition to your table. Featuring realistic stone masonry, classic paned windows, and a beautifully textured shingle roof, this model takes paint exceptionally well – especially drybrushing techniques, allowing you to easily achieve a weathered, realistic look. Key Features: Filament-Saving Design: The model is hollow on the inside, this design choice significantly reduces filament usage and print time without sacrificing any of the exterior structural integrity or detail. Detailed: Deep stone and wood textures make painting with washes and drybrushing an absolute breeze. Tabletop Ready: Scaled perfectly for standard 28mm and 32mm miniature games such as Dungeons & Dragons, Pathfinder, and Frostgrave. Supports: Designed to print easily, but will require tree supports for the steepest overhangs. Brim: Recommended if you have adhesion issues, to ensure the base stays flat during the print. Finishing Tips: For the best results, prime the model in black or dark gray. Apply a drybrush of light gray over the stone walls, and a warm brown on the roof, door, and window frames to make the details pop.

description: Guard Miniature – Vigilant Defender of the Realm This miniature is part of the Monster Manual 2024 Collection , a series of iconic creatures faithfully reimagined as dynamic, tabletop-ready sculpts. The Guard represents the disciplined soldiers that protect towns, castles, temples, and trade routes throughout countless fantasy settings. While individually less powerful than seasoned adventurers, Guards form the backbone of every civilized realm. Their equipment is practical, standardized, and built for reliability rather than heroics. The Guard stands upon a Medium (25 mm) round tabletop base in a disciplined defensive stance. Both feet are planted firmly on uneven cobblestones, with the weight distributed evenly to create a stable and believable pose. Rather than charging forward or posing dramatically, the Guard stands ready to receive an approaching threat, conveying professionalism and restraint. The body is realistically proportioned beneath practical clothing and armor. The figure wears a quilted red gambeson that extends to mid-thigh, providing protection while allowing freedom of movement. Heavy folds in the fabric create strong sculptural depth, making the miniature rewarding to paint without introducing unnecessary complexity. A simple steel helmet protects the head. It features a rounded dome with a reinforced brow and subtle rivet detailing, remaining thick enough for reliable printing. Beneath the helmet, the Guard's face is stern and focused, with a determined expression suited to a veteran soldier accustomed to long watches and dangerous patrols. Around the neck rests a wrapped cloth scarf or padded collar that softens the transition between helmet and torso while adding visual interest. The clothing beneath the gambeson remains practical, with loose sleeves gathered beneath simple leather cuffs. The Guard's right hand firmly grips a long spear held vertically beside the body. The shaft is thick enough for durability while remaining visually straight and elegant. The spearhead is broad and leaf-shaped with reinforced proportions that preserve its appearance without creating fragile edges. The spear's butt rests naturally against the base, creating an additional structural anchor. The left arm carries a sturdy kite shield positioned slightly forward in a defensive posture. The shield closely matches the uploaded reference, featuring a wooden construction reinforced by metal edging and a pronounced central boss. Broad panel divisions create excellent painting opportunities while maintaining a robust printable design. The shield is securely attached to the forearm rather than floating independently. A leather belt secures the gambeson at the waist, supporting several practical pouches and a simple utility knife. These accessories remain integrated into the sculpt, adding realism without cluttering the miniature. The trousers are practical and loose-fitting, tucked securely into rugged leather boots suitable for long marches. The boots stand firmly upon the terrain with both feet making complete contact with the base, maximizing stability. The round base depicts a weathered cobblestone street or castle courtyard. Uneven paving stones, shallow cracks, scattered dirt, and sparse patches of dry grass provide subtle environmental storytelling while keeping the Guard as the clear focal point. The terrain remains intentionally low-profile, making the miniature suitable for use in nearly any settlement or fortress encounter. The recommended colour palette follows the uploaded reference. The gambeson is painted in muted crimson or dark red with brown shading and lighter red highlights. The helmet, spearhead, shield rim, and shield boss use worn steel with restrained edge highlights. Leather belts, boots, and pouches work well in dark brown, while the wooden spear shaft and shield face are painted in weathered oak. The shield itself features deep red panels bordered by dark metal, matching the classic town guard appearance. Steadfast at the gate. Watchful through the night. The first line of every kingdom's defense. ✨ Key Features Faithful Guard inspired by the Monster Manual 2024 . Classic defensive pose based on the uploaded reference. Medium humanoid miniature with realistic proportions. Practical quilted gambeson and simple steel helmet. Long spear with reinforced printable shaft and spearhead. Sturdy kite shield featuring a raised central boss. Utility belt with integrated pouches and equipment. Fully grounded stance with excellent tabletop stability. Cobblestone town or castle base suitable for countless settings. No floating parts, magical effects, smoke, aura, or oversized scenery. Strong silhouette immediately recognizable as a professional town guard. Optimized for high-detail resin printing and suitable for carefully tuned FDM printers. 🎨 Great for Painting Prime the miniature in black before applying a deep crimson basecoat to the gambeson. Shade the folds with dark brown washes before layering progressively brighter reds across the raised fabric. Paint the armor using dark steel with black washes and restrained silver edge highlights. The shield looks excellent with weathered red panels framed by gunmetal edging and a polished central boss. Use rich brown tones for the leather boots, belt, and pouches, while the spear shaft benefits from warm oak highlighted with lighter wood grain. The cobblestone base works well in layered cool greys with brown washes between the stones and sparse tufts of dry grass for subtle realism. Finish the terrain with a matte varnish while leaving the armor with a restrained metallic sheen. 📏 Scale & Compatibility Creature Size: Medium Recommended Base: 25 mm round tabletop base Compatible with standard 28 mm, 32 mm, and heroic-scale fantasy tabletop games, city encounters, castle garrisons, military campaigns, and premium miniature collections.

Cable Buddy - Panda Hey everyone, I want to share the latest addition to my CripWorks designs: The Cable Buddies. I was looking for a way to stop my charging cables from bending and breaking at the connector, and I decided to make a cute and functional solution. The concept is simple. The Cable Buddy essentially "bites" onto the end of your cable. This not only protects the weak spot of the cord from wearing out, but it also gives you a much better grip when you are unplugging your devices. It is designed to fit standard USB-C cables comfortably. As you can see from the pictures, the print requires some support material under the belly and inside the mouth area. This is honestly somewhat fiddly to remove - a small flat screwdriver did the trick for me. Just be careful not to break off the teeth. It took quite a while to design and color them. I redesigned the USB cable to make it more suitable for different USB-C cable types. As a workaround for not repainting them after the redesign, I simply added the new cable as a negative → This should not be removed in the slicer. Print Recommendations: Material: PLA or PETG works perfectly fine. PETG is my favorite as it is a little more sturdy. Layer Height: Variable layer height for more details. Infill: 15% Fuzzy Skin: Enabled Supports: Skinny tree This Panda is part of a larger Cable Buddy series I am working on, so keep an eye out for more animals coming soon. I hope you enjoy printing this little guy as much as I enjoyed designing it. Happy printing! description: This BONBON capsule introduces you to the colourful world of Hoardlings , a race of tiny treasure-seeking dragons . Inside is a complete miniature experience , including an easy-to-build kit card , a gold coin , a coin-purse lair , and a full-colour illustrated field guide . Everything fits neatly inside a 2.7" BONBON with plenty of room to add extra coins if desired. Finally, the scroll rounds out the entire package with easy assembly instructions and an inside look into the world of Hoardlings. No BONBON? No problem! Print as much or as little of the Hoardling experience as you want. Ready to Print* Your Own Hoardling? Let's begin! Just a few common sense things to be aware of: Small parts, choking hazard , keep away from babies/pets/cranky adults This is a miniature and not suitable for everyone Clean build plate is a MUST Textured build plate recommended (high tack plates may break cards upon removal) Fit differs between printers and filaments ; always do a test print before gifting or batch printing. Parts can break off prematurely while removing the card from the build plate unless you take a few simple and easy steps first. Use a freshly cleaned textured build plate . Let it cool completely first , then slowly and carefully flex the plate. The card should pop off easily if it hasn't already self-released. Easy peasy, I promise! Troubles? Please see any of my other kit card models for tips and tricks. Why not here? Because I'm working on a universal resource guide so I don't keep repeating myself :) *berri3D makes no guarantees about the law-abiding nature of your new Hoardling friend. Hoardlings can, will, and do (with joyful impunity) steal anything vaguely shiny, valuable, and/or structurally important to modesty/world peace. 📜 Paper Scroll 📜 For best results, download and print the PDF version of the guide ( not the image above). The PDF is a high quality vector file and can be found in the “Documentation” section below ⬇️ Print the guide double-sided on regular-weight paper. Cut out along dotted lines . If this will be put in a BONBON, trim paper close to the border edges so that overall width is ~50 mm (2"). This is to ensure a hassle-free fit inside the capsule. Print the scroll band from the print profile. Roll the field guide into a tight tube then slip the scroll band over to secure. 🪙 Coins 🪙 Coins can be printed in two ways: whole or notched. Coins with notches can be “held” by one or more dragons. Multi-notched coins can be found in the RAW file (click “Download STL/CAD Files”) beneath the Print Profile pane up above. They're either performing a cash summoning ritual or engaged in a 6-way tug-of-war for dominance. 👛 Coin Purse 👛 CREDIT: Although I'm not required to say so, it's only fair that I give a shout-out to one of the tools I used to create the purse. I modelled the base mesh in Fusion (as shown below) and then put it through Bumpmesh (a free, open-source browser-based app) to add the texture. Assembly should be done before placing into the BONBON or giving as a gift . The clasp will be a tight fit and may require using a hard surface to press it in. Once it clips in, it will be quite secure and will hold on its own. However, since it's technically possible to remove it with a bit of determination, a bit of glue is recommended as discouragement. description: Ghoul Lacedon Miniature – Drowned Hunter of the Deep This miniature is part of the Monster Manual 2024 Collection , a series of iconic creatures faithfully reimagined as dynamic, tabletop-ready sculpts. The Ghoul Lacedon is presented as an aquatic undead predator shaped by long exposure to black water, flooded crypts, and lightless coastal depths. It retains the ravenous anatomy of a Ghoul, but its body has become broader, heavier, and more adapted for movement beneath the surface. Webbed claws, fin-like growths, water-swollen flesh, and a low amphibious stance immediately distinguish it from the land-dwelling Ghoul while preserving the same corpse-born hunger. The creature has a powerful, hunched humanoid frame with broad shoulders, a thick upper back, and long arms that nearly reach the ground. Its torso is gaunt around the ribs and abdomen, but the shoulders, forearms, thighs, and calves remain dense with unnatural muscle. This contrast creates the impression of a drowned corpse that has become a specialised underwater hunter rather than a weakened cadaver. The spine curves sharply forward, lowering the head between the shoulders and giving the miniature a compact, predatory silhouette. Its head is large, bald, and distinctly aquatic. A broad mouth opens into a savage snarl, exposing irregular needle-like teeth and prominent fangs suited to tearing flesh. The jaw is heavy and slightly extended, while the lips are peeled back around the teeth. Deep-set eyes sit beneath a pronounced brow, giving the creature a hostile, animalistic expression. The nose is flattened and partially decayed, with wide openings that suggest an amphibious or drowned physiology. The cheeks and neck are deeply ridged, and the sides of the head may feature short fin-like membranes or hardened gill structures. A series of thick, jagged fins runs from the back of the skull along the neck and upper spine. Additional fin ridges appear on the forearms and calves, giving the creature a strong aquatic identity without resembling a fish-person or sea demon. These structures are broad, layered, and firmly connected to the limbs, avoiding thin translucent membranes or fragile spikes. Smaller ridges may continue along the elbows and shoulders, reinforcing the flowing direction of the body. The Ghoul Lacedon is posed in a wide, low crouch as though it has just dragged itself from the water. One foot is planted on a raised section of rock near the front of the base, while the other braces farther behind. Both feet are large and fully webbed, with thick clawed toes gripping the terrain. The torso leans forward, and both arms are extended to either side in an aggressive balancing posture. One claw reaches toward its prey, while the opposite hand is drawn slightly back, ready to strike. The hands are oversized and amphibious, with webbing between the fingers and long hooked claws. The fingers remain thick and partially grouped to ensure dependable printing. The webbed membranes are sculpted as solid, shallow connections rather than delicate sheets. Similar webbing stretches between the toes, giving the feet a broad footprint and increasing the model’s physical contact with the base. Its corpse-like skin has a slick, waterlogged texture. Deep folds gather around the neck, joints, and abdomen, while cracks and tears expose darker tissue beneath. Barnacle-like growths, scarred patches, and hardened nodules may appear across the shoulders and limbs, but these should be large and simplified enough to remain readable after printing. Ragged remains of cloth hang around the waist, soaked against the hips and thighs. The garment consists of broad connected panels with torn edges, avoiding long unsupported strips. The ideal palette combines dark teal, drowned blue-grey, cold green, and desaturated turquoise. The belly, face, palms, and inner limbs may be lighter and more corpse-pale, while the back and fin ridges can be darker. Purple, black-red, and brown shading around wounds and joints enhances the drowned appearance. Teeth and claws provide strong contrast in stained ivory or yellowed bone. The round tabletop base represents a flooded ruin or rocky shoreline. Uneven stone, shallow sculpted water, broken masonry, shells, and a few low aquatic plants surround the creature’s feet. The water remains a textured part of the base rather than a transparent effect, with ripples sculpted directly around the planted limbs. All environmental elements remain low, solid, and physically connected. Born beneath black water. Hunger that never drowned. The deep sends it ashore. ✨ Key Features Distinctive Ghoul Lacedon design based on the Monster Manual 2024 creature. Clearly differentiated from a standard Ghoul through aquatic anatomy and terrain. Broad, hunched silhouette with long arms and powerful swimming limbs. Large predatory head with recessed eyes, flattened nose, and fang-filled jaws. Thick fin-like ridges along the head, neck, spine, forearms, and calves. Webbed hands and feet with durable, integrated membranes. Oversized hooked claws suitable for both climbing and underwater hunting. Low amphibious crouch suggesting emergence from deep water. Both feet firmly planted with broad contact across the round base. Water-swollen corpse skin with scars, folds, wounds, and hardened growths. Ragged soaked garments securely connected to the hips and legs. Strong asymmetrical action pose with both arms spread for balance and attack. Thickened fingers, fins, claws, and joints for reliable miniature printing. Flooded ruin base with stone, ripples, shells, and compact aquatic details. No floating water, bubbles, spray, magical effects, smoke, or unsupported scenery. Designed for high-detail resin printing and achievable on finely tuned FDM printers. Excellent for underwater encounters, flooded crypts, coastal ruins, and undead groups. 🎨 Great for Painting Begin with a dark blue-grey, desaturated teal, or drowned green basecoat. Apply a deep navy, purple-black, or green-brown wash into the recesses around the ribs, joints, face, fins, and skin folds. Rebuild the raised areas with lighter turquoise-grey, pale green, or cold corpse-flesh tones. Use lighter, more desaturated colors across the chest, face, palms, and inner limbs to create a waterlogged appearance. Glaze the shoulders, elbows, knees, and wounds with muted purple, bruised blue, and blackened red. The fin ridges can be painted in darker teal or blue-black, followed by pale edge highlights to define their shape. Paint the mouth interior in dark burgundy or purple-red, with the teeth progressing from dirty beige to aged ivory. The claws can be finished in yellowed bone, dark horn, or pale grey. A small amount of gloss varnish on the skin, mouth, and webbing can create a convincing wet finish. The ragged garment works well in faded brown, black-green, or washed-out maroon. Paint the base in cold stone greys and muted coastal browns. Sculpted water can be layered with dark teal, medium blue-green, and pale blue-grey highlights along the ripples, followed by gloss varnish. Shells and stones offer small accents in beige, off-white, and muted orange-brown. 📏 Scale & Compatibility Creature Size: Medium Recommended Base: 25 mm round tabletop base Compatible with standard 28 mm, 32 mm, and heroic-scale fantasy tabletop games and miniature collections.

description: Ghast Gravecaller Miniature – Herald of the Restless Dead This miniature is part of the Monster Manual 2024 Collection , a series of iconic creatures faithfully reimagined as dynamic, tabletop-ready sculpts . The Ghast Gravecaller is depicted as a more cunning and ritualistic form of undead predator: a corpse-born summoner that does not merely hunt among the graves, but commands the darkness beneath them. Its silhouette combines the gaunt brutality of a Ghast with the visual authority of a necromantic leader, creating a miniature that is immediately distinct from the common Ghast while remaining clearly part of the same undead lineage. The creature has a tall, lean, and heavily emaciated humanoid body with long arms, powerful thighs, and a broad but hollow chest. Its posture is hunched forward, yet more controlled than the feral crouch of an ordinary Ghast. The Gravecaller stands with its legs spread widely across the base, one foot slightly advanced and the other braced behind, giving it a stable ritual stance. The torso twists subtly toward the outstretched arm, creating a strong diagonal line through the body and making the pose feel active without relying on magical effects. Its head is hairless and corpse-like, with a high, angular skull, pointed ears, deeply sunken eyes, and a mouth stretched open in a guttural command. The jaw is filled with irregular teeth and prominent fangs, while the cheeks are gaunt and drawn tightly against the bone. Several long, string-like tendons or decayed strips of flesh hang from the lower jaw and chin, giving the face a grotesque, ceremonial appearance. These strands should be grouped into thick, connected forms rather than sculpted as individual fragile threads. The left hand grips a tall grave-calling staff planted firmly into the base. The shaft is made from dark, weathered wood or bone-bound timber and is reinforced with wrapped cords, metal bands, and crude ritual bindings. At the top sits a large skull framed by smaller bones and curved supports, creating a dramatic focal point. Every decorative element is physically attached to the staff structure, and the lower end connects directly to the ground for added stability. The staff should appear ancient and macabre, but not overly delicate or overloaded with tiny ornaments. The opposite arm reaches forward with the palm open and the fingers curled, as if the Gravecaller is directing nearby undead toward its prey. The hand is oversized and clawed, with long but thickened nails. Its gesture is commanding rather than mindless, separating this creature from the more animalistic Ghast. The arm remains slightly bent at the elbow to reduce overhang and improve printing strength. The Gravecaller wears a collection of decayed ritual garments and scavenged grave ornaments. A torn mantle hangs from one shoulder and falls behind the upper arm in broad, connected folds. Around the waist is a heavy belt decorated with a central skull, bone plates, and several large talismans. Ragged cloth panels descend between and beside the legs, forming a dark ceremonial skirt. The fabric is heavily damaged, with irregular pointed edges, but all hanging pieces connect to one another or to the legs to avoid unsupported sections. Its exposed skin is stretched tightly over the ribs, shoulders, arms, and legs. Scars, open wounds, hardened growths, and areas of rough necrotic tissue cover the body. The chest remains visibly hollow and starved, while the thighs and shoulders retain enough muscle to suggest the unnatural strength of a Ghast. The fingers and toes end in hooked claws, and both feet are planted securely against the base. The color palette is dominated by desaturated green-grey, pale corpse flesh, and bruised blue. Dark purple and blackened red can be used around wounds, eyes, and the mouth. The garments suit faded violet, charcoal, dirty burgundy, or mouldy black, while the bone ornaments provide pale focal points. The staff works well in dark brown wood, aged ivory, tarnished bronze, and old blood tones. The round tabletop base represents a desecrated burial site. Several skulls, large bone fragments, cracked earth, and grave debris are embedded around the creature’s feet. The staff is planted among these remains, visually connecting the Gravecaller to the dead it commands. The terrain stays low and compact, ensuring that the model’s silhouette remains clear and that no scenery becomes fragile or distracting. A voice beneath the soil. A command the dead obey. The grave answers back. ✨ Key Features Distinctive Ghast Gravecaller design based on the Monster Manual 2024 creature. Clearly differentiated from the standard Ghast through ritual gear and commanding posture. Tall, gaunt undead anatomy with long limbs and visible ribs. Wide, stable stance suited to a necromantic battlefield leader. Grotesque head with pointed ears, sunken eyes, fangs, and hanging jaw tendons. Large grave-calling staff planted directly into the base. Staff topped with an integrated skull and securely attached bone decorations. One clawed hand extended in a commanding summoner-like gesture. Heavy ritual belt with skull ornamentation and large bone talismans. Torn shoulder mantle and layered ceremonial cloth panels. All fabric sections attached to the body or neighbouring garments for print safety. Thickened claws, tendons, staff details, and bone elements for dependable printing. Both feet firmly connected to the round base. Desecrated graveyard terrain with skulls, bones, and cracked earth. No floating spirits, magical energy, smoke, aura effects, or separate components. Strong asymmetrical silhouette suitable for encounter leaders and display collections. Designed for resin printing while remaining achievable on finely tuned FDM printers. 🎨 Great for Painting Begin with a muted green-grey, pale blue-grey, or dead flesh basecoat. Shade the recesses with dark purple, black-green, or brown washes, concentrating around the ribs, face, joints, and damaged tissue. Rebuild raised areas with pale grey, ivory, or desaturated green highlights. Add bruising with thin purple, burgundy, and blue glazes around the shoulders, knees, wounds, and mouth. Paint the ritual garments in faded violet, dark burgundy, charcoal, or mouldy brown. Apply a black or dark purple wash, followed by dusty grey or muted lavender edge highlights. Bone ornaments and skulls can be based in dark beige, washed with sepia, and highlighted through bone to pale ivory. For the staff, use dark brown or grey-brown wood with lighter streaks along the grain. Metal bands can be painted in tarnished bronze or blackened iron, with small green or orange corrosion accents. The skull topper should receive stronger highlights than the surrounding bones to make it the visual centre of the miniature. Finish the base with dark soil, grey stones, aged bone, and restrained dead grass tones. Selective gloss inside the mouth, around fresh wounds, or on the eyes can contrast effectively with the matte corpse skin and dusty clothing. 📏 Scale & Compatibility Creature Size: Medium Recommended Base: 25 mm round tabletop base Compatible with standard 28 mm, 32 mm, and heroic-scale fantasy tabletop games and miniature collections.

description: Goblin Boss Miniature – Cunning Tyrant of the Tribe This miniature is part of the Monster Manual 2024 Collection , a series of iconic creatures faithfully reimagined as dynamic, tabletop-ready sculpts. The Goblin Boss is presented as the ruthless leader of a goblin warband: louder, crueler, and far more confident than the warriors that follow it. Unlike a common Goblin Warrior, the Boss relies on intimidation, tactical positioning, and overwhelming numbers. Its commanding pose, superior equipment, and trophy-laden attire immediately distinguish it from lesser goblins while remaining practical for high-quality 3D printing. The Goblin Boss has the compact, wiry proportions characteristic of goblins, standing low to the ground with a broad, balanced stance. Although physically much smaller than most humanoid opponents, the miniature should project confidence through posture rather than size. The torso leans slightly forward while the legs remain spread wide, giving the impression that the Boss is barking orders while remaining ready to spring into combat. Its head is oversized compared to its body, creating the classic goblin silhouette. The face is angular and deeply expressive, with a broad flattened nose, pronounced brow, wrinkled forehead, sharp cheekbones, and a wide mouth filled with crooked yellowed teeth. The lips are curled into an aggressive snarl, exposing several oversized canines. Narrow eyes glare toward an unseen enemy with a mixture of arrogance and malice. The ears are long, broad, and sharply pointed, projecting outward from both sides of the head and giving the miniature an instantly recognizable profile. The Goblin Boss wears noticeably better equipment than ordinary members of its tribe. A reinforced leather cuirass covers the chest, strengthened with overlapping iron plates, rivets, and crude metal edging. One shoulder carries a large scavenged pauldron while the opposite shoulder remains lightly protected, creating an asymmetrical appearance typical of goblin craftsmanship. Numerous leather straps cross the torso, securing pouches, knives, and trophies without becoming overly cluttered. A heavy belt supports layered leather skirt panels that protect the hips and upper thighs. Attached to the belt are a skull trophy, several crude charms, and small pouches for stolen valuables or battlefield supplies. Every accessory remains firmly attached to neighbouring equipment to ensure print durability. The Boss wears a tattered cloak draped from one shoulder. Rather than flowing dramatically, the cloak hangs in broad, thick folds close to the body, with torn lower edges suggesting long campaigns and rough treatment. The cloth connects naturally to the back and legs, preventing fragile unsupported sections. One arm extends fully forward with an accusing finger aimed directly at its next victim. This gesture is the defining feature of the miniature, immediately communicating command, leadership, and ruthless authority. The extended arm remains slightly bent, while the finger itself is thick enough for dependable miniature printing. The opposite hand grips a broad curved falchion or heavy goblin scimitar. The blade is chipped, uneven, and obviously scavenged rather than expertly forged. It has a thick spine, reinforced guard, and compact point, making it both visually intimidating and structurally durable. The weapon hangs low beside the body, ready to swing after the Boss has ordered its followers into battle. Leather bracers reinforce both forearms, while wrapped bindings protect the wrists and lower legs. The feet remain bare, ending in broad splayed toes that grip the uneven ground securely. Every limb remains close enough to the body to maintain excellent structural integrity. The Goblin Boss should appear experienced rather than heroic. Small scars, damaged armour, patched leather, dented metal plates, and repaired straps all reinforce the impression that this creature has survived countless raids through cunning rather than honour. Its equipment should feel stolen, repaired, and reused many times. A fitting colour palette begins with yellow-green or olive skin highlighted toward lighter green across the face, hands, and ears. Leather should range from dark brown to reddish tan, while armour works well in blackened iron, tarnished steel, or aged bronze. The cloak provides an excellent opportunity for dark crimson, faded brown, or charcoal cloth. The skull trophy and scattered bones offer natural pale bone contrast. The round tabletop base represents a rough woodland trail or abandoned campsite. Low rocks, exposed roots, scattered gravel, and sparse patches of moss surround the Boss's feet. The terrain remains compact and unobtrusive, ensuring the commanding pointing gesture and curved blade remain the primary visual focus. Lead through fear. Strike through numbers. Mercy wastes opportunities. ✨ Key Features Distinctive Goblin Boss based on the Monster Manual 2024 design. Instantly recognizable commanding pointing pose. Compact goblin proportions with an aggressive forward stance. Oversized goblin head featuring long pointed ears and snarling expression. Broad curved falchion held low in a practical combat position. Reinforced leather and scavenged metal armour unique among goblin ranks. Large asymmetrical shoulder guard for a stronger silhouette. Tattered shoulder cloak sculpted in thick connected folds. Skull trophy, pouches, and crude ornaments integrated into the belt. Bare goblin feet firmly planted on the round base. Thickened fingers, weapon, ears, and cloak edges for reliable printing. No floating accessories, magical effects, smoke, or background scenery. Compact woodland terrain with stones, roots, and scattered debris. Clearly distinguished from the Goblin Warrior, Minion, and Hexer. Suitable for goblin encounters, tribal leaders, ambushes, and dungeon adventures. Optimized for high-detail resin printing and carefully calibrated FDM printers. 🎨 Great for Painting Start with olive-green or yellow-green skin, applying a brown-green wash into the facial wrinkles, fingers, ears, and muscles. Highlight raised areas using progressively lighter yellow-green and pale olive to emphasize the exaggerated goblin features. Paint the leather armour in varied browns, from dark mahogany to worn tan. Shade deeply around straps and stitching using dark brown washes before edge-highlighting with lighter leather tones. The cloak works especially well in faded crimson, charcoal, or dark brown, with dusty highlights across the raised folds. Use blackened iron or tarnished steel for the armour plates and sword. Apply orange-brown rust sparingly around rivets and damaged edges, followed by restrained silver highlights along the blade and armour corners. Paint the skull trophy in aged bone using sepia washes and ivory highlights. Finish the base with dark earth, grey stones, exposed roots, and muted green moss. A matte finish across skin, leather, and terrain contrasts nicely with satin metallic armour and subtle gloss on the eyes and teeth. 📏 Scale & Compatibility Creature Size: Small Recommended Base: 25 mm round tabletop base Compatible with standard 28 mm, 32 mm, and heroic-scale fantasy tabletop games and miniature collections.

description: Bring shattered crusader fortress architecture to your grimdark sci-fi battlefield with this detailed Black Templars Ruined Citadel Corner terrain piece. This model is designed as a large corner section of a ruined Black Templars stronghold, featuring heavy gothic walls, battle-damaged masonry, elevated upper platforms, arched entrances, prominent crusader iconography and piles of shattered rubble. The piece combines the monumental look of a fortress ruin with a strong battlefield silhouette, creating a dramatic mix of defensive structure, sacred strongpoint and tactical terrain. It works perfectly as cover, line-of-sight blocking terrain, objective scenery or a thematic centerpiece for your tabletop battlefield. With its substantial footprint and layered design, the model is ideal for forming the corner of a larger fortress complex, anchoring a ruined city board or serving as a major focal point in grimdark sci-fi battles. The elevated sections also make it especially useful for adding verticality and tactical positioning to the battlefield. All my models are real test prints, not just digital renders. I always try to find the best balance between print time, level of detail and filament usage, so the terrain looks impressive on the table without becoming unnecessarily difficult or wasteful to print. I also put a lot of effort into optimizing the files, removing print issues and making the models as user-friendly as possible. My goal is to offer terrain that prints cleanly, feels solid, and can be used straight from the printer or painted with simple drybrushing techniques. Designed with FDM printing in mind, the piece is suitable for PLA filament printing and looks great in simple grey material without any color changes. description: Lemure Miniature – The Lowest Soul of the Nine Hells This miniature is part of the Monster Manual 2024 Collection , a series of iconic creatures faithfully reimagined as dynamic, tabletop-ready sculpts. The Lemure is among the most pitiful yet disturbing fiends found in the Nine Hells—a damned soul stripped of identity and reduced to a quivering mass of tortured flesh. The miniature stands on a Medium (25 mm) round tabletop base , though its silhouette is unlike that of any humanoid. Rather than walking upright with confidence, the Lemure appears to be slowly pulling itself upward from a melting mound of its own body. One elongated arm stretches desperately toward an unseen victim while the opposite arm hangs limply at its side, giving the creature a tragic yet unsettling posture. The upper torso rises from a thick pool of malformed flesh that spreads across the base, creating a broad, stable foundation ideal for resin printing. Its anatomy deliberately rejects natural proportions. The body appears to have partially liquefied, with muscles, skin, and bone merging into flowing layers of flesh. The head is little more than a swollen skull wrapped in sagging skin, its enormous gaping mouth frozen in an eternal scream. Empty white eyes stare sightlessly into the distance, while broken teeth jut unevenly from twisted gums. The neck barely exists, swallowed by thick folds of distorted tissue that merge directly into the torso. Across the chest and abdomen, countless tormented faces emerge from the creature's flesh. Some scream silently with open mouths, others grimace in agony, while several seem only partially formed, as though trapped forever beneath the skin. Hands, fingers, and malformed limbs protrude randomly from the mass before disappearing back into it, reinforcing the impression that numerous damned souls have fused into a single infernal body. These grotesque details remain sculpted as thick reliefs rather than fragile protrusions, ensuring excellent printability while preserving the horrific visual complexity. The outstretched left arm provides the model's primary sense of motion. Long, bony fingers reach desperately forward, their stretched tendons and wrinkled skin emphasizing eternal suffering rather than aggression. The opposite arm hangs lower with curled claws, suggesting the creature barely possesses the strength to support itself. Both limbs remain proportionally thick and securely attached to the torso for maximum durability. The lower half dissolves entirely into a broad mound of flowing flesh. Instead of separate legs, thick organic folds spill downward across the base like melting wax. Additional screaming faces, grasping hands, and distorted features emerge throughout this mass, creating visual interest from every viewing angle while simultaneously providing exceptional structural stability. There are no unsupported overhangs or delicate contact points, making the model especially suitable for resin printing. The scenic base represents cracked infernal stone partly consumed by the Lemure's corrupted body. The creature appears almost fused to the ground itself, as if slowly crawling across the blasted surface of the Nine Hells. Small fractured paving stones and subtle ground texture provide visual contrast without distracting from the monstrous figure. Everything remains fully integrated into the base with no loose scenery or fragile details. The recommended paint scheme follows the uploaded reference closely. Pale flesh tones mixed with sickly pinks, bruised purples, and raw crimson washes emphasize the creature's diseased appearance. Recesses between folds benefit from deep violet and red shading, while careful ivory highlights pick out stretched skin and protruding faces. Teeth receive aged bone colors with brown washes, while the ground is painted in dark grey stone with subtle dusty brown highlights. A selective gloss varnish inside mouths and between fleshy folds can add an unsettling organic appearance while preserving the overall matte finish of the miniature. No soul remembers its own name. Only endless agony remains. The first step into eternal damnation. ✨ Key Features Faithfully inspired by Monster Manual 2024 . Closely matches the uploaded reference miniature. Horrific melting humanoid sculpt with flowing infernal anatomy. Large screaming primary face with distorted proportions. Multiple partially formed faces emerging throughout the body. Organic mound replacing traditional legs for exceptional print stability. Outstretched grasping arm creating dramatic tabletop presence. Thick sculpted folds designed for crisp resin printing. Scenic infernal stone base fully integrated with the creature. No floating parts, magical effects, smoke, or unsupported elements. Perfect for infernal encounters, devil armies, Nine Hells campaigns, or complete Monster Manual 2024 collections. 🎨 Great for Painting Prime the miniature in light grey or bone before layering pale flesh tones mixed with desaturated pinks. Apply crimson, burgundy, and violet washes deep into every fold to create the appearance of bruised, tortured tissue. Highlight raised skin with ivory and pale flesh while painting the embedded faces with slightly different flesh variations to make each one distinct. Teeth are best finished with aged bone colors and brown washes. The stone base benefits from layered greys with dusty brown drybrushing, while selective gloss varnish inside the mouths and deepest fleshy recesses enhances the grotesque organic textures. 📏 Scale & Compatibility Creature Size: Medium Recommended Base: 25 mm round tabletop base Compatible with standard 28 mm and 32 mm heroic-scale fantasy tabletop games. Perfect as a low-ranking devil, infernal horror, Nine Hells encounter, fiendish warband member, or essential addition to a complete Monster Manual 2024 miniature collection.

description: Bring natural icy battlefield scenery to your Star Wars: Legion tabletop with this detailed Hoth Frozen Scenery Set. This model set is designed as a collection of frozen rock formations, ice crystal clusters and rugged snow-covered terrain elements inspired by the harsh battlefields of Hoth. The pieces combine jagged crystal shapes, rocky outcrops and compact scenic bases, creating a thematic mix of natural cover, battlefield decoration and atmospheric terrain. They work perfectly as scatter terrain, objective scenery, line-of-sight shaping elements or background detail for frozen sci-fi battlefields. Its varied design makes the set especially useful for building immersive Hoth-themed tables. The larger rock formations can help break up open spaces and create stronger battlefield silhouettes, while the smaller crystal clusters and rocky pieces add detail, atmosphere and tactical variety without overwhelming the table. The set fits naturally into Echo Base surroundings, icy wastelands, frozen outposts or any snow-covered sci-fi battlefield. All my models are real test prints, not just digital renders. I always try to find the best balance between print time, level of detail and filament usage, so the terrain looks impressive on the table without becoming unnecessarily difficult or wasteful to print. I also put a lot of effort into optimizing the files, removing print issues and making the models as user-friendly as possible. My goal is to offer terrain that prints cleanly, feels solid, and can be used straight from the printer or painted with simple drybrushing techniques. Designed with FDM printing in mind, the pieces are suitable for PLA filament printing and look great in simple grey material without any color changes. description: About Models: These models are designed to represent real animals as naturally as possible, with focus on accurate size, shapes, proportions, colors, fine details, and natural movement or pose. Level 3 / Supports: For higher difficulty models, especially Level 3, I recommend using Support Material for PLA. It can make support removal much easier, cleaner, and safer for delicate parts. This is especially helpful when the model has many supports, thin details, legs, antennas, or other fragile areas. Note / Handling: Some models may have very small hinge parts or delicate thin areas, such as legs, antennas, tails, or other small details. description: Kuo-Toa Miniature – Fanatical Deepwater Spear Hunter This miniature is part of the Monster Manual 2024 Collection , a series of iconic creatures faithfully reimagined as dynamic, tabletop-ready sculpts. Dwelling in the darkest lakes, flooded caverns, and forgotten underwater ruins, the Kuo-Toa are unsettling amphibious humanoids whose unwavering religious fanaticism and unpredictable behavior make them some of the Underdark's most memorable inhabitants. This miniature faithfully recreates the classic Kuo-Toa warrior shown in the uploaded reference, depicting a cautious but battle-ready sentry armed with a long spear and prepared to defend its submerged domain. The miniature stands on a Medium (25 mm) round tabletop base in a broad, defensive stance. Both large webbed feet are firmly planted in shallow marshy ground, with bent knees lowering the creature's center of gravity. The pose immediately conveys alertness rather than reckless aggression, suggesting a hunter patiently waiting for prey to venture too close before striking with its spear. The wide footing also provides excellent balance for printing and gameplay. The anatomy remains unmistakably piscine. The torso is lean and muscular without appearing overly heroic, reflecting a creature adapted for swimming and sudden bursts of movement. Long arms end in broad webbed hands capable of gripping weapons securely, while thick digitigrade legs terminate in wide amphibious feet with individually sculpted webbing between the toes. The proportions remain faithful to the Monster Manual depiction, giving the creature an awkward yet surprisingly capable physical presence. The head serves as the miniature's strongest focal point. Large bulging fish-like eyes protrude prominently from either side of the skull, immediately identifying the creature as a Kuo-Toa. The eyes stare forward with an unsettling, almost vacant intensity that perfectly captures the race's strange demeanor. A broad amphibious mouth stretches across the face, filled with rows of small pointed teeth visible between slightly parted lips. Fine gill slits and subtle folds around the jaw reinforce the aquatic anatomy without becoming overly delicate for printing. The creature's skin displays layered amphibious textures that transition naturally across the body. Smooth, damp-looking areas cover the chest and abdomen, while fine scales and rougher textures appear along the shoulders, limbs, back, and head. Slight ridges running across the spine hint at primitive dorsal fins without creating fragile protrusions. These varied textures provide painters with numerous opportunities for shading and highlighting. The Kuo-Toa carries a long double-ended spear held horizontally across its body with both hands. The thick wooden shaft is wrapped with coarse rope bindings near each grip, while both spearheads feature rugged forged metal points appropriate for a tribal civilization. The weapon remains close to the torso, ensuring excellent structural integrity while reinforcing the miniature's defensive posture. Its clothing remains simple and functional. A rough leather harness crosses the shoulders, supporting a short weathered cloak draped across the upper back. Around the waist hangs a layered cloth loincloth secured with braided rope, accompanied by small leather pouches suitable for carrying fishing tools, charms, or ritual objects. Rope wrappings around the wrists and ankles further emphasize the primitive craftsmanship associated with Kuo-Toa society. Every accessory remains securely attached to the figure, avoiding thin unsupported elements while maintaining visual authenticity. The scenic base follows the uploaded reference closely. Uneven rocky terrain surrounds a shallow pool of stagnant water beneath the creature's feet, suggesting the muddy shoreline of an underground lake or flooded cavern. Small stones emerge through patches of damp earth, while subtle puddles reinforce the amphibious environment without overwhelming the composition. The base remains clean and compact, complementing rather than distracting from the miniature itself. The recommended paint scheme reflects the classic coloration shown in the reference. The skin begins with muted blue-green tones, shaded with dark teal washes before gradually transitioning toward lighter turquoise highlights across the raised muscles and facial features. The underside of the jaw, abdomen, and palms may receive slightly lighter desaturated green or grey-blue tones to create natural contrast. The enormous eyes become instant focal points when painted with rich amber or golden-orange irises surrounding glossy black pupils. Teeth are painted in aged ivory with subtle sepia shading, while the spear combines weathered brown wood with dark iron spearheads. Leather equipment uses worn reddish-brown tones, and the damp base benefits from earthy browns, dark greys, green algae effects, and gloss varnish applied selectively to the water surface for a convincing wet appearance. Silent beneath black waters. Faith guides every spear. The depths are always watching. ✨ Key Features Faithful Kuo-Toa based on Monster Manual 2024 . Closely matches the uploaded reference miniature. Classic fish-like humanoid anatomy with amphibious proportions. Large bulging eyes and distinctive aquatic facial features. Defensive two-handed spear pose with strong silhouette. Detailed scaled skin and organic amphibious textures. Primitive leather clothing and rope accessories. Marsh-themed scenic base with shallow water effects. No floating parts, magical effects, or fragile unsupported details. Excellent addition to Underdark encounters and aquatic monster collections. 🎨 Great for Painting Prime the miniature in black before layering muted blue-green across the skin. Apply dark teal washes into the recesses before highlighting raised scales with lighter turquoise and pale green edge highlights. Use subtle satin varnish to create a naturally damp appearance. Paint the eyes with bright amber or orange surrounded by glossy black pupils for an unsettling expression. The leather harness and loincloth benefit from layered reddish-brown tones with light weathering, while the spear shaft can be painted weathered wood with dark iron spearheads. Finish the base using layered mud browns, cold grey rocks, green algae washes, and selective gloss varnish to create convincing shallow swamp water. 📏 Scale & Compatibility Creature Size: Medium Recommended Base: 25 mm round tabletop base Compatible with standard 28 mm, 32 mm, and heroic-scale fantasy tabletop games, particularly Underdark adventures, flooded caverns, subterranean lakes, aquatic encounters, and complete Monster Manual 2024 miniature collections.

description: Description: Bring your tabletop adventures to life with this Classic L-shaped Townhouse. Whether your party is exploring a bustling fantasy city, sneaking through a medieval village, or setting up an ambush in a historical wargame, this highly detailed terrain piece is the perfect addition to your table. Featuring realistic stone masonry, classic paned windows, and a beautifully textured shingle roof, this model takes paint exceptionally well – especially drybrushing techniques, allowing you to easily achieve a weathered, realistic look. Tabletop Ready: Scaled perfectly for standard 28mm and 32mm miniature games such as Dungeons & Dragons, Pathfinder, and Frostgrave. Dimensions: Length: 21 cm Width: 20 cm Height: 12 cm Printing Recommendations: Filament: Standard PLA works perfectly for tabletop terrain. Layer Height: 0.16mm will give you a good detail on the roof tiles and stone walls. Infill: 5-10% is sufficent for strenght. Supports: Designed to print easily, but will require tree supports for the steepest overhangs. Brim: Recommended if you have adhesion issues, to ensure the base stays flat during the print. Apply a drybrush of light gray over the stone walls, and a warm brown on the roof, door, and window frames to make the details pop.

description: Lich Miniature – Undying Master of Forbidden Magic This miniature is part of the Monster Manual 2024 Collection , a series of iconic creatures faithfully reimagined as dynamic, tabletop-ready sculpts. The Lich stands among the most feared spellcasters in all of fantasy—a skeletal archmage who willingly embraced undeath to achieve eternal mastery of arcane power. The miniature stands upon a Medium (25 mm) round tabletop base , where the flowing robes occupy much of the footprint while leaving the model perfectly balanced. Unlike dynamic melee creatures, the Lich stands with calm confidence, radiating complete control. The pose is static yet commanding, emphasizing centuries of accumulated knowledge rather than physical strength. The skeletal body is tall and unnaturally thin. Bare ribs and vertebrae remain visible beneath the open robes, while elongated bony arms stretch confidently outward. The exposed skeleton is anatomically clean and sharply sculpted, with every rib, finger bone, and joint clearly defined without becoming overly fragile. The feet emerge from beneath the robes as exposed skeletal bones planted firmly upon cracked stone flooring. The skull serves as the unmistakable focal point of the miniature. Empty eye sockets glow with unnatural magical power, while the permanent skeletal grin creates an expression that is simultaneously calm and terrifying. Long strands of ancient black hair still cling to the skull, hanging behind the shoulders in weathered locks that hint at the Lich's once-living appearance. Resting upon the brow is an elegant crown of dark metal adorned with sharp golden points, symbolizing forgotten kingdoms and immortal authority. Flowing around the skeletal body are magnificent layered robes that create the majority of the miniature's silhouette. Thick overlapping folds sweep naturally toward the base, producing dramatic movement without relying on unsupported fabric. The outer robes feature ancient embroidered borders and ornate trim inspired by long-lost arcane empires, while the inner garments remain darker and heavier to create visual depth. Small tears and worn edges reveal centuries of decay without compromising structural integrity. Across the chest hangs a collection of ancient necklaces, talismans, and arcane ornaments. Suspended from the waist are elaborate ceremonial decorations featuring sculpted skulls, infernal masks, carved bone icons, and hanging charms that remain thick enough for dependable printing. These decorative elements reinforce the Lich's role as an immortal master of necromancy without creating delicate unsupported pieces. The left arm extends outward with claw-like skeletal fingers partially curled as though directing unseen magical servants or issuing a silent command. Rather than depicting visible spell effects, the pose alone communicates overwhelming magical authority while keeping the model completely free of floating magical energy, smoke, or visual effects. In the opposite hand the Lich firmly grips an ancient wizard's staff that reaches from the base nearly to the height of the skull. The twisted wooden shaft appears weathered by centuries of use, while its upper section is crowned by a polished humanoid skull that serves as both arcane focus and symbol of mastery over death. The staff remains fully connected to the base through the Lich's hand, ensuring excellent stability during printing. The scenic base depicts cracked stone flooring from a forgotten crypt or ruined throne room. Scattered skulls, broken bones, loose flagstones, and fragments of ancient masonry surround the Lich's feet, subtly reinforcing the atmosphere without distracting from the central figure. Every scenic element is sculpted directly into the base to maximize durability. The recommended paint scheme follows the uploaded reference closely. The skeletal anatomy should be painted with aged bone colors shaded using sepia and brown washes before being highlighted with warm ivory. The robes combine deep black, charcoal, dark violet, and rich burgundy layered together with subtle edge highlights. Ornamental trim, the crown, and jewelry should be painted using antique gold with selective weathering. The staff is best rendered in aged wood with bone-colored highlights on the skull, while the stone base benefits from layered greys and dusty brown pigments to create the feeling of an ancient tomb. Death became a doorway. Knowledge became eternity. The king of undeath still waits. ✨ Key Features Faithfully inspired by Monster Manual 2024 . Closely matches the uploaded reference miniature. Regal skeletal archmage with commanding upright pose. Exposed ribcage, skeletal hands, and ancient skull with flowing black hair. Elegant crown emphasizing immortal authority. Layered ceremonial robes with rich sculpted folds. Ancient necromantic jewelry, skull ornaments, and arcane decorations. Twisted wizard's staff crowned with a sculpted skull. Scenic crypt base with broken stonework and scattered skulls. No floating magic, smoke, or unsupported spell effects. Ideal centerpiece villain for undead armies, ancient tombs, legendary campaigns, and complete Monster Manual 2024 collections. 🎨 Great for Painting Prime the miniature in black before painting the skeleton with layered bone colors shaded using sepia and dark brown washes. Highlight the skull and ribs using warm ivory to emphasize the sculpted anatomy. Paint the robes with rich blacks, charcoal greys, deep purples, and burgundy highlights to create luxurious yet ancient fabrics. Use antique gold for the crown, jewelry, embroidered trim, and ceremonial ornaments. Finish the staff with weathered wood tones and the crypt floor with layered stone greys, dusty browns, and scattered bone-colored skulls for a suitably ancient atmosphere. 📏 Scale & Compatibility Creature Size: Medium Recommended Base: 25 mm round tabletop base Compatible with standard 28 mm and 32 mm heroic-scale fantasy tabletop games. Perfect as a final campaign villain, undead overlord, master necromancer, legendary dungeon boss, or centerpiece for complete Monster Manual 2024 miniature collections.

description: Hobgoblin Captain Miniature – Iron Commander of the Crimson Legion This miniature is part of the Monster Manual 2024 Collection , a series of iconic creatures faithfully reimagined as dynamic, tabletop-ready sculpts. The Hobgoblin Captain is a veteran battlefield commander whose authority is earned through discipline, tactical brilliance, and personal martial prowess. Unlike ordinary Hobgoblin soldiers, a Captain leads from the front, directing formations while fighting alongside their troops. The Monster Manual 2024 depicts Hobgoblins as highly organized military societies, and this miniature faithfully reflects that philosophy. Based closely on the uploaded reference, the model presents a commanding officer issuing orders while remaining fully prepared to engage the enemy. The Hobgoblin Captain stands upon a Medium (25 mm) round tabletop base in a confident command stance. His feet are planted wide apart across rocky ground, creating an exceptionally stable posture that communicates complete battlefield control. Rather than rushing into combat, he has paused at the critical moment to direct his troops, embodying leadership through action rather than spectacle. His physique is broader and more muscular than that of a standard Hobgoblin Warrior. Thick shoulders, a powerful chest, and strong forearms suggest years of campaigning while maintaining realistic proportions suitable for a disciplined military officer. The head follows the uploaded reference closely. The skin is a warm bronze-brown with subtle olive undertones characteristic of Hobgoblins in the Monster Manual 2024. A deeply furrowed brow, sharp cheekbones, and pronounced jawline give the face a hardened, uncompromising expression. His eyes remain intensely focused on the battlefield ahead, conveying tactical calculation rather than uncontrolled fury. Long pointed ears project outward from the sides of the head while remaining thick enough for reliable printing. His dark hair is gathered into a tightly bound warrior's topknot positioned high on the crown, reinforcing the clean military appearance expected of a commanding officer. The torso is enclosed within heavy layered plate armor worn over chainmail. Large angular pauldrons protect the shoulders while a reinforced breastplate dominates the chest with broad overlapping steel plates. The armor features restrained rivets and practical construction instead of elaborate ornamentation, emphasizing the Hobgoblin philosophy of military efficiency. A deep crimson officer's tabard hangs from beneath the breastplate, extending to mid-thigh in broad layered folds. The cloth provides a striking visual contrast against the dark steel armor while clearly distinguishing the Captain from ordinary soldiers. Behind him, a heavy crimson cloak flows naturally from the shoulders, draping behind the legs in broad supported folds. The cloak remains connected to both the shoulders and lower body to ensure durability without sacrificing movement. The Captain's left arm extends dramatically forward with the index finger pointing directly toward the enemy. This commanding gesture defines the entire miniature. Rather than appearing delicate, the fingers remain slightly thickened and naturally supported by the forearm's angle, ensuring excellent printability while preserving the unmistakable impression of issuing battlefield orders. His right hand firmly grips a practical longsword held low beside the body. The blade is broad, straight, and reinforced with a thick spine, ideal for tabletop durability. The sword hangs in a ready position rather than an exaggerated attack pose, reinforcing the Captain's role as a leader who fights only when necessary. At his waist hangs a second sheathed weapon secured by broad leather belts crossing the hips. Multiple pouches, buckles, and utility straps provide additional military realism while remaining closely integrated into the armor. Layered chainmail skirts emerge beneath the plate armor around the hips before transitioning into heavily armored greaves protecting the legs. Thick leather boots stand securely upon uneven rocky terrain, with both feet making full contact with the base. The round base depicts a rugged battlefield strewn with loose stones, compact earth, and scattered debris. A damaged crimson shield bearing the Hobgoblin legion's insignia lies discarded near the Captain's feet, exactly as shown in the uploaded reference. This broken shield subtly reinforces the ongoing battle while remaining fully integrated into the terrain without creating fragile elements. The recommended colour palette closely follows the uploaded miniature. The skin is painted warm bronze-brown with olive shading and lighter flesh highlights across the face and hands. The armor uses dark weathered steel shaded with black washes before receiving restrained silver edge highlights. The tabard and cloak are painted rich crimson fading into deep burgundy shadows. Leather belts and boots use dark walnut tones with lighter brown highlights. The discarded shield matches the tabard with a dark crimson face and black legion emblem. The rocky terrain combines muted earth browns, weathered greys, and sparse dry grass. Advance. Hold the line. Victory belongs to the disciplined. ✨ Key Features Faithful Hobgoblin Captain inspired by the Monster Manual 2024 . Closely based on the uploaded reference miniature. Dynamic command pose with extended pointing arm. Broad military plate armor over richly textured chainmail. Stern veteran facial expression with traditional warrior's topknot. Heavy crimson officer's cloak and tabard. Practical longsword held in disciplined ready position. Additional sheathed weapon and integrated military equipment. Wide stable stance emphasizing battlefield authority. Battlefield base featuring discarded legion shield, stones, and rubble. No floating parts, magical effects, smoke, aura, or detached scenery. Strong readable silhouette immediately recognizable as a commanding officer. Optimized for high-detail resin printing and suitable for carefully tuned FDM printers. 🎨 Great for Painting Prime the miniature in black before applying a warm bronze-brown basecoat to the skin. Shade the facial features with olive-brown washes before layering lighter flesh tones across the brow, nose, cheeks, and hands. Paint the armor using dark gunmetal followed by black washes to deepen every plate junction. Highlight the edges using restrained silver to create a battle-worn but well-maintained appearance. Chainmail benefits from controlled steel drybrushing to emphasize its texture. The crimson tabard and cloak should be layered from dark burgundy into rich red highlights along the folds and edges. Leather belts, boots, and scabbards work well in dark walnut highlighted with warm tan. Paint the discarded shield to match the Captain's colors, weathering its edges with scratches and exposed steel. Finish the rocky battlefield base using layered earth browns and cool greys with sparse tufts of dry grass. Apply a matte varnish to the cloth and terrain while allowing the armor and sword to retain a restrained metallic sheen befitting an experienced legion commander. 📏 Scale & Compatibility Creature Size: Medium Recommended Base: 25 mm round tabletop base Compatible with standard 28 mm, 32 mm, and heroic-scale fantasy tabletop games, military campaigns, organized Hobgoblin warbands, fortress assaults, and premium miniature collections.
