description: Lizardfolk Geomancer Miniature – Tribal Master of Stone and Earth This miniature is part of the Monster Manual 2024 Collection , a series of iconic creatures faithfully reimagined as dynamic, tabletop-ready sculpts. The Lizardfolk Geomancer represents one of the tribe's ancient spiritual leaders, channeling the enduring strength of stone and the deep power of the earth rather than raw physical dominance alone. The miniature stands on a Medium (25 mm) round tabletop base in a commanding, balanced pose. One clawed foot is planted slightly ahead of the other, creating the impression that the geomancer is advancing while simultaneously calling upon the ground beneath its enemies. The torso twists slightly toward the viewer as one muscular arm reaches forward with an open claw, while the opposite hand grips a towering ritual staff planted firmly beside the body. This asymmetrical composition creates an expressive silhouette without sacrificing structural stability. The Lizardfolk possesses the powerful anatomy typical of its kind. Thick reptilian legs, broad shoulders, muscular forearms, and a heavily scaled torso emphasize both strength and resilience. Large overlapping scales cover the limbs and tail, while the chest and abdomen transition into smaller armored belly plates. A thick tail curls naturally behind the legs before resting against the ground, providing both anatomical realism and an additional point of support for the printed model. Its head displays the unmistakable features of an experienced reptilian shaman. A broad crocodilian snout reveals rows of sharp teeth arranged in a confident, almost predatory grin. Narrow reptilian eyes suggest intelligence rather than savagery, while short cranial spines and ridged scales continue across the top of the skull and down the neck. The expression conveys calm authority, as though the geomancer commands the battlefield through patience rather than fury. Unlike the heavily armored Lizardfolk Soldier, the Geomancer wears ceremonial tribal armor suited to a respected elder. Layered shoulder guards carved from wood and reinforced with bronze fittings rest over leather harnesses crossing the chest. Numerous carved skulls, primitive talismans, beads, and bone ornaments decorate the armor, reflecting years of spiritual leadership and ritual significance. Wide leather bracers wrap around both forearms, while engraved hanging cloth panels descend from an ornate belt decorated with carved masks and tribal motifs. Every decorative element remains thick, interconnected, and securely attached to the body for excellent printability. The focal point of the miniature is its imposing ritual staff. Crafted from a thick wooden shaft wrapped with leather bindings, the weapon terminates in a massive cluster of rough-hewn stone crystals secured within primitive bindings. Rather than appearing magical through floating rocks or visual effects, the power is implied entirely through the sculpt itself. The staff stands planted firmly upon the base, providing another strong structural anchor while reinforcing the geomancer's commanding posture. The extended left hand reaches toward unseen enemies with spread claws, suggesting the casting of earth-shaping magic. Because no magical energy, floating stones, or spell effects are included, the model remains fully compatible with practical resin printing while still conveying dynamic action through pose alone. The scenic base depicts cracked earth scattered with broken stones, weathered skulls, fractured rock formations, and sparse desert vegetation. Beside the staff lies a partially collapsed stone shrine with primitive offerings, subtly reinforcing the geomancer's connection to ancient earth spirits. Every scenic component is sculpted directly into the base to maximize strength and eliminate fragile separate pieces. The recommended paint scheme closely follows the uploaded reference. Olive-green scales shaded with darker moss tones contrast beautifully against pale tan belly scales. Wooden armor receives warm brown tones highlighted with lighter drybrushing, while bronze fittings gain depth through verdigris or dark washes. Bone ornaments are painted with aged ivory and sepia shading. The ritual staff combines rich wood grain with layered grey stone, while the base uses dusty browns, muted rocks, scattered bones, and touches of dry vegetation to complete the rugged wilderness appearance. The earth remembers every step. Stone answers only the patient. The oldest wisdom lies beneath your feet. ✨ Key Features Faithfully inspired by Monster Manual 2024 . Closely matches the uploaded reference miniature. Powerful reptilian geomancer with commanding ritual pose. Muscular lizardfolk anatomy with highly detailed overlapping scales. Extended spellcasting hand without fragile magical effects. Massive earth-themed ritual staff topped with bound stone crystals. Ceremonial tribal armor featuring carved wood, bronze fittings, skulls, and bone ornaments. Ground-supported tail providing additional structural stability. Scenic wilderness base with rocks, skulls, primitive shrine, and scattered debris. No floating elements, smoke, spell effects, or unsupported components. Perfect for wilderness encounters, tribal shamans, earth priests, reptilian civilizations, and complete Monster Manual 2024 collections. 🎨 Great for Painting Prime the miniature in black before layering olive greens and moss tones across the scales, gradually highlighting raised edges with lighter yellow-green. Paint the belly scales using warm tan and bone colors shaded with brown washes. The ceremonial armor benefits from rich leather browns, weathered wood tones, and bronze metallic accents. Bone ornaments are best painted with ivory, sepia washes, and cream highlights. The ritual staff combines textured wood grain with layered grey stone drybrushing, while the scenic base uses dusty earth, weathered rocks, scattered skulls, and muted vegetation to emphasize the geomancer's connection to the land. 📏 Scale & Compatibility Creature Size: Medium Recommended Base: 25 mm round tabletop base Compatible with standard 28 mm and 32 mm heroic-scale fantasy tabletop games. Ideal as a tribal shaman, wilderness spellcaster, reptilian elder, earth priest, encounter leader, or centerpiece for Lizardfolk-themed adventures within a complete Monster Manual 2024 miniature collection.

description: Winged Kobold Miniature – Dragonkin Aerial Ambusher This miniature is part of the Monster Manual 2024 Collection , a series of iconic creatures faithfully reimagined as dynamic, tabletop-ready sculpts. While ordinary kobolds rely on numbers and cunning traps, Winged Kobolds add an entirely new dimension to the battlefield. Blessed—or perhaps cursed—with leathery draconic wings, they dive from cavern ceilings, ruined towers, and dragon lairs to harass intruders from above before disappearing into darkness. This miniature faithfully follows the uploaded reference, portraying a Winged Kobold poised in a low, aggressive stance with its wings fully extended, spear in hand, ready to launch into combat. The miniature stands on a Small (25 mm) round tabletop base in a broad, crouched pose that immediately communicates speed and agility. Both clawed feet are firmly planted among scattered rocks, with deeply bent knees and a low center of gravity that suggests the creature has only just landed—or is moments away from taking flight. The pose creates an energetic silhouette while maintaining excellent structural integrity for printing. Its anatomy follows the classic draconic proportions of a kobold. The body is compact, lean, and wiry, built for speed rather than brute strength. Long forearms, digitigrade legs, and a flexible tail emphasize the creature's reptilian heritage. The tail emerges naturally from the lower back and curves around the rear of the base in a wide arc, remaining close to the ground to provide additional visual balance without creating unsupported overhangs. The head is unmistakably draconic, featuring an elongated snout filled with sharp triangular teeth displayed in an open snarl. Narrow reptilian eyes glare fiercely beneath ridged brows, while large pointed ears angle backward alongside small horn-like protrusions that rise from the crown. The facial expression conveys equal parts confidence, aggression, and mischievous cunning, perfectly fitting the unpredictable personality of Winged Kobolds. The creature's defining feature is its pair of fully extended dragon-like wings. Rather than feathered wings, these are leathery membranes stretched between sturdy finger bones, closely resembling those of small dragons. Each wing connects naturally to the shoulders with thick musculature before extending outward in a broad, symmetrical display. The membranes feature subtle wrinkles, stretched textures, and reinforced wing fingers that create dramatic visual appeal while remaining thick enough for dependable resin printing. Their wide span gives the miniature an instantly recognizable aerial silhouette without becoming excessively fragile. The right hand grips a crude short spear held low beside the body, ready for quick thrusting attacks during aerial dives or skirmishes. The spear has a thick wooden shaft bound with rope and fitted with a rugged forged metal spearhead that reflects improvised kobold craftsmanship. The left hand remains open with extended claws, reaching toward an approaching enemy as though preparing to grab hold or maintain balance during flight. The Winged Kobold wears only minimal equipment appropriate for its lightweight role. A simple stitched leather chest harness provides modest protection without restricting wing movement. Rough cloth wrappings cover the forearms and portions of the legs, while a worn loincloth hangs from a rope belt. A small pouch attached at the hip hints at tools, sling stones, or scavenged valuables collected during raids. Every accessory is kept compact and securely attached to avoid fragile components while reinforcing the creature's practical survivalist nature. The scales covering the body vary naturally in size. Larger armored plates protect the chest and shoulders, while smaller textured scales wrap around the limbs, neck, and tail. The leathery wings contrast beautifully with the harder scales, providing painters with multiple textures to explore. Thick clawed fingers and powerful talons complete the anatomy, reinforcing the Kobold's ability to climb cave walls and cling to rocky ledges. The scenic base closely follows the uploaded reference. Jagged stones and uneven rocky terrain suggest a dragon's cavern, mountain cliff, or ancient ruin. One larger rock formation beneath the extended wings helps visually anchor the model while maintaining a clean, uncluttered composition. Every scenic element remains integrated into the base, ensuring durability and easy tabletop use. The recommended paint scheme reflects the reference miniature. The scales are painted in rich reddish-brown tones with darker mahogany washes between the scales before warm orange highlights define the raised surfaces. The wing membranes transition toward darker brown with reddish undertones and lighter edge highlights to emphasize their leathery texture. Bone-colored horns, claws, and teeth provide natural contrast, while the leather harness uses muted browns and dusty tan cloth. The spear combines weathered wood with aged steel, and the eyes glow bright amber or yellow to give the miniature an alert, predatory appearance. Small wings. Fearless heart. Every shadow hides another dive. ✨ Key Features Faithful Winged Kobold based on the Monster Manual 2024 . Closely matches the uploaded reference miniature. Classic dragonkin anatomy with compact agile proportions. Large fully extended leathery dragon wings. Dynamic crouched landing pose with strong visual movement. Fierce draconic head with snarling expression. Short spear designed for aerial skirmishing. Lightweight leather harness and simple adventuring gear. Curved tail positioned for stability and print reliability. Rocky dragon-lair themed scenic base. No floating parts, magical effects, smoke, or unsupported scenery. 🎨 Great for Painting Prime the miniature in black before applying warm reddish-brown base coats across the scales. Use deep brown washes to define the individual scales and highlight them with lighter orange-brown edge highlights. Paint the wing membranes in dark reddish-brown with thin lighter highlights stretched across the membranes to emphasize their natural texture. Use bone or ivory tones for the horns, claws, and teeth, while the leather harness and wrappings benefit from layered browns with subtle weathering. The spear shaft can be painted weathered wood with metallic steel for the spearhead. Finish the eyes in vivid amber or glowing yellow to create a striking focal point. The rocky base works beautifully with layered stone greys, earth pigments, and sparse dry grass tufts, creating the atmosphere of a rugged cavern or mountain dragon's domain. 📏 Scale & Compatibility Creature Size: Small Recommended Base: 25 mm round tabletop base Compatible with standard 28 mm, 32 mm, and heroic-scale fantasy tabletop games, dragon lairs, mountain encounters, subterranean adventures, kobold warbands, and Monster Manual 2024 miniature collections.

The Peacock Bass is not a peacock or a bass. It's actually the largest member of the cichlid family, not related to largemouth or smallmouth bass at all. It gets its name from the eye-like circle on it's tail that, like the markings on peacock feathers are used to deter predators. This vibrant fish is native to the Amazon and Orinoco river basins but has been transplanted to other tropical environments like southeast Asia and Florida. They are sought after by anglers for their violent fights, they have a reputation for damaging or destroying fishing equipment when they strike. These fish can reach up to about 1 m (3.3 ft) and weigh 13 kg (29 lbs). During the rainy season, males will develop a large fatty pump on their foreheads. The fish comes in a variety of subspecies, each with their unique patterns. The print profile I've uploaded includes 3 different color variations (same model, just different painting); spotted PB, Butterfly PB, and a blank for you to paint your own pattern on either in BambuStudio or with acrylics after printing. Like my other fish models, this Peacock bass uses interlocking scale units to swim. After printing, the two halves can be aligned with the registration pin and glued together by their head, tail, and perimeter scales. Happy printing (and fishing)!!

description: Make your own text stamp for clay, soap, leather, play dough, fondant, and normal ink-pad stamping. Up to three lines of custom text, round or rectangular head, emboss or deboss, optional border, and a comfortable twist-lock handle. Prints support-free. Type your text and print a personal stamp. The rigid PETG/PLA version presses crisp, readable impressions into polymer clay, air-dry clay, soap, soft leather, play dough, fondant, and similar soft materials. For normal ink-pad stamping, a tested option is to split the stamp face in the slicer and print the actual raised letters/rim in TPU, with the base and handle in PETG, so the letters flex slightly like a softer stamp face. Features: - Up to three lines of text, automatically centered. - Mirrored text by default, so the stamped impression reads correctly. Turn mirroring off to print a readable display plaque instead. - Two impression styles: "raised" presses your text INTO the material (debossed impression), "recessed" leaves your text standing proud (embossed impression). - Round or rectangular head with adjustable size and optional border ring - the border stamps a clean frame around your text. - Adjustable text depth (0.8-3 mm) for shallow or deep impressions. - Comfortable mushroom handle with a bayonet twist-lock: insert into the head back and twist clockwise to a firm stop. The locked handle cannot pull off, even when lifting the stamp out of sticky clay. Print one handle and many heads: name stamps, date stamps, logo text, gift tags. - Tested TPU-face workflow: print the raised letters/rim in TPU and the base + handle in PETG for a softer face that also works better as a normal ink-pad stamp. - Console warning if your text is too wide for the chosen head size. - Both parts print flat with no supports. The model checks your text width against the head size and prints a note in the customizer console if a line will not fit. Note: rigid PLA/PETG stamp faces are best for clay, soap, leather, dough, and other soft materials. For normal ink-pad stamping on paper, the tested TPU-face workflow gives a more forgiving contact surface than a hard FDM face. Results still depend on ink pad, paper, layer height, and surface finish, so test first. Custom Fonts: You can use any font MakerWorld has installed , type it into font_name as "Family:style=Style". Examples: Liberation Sans:style=Bold (default) Liberation Serif:style=Bold (bookplate look) Liberation Mono:style=Bold (typewriter) Liberation Sans Narrow:style=Bold (fits longer text) DejaVu Sans:style=Bold DejaVu Serif:style=Bold Stick to Bold styles thin strokes don't stamp well and can be fragile. Customization Notes - line_1 / line_2 / line_3: your text; leave lines empty to use fewer lines. - font_name: keep the default Liberation Sans Bold for reliable width warnings; other bold fonts work, but check the preview. - mirror_text: leave ON for stamping. Turn off only for display plaques. - text_style: "raised" = pressed-in (debossed) impression, "recessed" = raised (embossed) impression. - text_depth: 1.5 mm default; use 2-3 mm for soft doughs, 1-1.5 mm for firm clay and leather. - head_shape / head_diameter / head_width / head_height: face size. Bigger faces fit longer text. - border_enabled / border_width / border_inset: frame ring around the text. - border_depth: rim height, independent of text_depth. Match text_depth for a classic one-level stamp, or make the rim taller than the text so it contains the material and controls impression depth like a cookie-cutter frame - useful for wax-seal-style stamps and uniform clay medallions. - fit_clearance: twist-lock clearance. Increase by 0.05-0.1 if the handle is hard to insert or twist; decrease toward 0.05 for a tighter lock. - part: "all" prints both pieces; "head" alone for extra stamp faces for a handle you already printed; "fit_preview" is preview-only - do not print. description: Windproof Heavy Duty Sand Pegs Stakes with 19mm HEX Designed For Extreme Beach Camping Stop watching your tent fly away in coastal gales. Built out of pure necessity, these heavy-duty screw-in sand pegs were designed to withstand the brutal realities of off-grid wild beach camping. When you are exposed to relentless 70–80 km/h winds , standard tent stakes just won't cut it. These aggressive, deep-threaded spiral anchors bite hard into loose ground to keep your shelter, tarp, or beach umbrella firmly rooted. Smart, Optimized 3D Print Design As a maker and avid camper, I designed these pegs from scratch to solve two major problems: weak ground holding and wasteful printing. The geometry has been carefully tuned for the 3D printing process: Zero Supports: Engineered to print completely support-free, saving post-processing time. Fast & Efficient: Optimized design drastically cuts down on print time and filament waste without sacrificing structural integrity or toughness. 3 Included Models & Sizes To ensure you have the perfect anchor for any beach topography, the package includes 3 distinct variations: 1x Medium Size: Great for compact packing, firmer damp sand, and standard setups. 1x XL Standard: Extended length for deep penetration into shifting, loose sand to provide massive pull resistance. 1x XL Wide-Thread: Features a significantly wider screw thread configuration. This is engineered specifically for extra strength and maximum surface area bite if you are dealing with ultra-fine, super dry, or powdery sand. 1x XXL Ultra Wide-Thread (19mm Hex): A beefed-up, heavy-duty version featuring our widest thread yet and a robust 19mm hex head for maximum torque and strength. (Note: Untested, feedback welcome!) Print Settings & Material Recommendations ⚠️ For Best Results: Print with high infill (minimum 40-50%) and at least 4-5 perimeters/walls to ensure maximum torsional strength when screwing them into the ground. ASA (Highly Recommended): If your stakes are going to sit in the blistering direct sun all day, ASA is the top choice . It offers excellent UV resistance and high thermal stability, ensuring the pegs won't soften, warp, or deform under intense beach heat. PETG (Budget/Alternative Option): PETG works perfectly fine with a simple trick! If you use PETG, dig a hole in the sand until you reach the damp, harder layer, screw the pegs in there, and then bury them back up with sand. As long as they are buried away from direct sunlight, PETG will stay cool enough to maintain its strength and hold your gear secure. Pro-Tip for Maximum Hold in Loose Sand: To get the absolute best anchorage on windy beaches, don't just screw them into the dry, powdery top layer. Dig a small hole until you reach the dense, wet sand underneath. Screw the anchor directly into that wet layer so the wide threads can lock into the compacted sand. If the sand is completely dry or you can't dig deep enough, pour a bottle of sea water over the area after screwing it in to tighten and pack the sand around the threads. Fill the hole back up and stomp it down! Update: New Model Added! (4. description: After trying several printable designs, I found that many weren't durable enough for repeated use, and the sharp edges around the wire guides created unnecessary friction when pulling longer cables. Features Fast print (approx. 50 g / 1.5 hours) No assembly required No supports Ready to use straight from the build plate Strong, rigid body Large chamfers for smooth cable feeding Printed so the cable travels along the layer lines , reducing friction Metric and Imperial markings Eight wire sizes in one tool Wire Sizes Metric Imperial 3 mm 1/8" 4 mm 5/32" 6 mm 1/4" 8 mm 5/16" 10 mm 3/8" 13 mm 1/2" 16 mm 5/8" 19 mm 3/4" How to use Mount the tool securely to a workbench or piece of wood. description: This one was quite the task! I originally did my clicker bar using these transparent bead storage cases which worked perfectly fine while making the odd one at home but I ran into a bit of an issue when we took it to our events. The first was they were quite small in height meaning I couldn't put a lot of keycaps in them, it also caused overflow into the other containers when people were digging around for the colour they wanted so I had random letters mixed in with each other. 😩 They were also a pain to put out on display because they came with an attached lid so I had to keep them closed after people left or use double the space to keep them open. Not great when you're already busy enough building the actual clickers and limited on table space! That got me motivated to upgrade the display - I looked around for a while but couldn't find anything that really matched what I needed so I set myself to work. The main issues I needed to resolve were: It had to be modular so I can always add extras for new keycaps if needed. Had to be held together somehow during the events so it doesn't get pushed over easily by people but needs to be able to accommodate for different sized bins and layouts due to table restrictions. A slot to show the letters/symbols as people often got lost trying to find letters if keycaps were flipped upside down in the box, worse if letters got mixed around already. Ideally stackable so I can just stack them together after events and pack it away in a box for ease of use. A lid preferably so they don't accidentally fall out or have other small objects fall into them. Features of the storage bins: Fully modular. x1, x4 and x9 bins. Bins are stackable. Please note x9 bin requires 256mm x 256mm build plates but you can print a x4 with x1 and combine to make a x9 for A1 Mini users. Two coupler versions for joining displays. Bins can be attached with the row or the quad coupler. There are both snug and loose fits so print the one best for your printers/filament calibration. Quad couplers are for holding 4 bins together or for joining large 9 bins with 4 bins. The row coupler is if you wanted to build horizontally/vertically only. Display slot version and one without. Slots are slide in and can be removed after event completion by placing it inside the bin with the keycaps for easy storage. Personally I like the slot version but I included one without in case others wanted to use these for other purposes. Stackable. Please note there is a small gap where they are stacked - this finger gap is INTENTIONAL so you can actually separate them easier without them getting stuck. (Mishaps have happened during testing...) Various lid options. x1 lids have handles and coupler holes, x4 lids have coupler holes, x9 lid have no holes. If using the handle versions for x1, please secure handles using GLUE. I could add more variations but I feel like for most people these versions should suffice. For handles I have a short and a taller version as well. There are two sizes to these in case you find them too tight to fit into the hole on the lids. Recommended Print Settings: Layer Height: 0.2mm Nozzle: 0.4mm Wall Generator: Classic Infill: 15-20% Gyroid Supports: Not required Speed: 20-50mm/s for layer 1, then 150-200 for the rest. description: Ultimate Parametric Pipe & Cable Clip Looking for a pipe or cable clip that fits your exact needs? This fully parametric generator lets you customize almost every important dimension, making it easy to create a clip tailored to your application. Create perfectly sized clips for pipes, cables, hoses, conduits, and many other round objects without having to modify the model manually. Simply adjust the parameters and generate the size you need. Whether you're organizing cables, mounting plumbing, or securing larger pipes, this generator gives you complete control over the most important dimensions. Features Fully parametric design Adjustable pipe/cable diameter Adjustable clip width Adjustable arm thickness Adjustable opening angle Adjustable wall distance Adjustable mounting hole diameter Compatible with multiple mounting methods: Countersunk screw (default) Socket head screw Hex nut By default, the model is generated with a countersunk screw recess. If you prefer a socket head screw or a hex nut , simply adjust the corresponding parameters described in the guide below. For rigid pipes, I recommend using a slightly larger opening angle to make installation easier. For cables, you can even print the clip in TPU . Thanks to the flexibility of the material, the cable can be inserted easily while still being held securely in place. Parameter Guide Gap Angle Controls how far the clip arms are opened. Adjust this value to change how tightly the clip wraps around the pipe or cable. Do not exceed 150° , as larger values may cause the model geometry to become invalid. Wall Distance Controls the minimum distance between the wall and the nearest point of the pipe or cable . A minimum value of 10 mm is recommended, but feel free to experiment. Need to move the pipe farther away from the wall? Simply increase this value and use a longer mounting screw. Arm Thickness Controls the thickness of the clip arms. Thicker arms provide greater stiffness and strength. A value between 3–5 mm is recommended for most applications. Larger pipe diameters may benefit from thicker arms. Pipe Diameter Outside diameter of the pipe or cable. Remember to add a small clearance (for example 0.1 mm ) unless you want a tight press fit. Clamp Width Controls the overall width of the clip. Increase this value for larger or heavier pipes and cables if additional strength is required. Hole Diameter of the mounting hole. Remember to add enough clearance so the screw can pass through freely. Head Nut Depth Used when mounting with a socket head screw or a hex nut instead of the default countersunk screw. Measure the height of the screw head or nut, add a small clearance (approximately 0.2 mm ), and enter the result here. Head Size Controls the diameter of the socket head screw recess. The default value is 1 mm , which disables the recess. If you're using a socket head screw, simply measure the screw head diameter, add a small clearance, and enter the result here. When using this parameter, keep Nut Size set to 1 mm. Nut Size Controls the size of the hex nut pocket. Measure the nut across the flats , add approximately 0.2 mm of clearance, and enter the result here. When using this parameter, keep Head Size set to 1 mm. Printing Recommendations Recommended material: PETG TPU is an excellent choice for cable management applications No supports required Print flat on the build plate I designed this generator to eliminate the need for creating a new model every time you need a different pipe or cable diameter. With just a few parameter changes, you can generate a custom clip that perfectly matches your application. If you find this model useful, I'd really appreciate a Like 👍 and a Boost 🚀 . Feel free to upload your makes, share your settings, and leave a comment with your experience or ideas for future improvements. Happy printing! 😊

Fully 3D Printable Pocket Grips After seeing the fantastic all-metal Pocket Grips available from MetMo, I wondered whether it would be possible to create a similar version that could be produced entirely on a standard FDM 3D printer—with no screws, pins or additional hardware. This model is the result of that challenge. Although inspired by the original concept, this isn't simply a copy. Considerable CAD modelling, prototyping and testing went into re-engineering the mechanism so it could be manufactured as a practical, fully 3D printable assembly. Inevitably, some features of the original metal design had to be simplified or omitted in order to achieve that goal. For example, this version does not feature interchangeable jaw inserts or integrated wire-cutting edges, allowing the mechanism to remain printable while still capturing the satisfying functionality of an adjustable pocket-sized grip. One feature I'm particularly pleased with is the pivot for the adjustment screw. Rather than requiring a metal pin or fastener, it simply uses a short piece of standard 1.75 mm filament, making this a genuinely hardware-free print that can be assembled straight off the printer. Assembly Please refer to the included exploded-view assembly video before putting the model together. Important: the adjustment screw and thumbwheel must be installed before the two handle halves are joined together. Once the handles are assembled, these components cannot be fitted without disassembly. Printing PLA is fine, I recommend printing with a generous number of walls/perimeters and for the best strength, a more durable filament such as PETG, ABS, ASA. Even then, remember that this is a plastic tool and should be treated accordingly. A Note on Expectations While these printed grips are surprisingly functional and great fun to build and use, they are not intended to compete with the strength, precision or durability of the original machined metal product . If you're looking for a professional-grade tool that will withstand years of heavy use, the original Pocket Grips are exceptionally well made and well worth a look. This project was created as a personal engineering challenge and as something enjoyable for the 3D printing community to build—not as a replacement for the original product. If you'd like to see (or purchase) the beautifully machined metal version that inspired this project, you can find it here : If you print a set, I'd love to see your makes and any improvements or remixes you come up with. La tenuta non avviene stringendo progressivamente il filetto, ma tramite la guarnizione presente nel raccordo femmina , che lavora contro la faccia frontale del raccordo maschio (appositamente predisposto in questi raccordi). Non è intercambiabile con NPT, BSP o GAS. Prima della stampa e dell’utilizzo verifica sempre che il componente su cui verrà montato il raccordo sia realmente 3/4'' GHT femmina . Ecco un progetto semplicissimo per rinfrescarvi nelle estati roventi davanti al pc. Un creativo e funzionale modello di Ice Cooler, a praticamente costo zero. L'idea è piuttosto semplice: sfruttare il ghiaccio per rinfrescare l'aria. Mettete una bottiglia di plastica da 500ml nel vostro freezer (attenzione a lasciare la bottiglia piena solo al 75/80% massimo, altrimenti esploderà!) e lasciatela congelare. Inseritela nell'alloggiamento del mio Ice Cooler e avviate la ventola. Entro pochi secondi, aria freschissima uscirà e vi donerà un gradevolissimo refrigerio. E può funzionare per diverse ore prima che il ghiaccio sia completamente sciolto e perda la sua efficacia!!!! Tutto quello di cui avrete bisogno è: - 1 ventola da PC 120x120mm a 12v - Un alloggiamento Batterie da 9v - 4 viti almeno da 50mm Io ho utilizzato questo hardware perchè il più comodo per me: ciò non toglie che potete valutare un'alimentazione da USB, o da PowerBank, con Regolatori di velocità etc etc. Sta solo a voi: il mio modello esige solo una ventola da 120mm; il cavo della ventola fuoriesce dal posteriore del Case e da lì potete fare quello che preferite. Una volta stampato tutto, testate i contatti della ventola unita al pacco della batteria da 9v, in modo da poter verificare la corretta direzione di rotazione della ventola (deve buttare aria FUORI dal Case, non dentro). Sì, la ventola è un 12v e la batteria un 9v, ma funzionerà benissimo, ad una velocità leggermente inferiore. Una volta verificato questo e segnato i corretti fili, inserite il filo della ventola nel buco in alto a sinistra e fatelo uscire dal posteriore, unendolo poi al pacco batteria. Avvitate la ventola nel case e inserite l'alloggiamento della bottiglia nel Case, prestando attenzione che la parte aperta sia in direzione della ventola. Ora, potete inserire la bottiglia ed accendere! Potete anche utilizzare il tappo per contenere al meglio la temperatura della bottiglia, migliorando la resa grazie anche ad un piccolo effetto “Venturi” causato dai piccoli fori in alto da cui viene aspirata l'aria che, scendendo attraverso la spirale, si raffredda più velocemente. Entro pochi secondi, sentirete una magnifica aria fresca uscire dal vostro nuovo Ice Cooler! Non dimenticate, quando cambiate la bottiglia, di verificare se la vaschetta di raccolta dell'acqua causata dalla condensa è da svuotare (alla base del Case dove va in appoggio la bottiglia). Buona estate a tutti!!!

description: Kumihimo Marudai Bracelet/Rope braiding stand This is a beginner friendly Kumihimo Marudai stand to make bracelets or rope using the ancient Japanese artform of Kumihimo , which is done by weaving strings of silk, rope or yarn together using a disc to form a rope/bracelet with artistic patterns in the process. The Marudai (Japanese, lit. “ Round Stand ”) allows you to move multiple strings at once using even back and forth movements of string to interlace the strings to form the weave of the bracelet or cord. This results in a faster weave compared to a hand-held portable Round Kumihimo Disc for round bracelets , but is less portable due to its larger form factor. Marudai stand with weighted bobbins and counterweight Usage A Kumihimo weave being formed through the center hole and pulled down by a counterweight attached to it The Marudai is used together with a center weight to pull on the formed weave through the hole in the center, and smaller weighted bobbins , called tama, on each individual string around the outsides. Commonly, the ratio of the weight is that the center weight will be between ½ to ⅔ of the combined weight of the outside weights. This balance ensures that the woven pattern will be consistent between each movement and result in a uniform shape and pattern of the bracelet/ropes. There is no hard rule of which side of the spectrum you decide on, it can depend on the particular use case of the weave. Using a heavier center weight will increase the pulling force and can result in a looser weave, whereas less center weight will provide lower resistance and give a tighter weave. You may purchase weighted bobbins and counterweights online or use 3D printed ones such as my Weighted Bobbin for Kumihimo braiding - Tama . Many different patterns of braids can be formed using a Marudai, such as alternating lines, dotted patterns, spirals and more. Assembly The assembly is quick and easy and can be done without tools. Hardware required Printed base , I recommend printing the weighted base, which gives the stand a stronger support Printed top disc , pick from a series of different discs depending on your level of experience and convenience desired Numbered Top disc with 32 notches and markers for 8-string and 16-string braids Great for beginners or those transitioning from a Kumihimo hand disc due to the familiar style Numbered Top disc with 32 round guides and markers for 8-string and 16-string braids A nice balance between full notches and a fully round disc, giving the best of both worlds holding the strings loosely in position, but being able to move them with a push rather than having to lift them out of the notches to re-arrange for complex patterns Top disc with 32 round guides and markers for 8-string and 16-string braids Same disc, but without number labels Numbered Top round disc without indentations. Markers for 8-string and 16-string braids This is the traditional form of a marudai disc and allows for quick re-arranging of strands following a series of moves. This requires practice as the strings will only be held in place by gravity as they are not guided to a particular location Top round disc without indentations. Markers for 8-string and 16-string braids Same disc, but without number labels Connecting rods (4x) You can either: Get 1/2 inch (12.7mm) round dowel rods (such as round wooden dowels ) from your local hardware store and cut them to size (I recommend a length of ~9inches, or 20-25cm for each rod) Or print the provided rods (24cm in length - you may resize the length as desired and based on your printers print bed) Optional rod connectors to extend the heigh of the stand, by connecting multiple rods together to form a taller stand A1 mini print size variant Someone requested a variant to fit on the A1 mini print bed, so I've published a A1 mini (180mm) size print profile - the top discs are resized to fit the bed and the connecting rods shortened as well. The weighted base is the same between the A1 mini and regular size and can be used interchangably with the same spacing between rods. The A1 mini profile contains 3 top disc variants: Notches with numbers and guide marks Round guide petal with guide marks Round disc with guide marks Assembly steps Place the bottom disc on the table or stable surface - this may either be the weighted bottom disc Weighted bottom disc or you can also decide to use one of the other pattern top disc as a bottom disc Round top disc being used as a bottom disc Push the four (4) connecting rods into the slots If you want to give it a stronger hold, you may use some glue and attach them permanently to the base Now attach the top disc to the top side of the connecting rods If you want to be able to change between different top plates, then I recommend not using glue for the top side. Optionally: if you want to make the stand taller , use the printable rod connectors to connect multiple rods to form a taller stand You may want to place additional weights onto the bottom to ensure the stand remains stable Rods extended using the optional rod connector Print Settings Supports / Brim: No Layer height: 0.20 mm Infill: 15% cubic for parts, 100% rectilinear for weighted base Walls: 2 Wall generation: Arachne for smooth curves Top/bottom pattern: Monotonic Orientation: Flat on the bed Material: PETG or PLA Kumihimo collection I've made a series of Kumihimo braiding related models to help me make neat Kumihimo braids, check them out: Weighted Bobbins for Kumihimo braiding To complement your Marudai, if you don't already have weights, you can print a set of Weighted Bobbin for Kumihimo braiding which make it easier to make neat braids by maintaining an even tension on the braid. MODYLO Quiver Same idea as the MODYLO Column rod, but for tubes. Open the Customizer, set the length and the inner diameter you want, hit Generate. It works out how many segments you need, lays them out on the plate, and you screw them together afterwards. I built it to store posters. Then I built a fat one to hold the tablecloth that lives rolled on a Column. If you read one thing, read this Segments print standing on the bed, and tall standing prints topple if adhesion is not right. This is the single thing that goes wrong. The Quiver is much steadier than a Column rod, because a 40 to 90 mm tube has a far wider footprint than a 30 mm stick. I did not need a brim. But if you have had tall prints fail before, here is the order to reach for: Clean plate. Soap, then isopropyl. A Cool Plate SuperTack helps a lot. Lower Max segment height. More segments, shorter ones, far less leverage. This is the most effective dial you have. Add an external brim to the segments (not the caps). Use Quiver Braced. Two versions in this listing Quiver - no internal bracing. Fewer parts, less filament, faster. Use this if you have your process under control. Quiver Braced - generates a sacrificial support tube inside each segment. It has a wide base for bed grip and is held to the inner wall by a few small tabs, so the segment can't pivot on its base and the tabs break away cleanly afterwards. Minimum length 180 mm. Both use the same geometry and the same thread. The braced version just leaves the support features enabled. Pick whichever suits your printer, they assemble together. The bracing costs about 185 g and 3h40 on a 1.4 m tube. If your printer handles tall prints and your plate adhesion is good, skip it. If you have had segments fall, it is worth every gram. MakerWorld's Customizer cannot switch a Fusion feature on and off, which is why this is two entries rather than one checkbox. What you can set Parameter Range What it does Total length 30 to 3000 mm (Quiver) 180 to 3000 mm (Quiver Braced) The usable space inside the finished tube. Inner diameter 40 to 90 mm The narrowest opening inside the tube. Whatever you want to store has to fit through this. Extra wall thickness 0 mm and up Added on top of the 2.8 mm default wall. Max segment height Quiver only The longest a single segment is allowed to be. Lower it for more segments, shorter ones, and less chance of anything toppling mid-print. Length is usable internal length. It does not include the threads or the caps. If your poster is 841 mm, ask for 841 mm. Ask for 850 if you want a little slack. Add roughly 17 mm to the outside length when you are working out shelf space. Inner diameter is the narrowest point, which is the wall inside the top thread, not the middle of the tube. So the number you set is the number that matters: if it says 60, a 60 mm roll goes in. Extra wall thickness does two jobs: a stiffer tube, and a heavier, more stable segment while it prints. At 40 mm diameter and full height, a millimetre or two is cheap insurance. Max segment height is the toppling dial. If your printer struggles with tall prints, bring it down. You get more joints and a slightly longer total print, and much less risk. It is only on the unbraced version, since the braced one solves the same problem a different way. What size do I need? Length, by content: Content Short side Ask for A3 297 mm 300 mm A2 420 mm 425 mm A1 594 mm 600 mm A0 841 mm 850 mm US 24 × 36 in 610 mm 615 mm Inner diameter, by use: Use Suggested ID One or two posters, light stock 40 mm Several posters, or heavy / matte stock that creases 60 mm Rolled around a 30 mm Column rod (tablecloth, fabric, banner) 60 mm Rolled around a Column with a thick fabric, or a big stack 90 mm Tight rolls leave memory creases in heavy paper. If in doubt go one size up, the extra filament is mostly in the length, not the diameter. Printing Segments print standing on the bed, threaded socket down . The caps print flat. The Customizer lays this out for you, but the plate layout is not preserved if you re-slice from a saved profile, so check it. Quick self-check: if your slice is full of supports, the orientation is wrong. Layer height: 0.2 mm Walls: 2 Infill: lightning. This one matters. A gyroid or grid infill sends the toolhead darting back and forth on every layer, and on a tall thin segment that is exactly the force that tips it over. Lightning leaves the head running smooth continuous loops around the wall. Less filament, less time, and much less shaking. Supports: none. All overhangs clear along the vertical axis. Brim: I did not need one. The tube footprint is much wider than a Column rod, so it sits far more solidly. If you see any lifting, or you have had tall prints fail before, add an external brim to the segments and leave it off the caps. Filament: standard PLA Real slice, 1.4 m tube, 60 mm inner diameter, 7 segments of 200 mm on one plate: Version Filament Time Quiver 595 g 12h39 Quiver Braced 780 g 16h19 If you have had segments topple, print fewer per plate. The risk is not really about any single segment, it is about how long they all stand there and how much the toolhead has to travel between them. Seven segments standing for twelve hours is seven chances, and one faller can take out its neighbours. Printing them one at a time costs surprisingly little: about 1h50 each plus a few minutes of prep, so roughly 40 minutes more machine time across the whole tube. You pay for it in plate changes, not in printing. Worth it if the alternative is losing a plate at hour ten. Worth being straight about this: a cardboard poster tube costs a few euros and this does not beat it on price. That is deliberate: faster, lighter, and far more stable on a tall segment. Plenty stiff for storage. Do not stand on it. Assembly Screw the segments together. The thread is a 3-start thread with a detent, so it seats firmly and does not back out on its own. Every segment is identical, so: Assemble them in any order A cap screws onto any segment, at either end A 900 mm tube can be taken apart and rebuilt as two shorter ones with a second pair of caps Print one spare segment now and extend the tube later instead of reprinting it Dry-fit keeps it adjustable. A drop of glue on the threads makes it permanent and noticeably stiffer. Your call. Seam tip: set seam position to Back before slicing. Not Aligned. Aligned drifts the seam around from segment to segment and you can never line them up. Back puts it in the same place on every segment. Then, because the thread is 3-start, each joint seats in three positions 120° apart. Dry-fit and try all three at each joint, keep the one that lines up. You end up with a seam running close to straight down the whole tube instead of spiralling. Pairs with MODYLO Column MODYLO Column is the same idea as a solid rod. description: Platethora , the open-source, public-domain, quick-release Plate system with a Plethora of applications. Platethora was inspired by systems like Gridfinity, the Honeycomb storage wall, and tripods. I aimed to create a quick-release plate you could use for anything you want, not just cameras. I tried to make the design as simple as possible while using also as little hardware as possible, but an M4x14-16 screw with a nylon nut is still required, although a regular nut with some superglue should also work. The main goal is for people to create their own bases and plates for whatever they need, which is why I shared the editable step files and put the whole project into the public domain, meaning you can do whatever you want with these files. I recommend printing in PETG in the orientation shown above. This isn't supposed to be a replacement for conventional tripods for cameras and such. It's supposed to be an option to be able to use tripods and quick-release plates with things you usually can't use them with. Things like lights and the other examples in the photos. If you have a really nice camera, then I encourage you to buy a nice tripod for it with a proper metal quick-release plate. But if you want something a little more out there, like helping hands that can be switched from being used on a flat surface to being used with a desk clamp, then I would argue my system is the better option. It's a solution for very specific problems, which is exactly what 3D printing is for.

Want a cute storage solution for your knick-knacks? Wish you had a quick and easy setup for displaying them at a market or craft fair? Look no further! I combined these concepts into one 3-tiered solution. This is the mini version, meaning each box is ~45mm wide and ~35mm deep (except for the bottom box, which is closer to 40mm deep). (Full-size version is near-complete, but it doesn't stay together as securely as Id like!) I designed them to sit nicely on top of each other when closed, and used the back-brace as a way to secure it all together as well as support it when displayed. When fully open for display, I noticed the middle box sagged backwards a little, so I made a little spacer that wedges into the middle divider and against the topmost box to keep it straight! The back-brace also shifts down to support the full height of the display when open, and back up when it's packed up again. I can hold and shake this thing sideways, frontways, upsidedown, and toss it into a large box with other loose things, and it stays closed quite well! I recommend PETG for the bolts that hold the screws on, but PLA should work too. (Just be sure to sloooow down the first layer of PETG if you use it, I had a fun time working out how to get the thing to stick down with such a small object). Requires: Two (2) 2.5mm x 10 mm screws (to hold the back brace on) and Sixteen (16) 2.5mm x 8mm screws (to attached the levers to the boxes). I used machine screws as that's what I had, but any screw in those sizes should work! The holes for the screws may need a bit of loosening if your filament has sagged down, I found this was easier than dealing with supports for them. Assembly is as simple as attaching the levers and the back-brace to the boxes as shown in the photos. The top lid slides on and off, and has a small lip to secure it in place when closed. I usually just keep the spacer wedge for the middle box inside one of the middle compartments for when I open it up. This is my first proper 3D model! I'm very open to improvements, so please try it out for yourself and let me know what you think!

It builds on V2's aesthetic restyling — rounded body, central anti-wobble guide tongue, fillets at the root of the arms, chamfered mouth — and adds a robustness pass on the latch holes, a true new D-ring attachment, independent bulge controls on X and Y, optional insertion guides, and a reorganized, multilingual Customizer menu. Every dimension stays parametric and protected by automatic safety clamps. What's New in V3 Robustness pass: the minimum wall margin around each drilled attachment has been increased from 1.2 mm to 1.6 mm, for cord/paracord/D-ring tabs that print reliably. New true D-ring attachment ("d_ring"), for closed/welded D-ring hardware: it is a straight round hole, drilled horizontally through the tab from side wall to side wall (like a hinge-pin hole), not vertically through the top/bottom faces. It is invisible from above and shows only as a hole in the side walls of the tab. The diameter matches the dring_wire parameter, i.e. the diameter of the ring's wire/stock (not its overall size): the ring opens, hooks into the hole and closes again, without having to thread the whole buckle through it. description: 🦷 Dental Tooth & Gum Demonstration Model with Weighted Display Stand This is a realistic dental demonstration model (cartoonish picture with the real dentist for proprotions) designed for dentists to clearly explain treatments and procedures to their patients. It represents a cross-section of a tooth and surrounding gum , allowing patients to better understand tooth anatomy and what their treatment involves. The project was developed in collaboration with a practicing dentist , ensuring it meets the needs of daily clinical use while remaining practical, durable, and visually engaging. The tooth and gum are separate pieces , allowing the tooth to be removed from the gum and shown more closely to patients during consultations. The display stand was designed in Fusion 360 , while the tooth and gum were sculpted in Nomad Sculpt to achieve a realistic organic appearance. The stand includes a hidden cavity that can be filled with weights, such as old screws, nuts, or other metal pieces, giving it excellent stability and preventing it from tipping over during demonstrations. For the model shown in the photos, I used clear UV resin to recreate the enamel, producing a remarkably realistic translucent effect. I also used thin electrical wires to represent the nerves and blood vessels inside the tooth. Once positioned, they were secured with super glue and encapsulated with UV resin for a clean, natural finish. Rather than using an AMS, I chose to hand-paint the entire model using an airbrush and fine brushes. This gave me much greater control over the colours and subtle shading, resulting in a unique, highly realistic finish. Of course, if you have an AMS, you can also download the individual parts and create your own multicolour version. I would recommend printing all the parts in white filament and treating the painting as part of the project. It's incredibly rewarding and allows you to achieve a truly professional-looking result. This model has taken many months of design, sculpting, testing, and refinement , and I'm incredibly happy with how it turned out. My dentist friend was genuinely surprised by how professional and useful it looked, which made all the effort worthwhile. If you decide to print it, I'd be truly grateful if you could share a photo of your make . Seeing other people enjoying and using my designs is the best reward I could ask for. Thank you very much, and I hope you enjoy building and painting it! The display stand looks stunning on Wood PLA, also includes a small name plate at the front, allowing you to personalize the model with a dentist's name, clinic name, or logo from the bambulab text option . This adds a professional touch and makes it ideal for use in dental practices, consultation rooms, or educational displays. I was tired of "one-size-fits-all" sink caddies that sat loosely in the middle of my divided sink, slid around, and got in my way. I also hated that I couldn't put them at the top or bottom of my sink due to its curves. So, I designed a sink caddy that looks “built in”; it hugs the dimensions of my sink, fits flush with the upper or lower curves, and eliminates wobble. Sweet. I wanted to make some for friends, but their sinks were all shaped differently… Lame. My only viable option was to turn the model into a parametric caddy that could be customized after taking a few measurements of their sink. When that was done, I decided to go ham and make the basket sizes individually customizable, and then added a single basket option as well. 🧮 Customization for everything but the kitchen sink Use the customize button to tweak your dimensions and even print a fit test before committing to the full caddy. Basket sizes and combinations: Adjust the total length of the caddy from front to back. Independently configure how deep each basket sits inside your sink and how far out it extends into the basin. (Height + Width) Toggle either side on/off to generate a single sturdy basket. Generate unlimited combinations sized for various items or needs, while keeping a clean, built-in look. Sink dimensions (measurement guide at the end): Inner Sink Curve Radius: Hugs the exact rounded (or straight) corners of your basin where the divider meets the sink walls. Divider Width and Top Curve Radius: Generates a perfectly snug bridge over your sink divider. The top curve can be 0 (flat), but it looks nicer if there are no gaps. Advanced/Optional Settings: Counter Overhang - My sink has a nasty overhang so I created this setting to automatically notch the back of the baskets so they slide underneath. If you also have an overhang, I'm sorry. But at least it gives us added stability. Sink Taper/Grade - Angles the baskets to match the slope of your sink walls to sit flush. Most people won't have to touch this. Fit test for the filament frugal: Toggle the “Generate Fit Test Cutout” option to remove the baskets and print only the divider bridge to ensure everything sits flush. “Fit test height” allows you to print a taller or shorter segment to test your sink’s taper, or test only the bridge itself. Note: fit tests get printed upside down to minimize support filament. 🖨️ Printing Instructions & Best Practices using Bambu Studio/Handy If you follow the measurement guide below you will be fine printing directly from the Bambu Handy customizer to get a sturdy flush-fit caddy. The only exception being a multi-height basket (see support section). Included Profile to boost customizer print quality in Bambu Studio: Because the parametric model maker only allows limited slicer optimization, I made the “Customizer Profile” to apply all my highly-optimized global slicer settings (walls, seams, speed, overhangs, strength, etc.). The only other thing I might suggest is adding extra cooling to your filament profile. I set my Bambu Matte PLA to 100% Part/Aux fans after the 2nd layer. Here is how to use it: Generate your caddy via the customizer, download STL (optional) Enable “fit test” in customizer, click generate, download .3mf, print to ensure fit Download/Open the “Customizer Profile” in Bambu Studio Import your customizer STL file, replace model on the plate You are ready to roll!! Bridge/Basket Support: Same height baskets will print with slim trees to support the divider bridge via the .3mf. It works great, but of course if you have a dual nozzle you can flip the support interface to PETG. If you are printing a "Multi-Height" variation where one basket floats in mid-air, a 0 Z-gap PETG support interface is strongly recommended to provide a solid floor for the basket corners to print on. Bambu Studio will probably want you to use normal support, but tree [strong] is just fine. 🛠️ Advanced 3D Printing Engineering This model is a bunch of pieces that all sync together with code based on your inputs. The geometry is heavily optimized for customization but a few caveats: I spent an incredible amount of time testing various sink dimensions and basket sizes, tweaking the code to ensure a clean print and that all reasonable dimensions will work without breaking the model. That said, I can't guarantee every single combination of basket size, sink curve, height, etc will work, and there may be small issues and edge cases. If you find one, comment with your dimensions and I’ll take a look. If you aren't sure about your measurements, please use the print test customization option to print a small section to ensure a good fit! 📏 How to Measure Your Sink for a Flush-Fit Caddy These don't have to be exact, but you'll have a sturdier and better looking caddy the closer you get. If you aren't sure about any measurements, print the customizer’s fit test option before printing a full caddy. Measuring will take about 5 minutes once you have what you need. Let’s go! 1. Inner Sink Curve Radius This is the curve of your sink's corners. Because it's hard to measure with a ruler, I suggest printing this awesome tool: If you have a large curve: RadGauge Dual Mega If you have a small curve: RadGauge Dual Quick hack: Find any circular object (I initially used a coaster) that fits nicely in your sink’s upper divider corner, measure the width, divide by two, done. Alternatively, tie some string to a pencil and make some circles on paper. 2. Divider Width & Top Curve Radius Measure the thickness of the bridge between your two sink basins. Make sure to measure the thickness below the top curve (where the walls straighten out) so the caddy doesn't get stuck. If the top edges of your divider are curved, you can use the outer-curve side of the RadGauge Dual to measure it. Quick hack: You can get away with measuring tape on the width (when in doubt round up) and leaving the top curve at low number. 3. Sink Taper / Grade Grab any straight flat object like a ruler or remote and press it flat against the top half of your sink divider. If it looks perfectly vertical, go with 0. If it looks only very slightly off, leave the preset .5mm or bump to 1mm. You can also measure how much the sink wall moves inwards per 100mm with two rulers. When in doubt, use the customizer fit test height option to print a tall test. If anyone wants taper tests let me know, I'll upload a plate. 4. Counter Overhang (if needed) If you have an under-mount sink where the countertop sticks out over the basin, measure how far the counter protrudes past the sink wall. Input this number in mm to generate a custom notch so your baskets slide underneath. 🔥And that's it! 🔥 Thanks for checking out my project. I’m new to 3d printing so if anyone has any advice or suggestions on how to improve the model or profile settings, I’m all ears. If you decide to print a basket, I would love to see it. Cheers, WK Changelog Update 7/24/26: Based on feedback, added adjustable chamfers to all interior and exterior edges that are not hugging the sink (enabled by default). Should be easier to clean and much harder to get scraped by a sharp edge. Update 7/24/26: Fixed chamfer extrusion when generating single basket caddy.

description: Measure your T-track, customize the runner, print and assemble a full miter gauge that actually fits your saw. No more wobbly stock gauges with sloppy side play. This is a complete, fully 3D-printed miter gauge system with a customizable T-track runner, adjustable fence, two-color angle scale (0 to 60 degrees both sides), ergonomic locking knob and a runner lock for repeatable positioning. The runner uses MakerWorld's built-in customizer, so you can dial in the exact cross-section of your T-track (check the description below) and get a snug, zero-play fit on any table saw, band saw or router table. Designed and tested on an Evolution R255TBL+ table saw. Works with any machine that has a T-slot miter channel, as long as you measure and customize the runner to match. Key features Customizable T-track runner fits any non-standard slot profile 120-degree range (60 degrees each side of zero) Two-color scale, printed separately (no AMS required) Adjustable fence (19.4 cm top, 25 cm bottom), slides along two slots for positioning Runner lock with optional spring for progressive clamping feel Reinforced pivot boss (6 wall loops) for long-term durability under side load Lightening holes reduce weight without sacrificing stiffness All hardware is standard M6, easy to source anywhere Hardware required 1x M6 x 25mm hex head bolt (pivot) 1x M6 x 45mm bolt (main locking knob) 1x M6 x 25mm bolt (runner lock) 2x M6 x 35mm bolt (fence) 5x M6 nut 1x M6 washer, minimum 10mm outer diameter Optional: spring, approximately 25mm long, any type that fits over M6 shaft (recommended for runner lock) CA glue (optional, for extra security when attaching the scale) How to get your parts This listing has two buttons: "Open in Bambu Studio" and "Customize." "Open in Bambu Studio" gives you the full print profile with all 6 plates (base, scale, knob, small parts, fence, example runner). All print settings are pre-configured. "Customize" opens the parametric runner generator. Enter your T-track measurements (top_width, bottom_width, top_height, bottom_height), generate an STL, then either add it as a new plate in Bambu Studio or replace the example runner plate (plate 06) with your custom runner. Important: measure your T-track before printing the runner! The example runner included in the print profiles is sized for the Evolution R255TBL+ table saw with the following default values: bottom_width = 24.30 mm bottom_height = 4.30 mm top_height = 6.00 mm top_width = 19.40 mm Your saw almost certainly has different slot dimensions. Use the Customize button to adjust these four parameters to match your specific T-track. A caliper measurement accurate to 0.1mm will give you the best fit. Printed parts (6 plates) 01 - Scale (two-color, no AMS needed, print in contrasting colors) 02 - Base (main mitre gauge body) 03 - Knob (large locking knob + cap) 04 - Small knobs + pivot cap + scale bolts (all small parts on one plate) 05 - Fence 06 - Example runner (customize before printing) Assembly 1) Measure your T-track slot dimensions and customize the runner model (top_width, bottom_width, top_height, bottom_height). Use the included example runner as a reference for print settings. 2) Insert 3x M6 nuts into the runner slots (from the bottom). 3) Align the scale with the cutout on the base, press the locating tabs in. The scale should hold on its own. Optionally apply CA glue for extra security. 4) Place the base onto the runner. Insert the pivot bolt (M6 x 25mm hex head) through the boss into the runner nut. The hole is intentionally tight to eliminate play, you may need to screw the bolt in rather than push it through. Press the cap onto the bolt head. 5) Insert the M6 x 45mm bolt from the top of the large knob (push through the hex channel, use a screwdriver to press it down). Place the M6 washer (min 10mm diameter) onto the bolt shaft from the bottom. Pass through the arc slot and tighten into the runner nut with moderate force. Press the cap onto the top of the knob. 6) Press 2x M6 x 35mm bolts into the fence holes (press-fit). 7) Insert an M6 nut into each of the two small fence knobs, close with caps. 8) Slide the fence bolts through the slots in the base, thread the small knobs onto the bolts. 9) Insert the M6 x 25mm bolt into the runner lock knob, place the spring (recommended) onto the bolt shaft, screw the assembly into the nut at the end of the runner. Press the cap onto the knob. Using it Loosen the large knob, set your angle using the scale markings, tighten the knob. The runner lock at the end of the bar lets you fix the gauge position along the T-track. For repeatable cuts, tighten the runner lock once you find your position, then only adjust the angle knob between cuts. Print hints Material: PLA works well. PETG is fine if you want extra durability. The base prints flat. The large knob prints vertically with a brim. The scale is a separate print in a contrasting color (white scale on dark base or vice versa). No AMS needed, just filament swap in the middle. The example runner profile is customized for the Evolution R255TBL+. You must customize it for your own saw before printing. If you print it, please leave a rating, it helps a lot. description: Membership 🔐 MEMBERSHIP UNLOCK 🎁 Monthly custom model just for YOU 🛍 Full print/sell rights on all my models 📸 Access to my photos & post templates 🙏 Support my family + fuel my madness Parametric Funnel Generator Need a funnel for one specific bottle, container, machine, fluid, powder, seed, pellet, or other oddly sized opening? This generator lets you create one instead of digging through drawers full of funnels that are somehow all the wrong size. Adjust the funnel bowl, outlet, wall thickness, spout length, taper, and bend geometry to create everything from a basic straight funnel to a long offset funnel with two smooth bends. The default two-bend setup curves away from the center and then bends back so the final outlet points straight down again. Everything is generated as one continuous model with a smooth internal flow path. 🔧 Funnel Body Controls Setting What It Does Top Opening Diameter Controls the inside diameter of the large funnel opening. Outlet Diameter Controls the inside diameter where the funnel bowl transitions into the spout. Funnel Height Changes the height and steepness of the funnel bowl. Wall Thickness Controls the thickness of the funnel body and spout walls. Top Rim Turns the reinforced rim around the top opening on or off. Rim Height Controls how tall the rim extends above the funnel body. Rim Thickness Controls how far the rim extends outward. 📏 Spout Controls Setting What It Does Spout Length Controls the total centerline length of the complete spout, including all straight and curved sections. Spout Style Selects a straight-diameter or tapered spout. Spout End Diameter Controls the outlet diameter at the very end when a tapered spout is selected. Spout Path Selects a straight spout, one bend, or two bends. The spout length is measured along the entire path, not just vertically from the funnel. Increasing a bend angle or radius uses more of the selected spout length. ↪️ First Bend Controls Setting What It Does First Bend Start Distance Controls how far the spout travels straight down before the first bend begins. First Bend Angle Controls how far the first bend turns away from vertical. First Bend Radius Controls how tight or wide the first curve is. First Bend Direction Selects whether the spout bends left or right. A larger bend radius creates a smoother, wider curve. A smaller radius creates a tighter elbow. ↩️ Second Bend Controls Setting What It Does Distance Between Bends Controls the straight section between the end of the first bend and the beginning of the second. Second Bend Angle Mode Selects whether the second bend automatically matches the first bend or uses a custom angle. Second Bend Angle Controls the second bend angle when Custom mode is selected. Second Bend Radius Controls how tight or wide the second curve is. Second Bend Direction Selects whether the second bend continues in the same direction or bends back the opposite way. Match First Mode When the second bend is set to Match First and the direction is set to Opposite , the second bend automatically cancels the angle of the first bend. For example: First bend: 55° right Second bend: 55° left Final outlet direction: straight down This creates an offset spout while keeping the outlet vertical. Custom Mode Select Custom to control the second bend independently. This allows the final outlet to point inward, outward, sideways, or at any angle between the available limits. 🛡️ Automatic Geometry Protection The generator automatically checks the selected measurements and adjusts impossible combinations that would otherwise create broken geometry. This includes: Bend angles that consume more than the available spout length Bend start distances that are too long Excessive spacing between the bends Bend radii that are too tight for the selected spout size Negative final straight sections Invalid outlet or wall-thickness combinations Any automatic adjustments are shown in the OpenSCAD console so you can see which setting was limited. 💡 Possible Uses Automotive fluid funnels Oil and coolant funnels Bottle filling Powder transfer Seed and pellet funnels Resin and paint transfer Workshop machines Aquarium equipment Kitchen containers Hard-to-reach fill ports Offset container openings Custom replacement funnels Because every dimension is adjustable, the same generator can create a small precision funnel or a large workshop funnel. 📐 Design Notes The curved spout is generated as one continuous swept tube. Both the inside and outside follow the same centerline path through the straight sections and bends. Features Quick, individually removable containers Strong, easy-to-operate wall locking mechanism Smooth pull-out and rotate action for easy access to parts Full tray access when removed from the wall and laid flat Interchangeable tray labels Modular design for easy expansion Optimized for strength with minimal support material Easy assembly No additional hardware required, except your chosen wall mounting method (4 mm screws or adhesive) Dimensions Case: 60 × 60 × 60 mm (excluding protruding handle) Internal tray storage: approximately 45 × 44 × 40 mm Included Files (STEP) STEP files are included for self-slicing, modification, and further development (encouraged!). Bracket – Expandable snap-together wall bracket. Central mounting hole designed for a 4 mm screw with a maximum head diameter of 10 mm. Case – Main housing for the tray and locking mechanism. Tray – Sliding and rotating storage container. Label – Removable label insert with an easy-removal leverage tab. Lock – Sliding latch that mounts the container to the wall bracket. Snaps together with the handle. Handle – Used to remove the container from the wall bracket. Snaps together with the lock. Print Settings The print profile includes all of these settings by default, but if you'd prefer to slice it yourself, here are my recommendations. Global Settings Layer Height: 0.20 mm Walls: 3 Top/Bottom Layers: 4–5 Infill: 15% Gyroid or Cross Hatch Material: PLA is recommended due to easier support removal, although any material that allows clean support removal should work well. Supports: Manual Tree Supports (Case & Bracket) Part Settings Bracket – Manual tree supports on the four overhanging surfaces. Case – Manual tree supports on the three overhanging surfaces. Tray – Print-in-place part. Do not disassemble or split. Label – Edit the text before slicing. A 5–6 mm font works well. Use Arachne wall generation for improved text definition. Assembly (See the photo instructions in the carousel.) Print all required components, remove the supports, and ensure all supported surfaces are clean and free of debris. Needle nose pliers work well for bracket support removal. Container Assembly Take the case and tray and rotate them upside down so the print-in-place legs are secured. Press the leg tabs inward while pushing the tray into the case. This requires a fair amount of force, so don't be concerned. Once inserted, slide the tray back and forth a few times to ensure the tabs are seated correctly in the channels. Turn the assembly upright and insert the lock through the rear of the case with the "Top" text facing upwards. Insert the handle through the front of the case, again with the "Top" text facing upwards. Press the handle firmly into the lock until it clicks into place. Press the label firmly into the tray slot. To replace a label later, insert a flat-head screwdriver into the horizontal opening and gently pry it out. Check that the tray slides smoothly and locks in the parked position. Check the handle and lock operate freely under their own weight. If the handle does not go all the way down when locking to the bracket, this is because there is support material still on the bracket piece that needs removing. Bracket Assembly The brackets can be assembled before mounting or snapped onto an existing wall-mounted bracket assembly. Place one bracket onto another so the snap hooks overlap. Press firmly near the overlapping hooks until they snap together. Due to the strength of the snap-together design, only every other bracket in an array needs to be fixed to the wall. description: Hey guys, the new mushroom hole punch you’ve been waiting for is finally here! This is the first in a new series of fully 3D printed mushroom-style punches designed for discbound notebooks and pocket-sized planners. It lets you punch your own paper, photos, dividers and other inserts, so you’re no longer limited to buying pre-punched sheets. The entire punch prints in place in around 1.5 hours , including the smooth hinged mechanism. Small side guides help position paper up to approximately 108 mm wide , making it ideal for smaller notebooks and pocket-sized discbound systems. A lot of testing went into this design. I went through nearly ten different versions of the mushroom cutting profile alone, trying to get the cleanest and most reliable cut possible. I eventually narrowed it down to two profiles: W-Shaped Profile This gave me the best overall results across most of my testing. Curved Profile This performed better with certain paper types and thicknesses. Directions for Use Place the paper right up against the hinge, then move the guide into position so it just touches the edge of the paper. Put both hands on the press and apply equal pressure on both sides. Push down firmly in one clean motion until you hear and feel a solid click. If one side goes down before the other, the cuts may vary. For the cleanest result, press straight down evenly with both hands in one smooth “thoom.” …………………………… Both versions are included, so you can test them and decide which works best for the paper you use. One of my main goals was to make it capable of punching 160 GSM paper , as this is a popular thickness for making sturdy notebook pages. It can also work with thinner or thicker paper, although results may vary depending on the material and cutting profile. Occasionally, some paper may leave a tiny whisk of material that can be removed with almost no effort. Considering this is a fully printed, free alternative to an expensive metal discbound punch, I think that is a pretty fair trade-off! As always, this model went through plenty of testing, tweaking and re-tweaking before release. I’m really proud of how smoothly the hinge works, and I hope it helps you create your own custom notebooks and planners. hope yous enjoy the pile of test prints haha :) ####I’ve also included a simple front and back cover , along with a ready-to-download print profile, to help you get started with your first pocket-sized discbound notebook.#### share your makes, results and which cutting profile worked best for you! This is only release one! Next up should be the eight-hole version , as I know that is the one a lot of commenters have been waiting for. After that, I’ll also be remaking the seven-hole version , and then we’ll see how far we can take the series from there. Thank you all for helping keep me motivated throughout this journey. This originally started as a fun little project for a family member, but your support has turned it into something much bigger than I expected. This is now my full-time job, so any boosts, shares, downloads, or support through my Buy Me a Coffee page would be massively appreciated. Thank you all so much for the encouragement and inspiration. Have a great day, everyone!
