Fully Parametric Custom Speaker Grills If you are into car audio fabrication, custom speaker builds, you know that finding a grills with the exact diameter, thickness, and hole spacing you need is a massive headache. As a dedicated car audio guy , I build a ton of custom grills for subwoofers, door speakers and cooling vents. Tired of fighting with basic 3D shapes in Tinkercad every time I needed a slight size tweak, I coded this fully parametric generator in OpenSCAD. Now you can customize and download the perfect grille in seconds! 🛠️ What Makes This Model Awesome? Unlike static STL files, this model is 100% parametric . Using MakerWorld's MakerLab / Parametric Model Maker, you can adjust everything on the fly: 3 Distinct Mesh Patterns: Choose between Honeycomb (classic hex), Grid (clean square mesh), or Circles (staggered bubble pattern). Fully Adjustable Outer Rim: Dial in the exact outer diameter, rim width, and total thickness. Smart Mounting Holes: Set your screw hole count (from 0 to 24), hole diameter, and edge spacing. The code automatically spaces them symmetrically! Custom Edge Chamfers: Add a smooth 3D chamfer to the top, bottom, or both sides of the outer rim to give your build a highly polished, professional finish. 🎛️ How to Customize Your Grills Click the Customize button here on MakerWorld. Main Dimensions: Put in your target outer diameter and desired plate thickness. Pattern Settings: Swap between honeycomb, grid, or circles, and adjust the cell size and wall thickness to control how "open" or "dense" the mesh is. Chamfer Settings: Set your chamfer size (e.g., 1mm or 1.5mm) and choose where you want it (e.g., select top to give your mounting screws a slightly countersunk look). Mounting Holes: Set the exact number of mounting screws your speaker or vent frame requires. Download & Print! 💡 My Car Audio Print Recommendations Because these grills are often used in demanding environments (like hot car interiors or high-vibration speaker enclosures), here are my personal fabrication tips: ⚠️ Material Choice: If you are installing this in a vehicle, do not use standard PLA —it will warp on a hot summer day. I highly recommend printing in ASA or PETG for excellent heat and UV resistance. (I use PETG i had no problems even in hot summer days on 40+ degrees in the car) Wall Loops: Set to at least 4 or 5 walls to ensure the thin honeycomb/mesh lines are printed solid and strong. Infill: 15% (since the model is thin, the walls and top/bottom layers will make up the entire print anyway).

description: SnapCore Parametric Resizable Vial Holder (Single Hinge / Single Latch) The SnapCore Resizable Vial Holder is a fully parametric storage system that automatically resizes to fit your needs. This version features a single printed hinge and single latch , making it ideal for small to medium-sized vial holders while maintaining the simple, hardware-free SnapCore design. Customizable size The model is fully customizable using the below parameters: When you export the model from the “customize” tab, it will appear as a fully assembled box. In the slicer, you can right click and “split to objects" as shown: once split it will all be in 1 pile on the plate you must drag each piece to position it, and make sure the lid and hinge flat side is on the plate. Adjustable Parameters The model includes parameters for: Number of vial spaces (Width) Number of vial spaces (Length) Vial diameter Vial spacing Box length (automatic) Box width (automatic) Latch width Hinge spacing Hinge insert clearance Hinge opening Wall thickness Base height Lid height Please ensure you are adjusting the base height and lid height for you vial needs. These do not update as it is difficult to tie those together so must be manually updates Important Notes ⚠ Single Hinge / Single Latch Design This version uses a single hinge and single latch . It performs exceptionally well for small and medium-sized boxes. As the box becomes larger, you may notice a small amount of lid movement or "wiggle" due to the increased span. This is normal for a single-hinge design and does not generally affect functionality. For very large configurations, a future multi-hinge/multi-latch version may provide additional rigidity. ⚠ Box Height Does NOT Automatically Resize The box automatically adjusts its length and width , but it does not automatically adjust the height for different vial sizes. If you change to a taller or shorter vial, you must manually adjust: Base Height Lid Height A good starting point is to make the combined base and lid height approximately 2 mm taller than your vial to provide adequate clearance for printing tolerances and easy removal. Example: 40 mm tall vial → Total inside height ≈ 42 mm To calculate inside height you must add wall thickness for both the lid and base, otherwise the inside height will be off by wall thickness X 2 ⚠ Latch Width The latch width is user adjustable. Larger boxes may benefit from a wider latch for additional strength, while smaller boxes can use a narrower latch. ⚠ Changing Vial Diameter Changing the vial diameter automatically resizes the footprint of the box, but remember to verify and adjust the box height separately if your new vial has a different overall height. description: Press the Customize button to customize! Funnels glug because a sealed bottle neck traps air with nowhere to go, so the liquid backs up and chugs instead of pouring in a steady stream. This funnel fixes that with vent ribs that hold the neck slightly open the entire time it's inserted, letting air escape while liquid pours in fast and uninterrupted. As far as I could find, no parametric fast-flow funnel existed anywhere before this one, so I built one from scratch: a fully parametric design built around a single smooth curve running through four diameters, from the spout tip up to the top opening, so you can shape anything from a classic single cone to a bulged, hourglass, or S-curved profile just by dragging four diameter sliders and three height sliders. Add a rim flange for a sturdier print and a hanging handle. Prints wide mouth down, spout pointing up, with no supports needed. I've tested the flow rate and the one in the default profile can fast flow a 2L bottle at about 200mL/s, so it can fill a 2L bottle in about 10s. Key Features Fast, glug-free flow: raised, round-profile vent ribs follow the shell's exact curve all the way from the spout tip to the rim, holding a bottle's neck slightly open so air can escape while liquid pours in at full speed instead of backing up and chugging; this is the entire reason the funnel exists Four-diameter taper profile: set diameter_1 (the spout tip) through diameter_4 (the top opening), and the three heights between them (height_1, height_2, height_3), for full control over the funnel's shape One continuous curve: the three tapered segments blend into each other with zero-slope tangency at every diameter, so there's no visible kink or seam anywhere along the profile True exterior diameters: every diameter you set is the actual printed OD at that height, including the vent ribs' bulge, so what you dial in is what comes off the bed Rim flange: optional flat flange around the top opening, wider than the taper, for extra bed contact and rigidity Hanging handle: optional flat handle with a hanging hole, with adjustable length, width, hole size, and placement angle around the rim Cross-section preview: switch view to cross_section and sweep cross_section_angle to inspect the wall thickness and curve before you commit to a print Print Settings Setting Recommended Orientation Print exactly as generated: wide mouth down on the bed, spout pointing up Supports Not required; the diameter only ever decreases going up, so every overhang is self-supporting Perimeters 2-3 Infill 10-15% Material PLA is fine for water and dry goods; use PETG, ASA, or ABS if you'll be pouring hot liquids, oil, fuel, or other automotive fluids through it Download the optimized print profile from this page, delete the sample models off the plate, and import your STL into it. How to Use Funnel Dimensions: set diameter_1 through diameter_4 and height_1 through height_3 to shape the taper, plus wall_thickness. Rim (optional): leave add_rim on for extra bed contact and rigidity, and adjust rim_added_diameter to taste, or turn it off. Vent ribs (optional): leave add_vent_ribs on for glug-free pouring, and adjust vent_rib_count and vent_rib_width, or turn it off. Handle (optional): leave add_handle on and adjust handle_length, handle_width, handle_hole_diameter, and handle_angle, or turn it off. Export the STL, delete the sample models off the plate, and import your STL into the print profile. Customization Use the MakerWorld Customizer. All parameters are grouped and annotated. View - view: funnel for the printable model, cross_section to preview a cutaway - cross_section_angle: angle of the cutting plane, degrees (cross_section view only) Funnel Dimensions - diameter_1: exterior diameter at the spout tip (bottom-most point), including any vent rib bulge (mm) - height_1: height of the tapered section from diameter_1 up to diameter_2 (mm) - diameter_2: exterior diameter at the first midpoint, including any vent rib bulge (mm) - height_2: height of the tapered section from diameter_2 up to diameter_3 (mm) - diameter_3: exterior diameter at the second midpoint, including any vent rib bulge (mm) - height_3: height of the tapered section from diameter_3 up to diameter_4 (mm) - diameter_4: exterior diameter at the top opening, including any vent rib bulge (mm) - wall_thickness: thickness of the funnel wall (mm) Rim - add_rim: add a flat rim flange around the top opening - rim_added_diameter: how much wider the rim flange's diameter is than the top opening (mm) Vent Ribs - add_vent_ribs: add vent ribs along the wall for fast, glug-free pouring (leave this on unless you have a specific reason to print a plain smooth cone) - vent_rib_count: number of vent ribs, evenly spaced around the circumference - vent_rib_width: width (diameter) of each vent rib's round cross-section (mm) Handle - add_handle: add a flat handle with a hanging hole, attached at the rim - handle_length: how far the handle extends outward from the rim (mm) - handle_width: width of the handle, and diameter of its rounded ends (mm) - handle_hole_diameter: diameter of the hanging hole (mm) - handle_angle: angle around the funnel where the handle is placed Why Fast Flow Every funnel I could find, printable or store-bought, seals against a bottle neck so tightly that air can't get past the liquid, which is exactly what causes the glug-glug-glug and slows the pour to a crawl. This design's vent ribs run the full length of the funnel wall, from spout tip to rim, so they hold the neck open just enough for air to escape the whole time liquid is flowing. That's the actual purpose of this project; the parametric taper, rim, and handle are all built around that one goal. Since I couldn't find a parametric fast-flow funnel anywhere else, this one is meant to fill that gap, so pull the sliders to whatever size and shape you need and it'll still pour fast. Shaping Notes Since all three tapered segments blend together with matching tangents at every diameter, you can make diameter_2 or diameter_3 larger than their neighbors on either side for a bulged, hourglass, or barrel shape instead of a plain cone, with no added kink or fillet needed to keep the curve smooth. Setting diameter_2 and diameter_3 equal to diameter_4 (a common case) collapses the middle section into a straight-sided neck between two tapers.

I love this model because it is easier to push, stronger, and more comfortable to hold than many commercial models I've bought in stores. I've gone through 23 iterations of the fan blade, and I made an Onshape Featurescript for it. It hits 6.525 revolutions per squeeze of the fan blade, so that's about 870-900 rpm. It creates a noticeable breeze even from a more relaxed distance so you don't have to hold it right in front of your face. List of Materials 85g of filament A 6.5x22mm extension spring (the place I bought it from is now unavailable, so any extension spring that's around 20mm long and < 9mm OD will work, but it may be harder to push in or slower to come out) 3 M3x8 self-tapping flat head screws Oil lubricant (Super Lube Multi-Purpose Synthetic Oil) Printing Make sure your filament is dry because if the axles for the gears have too much stringing, then they will turn less smoothly, and the fan blade won't work as efficiently. Also, the fan blade is using a layer height of 0.14mm, so don't mix it with the other objects, which use a layer height of 0.20mm. Assembly Confirm the spring's loops are in the correct position; make sure one of the loops of the spring is perpendicular to the coil and the other side is separated into a single cord, not a closed loop. I had to separate it myself and do some finicking to make the coil sit flat with the loop flat on the bottom. Put the spring in the tiny hole in the pusher part. Oil the big hole (the rotation axle) on the pusher part and then put it in the frame. Put in the gears in the order of the numbers in the picture, oiling the center hole and the teeth as you go. Put on the top cover, then the fan blade. Make sure the blade is pushed down until it is almost touching the frame. Screw it in (self-tapping), and then flip the whole thing over and screw in the bottom-most hole that's farthest from the blade. Screw in the hole on the middle-left, and only screw it in a tiny bit or the handle will be very hard to push in; the screw's top can even be flush with the bottom of the frame. If the model is hard to push in, the most likely reason is that this screw is screwed in too much. Happy printing!

model_name: Customizable Gridfinity Socket Holder with Text
description: I am still working on a adding Gridfinity to my toolboxes, and came across some specialized socket sets, one ratchets down like a drill, and the other was a Husky Passthrough Ratchet set. Problem was there wasn't really any Gridfinity holders for them. Especially with adding text like I needed for the socket set. So I decided to do a custom design via OpenSCAD that lets me define all the socket diameters (not the socket size) and in addition I can define text to match. The set can be as large or small as you like, the only real limitation is that I limited to two row (once I figure the math out, I may expand that). The nice thing about it, the script autosizes to standard grids, based on the diameters and text. So if the diameters and Grids edge into a wider or longer grid pattern, it sizes it for you. You can also play with some of the parameters to tighten that up, if needed. Need to do oversized sockets, here is the script. Need to do a set no one else has, here is your chance. So here are the parameters you can modify, also please read the notes, as they help to understand the script: Socket Diameters: a comma separated list of diameters of each socket in the set, not the size but the actual diameter in mm. (add 1 for variances in printers. Socket Depth: how far down do you want the socket to sit, when placed in the holder. Going too deep will cause the Height units to be limited. Socket to Socket Separation: when placing the sockets in the patter how far edge to edge. Making this smaller my reduce the X grid size. Number of Rows: the list can be split it two (if even), so that the second part of the list wraps under the first. See notes. Tray Height: how many Gridfinity 1U (7mm) units. The tray will always have a lip (so include that). Also because of socket depth, you may not be able to select below a certain size. Margin X: minimum margin between left and right walls, this may increase if the spacing requires it. Margin Y: minimum margin between top and bottom walls, this is also used if there are two rows to separate them. Socket Text: a comma separated list of text that will go under the socket holes. If the field is left blank no text is added, if there is text the number of items in the list must match the number of socket diameters list. Font Size: a set of predefined font sizes to choose from (the font is not selectable at this time). Arial Bold was chosen as it worked the best, with smaller fonts. Raised Text: do you want the text raised or embedded in the holder. Text Color: what color should the text be, you may need to do some painting on other spaces like the lip. Here are some examples of dia/text combinations. Example 1: The orange holder was done with no text, and the diameters looked like this. [32.5, 31.5, 27.7, 26.6, 25.2], the text field was empty. Single row was selected. Example 2: The yellow box with the wire strippers [23.5, 23.5, 23.5, 23.5, 23.5, 23.5], Text [8 awg, 10awg, 12awg, 14awg, sp, Cut], notice they are all the same diameter and the text is under this]. Since the set was even, I selected 2 rows so it wrapped it around (check the text). This also could have been done as a single row. Example 3: The Husky socket set, the diameters were [28, 25.2, 25, 24, 23, 20, 20, 20, 25, 24, 24, 23, 20, 20, 20, 20], and the text was [3/4, 11/16, 3", 5/8, 3/16, 1/2, 7/16, 3/8, 17, 16, 15, 14, 13, 12, 11, 10]. Notice how it goes high to low and second set also goes high to low. Have SAE on top, Metric on the bottom. Two rows were selected, it could have been done on one, but that would be very long. The only thing about the model is that the library adds colors to the lip and sides (I have not figured out how to remove them yet). So you will either need to keep them, color them, or select your own. Let me know if you run into any issues, I tested the combinations, but may have missed something. If you get a chance checkout some of my other organization items ( https://makerworld.com/en/collections/17112635-gridfinity ) or ( https://makerworld.com/en/collections/16603099-multiboard-hsw-opengrid ).

description: SnapCore – Parametric Mono Latch & Single Hinge SnapBox See here for double hinge version for your larger box needs - Please note this version has inserts, if you wish it to be just the box no need to print the inserts Introducing SnapCore – a fully parametric mono-latch storage box designed from the ground up to be simple, strong, and highly customizable. description: Description A fully parametric vial storage solution for 10ml crimp-top vials. Unlike 3ml vials, 10ml vials vary noticeably between suppliers — both diameter and height are Customizer settings from the start, so measure your own vials with calipers before printing. A validated alternate preset is included below. Includes optional label windows so you can read vial labels without opening the lid. Two ways to print: Ready-to-print profiles for common quantities — just load the plate you need and hit print Parametric OpenSCAD file for any custom configuration your storage needs require Need a Different Size or Vial? Use the Parametric File The included OpenSCAD file lets you generate any configuration using the built-in Customizer. Layout is controlled by vials_per_row and num_rows, up to 8x8 (64 vials) — the largest grid that fits a 256mm build plate at default vial size. Vial diameter and height are fully adjustable, so this same file works with 10ml vials from any supplier. Validated Vial Presets Default: 22.01mm diameter × 54.0mm tall Alternate (short/wide): 24.02mm diameter × 49.55mm tall Customizer Settings Vial Size vial_od — vial body diameter, measured at the widest point of the straight wall. Measure YOUR vials first — 10ml vials are not standardized across suppliers vial_h — total vial height, from the base to the top of the cap slot_depth_f — how deep the vial sinks into its pocket, as a share of its height. Default 0.65 leaves the cap and neck clear of the pocket Layout vials_per_row — number of vials per row (1–8) num_rows — number of rows (1–8) render_part — set to base , lid , or both Vial Windows show_windows — turns label windows on or off. On by default, so you can read vial labels without opening the lid. Note: the window cutout has a flat top edge that may need supports depending on your slicer/printer — check the slicer preview before printing, or turn this off to avoid the issue entirely Fit Tuning clearance — increases vial pocket diameter. Start at 0.5mm, adjust in 0.05mm steps if vials fit too tightly lid_gap_mode — auto or manual. Auto (default) widens the gap on small prints, which are stiffer and can squeak going on, and tightens it on larger ones. Set to manual to force an exact value lid_gap_manual — the gap used only when lid_gap_mode is set to manual Snap Feel snap_p — snap tab protrusion. 1.2mm is the PETG starting point (0.8mm is too soft for PETG at this scale) snap_z — tab position, affects how easy the lid is to pop off snap_tip_ratio — ramp shape. Lower = gentler on/off feel Recommended Materials PETG — recommended for freezer or long-term cold storage. Handles repeated freeze/thaw cycles without becoming brittle. Use snap_p of 1.2mm or higher. PLA — becomes brittle at freezer temperatures; fine for room-temperature storage or test prints only Printing Tips No supports required for the base or lid geometry itself — but if show_windows is on, check your slicer preview: the flat top edge of each window opening may need light supports depending on your printer and settings 15% infill or higher works fine — these are solid prints that don't need to be dense Print base and lid separately or use both to lay them out side by side automatically Always measure your vials and do a small test print (2x1) first before committing to a large grid — 10ml vial dimensions are not standardized Grids larger than 8x8 are possible in the SCAD file directly, but check your build plate size first Design Notes Designed in OpenSCAD, sharing the same snap-lid mechanism as the 3ml Parametric Peptide Vial Holder — a finger lift tab and chamfered entry for smooth on/off feel. Since 10ml vials vary significantly by supplier, this model was built parametric from the ground up rather than fit to one specific vial.

Planetary Gear Screwdriver A compact, dual-mode mechanical screwdriver powered by an internal 4:1 planetary gear system! Key Features: Dual-Mode Operation: Push the front lock back for high-speed driving (4 turns per single rotation of the handle), perfect for quickly running down long threads. Slide the lock forward to engage high-torque mode for final tightening. Two Build Options: Choose between the full-hardware version using standard 604/6702 bearings and 3x20 mm dowel pins, or the 100% printable version that requires only a single standard M3 screw! Complete PDF Assembly Manual: Step-by-step PDF instructions are attached below for both hardware and non-hardware builds, complete with troubleshooting tips. How It Works & How to Use It The screwdriver has two modes. For fast tightening or unscrewing, make sure the lock piece is in the back position. Holding the main body part with one hand and twisting the back piece will cause the front bit holder to rotate fast with a ratio of 4:1 (one turn of the back will cause the front to spin 4 times). This mode is ideal for long threaded screws to tighten them quickly. For final tightening or high-torque mode, engage the lock at the front by pushing the lock piece into the front position. This will lock the bit axle piece to the main handle piece so you can use it like a regular screwdriver. Printing Instructions & Parts Read all about how to print this model and what extra parts you'll need. Parts As mentioned before, there are two variants, and I've provided print profiles for both. You can also start with the no-hardware version and simply reprint a few parts later if you decide to build the full version, the main parts are completely compatible. Check the Kits and Parts section below to see what hardware is needed. In the picture below: Left: Parts used in both variants Middle: Extra parts required for the hardware version Right: Parts unique to the non-hardware variant Filaments & Settings The print profiles include the exact settings that worked best for me. For materials, I recommend PLA, PETG, or ABS. I would stay away from fiber-filled or silk filaments: fiber-filled materials can leave rough surfaces, and silk filaments tend to swell, making it harder to reproduce exact dimensions and tight tolerances. Assembly Check out the exploded view to get an idea of how everything goes together. For detailed step-by-step instructions, check the attached PDFs! Ten swappable texture rollers for play dough, air-dry clay, fondant and salt dough. Each roller is 150mm long and 30mm across with a bold 1.2mm raised pattern that stamps deep, crisp impressions in one easy pass. Every roller shares the same 8.6mm centre bore and spins freely on the included printed axle, held by two press-fit end caps, so you can swap patterns in seconds. Print them upright with no supports, one colour each, and build the whole collection over time. Dots - A field of 130 raised domes in neat staggered rows. The pattern has no direction, so it is the most forgiving roller of the set: roll it any way you like and the polka dots always line up. A great first print. Chevron - Five bands of bold zigzag arrows wrapping the barrel. Roll parallel passes and the chevrons tile into a striking knitted-jumper texture across the whole slab. Rings - Clean pinstripe rings with little dash rows between them, like it came off a lathe. Perfect for banded borders, ruled lines and anywhere you want a tidy, orderly finish. Daisy - Thirty-five little five-petal daisies scattered in offset rows. Rolls a soft floral wallpaper pattern that looks brilliant pressed into fondant or pastel clay. Weave - Classic basketweave with alternating pairs of bars, just like a woven pie crust. Turns any flat slab of clay into an instant wicker texture, and it feels great to roll. Hearts - Rows of chunky hearts marching around the barrel in offset ranks. The go-to roller for Valentine biscuits, love-note clay tags and general cuteness. Stripes - Six candy stripes spiralling the full length of the roller. Because the stripes are helical, they lay down as continuous diagonal lines for as long as you keep rolling, which is oddly satisfying. Night - Crescent moons alternating with sparkle stars in a checkerboard sky. Made for bedtime-themed play dough sessions and space-mad kids. Waves - Rippling zigzag wave bands rolling around the barrel. Reads as water, bunting or mountain ranges depending on which way up your imagination is holding it. Honeycomb - An offset grid of hexagon outlines like a slice of beehive. Pairs perfectly with bee cutters, and makes a great all-over texture for hex-tile fans. Axle kit One 7.9mm rod with a printing flat and two press-fit end caps. Drop any roller on the rod, push the caps on the ends, and the roller spins freely with 0.35mm of running clearance while your hands stay still. description: Ever needed a very specific binding post or Chicago screw size that just doesn't exist in hardware stores, or had 3D-printed threads snap off right at the head? Your door handles is loose and you don't want to go all the way to the hardware store just for one screw ? I designed this fully parametric OpenSCAD generator to create clean, robust, and perfectly fitting Chicago screws in seconds. Whether you're binding leatherwork, making custom album covers, assembling PCB stacks, or fixing door handles , you can generate the exact dimensions you need. ✨ Key Features Full ISO Metric Range: Standard sizes plus all intermediate options (M1.6, M2, M2.5, M3, M3.5, M4, M4.5, M5, M6, M7, M8, M9, M10, and M12) . Anti-Snap Reinforcement: Features a 45° conical fillet right at the neck junction. No more snapped screw heads when tightening! Independent Head Sizes: Adjust the male and female head diameters separately to fit flush into any counterbore. Smart Wall Thickness: Customize the female barrel wall thickness (with automated safety limits so it never prints too thin) . Super Fast & Manifold Mesh: Generated with pure mathematical polyhedrons in OpenSCAD, no CGAL rendering errors, no freezing, and instant STL export! 🎛️ Fully Customizable Parameters Using MakerWorld’s online Parametric Model Maker or OpenSCAD , you can tweak the following settings to get a 100% tailor-made fit: Thread Size (Thread_Size): Pick any standard metric thread from M1.6 to M12 . The script automatically handles ISO pitch calculations and depth for you. Fit Clearance (Clearance): Adjust the tolerance between threads (default 0.15 mm ). Increase slightly if your printer over-extrudes, or tighten it up for a snug precision fit (0.20 is a good compromise if 0.15 fails) . Head Diameters (Male_Head_Diameter & Female_Head_Diameter): Modify each head size independently so they match your project’s counterbore holes or clamping surface area. Lengths (Female_Length & Male_Length): Set the exact barrel depth and threaded rod length to perfectly fit your door backplate or material stack thickness. Barrel Wall Thickness (Female_Wall_Thickness): Reinforce the female post for heavy-duty mechanical strain. The script includes a built-in safety limit so the walls never print dangerously thin. Display Mode (Display): Render both parts side-by-side, or isolate just the female post or male screw if you need to re-print a single replacement part! 🖨️ Recommended Print Settings To ensure the threads turn smoothly right off the build plate without binding, here are my tried-and-tested slicer settings : Orientation: Print both parts vertically, heads flat on the bed. Supports: None needed! The thread angles print cleanly in mid-air. Wall Generator: Arachne (Highly Recommended for crisp thread detail) . Layer Height: 0.12 mm or 0.08 mm (finer layers = smoother threads) . Wall Loops: 4 to 5 walls (This makes the male threaded rod almost 100% solid plastic). Outer Wall Speed: Slow down to 40–50 mm/s for sharp thread profiles. Seam Position: Random (Prevents a single seam line from creating a bump along the threads). 💡 Pro Tip If your printer extrudes slightly heavy, you can adjust the Clearance parameter right in the script (default is 0.15 mm) , or use X-Y Hole Compensation (+0.05 mm) in your slicer. After printing, give the screw a quick run in and out with a screwdriver to smooth out any tiny layer lines! Enjoy the model, and happy printing! description: An adjustable shower head holder you can print at home. The head snaps into position with a satisfying click, so you can tilt it up or down and it stays exactly where you left it — no sagging, no re-adjusting mid-shower. WHY THIS ONE - Click-stop angle adjustment — a spring-loaded detent mechanism holds each position firmly, and lets you change it with one hand. - Universal fit — works on shower rails from 18 to 24 mm thanks to the clamping knob, so you don't need to measure before printing. - Replaces broken holders — most stock holders crack or lose their grip over time. This one is fully printable and repairable. - Simple hardware — just one screw and one nut, both easy to find. - Fully printable in PLA. Place the springs into their pockets in the fixed part. 2. Line up the rotating part (the fork that holds the shower head) with the fixed part, so the teeth on both halves meet. 3. Push the screw through the centre of both parts — this is the pivot the mechanism turns on. 4. Fit the self-locking nut on the other side and tighten it until the two halves are held together but can still rotate. Don't overtighten: the nut sets how firm the click feels, so adjust it to taste. 5. Slide the assembly onto your shower rail through the open U-shaped channel. 6. Screw on the clamping knob and tighten by hand until the holder sits firmly on the rail. No tools needed. description: Ultimate Maker Station | Soldering & Heat-Set Insert Organizer Get your workbench organized! This multi-functional maker station is specifically designed to keep your soldering tips, heat-set insert tools, and adapters neatly sorted and stored. This ensures your most important inserts are always perfectly at hand, while the integrated drawer and clever storage tray provide practical space for accessories. Key Features & Highlights: TS100 / TS101 Compatible: Features 7 precision-fit slots to keep your most important soldering tips organized and right within arm's reach. Storage for Ruthex Heat-Set Insert Tool: Offers 7 perfectly matched slots for sorted storage of the heat-set insert tool kit (M2 to M8), plus a separate slot for the corresponding adapter. Secure Soldering Iron Rest: An integrated holder designed to safely hold your soldering iron at a clean angle during work breaks. End Stop (Prevents Sliding): A built-in physical stop at the end of the rest ensures the tool stays securely in place and cannot slide off. Soldering Sponge Compartment: A custom-made compartment (55 mm x 70 mm x 13 mm deep) that is perfectly dimensioned. Fits the soldering sponge from Reichelt electronik, for example: https://www.reichelt.de/de/de/shop/produkt/schwamm_nassreinigung-16984 Or as an alternative, this sponge from Amazon: https://www.amazon.de/dp/B0F6JR44WT Handy Parts Tray: A small, semi-circular recess between the sponge compartment and the heat-set slots. Ideal for keeping the currently needed threaded inserts handy and ready while working. Magnetic Snap-In Drawer: Equipped with a hidden lower drawer for extra small parts. It uses four 3x6 mm magnets for a secure, satisfying snap-in closure. Slip-Resistant Base: The bottom features four recesses (10.5 mm diameter, 1.5 mm depth). Silicone or rubber feet can be glued in here to guarantee the station optimal stability and slip resistance on your workbench. Print Settings & Recommendations: Available Print Profiles: I have uploaded two fully pre-configured dual-material print profiles for you. In both profiles, the other material is used as an easily removable support interface to guarantee flawless overhang surfaces without any post-processing: Profile 1 (Recommended): PETG Main Body + PLA Support Interface (Higher heat resistance near the soldering iron) Profile 2: PLA Main Body + PETG Support Interface (The ideal alternative for pure PLA printing) Layer Height: 0.20 mm (Standard). Supports: Optimally configured in both profiles (approx. 25.43 g of support material). You do not need to change anything in the slicer! 💡 Note on Slicer Warning: Don't worry if your slicer displays a warning about mixing PLA and PETG when opening the file. This is completely normal and fully intended! The software is just being overly cautious, but we are specifically taking advantage of the fact that these materials don't stick to each other to create the perfect, easy-to-remove support interface. You can safely ignore the warning and confidently hit print. Assembly: Simply print and remove the support structures—absolutely no post-processing is required after that! Then press the four 3x6 mm magnets into the drawer mechanism. IMPORTANT: Before gluing or pressing them in, make absolutely sure the polarity of the magnets is correct so that the drawer and housing attract each other and don't repel! If the magnets sit a bit too loose (as was the case for me), they can easily be secured with a drop of super glue. (Optionally attach the four rubber feet to the bottom). That's it—enjoy your tidy workspace! Happy printing! Feel free to leave a boost or post your makes in the comments—I’d love to see your setups!

Parametrischer DIN-Schienen-Adapter (Hutschiene) — Smart-Home, Relais, Netzteile… d.h. alles was man gerne an diese genormten Schienen befestigen möchte. Damit befestigst du beliebige Komponenten (Smart-Home-Module, Relais, Shelly, ESP, Netzteile, Klemmen, Sensoren …) sauber im Schaltschrank oder Verteiler. Das Lochbild ist bewusst flexibel gehalten, damit fast jedes Bauteil verschraubt oder mit Kabelbindern an einer DIN / Hutschiene fixiert werden kann. Highlights DIN-Normen als Pull-down — die passende Schiene einfach im Customizer wählen (DIN EN 60715): TH 35 × 7.5 (Standard), TH 35 × 15 (schwere Lasten), TH 15 × 5.5 (Miniatur) oder Benutzerdefiniert . Zwei Klemm-Mechanismen Snap-on (Federclip) — auf die Schiene aufrasten, mit Lösehebel wieder abnehmbar. Slide-on (starr) — von der Seite aufschieben, maximal steif für schwere Bauteile. Flexibles Montage-Muster — Lochraster (exakte Anzahl Spalten × Reihen), Langlöcher, beides kombiniert, oder Blankoplatte. Bei beides sitzen die Bohrlöcher in der Mitte , die Langlöcher an den Seiten . Zusätzlich Kabelbinder-Schlitze an den Enden. DIN-Schienen-Normen (recherchiert) Maße nach DIN EN 60715:2018 (löste EN 50022 / 50045 ab): Norm (Auswahl) Gesamtbreite Höhe/Tiefe Hutbreite Blechdicke typische Nutzung TH 35 × 7.5 35 mm 7.5 mm 27 mm 1.0 mm Standard — Relais, Automaten, Smart-Home TH 35 × 15 35 mm 15 mm 27 mm 1.5 mm schwere/größere Geräte TH 15 × 5.5 15 mm 5.5 mm 10.5 mm 1.0 mm Miniatur / Reihenklemmen Benutzerdefiniert frei frei — — Sonderprofile Hinweis: Die G-Schiene (G 32, EN 50035) hat ein grundlegend anderes Clip-Prinzip (Untergriff von innen) und ist bewusst nicht enthalten — dieser Adapter deckt die weit verbreitete Hutschienen-Familie (TH/Top-Hat) ab, die ~95 % aller Smart-Home- und Elektronik-Anwendungen abdeckt. Quellen: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DIN_rail · de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tragschiene Standard-Maße Eigenschaft Wert Platte (B × L × H) 48 × 45 × 3 mm Schiene TH 35 × 7.5 Klemm-Modus Snap-on (Federclip) Lochbild Raster (M3-frei, Ø 3.4 mm) + Kabelbinder-Schlitze Alle Werte sind im Customizer anpassbar. Klemm-Modi im Vergleich Snap-on (Federclip) — eine Wand ist fix, die andere federt über einen dünnen Federhals aus und rastet über die Schienenkante. Ein Lösehebel oben erlaubt das Abnehmen mit dem Finger/Schraubendreher. Ideal für Module, die man wieder abnehmen will. Slide-on (starr) — beide Wände starr; der Adapter wird seitlich auf die Schiene geschoben. Maximale Steifigkeit für schwere Bauteile (z. B. Netzteile), kein Federbruch möglich. Montage — so wird's zusammengebaut Der Adapter macht nicht-DIN-Geräte hutschienentauglich . Aufbau von der Wand nach außen: Wand → DIN-Hutschiene → Clip/Schenkel → Grundplatte → dein Gerät Gerät anschrauben — dein Bauteil auf die Montagefläche (die ebene Seite ohne Clip) legen und mit Senkkopfschrauben festschrauben. Die Senkfasen liegen auf der Montageseite , d. h. die Köpfe sitzen bündig, das Gerät liegt plan auf, und die Clip-/Schienenseite bleibt völlig flach . Auf die Schiene setzen — die Baugruppe auf die Hutschiene aufrasten (Snap-on, mit Lösehebel wieder abnehmbar) oder von der Seite aufschieben (Slide-on). :warning: Schraubenlänge beachten: Die Löcher liegen mittig über dem Schienenkanal. Verwende kurze Schrauben (die im Gerät bzw. in Gewindeeinsätzen/Standoffs greifen), damit die Spitze nicht auf der Clip-Seite herausragt und im eingebauten Zustand an die Schiene stößt. Bei 3 mm Platte genügen Fasentiefe (~1.4 mm) + etwas Gewinde ins Gerät. DIN-Schienen-Norm — rail_norm (Pull-down). Bei Benutzerdefiniert : custom_rail_width, custom_rail_depth. Klemm-Mechanismus — clip_mode (snap/slide), wall_thickness, spring_wall_thickness, hook_catch (Untergriff), hook_height, fit_clearance (Spiel), neck_thickness (Federhals), release_lever + lever_height. Grundplatte — plate_width (quer zur Schiene), plate_length (entlang der Schiene), plate_thickness, corner_radius. Montage-Muster — mount_pattern (none / grid / slots / grid+slots), hole_cols × hole_rows (Anzahl Bohrlöcher), hole_diameter, hole_margin, countersink (Senkung für Senkkopfschrauben, auf der Montageseite), slot_count / slot_width / slot_length (Langlöcher), cable_tie_slots + tie_slot_width / tie_slot_length. Bei beides (grid+slots) liegen die Bohrlöcher in der Mitte , die Langlöcher an den Seiten der Mittelzone — überlappungsfrei. Alle Löcher bleiben zwischen den Klemmwänden (nie unter einem Schenkel → volle Druckstabilität). Tipp Fein-Fit: Klemmt der Clip zu stramm, fit_clearance in 0.1-Schritten erhöhen. Sitzt er zu locker, verringern. Rastet der Snap-Clip schwer ein, neck_thickness reduzieren (dünnerer Hals = leichter federnd). Druck-Empfehlungen Das Modell ist bereits korrekt ausgerichtet — bitte so drucken, wie es geladen wird: Orientierung: Montagefläche unten auf dem Bett, DIN-Clip nach oben. So entsteht eine glatte Sichtfläche, und die Haken haben nur kurze, selbsttragende 45°-Überhänge. Stützen: nicht nötig . Brim: 5–8 mm empfohlen — die schmalen, hohen Klemmwände (v. a. bei TH 35 × 15 und bei ABS/ASA/CF) neigen sonst zum Ablösen/Warping. Brim & Stützen stellst du selbst in Bambu Studio ein. Einstellung Empfehlung Schichthöhe 0.2 mm (0.16 mm für feinere Haken) Wände / Perimeter ≥ 4 (Klemmwände sind tragend) Top / Bottom Layer ≥ 4 Infill 40–60 % (Gyroid), tragende Teile Brim 5–8 mm Stützen keine Filament-Empfehlung (Stabilität & Wärme) DIN-Adapter tragen oft warme Bauteile (Netzteile, Relais) im geschlossenen Schaltschrank . Deshalb zählen Wärmeformbeständigkeit und Steifigkeit/Maßhaltigkeit mehr als bei Deko-Drucken. Richtwerte (Quelle: Simplify3D Materials Guide, Bambu Lab): Filament Wärmeformbest. (ca.) Steifigkeit Zähigkeit Eignung PLA / PLA+ ~50–60 °C hoch spröde nur kühle Umgebung / Testdruck PETG ~70–75 °C mittel hoch guter Allrounder, ideal für Snap-Clip ABS / ASA ~95–100 °C mittel hoch warme Schränke (ASA zusätzlich UV-fest) PC (Polycarbonat) ~110–120 °C hoch sehr hoch Hochlast + Hitze (schwer zu drucken) PA (Nylon) ~80–95 °C mittel sehr hoch zähe, langlebige Federclips PLA-CF ~55–65 °C sehr hoch spröder steife Blankoplatte, aber nur kühl PETG-CF ~75–80 °C sehr hoch mittel Empfehlung: steif + wärmestabil PA-CF / PET-CF ~120–180 °C (HDT) sehr hoch mittel Profi: max. Steifigkeit + Hitze Sind CF-Filamente sinnvoll? — Ja, aber gezielt Carbonfaser (CF) erhöht Steifigkeit und Maßhaltigkeit , reduziert Verzug (Warping) und hebt die Wärmeformbeständigkeit an. Das ist genau richtig für die Trägerplatte , damit sie sich unter Last (z. B. Netzteil) nicht durchbiegt. Aber: CF macht das Material spröder . Der dünne, wiederholt biegende Federclip (Snap-on) hält mit einem zähen Kunststoff länger. Daraus folgt: Slide-on (starr, keine Feder): → CF-Filament ideal (PETG-CF / PA-CF) = maximale Steifigkeit. Snap-on (Federclip): → PETG oder PA / PA-CF = genug Steifigkeit und Federzähigkeit. Reines PLA-CF hier meiden (der Federhals kann brechen). Beste Allround-Wahl: PETG-CF für die Platte + Snap-Clip, oder PETG wenn nur einer. Düse: CF/Glasfaser sind abrasiv → gehärtete Stahldüse nötig. Die Bambu Lab H2C, P2S und P1S haben serienmäßig gehärtete Düsen und sind CF-tauglich. CF-Filamente vor dem Druck trocknen . Lizenz & Autor Autor: Jan Tiedemann · 2026 · Lizenz CC BY 4.0 . The original version has its internal structure exposed. * Add angle limit to the interior of the rotating shaft A limit stop is incorporated inside the rotating shaft to maintain a consistent angle when pressed. The original version has no limit on the rotation axis, and it rotates randomly when pressed. *Gear cover with concealed buckle locking The gear cover features a concealed buckle design, which locks with a single press. The original version is complex to install, requiring materials to be inserted and fixed. Due to printing tolerances, it is sometimes difficult to insert them. * The innovative addition of a ring buckle allows for more playful ways to use it, and it can even be rotated without the need for a rubber band (completely without any additional accessories) The original version does not have this function *Introducing a smaller version with a diameter of 5cm. Welcome to The Crystal Mines , an original PlayGrid-compatible board game where every expedition is different. Venture deep into an ancient crystal cave filled with valuable ores, unstable tunnels, hidden dangers, and one enormous Crystal Heart at its center. Your goal is simple: gather as many valuable crystals as you can and escape before the mine becomes too dangerous. Unlike traditional board games, The Crystal Mines features a changing battlefield. Players physically mine crystal deposits, remove ore from the board, and replace them with empty tiles, permanently changing the map as the game progresses. Every crystal collected makes the cave feel a little more depleted—and every decision becomes more important. Scattered throughout the mine are colorful crystal veins, rocky obstacles, mine carts, wooden bridges, ladders, water crossings, and explosive TNT. These environmental features create countless strategic choices as you explore the cave. Do you take the shortest path? Risk using explosives? Race another player to a valuable crystal deposit? Or head back to safety before disaster strikes? At the center of the cave lies the massive Crystal Heart . While it contains incredible value, disturbing the heart may trigger catastrophic consequences. Stay too long underground, and you may lose everything you've collected. Every turn becomes a balance between greed and survival. To keep the game fresh, every match uses a procedurally generated map , meaning no two games are ever exactly alike. Different crystal locations, obstacles, pathways, and hazards create a new puzzle every time you play. description: Un simpatico T-Rex puzzle 3D facile da montare, educativo e perfetto per stimolare creatività, logica e manualità nei bambini. Pensato per unire gioco, creatività e manualità in un modello semplice, accattivante e piacevole da assemblare. Il modello è composto da singoli pezzi che si incastrano tra loro in modo intuitivo. Una volta assemblato, il T-Rex si sostiene in piedi, diventando sia un piccolo puzzle educativo sia un simpatico personaggio decorativo per camerette, scuole, asili o spazi gioco. Il design è pensato per essere adatto ai bambini: forme morbide, aspetto simpatico, sorriso inciso, dettagli scavati e dentini ricavati direttamente nel modello, senza necessità di parti aggiuntive o colori separati. Il modello è anche scalabile a piacere : puoi aumentare o ridurre le dimensioni in base alle tue preferenze, allo spazio disponibile o all’utilizzo che vuoi farne. Aumentando la scala, il T-Rex diventa più grande e scenografico; riducendola, diventa più compatto e veloce da stampare. Anche il riempimento/infill può essere aumentato per rendere i pezzi più robusti e resistenti, soprattutto se il puzzle viene utilizzato spesso. Con un infill più basso, invece, si ottiene una stampa più veloce e leggera. A dimensioni standard, il modello è pensato per una stampa rapida , indicativamente in circa 2 ore , a seconda della stampante, del materiale, della velocità, dell’altezza layer e delle impostazioni utilizzate. Consigliato in PLA , anche con piatto texturizzato / PEI texturizzato , per ottenere una finitura più pulita, piacevole al tatto e dall’aspetto più professionale. La faccia anteriore del modello risulta particolarmente gradevole se stampata a contatto con il piatto texturizzato. description: Classic Joker Display Figure (No AMS) Every model has a story. This one is dedicated to my son, Alexander . Alexander has always loved the Joker and already had an amazing Batman on his shelf. Naturally, he wanted Batman to have his greatest rival standing beside him. I found an excellent Batman model here: Batman Display Figure But after searching for quite a while, I couldn't find a Batman: The Animated Series (DCAU) inspired Joker that was designed as a No AMS multi-part build. So... I decided to make one. What started as "I'll just make Alexander a Joker" quickly turned into a month-long journey of learning Blender. Along the way I learned mesh restoration, topology cleanup, Booleans, part engineering, hidden seams, and multi-part assembly workflows. The final model you're downloading is the result of that entire learning process. Rather than relying on an AMS, every visible color is modeled as its own individual printable component. This allows clean color transitions with virtually no purge waste while making the model accessible to anyone with a standard single-extruder printer. Features 🃏 No AMS Required 🎨 Individual color-separated parts 🔧 Engineered for straightforward assembly 📏 Approximately 300 mm (30 cm) tall 🖨 Optimized for FDM printing 🧩 Hidden seams and alignment features Printing Tips Print each component using its intended filament color. Dry-fit parts before applying glue. A small amount of CA glue is recommended for final assembly. Assemble from the torso outward for the easiest alignment. I'd recommend using a .2 nozzle for the eyes. A Personal Note This model represents far more than just a printable figure. It marks the beginning of a workflow I've been developing to transform AI-generated foundation meshes into engineered, printable multi-part kits through extensive manual work in Blender. Most importantly, it gave me the opportunity to build something special for my son. If your finished Joker ends up standing next to Batman on your shelf too, I'd love to see a photo of your build. Happy Printing! 🖖 Noblesite

description: D20 Spinner – The Wheel of Fate Spin your destiny! Inspired by the satisfying feel of a fidget spinner and the iconic wheel from The Price Is Right , this D20 spinner brings a little game show excitement to every dice roll. Ensure both bearings are fully seated and spin freely. Install the Wheel Magnets Press-fit the 10 magnets into the wheel. Important: All magnets must be installed with the same polarity facing outward . Double-check the orientation before pressing each magnet into place. Attach the Side Walls Position the two side walls on either side of the wheel assembly, ensuring the magnet wall is on the correct side. Compatible switches can be purchased here: AliExpress: https://www.aliexpress.com/wholesale?SearchText=blue+mx+mechanical+keyboard+switches You can also experiment with other MX-compatible switches , including: 🔵 Blue – Loud, tactile click (recommended) 🟤 Brown – Quiet tactile bump 🔴 Red – Smooth linear press ⚫ Black – Heavier linear press 🟢 Green – Extra-heavy tactile click Each switch type gives the clicker a different feel, allowing you to customise the clicking experience to suit your preference. Print the letters face-up for the cleanest finish. Important Print Notes ⚠️ The snap-fit connection has been designed with tight tolerances to provide a secure fit. For the best results: Ensure your printer is properly calibrated. Check your flow/extrusion multiplier. Verify your dimensional accuracy. Avoid over-extrusion. Remove any elephant's foot before assembly if necessary. A well-calibrated printer will produce a satisfying snap fit while still allowing the letters to be swapped with ease. Assembly Carefully remove the two gold metal pins from the bottom of each MX switch using a pair of pliers or side cutters. These electrical contacts are not required for this project. Press the switch firmly into the printed base until it is fully seated. Snap your chosen letter into the top of the base. Connect additional bases together to build names or words of any length. No glue required—everything is designed to snap together securely. The croissant sits on a white paper liner and a tiny wooden cutting board, creating a warm bakery-style display scene. Press the croissant to activate the hidden MX-style mechanical keyboard switch and enjoy a satisfying click with springy feedback. Features Satisfying Clicky Action Press the croissant to enjoy a satisfying clicky fidget experience. The croissant is the main interactive part of the model, while the wooden cutting board base hides the internal switch and supports the clicky mechanism. Classic Croissant Shape The croissant features a rounded curved shape with soft layered details inspired by a classic bakery croissant. The design keeps the main croissant silhouette clear and cute, without making the surface too overly detailed or fragile. Wooden Cutting Board Base Unlike the previous Clicky Bread models that use woven baskets or proofing baskets, this model introduces a tiny wooden cutting board base. The cutting board creates a warm serving scene and gives the model a different display style within the Clicky Bread series. The round hole in the cutting board handle can also be used to attach your own keyring or charm hardware. Paper Liner Detail The white paper liner sits between the croissant and the wooden cutting board. It adds a bakery display feeling, visually separates the golden croissant from the wooden base, and makes the model easier to customize with different color combinations. Desk Toy or Keychain This model can be used in two ways: Desk Toy – place it on your desk and press the croissant whenever you want a small fidget moment. Keychain Charm – attach your own keyring to the hole in the cutting board handle and carry it with you. Both uses are based on the same model. No separate keychain STL is needed. Separate Parts for Easy Color Printing The model is divided into separate printable parts: Croissant Paper Liner Wooden Cutting Board Base Each part can be printed in a different color, so no additional painting is required. A multi-color printer is not necessary. The parts can be printed separately and assembled afterward. Print Profile Options Two print profiles are included. Both profiles create the same final model. The difference is the printing method for the Paper Liner. Standard Print Version This version uses the regular Paper Liner model. Supports are mainly handled by the slicer settings, making it suitable for users who prefer to adjust support settings by themselves. Paper Liner Enhanced Support Version This version includes a pre-designed enhanced support structure for the Paper Liner to help improve printing stability. After printing, the enhanced support structure can be snapped off by hand or carefully trimmed with scissors. The trimmed area will be hidden inside the assembled model, so it does not need to be perfectly smooth. Just make sure not to cut into the actual Paper Liner part. Additional Parts Required One compatible MX-style mechanical keyboard switch is required to create the clicky movement. If you want to use it as a keychain, you will also need your own keyring or suitable keychain hardware. The mechanical switch and keychain hardware are not included with the printable model files. Assembly Install the mechanical keyboard switch into the square hole on the croissant. Insert the paper liner into the slot on the cutting board. Place the croissant onto the cutting board, aligning it with the cross-shaped hole. Press the croissant several times to make sure it moves smoothly and returns properly. If you want to use it as a keychain, attach your own keychain hardware to the hole in the cutting board handle. Printing Notes The croissant, paper liner, and wooden cutting board base are separate parts and can be printed in different colors. Please use the provided print profiles for the recommended orientation and print settings. If your chosen assembly method requires glue, check that all parts fit correctly and make sure the croissant can move freely before applying it. description: Un tenero draghetto puzzle 3D stile Montessori , pensato per unire gioco, creatività e manualità in un modello originale, colorato e divertente da assemblare. Il modello è composto da singoli pezzi che si incastrano tra loro in modo semplice e intuitivo. Una volta assemblato, il draghetto si sostiene anche in piedi, diventando sia un piccolo puzzle educativo sia un simpatico personaggio decorativo per camerette, scuole, asili o spazi gioco. Il design è pensato per essere accattivante e adatto ai bambini: forme morbide, espressione simpatica, ali, coda, zampe e dettagli incisi che rendono il modello riconoscibile e piacevole anche in stampa monocolore. Puoi realizzarlo tutto dello stesso colore, in versione bicolore oppure con più colori diversi per un effetto ancora più creativo. Il modello è anche scalabile a piacere : puoi aumentare o ridurre le dimensioni in base alle tue preferenze, allo spazio disponibile o all’utilizzo che vuoi farne. Aumentando la scala, il draghetto diventa più grande e scenografico; riducendola, diventa più compatto e veloce da stampare. Anche il riempimento/infill può essere aumentato per rendere i pezzi più robusti e resistenti, soprattutto se il puzzle viene utilizzato spesso. Con un infill più basso, invece, si ottiene una stampa più veloce e leggera. A dimensioni standard, il modello è pensato per una stampa semplice, indicativamente in circa 2 ore , a seconda della stampante, del materiale, della velocità, dell’altezza layer e delle impostazioni utilizzate. Consigliato in PLA , anche con piatto texturizzato / PEI texturizzato , per ottenere una finitura più pulita, piacevole al tatto e dall’aspetto più professionale. La faccia anteriore del modello risulta particolarmente gradevole se stampata a contatto con il piatto texturizzato. description: Turn your kid into an excavator. Slide your forearm into the sleeve, grab the roller bar inside the bucket, and dig - the bucket curls on real pivots just like the actual machine. Scoop, lift, dump, repeat. Works just as well in snow as in sand. Why you'll like printing this one: Zero supports, zero glue. Every part prints in its ideal orientation. Everything assembles with a coin or finger. All joints use chunky printed trapezoidal screws - two pivot bolts and one grip axle. Fully serviceable: any part that ever breaks can be reprinted and swapped. Bike-pedal grip. The bucket handle is a free-spinning roller on a fixed axle - comfortable for repeated scooping, and the axle cross-ties the bucket for stiffness. Sand-proof by design. Loose 0.6mm running clearances at every moving joint so grit won't seize it. If it gets crunchy, rinse and go. Parts list (one full toy): 1× sleeve, 1× bucket, 1× grip axle + 1× grip tube, 2× pivot barrels, 3× screws. Print settings: PETG strongly recommended (sun and rough play; PLA gets soft in a hot car). 0.20mm layers, 15% gyroid, 3 walls - use 4 walls on the barrels, screws, and axle if you want better strength. Assembly (about 2 minutes): Hold the grip tube between the bucket cheeks, slide the axle through - its square head seats into the side pocket - and snug a screw into it from the far pocket with a coin. Then set the bucket between the sleeve plates, push a barrel through each side from the outside, and screw a screw into each from inside the bucket. Snug until the head meets the barrel end, then back off 1/8 turn so the bucket swings freely. Optional velcro strap through the floor slots keeps it on smaller arms. Sizing: Default fits smaller adults all the way down to little kids (88 × 78mm forearm opening). Safety: Adult assembly recommended. Not for children under 3 - contains small parts (screws). Check screws for snugness now and then; a tiny dab of glue on the threads makes them permanent.

description: Use a small amount of lubricant oil in the bearings for a smoother experience and a longer spin time. Lubricant oil tubes are included with all Bambu Labs printers. This bearing gear spinner combines two interlocking herringbone gears , each spinning smoothly on its own internal roller bearing system . Using a bearing instead of a standard print-in-place joint is unusual for a fidget like this, but it makes the spin dramatically smoother than a regular pin joint ever could. The gear teeth mesh together so spinning one wheel drives the other , letting you flick either side and watch the motion transfer between them. Each bearing hub is a scaled-down version of my previous viral bearing fidget , shrunk down and re-tuned so the rollers still spin freely and smoothly at the smaller size. A separate connecting handle rests on top, spinning freely around both bearing hubs and giving you a third way to interact with the mechanism. This fidget is entirely print-in-place , meaning it comes off the build plate already assembled and ready to spin with no additional hardware or post processing . The bold gear teeth and dual-bearing design give it a satisfying mechanical look , while the wide, chunky handle offers a comfortable grip for one-handed spinning . This fidget is perfect for anyone who loves clever mechanisms and craves that buttery-smooth spin . Membership Want to sell my 3D printed fidget toys? description: " I am the hope of the universe! " Bring the legendary Super Saiyan to your collection with this fully articulated 3D printable figure of Goku from Dragon Ball Z . Designed to be a centerpiece for any fan's shelf, this model captures Goku in a dynamic, powerful stance, ready for his next battle. Key Features: Fully Articulated: Ball-jointed shoulders, elbows, wrists, hips, knees, and ankles allow for a wide range of dynamic poses. The neck and torso are also articulated, letting you recreate iconic moments from the series. Anime-Accurate Design: Sculpted to reflect Goku's heroic and muscular physique, featuring his iconic black hair, orange gi, and blue undershirt. The design aims to capture the spirit of the world's greatest warrior . Compact Scale: Stands at approximately 14-15 cm tall when assembled, making him a perfect desk companion. Includes One Set of Hands: Comes with one set of hands (fists/open palms). Additional hand options can be printed from the Dummy 13 base model at 1.5x scale. Snap-Fit Assembly: Parts connect with integrated pins and sockets. Please note: Due to the high detail and tight tolerances of this remix, some parts may have a very snug fit. WARNING: THIS IS A COMPLEX MODEL THAT IS HARD TO FIT. ⚠️ IMPORTANT: A CHALLENGING BUILD ⚠️ This is not a beginner-friendly model. It is a complex remix designed for experienced makers. Please be prepared for the following: Difficult Fit: The armor and clothing details are designed to fit closely. Expect a tight, sometimes frustrating fit. Be patient and persistent. Reprints are Likely: Some parts, especially joint pins and connection points, may need to be reprinted to achieve the perfect fit. Do not be discouraged if your first attempt is not perfect. Multiple Test Fits: You will need to test-fit parts multiple times, sanding or heating connections slightly to get everything to work together smoothly. High Detail: The model features fine details (hair, facial features, clothing folds) that require careful printing and handling . Printing Notes: Supports Required: Due to overhanging parts (especially the hair and dynamic posing), supports will be needed for a successful print. Enable supports in your slicer. Recommended Layer Height: 0.12mm – 0.16mm for the best detail on the face, hair, and gi . Recommended Material: PLA or PETG. For the frame/skeleton, PETG is recommended for maximum strength and flexibility. Using a rainbow or silk PLA can add a striking visual effect . Infill: 15–20% for body parts; 100% for small joint pins if printing them separately. Scale: ~14-15 cm (5.5-6 inches) tall when assembled. This size is optimized for detail and joint mobility. You can scale the model, but note that scaling down may reduce joint mobility and make the tight fits even worse. Post-Painting Friendly: The model is not split into colour zones, so it prints as a single-colour model—perfect for painting Goku's vibrant gi, hair, and skin with your own custom finishes. Alternatively, a multi-colour printer can be used to achieve an impressive, paint-free result . QWIRKLE CUBES - Bookcase Edition QWIRKLE CUBES - Bookcase Edition is a sequel to Qwirkle with the goal of the game to create rows and columns in which the cubes all match either in color or symbol in order to score points. Each time you add cubes to the playing area, you score points equal to the rows/columns that you create or add to. In QWIRKLE CUBES - Bookcase Edition the tokens have six faces in the same color, with each face having a different one of the six symbols. Players roll cubes, then play the cubes to build color lines and symbol lines to score points. The player with the most points wins! This bookcase edition box can be stored on a shelf with your other matching bookcase edition games. The box includes storage areas for the all the QWIRKLE Cubes, 4-Part Board and Player Tokens. To store the parts, first add all the cubes to the box. Then place the boards above the cubes. The Player Tokens are stored at the inner edge of the box beside the boards. INFORMATION & ASSEMBLY All parts were printed with PLA filament, matt or flat colored PLA filaments work best for bookcase edition games. I use a textured plate for adhesion. Some parts will need to be superglued, for example, the book spine is glued to the square cornered side of the bookcase box. A small drop of printer oil on the edges of the box lid will help with the slide into the box top. description: ASSEMBLY: The Trammel of Archimedes is a fascinating mechanical fidget that turns a simple rotating motion into a perfectly smooth elliptical path. As you rotate the textured handle, the two sliding joints travel back and forth through the intersecting tracks, guiding the arm around the centre in a mesmerizing continuous motion. This classic mechanism is often called an ellipsograph because a point along the rotating arm traces the shape of an ellipse as it moves. Every clearance was carefully tuned to keep the sliders moving smoothly through the tracks without feeling too loose or easily coming free. The detailed frame, mechanical arm, and textured handle give the model a clean industrial appearance while also making it comfortable and satisfying to operate. Taking less than 68 minutes to print and using under 22 grams of filament , the Trammel of Archimedes is a quick and low-cost print that is perfect for anyone who enjoys mechanical demonstrations, mathematical designs, or satisfying motion fidgets. description: " Know Pain. Feel Pain. Accept Pain. " Bring the leader of the Akatsuki to your collection with this fully articulated 3D printable figure of Pain from Naruto Shippuden . Captured in his iconic, imposing stance, this model is designed for fans and collectors who want to display the power of the Six Paths on their shelf. Key Features: Fully Articulated: Ball-jointed shoulders, elbows, wrists, hips, knees, and ankles allow for a wide range of dynamic poses. The neck and torso also feature articulation for expressive combat stances. Anime-Accurate Design: Sculpted to reflect Pain's tall, lean physique, with attention to his signature orange-red hair, the Rinnegan eyes, and the iconic Akatsuki cloak with its red clouds . Compact Scale: Stands at approximately 14-15 cm tall when assembled—matching the scale of other figures in this series and similar to the official S.H.Figuarts release . Includes One Set of Hands: Comes with one set of hands (open palms/fists). Additional hand options can be printed from the Dummy 13 base model at 1.5x scale. Snap-Fit Assembly: Parts connect with integrated pins and sockets. Please note: Due to the high detail and tight tolerances of this remix, some parts may have a very snug fit. ⚠️ IMPORTANT: A CHALLENGING BUILD ⚠️ This is not a beginner-friendly model. It is a complex remix designed for experienced makers who enjoy a challenge. Please be prepared for the following: Difficult Fit: The Akatsuki cloak and clothing details are designed to fit closely over the base frame. Expect a tight, sometimes frustrating fit. Be patient and persistent. Reprints are Likely: Some parts, especially joint pins and connection points, may need to be reprinted to achieve the perfect fit. Do not be discouraged if your first attempt is not perfect. Multiple Test Fits: You will need to test-fit parts multiple times, sanding or heating connections slightly to get everything to work together smoothly. High Detail: The model features fine details (hair, facial features, cloak folds) that require careful printing and handling. Printing Notes: Supports Required: Due to overhanging parts (especially the hair and the Akatsuki cloak), supports will be needed for a successful print. Enable supports in your slicer. Recommended Layer Height: 0.12mm – 0.16mm for the best detail on the face, hair, and cloak. Recommended Material: PLA or PETG. For the frame/skeleton, PETG is recommended for maximum strength and flexibility. Infill: 15–20% for body parts; 100% for small joint pins if printing them separately. Assembly: Warm the receiving holes slightly with a hair dryer if joints feel too tight. Move each joint carefully after assembly to break in the articulation. Do not force parts —if something doesn't fit, reprint or carefully sand the offending area. What's Included in the Download: Complete STL set for the articulated figure (including Akatsuki cloak details) One set of hands (open palms/fists) Scale: ~14-15 cm (5.5-6 inches) tall when assembled. This size is optimized for detail and joint mobility. While you can scale the model, note that scaling down may reduce joint mobility and make the tight fits even worse. The official S.H.Figuarts version is approximately 15.5 cm, so this matches well . Post-Painting Friendly: The model is not split into color zones, so it prints as a single-color model—perfect for painting Pain's distinctive orange-red hair, the black Akatsuki cloak with red clouds, and his pale skin with your own custom finishes. Alternatively, a multi-color printer can be used to achieve an impressive, paint-free result. Disclaimer: This is a fan-made artistic tribute. Description When I assembled Dummy 13, I found it very inconvenient and frustrating to search through the many parts that were printed all at once. To solve this problem, I created this model. You no longer need to deal with a large number of mixed parts. Each card kit is organized with the part names and the assembly direction clearly marked in order. Simply follow the sequence and assemble the parts step by step. All accessories shown in the picture (e.g., guns, body armor, etc.) are available on my profile. There are many options, so feel free to choose and download whichever ones you like. What's Changed in This Remix One of the biggest challenges when assembling Dummy 13 is failed prints and the confusion caused by the large number of parts. With so many pieces, it's easy to lose track of the assembly order. To solve this, I separated the runners (frames) by body section. For example, the LEG runner contains only the parts needed to assemble the legs, allowing you to complete the entire leg assembly before moving on to the next section. Each runner is also clearly labeled in English (such as LEG , ARM , BODY ) so you can immediately identify which body section the parts belong to. In addition, the layout of the parts on each runner follows the assembly order. Simply start with the part at the top of the runner and work your way down—the parts are arranged in the exact order they should be assembled. ⚠️ Important Do not remove all the parts from the runner before you begin. Instead, detach only the part you need at each step and continue assembling from top to bottom. ⚠️ Printing Recommendations The armor parts can be printed in either PETG or PLA . However, the frame parts should be printed in PETG for the best durability and long-term performance. Print Settings Do not change the layer height from 0.16 mm. Gravity Shift ist eine neue, dreidimensionale Weiterentwicklung des beliebten Spielklassikers „Vier Gewinnt“, speziell entwickelt für das PlayGrid-System. Die Spieler werfen ihre Spielsteine in das vertikale Spielbrett und versuchen, eine Reihe aus vier eigenen Steinen zu bilden. Doch im Gegensatz zum klassischen Vorbild bleibt das Spielfeld nicht immer gleich: Mit dem mitgelieferten Deckel kann das gesamte Spielfeld während des Spiels verschlossen und anschließend um 180° gedreht werden. Dadurch verändert sich die Richtung der Schwerkraft und alle Spielsteine fallen an neue Positionen. Eine scheinbar sichere Strategie kann sich innerhalb eines Augenblicks auflösen – oder plötzlich zum Sieg führen. Da die räumliche Anordnung der Spielsteine mit zunehmender Spieldauer immer komplexer wird, besitzt Gravity Shift eine besondere Siegregel: Wenn ein Spieler glaubt, vier Steine in einer Reihe zu haben, erklärt er sofort seinen Sieg. Anschließend wird das Spielfeld gemeinsam kontrolliert. Ist die Behauptung korrekt, gewinnt dieser Spieler. Ist die Behauptung falsch, gewinnt sofort der Gegner. Diese Regel sorgt für zusätzliche Spannung, Aufmerksamkeit und taktische Entscheidungen. Gravity Shift nutzt die Modularität des PlayGrid-Systems auf kreative Weise und erschafft ein Spielerlebnis, das mit einem klassischen Spielbrett kaum möglich wäre. Eigenschaften Vollständig PlayGrid-kompatibel Einzigartige Schwerkraft- und Drehmechanik Schnelles und spannendes Gameplay Einfach zu drucken Familienfreundlich Hoher Wiederspielwert Unterstützt 2 bis 4 Spieler Keine Stützstrukturen erforderlich Enthaltene Teile PlayGrid-Spielbrett Verriegelbarer Deckel Spielsteine in verschiedenen Farben Spieleranzahl 2 Spieler (empfohlen) Optional 3 oder 4 Spieler Spieldauer ca. 5–15 Minuten Schwierigkeitsgrad Einfach zu lernen, schwer zu meistern. Spielregeln Ziel des Spiels Bilde eine Reihe aus vier eigenen Spielsteinen. Die Reihe darf verlaufen: Horizontal Vertikal Diagonal Spielaufbau Das Spielbrett auf eine ebene Fläche stellen. Jeder Spieler wählt eine Farbe. Der Startspieler wird zufällig bestimmt. Spielablauf Der Startspieler beginnt. In seinem Zug: Wähle eine Spalte. Wirf einen Spielstein in die Spalte. Der Stein fällt bis zum nächstmöglichen freien Platz. Danach ist der nächste Spieler an der Reihe. Gravity-Shift-Regel Vor dem eigenen Zug darf ein Spieler das Spielfeld drehen: Deckel aufsetzen. Spielfeld verschließen. Das gesamte Spielbrett um 180° drehen. Deckel entfernen. Durch die veränderte Schwerkraft fallen alle Spielsteine auf ihre neuen Positionen. Dadurch entstehen völlig neue Spielsituationen und Strategien. Siegregel Sobald ein Spieler glaubt, vier eigene Steine in einer Reihe zu haben, ruft er: „Gewonnen!“ Das Spiel wird sofort unterbrochen. Anschließend überprüfen alle Spieler gemeinsam das Spielfeld. Wenn die Siegesbehauptung korrekt ist: Der Spieler gewinnt. Wenn die Siegesbehauptung falsch ist: Der Gegner gewinnt sofort. Diese Regel belohnt Aufmerksamkeit und räumliches Denken. Variante für 4 Spieler Jeder Spieler erhält eine eigene Farbe. Gespielt wird im Uhrzeigersinn. Der erste Spieler mit vier Steinen in einer Reihe gewinnt. Draw & Fire: Hold the grip, pull back the flexible bow arms, click it into the trigger lock, aim, and squeeze the trigger to unleash the ultimate barrage! IMPORTANT: Read Before Printing! Vortex Cannon Growing up, one of the funniest things to mess around with was an airzooka, so I figured it was time to make one you could print yourself. Just pull it back and let it fly to launch satisfying vortex rings across the room. And if you really want to catch someone off guard... let's just say it pairs suspiciously well with a tiny spritz of fart spray from a safe distance. 😄 It's easy to print, simple to assemble, and guaranteed to get a few laughs. Happy printing! VORTEX CANNON Assembly Guide Before You Begin You'll Need: All printed parts 3 plastic shopping bags (or 1 standard kitchen trash bag) 2 rubber bands (cut into straight strips) STEP 1 – Lay Out the Parts Lay out all printed parts and verify that nothing is missing before beginning assembly. STEP 2 – Prepare the Rubber Bands Cut two rubber bands so they become straight elastic strips. STEP 3 – Install the Elastic Bands Place the center retention clamp in position. Tie one elastic strip to each pair of opposing interior mounting tabs while routing both bands through the center retention clamp. Pull the bands tight before tying the knots. STEP 4 – Verify Band Installation The elastic bands should: Be centered across the opening Pass through the center retention clamp Have equal tension on both sides STEP 5 – Install the Bags Place three shopping bags (or one trash bag) over the rear opening of the cannon. Leave enough material hanging over the edge to be captured by the retention ring. STEP 6 – Install the Retention Ring Important: Install the ring from underneath and slide it upward toward the top of the cannon. Make sure the tapered side of the ring faces upward , toward the widest opening of the cannon. Continue sliding the ring upward until it rests just below the top lip. Tip: Do not trim the excess bag material until assembly is complete. STEP 7 – Lock the Bags in Place Push the center of the bags inward until they reach the installed elastic bands. While holding the bags inward, press the retention ring upward until it snaps securely into place. The bags should now be tightly clamped around the entire opening. STEP 8 – Install the Rear Plate Position the rear plate with the four locating pins over the center of the bags. Push the pins through the bags and into the center retention clamp until fully seated. This securely locks the bags in place. STEP 9 – Install the Threaded Stud Thread the small threaded stud into the center of the rear plate. Tighten until snug. Do not overtighten. STEP 10 – Install the Handle Slide the handle onto the mounting bracket located on the outside of the cannon. Align the holes in the handle with the mounting bracket. STEP 11 – Install the Locking Pin Insert the small straight locking pin through the aligned holes in the handle and mounting bracket. Push the pin in completely until it is fully seated. STEP 12 – Finished Assembly Just trim off the extra bag ends and your Vortex Cannon is now ready to use. Grip the handle, pull it straight back, and release to launch a powerful vortex of air. Tips Three shopping bags produce the best diaphragm. A kitchen trash bag also works well. Replace the bags if they become torn or stretched. Keep the elastic bands evenly tensioned for the strongest vortex. Membership
