description: The YAPR™ (pronounced "YAP-er") — Yet Another Purge Receptacle Featuring BinLock™ push-button locking technology Not being completely satisfied with the first purge bin I ever printed, I set out to design (overengineer?) my own after getting the A2L. I wanted a purge bin that looked like it belonged on the printer , stayed exactly where I put it, and came off with a simple button press—without magnets, awkward removal angles, or extra hardware. I was tired of: Awkwardly angling or shifting the purge bin to remove it every time I emptied it (and sometimes spilling purge in the process) Constantly nudging the bin back against the printer because it would slowly vibrate away after a print or two Small pieces of purged filament finding their way between the bin and the printer Liners that frequently broke or cracked and needed to be reprinted The YAPR is a push-button A2L purge (or poop!) bin that locks securely in place, prints mostly in place, and requires no magnets or extra hardware . Designed to be the last purge bin you'll ever need to print. Features Easily attaches and detaches using exclusive BinLock™ push-button technology—no bin gymnastics required Securely locks in place and won't slowly vibrate away from the printer Matching side contour helps prevent stray filament from falling between the bin and the printer Contoured to match the printer's lines for a clean, OEM-inspired appearance Prints mostly in place with only a small amount of support beneath the button Available in three sizes: Slim (100mm wide — best for tight spaces), Standard (125mm wide — the daily driver), and Wide (150mm wide — ideal for heavy AMS printing and lower maintenance) Optional liner fully protects the bottom of the bin (unlike many liners with fully cut-out patterns) while also helping reduce purge rattling Won't block your printer's ventilation ports Angled bottom makes it easy to grab those last stubborn pieces of purge Assembly Notes This is specifically designed for the A2L only. For the easiest assembly, assemble within two hours of printing. The BinLock™ mechanism is intentionally designed with a tight initial fit and has a short break-in period. It will become noticeably smoother with use. If the button doesn't move smoothly after pressing it several times, grasp it with pliers and work it in and out a few times. The additional travel and force help speed up the break-in process. Instructions Choose your preferred size, print the bin , peg , and peg cover , then remove the small amount of support beneath the button. If using the optional liner, print the matching size in PETG (or PLA if you primarily print PETG). Press the BinLock™ button (located on the bottom right of the bin) several times to begin the break-in process (The first press requires a fair amount of force, so using two thumbs while bracing the bin against a countertop or table is recommended.) Hold the BinLock™ button down and rub a crayon over the small internal slide (see the second to last model photo for the exact location). While this may seem like an unusual step, it is important for smooth operation of the BinLock™ mechanism. The next few assembly steps are a little tricky—but thankfully, you only need to do them once. Turn the peg cover upside down with its tallest side facing you. Insert the peg upside down so the shortest side of the peg's triangular base faces to the right. The angle of the peg should *not* match the angle of the peg cover. Please see the last model photo for up close pictures. Without disturbing the peg, and with the longest side of the peg cover facing you , insert the peg and cover together into the bin until the cover snaps into place. Turning the bin upside down during this step usually makes assembly easier, and engaging the snap-fit may require a firm push. With the bin upright, press the BinLock™ button several more times. You should notice the peg moving slightly with each press as the mechanism continues to break in. If the button mechanism isn't working correctly, the peg may not be fully seated. Grip the peg firmly with pliers, pull it straight out with steady force (the peg and cover will come out together), then repeat the installation process. Connect to printer Hold the BinLock™ button. Slide the bin fully against the rear frame and side of the printer. Release the button to lock the bin in place. Disconnect from printer Hold the BinLock™ button. Pull the bin straight toward you. Print one. Lock it in. Forget about it.

description: AMS HT Side Mount für Bambu Lab H2 Serie Diese Halterung ermöglicht es, das AMS HT seitlich am oberen Rahmen eines Druckers der H2-Serie zu befestigen. Dadurch kann TPU direkt über die Bypass-Öffnung des AMS HT zum Druckkopf geführt werden. Der große Vorteil dieser Positionierung ist der extrem kurze und nahezu geradlinige Filamentweg. Das reduziert den Wiederstand beim fördern des Filaments auf ein Minimum und verbessert insbesondere den Druck mit sehr weichen TPU-Filamenten, die empfindlich auf lange oder stark gekrümmte Filamentwege reagieren. Zusätzlich kann das AMS HT während des Drucks weiterhin als Filamenttrockner genutzt werden. So bleibt das TPU während des gesamten Druckvorgangs trocken, was die Druckqualität zusätzlich verbessert. Einfache Konstruktion Die Halterung besteht aus drei Steckteilen, die ohne Schrauben oder weiteres Montagematerial zusammengesteckt werden. Diese Bauweise bietet mehrere Vorteile: Sehr einfacher und zuverlässiger Druck. Durch die modulare Bauweise, kann der Halter durch austauschen des Hakens auch für andere Druckermodelle genutzt werden. Nur eines der drei Bauteile benötigt eine winzige Stützstruktur. Die Halterung lässt sich jederzeit wieder zerlegen und dadurch besonders platzsparend verstauen. Hinweis: Je nach verwendeten Material und Kalibrierung des Druckers und Filament, kann es sein, dass die Steckverbindung schwergängig ist. Versuche nicht die Teile mit Gewalt zusammen zu stecken! In diesen Fall ist es hilfreich die Steckverbinder mit etwas Schlafpapier nach zu arbeiten. Etwas Gleitmittel wie Balistol oder WD40 kann ebenfalls helfen. Einfache Montage Für die Montage muss lediglich der Glasdeckel des Druckers entfernt werden. Anschließend wird die Halterung einfach über den oberen Rand des Druckers gesteckt. Das AMS HT wird danach nur auf der Halterung abgestellt - ganz ohne zusätzliche Befestigung. Druckprofile Für dieses Modell stelle ich 2 Druckprofile zur Verfügung: Profil 1 - H2D / H2C Dieses Profil ist ausschliesslich für den H2D und H2C vorgesehen. Das Bauteil wird aus PETG gedruckt, während die Interface-Schichten der Stützstrucktur aus PLA bestehen. Profil 2 - H2S Dieses Profil ist speziell für den H2S erstellt. Hier werden sowohl das Bauteil als auch die Stützstruktur aus demselben Material gedruckt- in meinem Fall PETG Halter für P2S & X2D Hier geht es zum AMS HT Seitenhalter für den P2S und X2D: https://makerworld.com/de/models/3075472-ams-ht-tpu-side-mount-for-p2s-x2d#profileId-3462867 Bis auf den Haken zum einhängen am Drucker sind die Teile für P2S/X2D und H2-Serie identisch! Durch austauschen des Hakens, kann man somit eine Halterung für verschiedene Druckermodelle nutzen. Falls dir das Modell gefällt, freue ich mich über einen Like, einen Download, einen Boost und natürlich über Fotos deiner Drucke! Viel Spaß beim Drucken!

model_name: Snapmaker U1 + Sunlu Filadryer S4 Feeder Adapter
description: Humidity, my worst enemy… Snapmaker sent me the U1, and unfortunately, I'm not able to get good prints with printers that have open-air spools (because of the humidity at my location). So I looked for the best way to deal with it, and none of the projects I found were good enough. The closest one used a Sunlu Filadryer S4, so that was my baseline to start this project: Snapmaker u1 + Sunlu Fliladryer S4 Setup Compact setup Air-tight (at least as much as the original S4) It has the feeders as close as possible to the spools → Easier loading and unloading This is a DIY project, so you will need some tools and materials: M3 x 6 Screws, 4 of them with nuts and washers 2 x PTFE connectors. The ones that allow the 4 mm PTFE tube to pass through Drills (3.5 mm for the screws, and one for the size of your PTFE connectors) Extra PTFE tubes (4 mm OD, 2.5 mm ID) to replace the ones that go from the original feeder location to the back of the printer. Feeder extension cable. This might be the trickiest. They can be found as GH1.25 or JST GH1.25. Be sure they are 15-pin and male-female configuration. The length depends on your setup; measure both sides from the feeder's original location to the back of the Sunlu S4. I recommend 50 cm. I'll leave some links in the comments. I don't have measurements of the process, because I did it on the go and wasn't planning to upload it anywhere. But I have some pictures taken from the video I recorded: Depending on your setup, you would want to place the S4 on the right or the left of the U1. Therefore, you need to install the feeders on the side of the S4 that faces the back (as shown in the pictures above). You need to measure the distance between the feeder inputs, and drill the holes in the S4 to install the PTFE connectors. Then, assemble the feeders in the printed holder, and place it with the holes aligned to the filament input. Mark the Holder holes, and drill the 3.5 mm holes for the screw assembly. Assemble it, place the numbers from the inside, and then the funnels (optional, but recommended) Then, place the U1 and S4 in the final position, measure, cut, and install the PTFE tubes from the printer to the feeder. Don't make them too short or they might bend; leave some extra for them to wiggle around with smooth curves. That's about it. As I said, I made it on the go, so I'm not sure if I'm forgetting something 😂

PTFE Clips Helps prevent PTFE tubes from rubbing against the top glass These lightweight PTFE tube clips are designed to help keep the tubing from wearing on the upper glass panel on enclosed Bambu Lab printers. They have been tested on the Bambu Lab X2D and are designed for standard 4 mm PTFE tubing , so they may also fit other compatible Bambu Lab models. Why I designed them As the toolhead moves around the printer, the PTFE tubes naturally twist, bend and change position. Some tube-management solutions hold multiple tubes tightly together to create a neater appearance. While this may look tidy, it can also introduce unnecessary tension, stress or twisting into the tubing as the toolhead travels. These clips are designed to support each tube individually. This helps reduce wear on the PTFE tubes from the top glass while still allowing the tubes to move as designed. Key features Helps prevent PTFE wear from rubbing on the top glass Designed for standard 4 mm PTFE tubing Tested on the Bambu Lab X2D Allows each tube to move independently Applies only light tension to the tubing Lightweight and low profile Quick snap-on installation No tools or printer modifications required Small and fast to print How many should I use? I currently use four clips , which provides good support and separation. More clips can be installed if additional support is required, but avoid using so many that the tubing becomes stiff or restricted. Recommended print settings These were successfully printed using: Layer height: 0.16 mm Walls/perimeters: 3 Bed temperature: 60°C Part cooling fan: 0% for the first 2 - 3 layers, then a maximum of 25% Brim: Not required Supports: Not required Keeping the cooling fan low helps prevent these small parts from cooling too quickly, warping or lifting from the build plate. Material recommendations PLA is suitable for normal use where the heated chamber is not being used. For printers operating with a heated chamber, use a more temperature-resistant material such as: PETG ABS ASA Another suitable heat-resistant filament PLA may soften or deform when exposed to elevated chamber temperatures for extended periods. Installation Carefully snap each clip over a PTFE tube. Position the clips along the tubing where support is required. Move the toolhead through its full range of travel. Check that each tube can still bend and move freely. Reposition or remove clips if any tension or restriction is present. Important notes These clips are intended to gently guide the PTFE tubes, not lock them rigidly in place. After installation, confirm that: The tubes still move freely The clips do not contact the cable chain The tubing is not stretched, kinked or twisted The toolhead can reach the full build area The clips remain clear of all moving components Compatibility Tested on: Bambu Lab X2D Tube size: 4 mm PTFE Other models may be compatible but have not yet been tested Support the design

description: Snap-On Remix for Fixed-End Spool Holders A snap-on remix of David D.'s Hanging (Pendulum) Filament Guide, a weighted arm that hangs on your spool holder and keeps light tension on the filament path from external spools, so the line can’t drift off the spool and tangle. His original closed eyelet is the right design when you can slide it onto the rod from one end, and it comes in three eyelet sizes (26, 36, and 46mm). If your spool rod is removable, go print his version. But some holders have fixed ends with flares or caps, like the Bambu X2D stock top mount, and nothing threads onto those. This version converts the 26mm eyelet to a C-clip that snaps onto the holder radially and stays put. The Engineering The opening size is not a guess. The gap is a 90 degree segment sized from bending strain math for a C-ring flexing over a 26mm shaft. Peak strain during snap-on lands around 1.4 percent, comfortably inside PETG’s working limit. Rounded entry bulbs on the tips guide the shaft in and spread the ring smoothly. The gap is also rotated 60 degrees off the arm centerline, so the load path never rests on the opening. It goes on with a firm push, a positive click, and swings freely as a pendulum. Tested on an X2D stock top holder and others (as seen in the photos) in PETG HF. Bonus: Light Spool Keeper Many fixed-end holders are graduated, widening toward the flared end. Because this clip fits snugly instead of loosely, it doubles as a spool keeper: it blocks the spool from walking outward off the end while still penduluming freely guiding your filament with ease. Material Matters Print this in PETG, ASA, or ABS. The snap fit depends on flex. PLA has roughly half the strain tolerance, so it will probably survive a couple installations, but repeated cycles with PLA will likely cause stress cracking, and matte PLA is even worse. I haven't tested PLA to failure on this, so YMMV, but I'd just use PETG or something with better strength and flex than PLA. ⚠️ IMPORTANT PRINT NOTE Use 4 or more wall loops (the profile has this set). The ring works as a spring and needs solid perimeters in the bending section, not sparse infill. Everything else stays at defaults. The plate includes mirrored left and right arms, plus the original design’s small locking pins as an optional backup if the detents ever wear. The original designer reports the detents holding fine on their own and that has been true for me as well, but they're there if you need them.

description: This is a simple magnet fit tolerance test kit for common round magnets used in 3D printed projects. Instead of guessing the perfect hole size for your magnets, print the test strip that matches the magnets you have, press your magnets into the different holes, and choose the fit that works best for your printer, slicer settings, filament, and material. The kit includes separate test pieces for: 3×2 mm magnets 4×2 mm magnets 5×2 mm magnets 6×2 mm magnets 8×2 mm magnets 10×2 mm magnets Each size is a separate part, so you do not need to print the whole kit. Just print the strip for the magnet size you actually have. Each strip includes multiple hole diameters around the nominal magnet size, with the tolerance clearly labelled above each hole. For example, the 6×2 mm strip tests hole sizes from 5.95 mm to 6.25 mm. The magnet pockets are designed for 2 mm thick magnets. The back of each pocket is intentionally thin so the magnet can be pushed back out after testing. Why use this? Magnet fit can vary a lot depending on: Printer calibration Filament type Material shrinkage Nozzle size Slicer settings Hole compensation settings Whether you want a press fit, loose fit, or glue-in fit For best results, print the test strip in the same material you plan to use for your final project. For example, if your finished part will be PETG, print the test strip in PETG. If your final part will be ABS, print the test strip in ABS. description: X2D Auxiliary Fan Duct The Bambu Lab X2D auxiliary fans can direct a significant amount of cool air across the left and right edge of the build plate. For materials such as PLA, and particularly PETG, this concentrated airflow may contribute to uneven cooling, edge lifting, corner warping or reduced first-layer adhesion on some models. These deflectors redirect the auxiliary fan airflow upward and away from the print bed, helping prevent the fans from blowing directly across the edges of the print while still allowing air to circulate inside the chamber. Why I designed these I began experiencing prints lifting primarily along the edges closest to the auxiliary fans, which indicated that the concentrated airflow across the front of the build plate was contributing to uneven cooling. Although auxiliary-fan values can be adjusted within the filament and process profiles, the commanded settings do not always appear to remain in effect during printing. In some situations, the printer’s internal control logic applies its own auxiliary-fan behaviour and overrides the values defined in the slicer. This means the fan may continue operating at a higher speed than expected, even after the cooling profile has been adjusted. Because the underlying firmware-controlled behaviour is not currently exposed as a separate user-adjustable setting, it can be difficult to reliably prevent direct airflow from reaching the front edge of the print bed. These deflectors provide a mechanical solution by changing the direction of the airflow itself. Rather than attempting to reduce or disable the fan electronically, they redirect the output upward and away from the build surface while still allowing air to circulate within the chamber. Key features Redirects auxiliary fan airflow upward and away from the build plate Helps reduce concentrated cooling along the edges of the print area May help reduce edge lifting and corner warping Maintains airflow inside the printer rather than completely blocking the fans Installs without permanent modification to the printer Can be easily removed when not required Designed as separate left- and right-hand deflectors Compatibility These deflectors have currently only been tested on the Bambu Lab X2D. Should fit P2S right side Aux Fan They are designed specifically around the X2D auxiliary fan outlets and surrounding clearances. Compatibility with other Bambu Lab printers has not been confirmed. Installation Fit each deflector over its corresponding auxiliary fan outlet, ensuring it is fully seated and secure. The outlet should face upward and inward, redirecting the airflow away from the surface of the build plate. After installation: Check that both deflectors are securely fitted. Confirm that neither deflector contacts the build plate, toolhead or any moving component. Manually move the toolhead throughout the complete build area. Run the printer’s normal homing or movement checks before beginning a print. Do not begin printing until full toolhead and build-plate clearance has been confirmed. Print settings The included print profile is the profile I used successfully for these parts. Recommended starting settings: Layer height: 0.16 mm Walls/perimeters: 3 Supports: Not required Brim: Painted on edges only to prevent lifting Orientation: Print in the supplied orientation The parts should be allowed to cool before removal from the build plate to avoid distortion. Material PLA is suitable for testing and general use. PETG, ABS or ASA may provide improved temperature resistance for long-term use inside the enclosed printer, particularly when printing materials that require elevated chamber temperatures. Important notes These deflectors change the direction of the auxiliary fan airflow. They do not provide electronic control over fan speed. Cooling requirements vary depending on: Filament type Model geometry Print speed Chamber temperature Bed temperature Auxiliary fan speed These parts are intended as a practical airflow-management accessory, not as a guaranteed fix for every adhesion or warping issue. Bed cleanliness, first-layer calibration, filament condition and suitable temperature settings should still be checked.

description: Give your Bambu Lab printer a retro gaming makeover! I couldn't find a PS Vita inspired screen cover for my X2D or P2S, so I decided to design one myself. The goal wasn't just to make something that looked similar, it was to capture the proportions, spacing and overall feel of the original handheld while making it work naturally with the printer's touchscreen. The printer's display is slightly larger than the PS Vita's, so I chose to keep the bezel true to the console's proportions rather than shrinking the design and throwing off the iconic look. If you prefer to mount your screen flush against the printer, this design may not be suitable. However, I personally keep my screen slightly offset from the unit, so this has never been an issue for me. You still retain almost the full range of movement only the final portion of travel, when the screen is pushed completely flush against the printer, is lost. For me, preserving the correct proportions was well worth the small compromise. The shoulder buttons and camera lens are designed to be printed in a transparent filament for the best appearance, but they can also be printed in any colour you like. Whether you're a PlayStation fan, a retro gaming enthusiast or just want to personalise your printer, this is a fun little project that adds plenty of character without affecting everyday usability. description: This full-bed calibration test is designed to quickly check the quality and consistency of the first layer across almost the entire usable build plate. description: Flashforge Creator 5 Pro Spool Holder Adapter – Clog & Layer Shift Fix Overview This model is a slip-on cylindrical adapter / extension sleeve designed specifically for the stock spool holder on the Flashforge Creator 5 Pro . The factory Flashforge spool holder is quite narrow and features open slots/holes; as a result, certain filament spools — especially reusable refill spools / master spools with internal locking tabs or ridges — can catch, drag, or get completely stuck. This friction restricts smooth filament feeding, triggering false "clog" errors and causing frustrating layer shifts mid-print. By sliding this sleeve over the original arm, you create a perfectly smooth, continuous surface with an optimal diameter. This allows any spool (including Bambu Lab master spools, as shown in the images) to rotate freely and effortlessly. Design Features Problem Solver: Completely eliminates generic clog errors and layer shifts caused by spool rotation friction. Broad Compatibility: Adapts the narrow factory mount to smoothly host Refill spools (with internal assembly notches) and other third-party brands with larger center holes. Toolless Installation: Simple slide-on fit right over the stock holder—no tools or permanent printer modifications required. Stay-Centered Lip: The pronounced outer rims keep the spool securely centered and prevent it from shifting or sliding off during high-speed printing. Recommended Print Settings Material: PLA, PETG, or ASA (depending on your printer's environment). Layer Height: 0.20 mm or higher. Wall Loops (Perimeters): 3 to 4 walls for optimal durability and wear resistance. Infill: 15% to 20% (Gyroid or Grid). Supports / Brim: None required. description: Successful detection. Every time. No compromises. This Model works only on the H2D and H2S. The H2C uses other ArUco Codes! This model is part of my ongoing BIQU Build Plate Accessories collection. Each model is conceived, printed, and endurance-tested on my own machines, refined through dozens of iterations to match the printer’s true mechanical behavior. Precision isn't assumed here, it’s verified layer by layer. Explore the full collection: BIQU Build Plate Accessories Follow me if you like my work, that kind of appreciation really dries my filament. Likes and boosts feed the Maker World algorithm and keep the new models coming Tested Compatibility, Fitting And Detection Checked BIQU Pyrogrip Build Plate for Bambu Lab H2D/H2S (350mm*325mm) Blue BIQU CryoGrip Pro Glacier Build Plate for Bambu Lab H2D/H2S (350mm*325mm) Mechanically Incompatible (No Honeycomp Handle) Matte Orange and Blue BIQU CryoGrip Pro FrostBite Build Plate for Bambu Lab H2C (330mm*320mm) Matte Orange and Blue BIQU CryoGrip Pro FrostBite Build Plate for Bambu Lab H2D/H2S (350mm*325mm) ArUco Incompatible (Use Other Model, See Collection) BIQU Pyrogrip Build Plate for Bambu Lab H2C (330mm*320mm) Blue BIQU CryoGrip Pro Glacier Build Plate for Bambu Lab H2C (330mm*320mm) The BIQU CryoGrip Pro Glacier is an outstanding build plate for ASA, but there is one annoying drawback: the printer cannot reliably detect it, and the supplied adhesive ArUco stickers are, frankly, a joke. This model puts an end to that. Three print profiles. “Engineering Plate” as suggested by BIQU. “Cool Plate Super Tack” as requested by the community. “Smooth PEI Plate” because why not. Developed specifically for the BIQU CryoGrip Pro Glacier on the Bambu Lab H2D and H2S, it provides a precisely aligned ArUco marker that delivers reliable build plate recognition every time. The integrated clips engage directly with the plate's honeycomb pattern, ensuring perfect alignment and a secure mechanical fit. For additional retention, a small strip of 3M 9080 LED tape can be applied underneath the mount. The design has been tested in both PETG and ASA. For science, I even printed the ArUco marker itself in PLA and used it on an ASA print with a chamber temperature of 65 °C. Surprisingly, it held up for several weeks. PETG is an excellent long term choice, while ASA is the ultimate install it once and forget about it solution. No more failed recognition. No more crooked stickers. Just perfect alignment and reliable detection, every single time.

description: Staffa Compatta, Inclinata e Ribassata per TPU Assistant (Compatibile con Bambu Lab X2D / P2S) Ho progettato questa staffa per la mia X2D (essendo al 100% compatibile anche con il modello P2S ) con un obiettivo principale: migliorare radicalmente l'orientamento dei tasti del TPU Assistant per renderli finalmente visibili dal davanti, ottimizzare la direzione del tubo in PTFE verso l'AMS HT ed eliminare una volta per tutte la necessità di scollegare i tubetti durante l'uso quotidiano o l'essiccazione. Le caratteristiche principali di questo design: Gestione lineare del tubo (Nessun bisogno di scollegare nulla): Molti progetti online richiedono di scollegare il tubo in PTFE dall'AMS HT quando il TPU Assistant non è in uso, ad esempio per inserire il tappo di sigillo e avviare la funzione di essiccazione dell'Hub. Questo spesso comporta il dover riporre il tubetto rimosso per non perderlo. Con questa configurazione, grazie alla distanza ridotta e all'allineamento, non è mai necessario scollegare il tubo . Il condotto rimane stabilmente al suo posto e sigillato, semplificando i passaggi: basta spingere il filamento dall'AMS HT direttamente nel TPU Assistant e si è pronti a stampare. Inclinazione ed Ergonomia dei Tasti: La staffa è posizionata più in basso e inclina il TPU Assistant verso lo sguardo di chi si trova davanti alla stampante. In questo modo la pulsantiera e i LED di stato sono facilmente visibili e comodi da raggiungere direttamente dal fronte. Geometria del percorso posteriore e specifiche tubi: Essendo una staffa ribassata, la distanza geometrica verso l'ingresso della stampante aumenta leggermente rispetto alla configurazione standard, richiedendo un percorso totale fisso di 200 mm . Nota per la community: Bambu Lab raccomanda solitamente 160 mm, ma non c'è assolutamente da preoccuparsi per il caricamento . Il sistema del TPU Assistant è infatti progettato per funzionare ufficialmente anche sulla H2D , che è una stampante molto più grande della X2D e ha un percorso interno del filamento nativamente molto più lungo. Visto che il sistema gestisce quel tragitto maggiore senza problemi, i 4 cm esterni in più introdotti su questo setup vengono digeriti dall'estrusore in totale sicurezza. Per installare il sistema avete due opzioni precise: Setup Diretto: Vi servirà uno spezzone di tubo in PTFE tagliato esattamente a 200 mm . Con Adattatore 4-in-1: Se utilizzate un connettore 4-in-1 come il mio (lungo circa 6 cm), dovrete compensare la misura tagliando il tubetto in PTFE a 140 mm (140 mm + 60 mm = 200 mm). Design Essenziale: La struttura è pensata per essere il più compatta e leggera possibile, riducendo la quantità di filamento necessaria e i tempi di stampa. 🔄 IMPORTANTE: Calibrazione post-installazione Come raccomandato dalle linee guida ufficiali Bambu Lab, dopo aver installato la nuova staffa e posizionato il tubo da 200 mm (o 140 mm con adattatore), è fondamentale lanciare la calibrazione del modulo . Questa procedura serve a far leggere al sistema la nuova lunghezza del percorso, misurando l'attrito per calibrare al millesimo la forza della spinta automatica. 👉 Potete seguire la procedura ufficiale passo-passo a questo link della Wiki Bambu Lab: Guida alla Calibrazione del TPU Assistant . 🛠️ Note di Stampa e Tolleranze Materiale di Test: Il progetto è stato sviluppato, stampato e testato in PETG . Nota sulle tolleranze: L'asola di incastro per il TPU Assistant è calibrata in modo preciso sul PETG. Se decidete di stamparlo in PLA o ABS/ASA, tenete conto che il diverso ritiro termico dei materiali potrebbe influire leggermente sulla tolleranza dell'incastro (potrebbe risultare impercettibilmente più stretto o largo). Per Inatallazione sono necessarie due viti ST 3x12 avanzate dal kit di assemblaggio del TPU Assistant Spero questa soluzione vi è utile!

A modular wall-mounted holder designed to organize and store filament spools in a clean and practical way. Each piece connects with a side joint, so you can build the holder as long as you need depending on how many spools you want to store. It is perfect for keeping PLA, PETG, ABS, TPU and other filament spools tidy and easy to access. There are two versions included : Standard module This is the main modular part, with one side wall. If both systems must share a window, install blast gates to prevent contaminated air, smoke, fumes, or odors from flowing back into the room. For maximum safety and performance, use separate windows whenever possible. This project is intended for venting air only. Always follow the manufacturer's safety recommendations for your printer, laser, and ventilation equipment. description: This is a dedicated mount that uses the A1 mini's Z-axis cover to attach the BMCU 370C to the right side of the printer. Most existing mounts position the BMCU behind the printer, feeding the PTFE tube from the rear toward the front. However, if your setup has limited rear clearance, this can create an excessively tight bend in the PTFE tube. To solve this problem, this mount routes the filament from the right side of the printer toward the left, allowing the PTFE tube to follow a smoother, more natural curve even in tight spaces. After testing several designs, I found that positioning the filament path at approximately a 45° angle while placing the BMCU slightly farther from the printer provided the best tube routing. The main model is based on this design. The Long 45° Version is the main model. Three additional optional versions are also included: Short 45° Version 30° Version Straight Version Feel free to choose the version you like best. Installation Notes Before installing this mount, remove the spacer secured to the printer's Z-axis cover with three screws. The original three screws are reused to secure this mount in place. No additional hardware is required.

model_name: Ultimate Exhaust Muffler System For X2D/P2S*
description: INTRODUCTION: This is my incredibly over-engineered take on an exhaust fan muffler for anyone tired of the constant buzz from the rear fan on the X2D or P2S. Most designs are a trade-off between airflow and noise reduction. But I decided that wasn't good enough for me. I needed to reduce exhaust fan noise by more than 10 decibels while preserving a large amount of airflow . Now, 4 days later, I've devised a system that can do it in style. FEATURES: 18 dB noise reduction. Interference fit assembly, no glue required! Easy to install and remove ; refer to GIF. Engine-inspired design. Decorative supports that also serve as effective air-cooling fins during high-temperature exhaust. Single-baffle muffler, reducing noise while preserving airflow . Screenshot from OnShape Included. Exhaust pipe can be placed under or to the left depending on personal preference. PRINTING/ASSEMBLY: Layer height: 0.16 mm recommended due to overhangs Infill: 15% Gyroid Material: No restrictions. My example is printed in PLA Basic, and I expect no issues. Changing the orientation of the Exhaust Pipe while slicing WILL CAUSE A FAILURE. It must remain vertical during printing due to the muffler's internal structure. Press the Exhaust Pipe into the slots on the Air Deflector while pushing an Exhaust Clip into the groove on the Exhaust Pipe, then pinch the Exhaust Clip to ensure that it has been fully seated. Lastly, install the Deflector Backplate. Post-processing will be required; make sure to use a sharp craft blade, like an X-Acto knife , while removing supports due to tight tolerances. If the Exhaust Pipe is not fitting in the slots on the Air Deflector, check for remaining supports; even one layer prevents assembly. Ensure that your machine is well calibrated before printing due to complex overhangs and tight tolerances . Also clean the build plate before printing the Exhaust Pipe due to a risk of it shifting during the print . TEST RESULTS I ran multiple tests to prove the design's functionality. Measuring at the exhaust exit, an uncovered exhaust fan can produce 80 decibels ; after installing the muffler, exhaust noise was lowered to 62 decibels. From 7 ft away, uncovered is 57, and muffled is 49. At most, this produces an 18 decibel reduction. It might not sound like much, but try it for yourself. I guarantee it's night and day. I also ran a flow test to see how quickly the fan alone could cool the chamber from 45 to 35 degrees Celsius. Without the muffler, this process took 9 minutes and 16 seconds. With the muffler, it took 9 minutes and 38 seconds. This isn't a direct airflow measurement, but it provides a practical comparison of cooling performance. If you have ideas for additional tests, I'd love to hear them in the comments

description: PETG Supportless Perfect Overhang Print Profile This is a print profile setting designed for supportless PETG printing with perfect overhangs, tested on a propeller model. Key features include: 1. Outer/Inner Wall Speed Reduced to 50/60 mm/s Slower printing speeds prevent under-extrusion and stringing. 2. Disable Overhang Speed Slowdown Disable slowdown for overhangs above 45°. This prevents the nozzle from dwelling too long in one spot, which causes heat buildup and sagging. 3. Enable Prime Tower (Wipe Tower) Allows extra layer cooling time and reduces filament blobs/droppings on the model. 4. Lower Layer Height to 0.12 mm A lower layer height provides better support for steep overhang angles. 5. Increase Outer/Inner Wall Line Width to 0.6 mm Enhances the structural support and stability of inner and outer walls. 6. Increase Part Cooling Accelerates model cooling to avoid high-temperature sagging and deformation. 7. Open the Top Lid, Keep the Front Door Closed Keep the top glass lid open for heat dissipation, but close the front door to prevent model warping. 8.Disable precision wall to improve the support between inner and outer wall. If you experience sagging like in the image below, please improve overall printer ventilation, turn on the AC, or print at night. However, do NOT change the heatbed temperature to avoid warping. Tested on: Bambu Lab P1S

Been having bridging issues with my prints so I put this together to be able to test for an ideal bridge flow ratio and speed combination to get the best results. Not a professional model maker by any stretch of the imagination, but it works for now! This test lays out 21 bridges on one plate — 3 print speeds (10 / 20 / 30 mm/s) across 7 bridge flow ratios (1.0–1.6) — so you can find the combination that gives flat, fully-fused strands with no sag. Uses only ~7 g of filament, so it's cheap to run as often as you calibrate your filaments. How to use: Print it, flip it over, and read the underside of each bridge. The cleanest, flattest strands mark your ideal bridge flow ratio for that speed. Set those values in your slicer and enjoy clean bridges. Printed on a Bambu Lab P1S. No supports, no brim needed. How to read the results: Flip the plate and look at the underside of each bridge: Best: strands are flat, straight, evenly spaced, and fully fused — no sag, no gaps. Too little flow / too fast: strands sag, droop, or break mid-span. Too much flow: strands bulge, blob, or fuse into a rough mass. Settings to modify in slicer Quality > Advanced > Bridge Flow Speed > Other Layers Speed > Bridge Feedback and comments are welcome, I have much to learn still! model_name: Creality Space Pi X4 Desiccant Drying System
description: Hello! I’m excited to introduce my desiccant drying system specifically designed for the Creality Space Pi x4 filament dryer. I dedicated a lot of time and effort to developing this model, going through numerous iterations until I reached this version. After experimenting with a model I found in MakerWorld and encountering several issues, I decided to create my own. My goal was to design a strong, modular system that ensures unobstructed airflow. I also wanted something at incorporated a pour spout without taking up a lot of space or using a lot of filament. This filament drying system is stackable, robust, and easy to use. It’s large enough to accommodate two boxes and a frame on each side of the Space Pi x4. It measures 1500mm by 150mm by 60mm, features 2mm holes and a pour spout in one of the corners. Each box can hold a maximum of 500 grams of desiccant, but I recommend not exceeding 300 grams to expedite drying times and prevent overloading the frame. I successfully dried approximately 400 grams (200 grams per side) of wet desiccant in about 6 hours at 85 degrees Celsius, which is significantly faster compared to other solutions. Please note that to achieve the optimal drying temperature of 85 degrees Celsius, I highly recommend printing this model in ASA filament. I’ve shared my personal settings in the profile I published, which is in ASA. For faster prints, I used a .6mm nozzle, but if you prioritize quality, you can print it with a .4mm nozzle. Make sure to adjust the print settings accordingly. Turn off all cooling, lower the volumetric flow to 12 cubic millimeters per second, heat up the chamber to 65 degrees Celsius, and heat the build plate to 100 degrees Celsius. If you don’t have a heated chamber, heat soak it for at least 30 minutes before printing to minimize the risk of warping. Additionally, ensure that you use a textured PEI plate or an engineering plate. Wash it with soap and warm water, and apply a glue stick. ASA emits toxic fumes so use air filters and a proper mask when printing with ASA. Your health is too important to risk it! If this solution proves beneficial for you, I would greatly appreciate it if you could consider boosting me. Your support means a lot to me. Please also take a moment to comment, bookmark this model, and share it with others. I value all feedback, especially suggestions for model improvements. Please be aware that commercial sales of this model are strictly prohibited.

description: 🌀 Efficiently Reactivate Your Silica Gel Bags Inside Your Bambu Spool! Get your damp silica gel bags back to their original state in no time! This clever insert was specifically designed for empty Bambu Lab plastic spools. It leverages the rotational design of standard filament dryers to reactivate up to 10 silica gel bags (up to 20g each) quickly, evenly, and gently. ✨ Key Features: Smart Space Utilization: Transforms an empty Bambu spool into a highly efficient drying station. Axial Alignment: The bags are perfectly positioned within the airflow. This ensures maximum air circulation and significantly reduces drying time. 360° Uniformity: Perfect for filament dryers that rotate the spool during operation – ensuring every bag is reactivated evenly from all sides. High Capacity: Securely holds up to 10 bags simultaneously (up to 20g each). 100% Support-Free: The design is fully optimized for printing without any support structures. ⚙️ Recommended Print Settings The model is extremely easy to print. You can simply use your slicer's default settings. However, please pay close attention to your material selection! Material: Must be at least PETG , but ABS or ASA is highly recommended. Since high temperatures are reached during the reactivation of silica gel in a dryer, standard PLA is not suitable and will deform. Support: None needed – the model is optimized for printing without supports. Infill & Walls: Your standard 0.20mm slicer profile settings are perfectly sufficient. 🚀 How to Use: Print the insert using a heat-resistant material (e.g., PETG). Simply insert the part into the center of your empty Bambu Lab spool. Place your damp silica gel bags into the axial slots (max. 10 bags, 20g each). Place the spool into your filament dryer (ideal for dryers where the spool rotates). Start the drying process – thanks to the rotation and optimized airflow, your bags will be ready to use again in no time! ❤️ Do you like this practical utility model? Desenvolvi este suporte para manter os tubos PTFE sempre alinhados ao centro dos carretéis de filamento, reduzindo o atrito durante a alimentação e proporcionando um fluxo muito mais suave e consistente. description: An honest, straightforward utility tool for Bambu Lab A1 series owners. This tool doesn't magically yank the tube out on its own, but it solves the main pain point: pressing down on the small black PTFE release collets near the extruder. Instead of digging your fingernails in or straining your fingers in a tight space, this tool lets you apply comfortable, even pressure across the entire collet ring. 🛠 How to Use & Troubleshooting Stuck Tubes Standard Removal: Place the tool over the black PTFE collet, press down firmly to disengage the collet teeth, and gently pull the PTFE tube out with your other hand. If the tube is stuck (Twist Technique): Don't just pull it straight up. Push the PTFE tube slightly downward , twist it , and then use the tool to depress the collet while pulling the tube out. description: An open-frame, highly configurable AMS riser designed around standard 2020 aluminum extrusions. Built for flexibility, expansion, and minimal material waste without requiring complete reprints when modifying your setup. KEY FEATURES Configurable & Expandable: Utilizes 2020 aluminum extrusions to allow custom attachments and easy adjustments as your setup evolves. Open & Lightweight: Minimizes filament usage and print times while maintaining structural rigidity. Forgiving Tolerances: Main frame pieces are separated from the interlocking connectors. If tolerances differ due to filament or slicer settings, only small connector pieces need quick reprinting—saving time and material. Reversible Assembly: Friction-fit tapered draft joints hold the frame together snugly without glue, allowing full disassembly if needed. Preserves all original factory (OEM) functions of the top glass lid (removable with lid closed sensor actuator). HARDWARE REQUIREMENTS Main Riser: 4x Corner Frame Sections + 4x Interlocking Keys Secure Brackets: 4x Printer Cabinet Retainer Clips AMS Mounts: 8x AMS Corner Retainers (4x Left, 4x Right) Threaded Inserts: 4x M4 Heat Set Threaded Inserts Magnet: 1x Small Magnet (4mm diameter x 1.75mm thick) 2020 Aluminum Extrusions: 8x 2020 end caps 2x Frame Side Rails (Cut to 475mm minus the thickness of your end caps) 2x AMS Support Rails (Cut to 760mm) Fasteners & Hardware: M4x8mm Socket Head Cap Screws (SHCS) M4 2020 T-Nuts 2020 90-Degree Corner Brackets Compression Spring (for Lid Sensor Switch) Optional: 2020 End Caps ASSEMBLY GUIDE Step 1: Assemble the Riser Frame Install Threaded Inserts: Heat-set one M4 threaded insert into the provided hole on each of the four main riser pieces (refer to diagrams for placement). Join the Frame: Lay out the four main riser pieces upside down on a smooth, flat surface. Insert the interlocking keys and cabinet retainer devices. Note: The interlocking components feature a slight draft taper to draw the joints tight as they seat. Make sure they are oriented correctly before pressing them together. No adhesive is required. Step 2: Attach Side Extrusions Mount the two 475mm side extrusions to the left and right sides of the main riser frame using the M4x8mm SHCS and M4 T-nuts through the pre-drilled countersunk holes. Step 3: Install AMS Crossbar Extrusions Mount the two 760mm extrusions across the frame using 2020 90-degree corner brackets. Rear Rail: Align flush with the riser assembly and tighten securely. Front Rail: Install loosely for now—you will adjust its position when seating the AMS units. Step 4: Fit AMS Units and Corner Retainers Install the 8 AMS corner retainers onto the support rails (pay attention to Left vs. Right orientation): Secure the four outer corner retainers first, ensuring they are square to one another. Attach the four inner corner retainers loosely so they can slide. Place an AMS unit onto its outer retainers, lower it into the inner retainers, and adjust until the unit rests flat without rocking. Carefully lift the AMS unit straight up and tighten the inner retainers. Repeat for the second AMS unit, then fully tighten the front crossbar rail. Step 5: Mount to Printer Remove the glass lid from the printer and set the riser frame into the top cavity. Engage the four retainer brackets so their fingers grip under the printer cabinet rim for a secure fit. Step 6: Assemble Lid Sensor Switch Install Magnet: Glue a small magnet (4mm diameter x 1.75mm thick) into the cavity on the end of the pushbutton shaft (refer to diagram). Assemble Pushbutton: Drop the two-part pushbutton assembly into the front-left hole of the riser: Place the spring inside the outer barrel. Insert the pushbutton stem, ensuring it glides smoothly. (If making a custom spring, wrap spring wire around an appropriate diameter mandrel until you achieve desired tension and bounce). Step 7: Final Set Up Reinstall the top glass lid onto the newly installed riser assembly, place your AMS units into the corner retainers, and run your lines.

description: AMS Reliability Kit Tired of cardboard spools falling off the AMS rollers? Frustrated when nearly empty filament rolls won't feed reliably? I designed the AMS Reliability Kit to solve both problems. This system keeps spools properly aligned on the rollers, prevents them from walking side-to-side, and adds extra weight to lightweight or nearly empty spools for more consistent feeding. After implementing this system I have have experenice significantly less mid print errors errors. Features ✔ Now you can use up those almost empty filament rolls instead of throwing them away. ✔ Now you can reliably print with cardboard spools. ✔ Keeps all four spools properly centered for smoother operation. ✔ Refillable spool weight improves traction for lightweight and low-filament spools. Spool Weight has a 2nd Inner cap so you dont have to worry about your weights falling out when moving to new spools ✔ Easy to print and install. Why I Made It I designed this system because my cardboard spools were constantly falling off the AMS rollers , especially as they became lighter. After dealing with countless failed prints, I decided to create a solution that keeps every spool where it belongs and improves feeding reliability. The Full kit includes: 2× Outer Spool Guides 2× Center Spool Guides 4× Refillable Spool Weight Whether you're printing with cardboard spools, plastic spools, or almost-empty rolls , the AMS Reliability Kit helps your AMS feed filament more consistently and lets you finish every last gram of filament with confidence. Assembly Instructions Outer Spool Guides The thin, flat section of each Outer Spool Guide slides between the inner black AMS tray and the outer transparent shell. The guides are intentionally not designed to fit rigidly. This prevents unnecessary pressure that could damage or warp the AMS tray or outer shell. A small amount of movement is normal. Inner Spool Guides The Inner Spool Guides have cutouts along the bottom that pressure-fit over the original short dividers built into the AMS tray. Press each guide down only far enough to hold it securely. Do not press the guides all the way down against the spool rollers. Contact with the rollers may prevent them from rotating properly. After installation, spin the rollers by hand to confirm that they move freely. Spool Weight Fill the Spool Weight Body with a suitable dense material. I recommend using 9 mm steel ball bearings , such as these ball bearings on Amazon . Other options include: Steel nuts, washers, or small sockets Fishing weights Other compact metal objects Do not use batteries , as damaged or aging batteries can leak, corrode, or create a safety hazard. Once the body is filled, thread in the Spool Weight Seal to secure the weights inside. Do not overfill the body, the seal must seat completely into the threads. You can confirm that the seal is fully seated by installing the Spool Cap . If the cap does not sit completely against the body, remove some weight and reinstall the seal. Once the seal is installed, the outer cap can be easily removed whenever you need to transfer the weight to another spool without the weights falling out. Funnel Saver In the .3MF File I have included the “AMS 2 Pro Funnel Saver Guides” from YelTrik Designs Refer to this Model for intructions and use case. They have complemented my AMS Reliabilty Setup well. Feedback and Modification Requests Have an idea for an improvement or need a modified version? Do not remove brim if you are not sure your print bed has insane adhesion. Print with PETG if you have a really hot chamber and want to prevent the chute from being damaged by the hot air from the chamber. erick974 said that this chute, if made of PLA, can deform when printing stuff made of ASA for example. Customizable Navigation Bar Holder / GPS Bar Clamp A customizable two-piece navigation bar holder for motorcycle GPS, phone, tablet and DMD-style mounts. This model is designed as a parametric OpenSCAD / MakerWorld Customizer file. You can adjust the bar diameter, clamp tolerance, block size, bolt spacing, nut pockets and corner radius directly in the MakerWorld customizer. Key Features Fully customizable bar diameter Designed for navigation bars, GPS bars and handlebar-style mounting points Bar runs through the short side of the block Two-piece clamp design: front and back part Both parts are placed print-ready with the groove facing upward M4 bolt holes Optional M4 hex nut pockets in the back part Rounded corners Adjustable clamp undersize for a tighter or looser fit Suitable for common adventure motorcycle navigation bars Common Diameter Examples Recommended starting values: BMW / adventure GPS bar: Bar_Diameter = 12.0 Clamp_Undersize = 0.30 Hardware M4 Bolt 25mm M4 nyloc nuts Some BMW navigation bars: Bar_Diameter = 16.0 Clamp_Undersize = 0.30 Hardware M4 Bolt 30mm M4 nyloc nuts Always measure your own bar with calipers before printing. Small differences matter for clamp fit. Important Assembly Note Both parts are shown in print orientation with the bar groove facing upward. For assembly: Place the back part against the navigation bar. Flip the front part over. Put the front part over the bar. Insert the M4 bolts. Tighten gradually and evenly. The two half-round grooves will clamp around the bar. Parameters Main customizer parameters: Bar_Diameter Nominal diameter of your motorcycle navigation bar. Bar_Offset_X Moves the bar groove left or right from the center of the block. This is useful when the navigation bar needs to sit slightly off-center. Default value: 0.0 mm Range: -10 mm to +10 mm Clamp_Undersize Reduces the actual groove diameter for a tighter clamp. Example: Bar_Diameter = 12.0 and Clamp_Undersize = 0.30 creates an effective 11.7 mm clamp . Block_Length Overall length of the clamp block. Block_Width Overall width of the clamp block. Half_Thickness Thickness of each half. Set to 0 for automatic thickness. Corner_Radius Controls the rounded corners. Bolt Parameters Bolt_Size Selects the bolt size used for the clamp. Options: M3, M4, M5 The model automatically adjusts the bolt hole diameter and nut pocket size based on this setting. Bolt_Clearance Adds extra clearance to the selected bolt diameter. Example : Bolt_Size = M4 Bolt_Clearance = 0.5 This creates a 4.5 mm bolt hole. Increase this value if your printer makes holes too tight. Manual_Hole_Diameter Manual override for the bolt hole diameter. Set this value to 0 to use automatic hole sizing based on Bolt_Size and Bolt_Clearance. Use this only if you want full manual control over the hole diameter. Hole_Spacing_X Horizontal spacing between the left and right bolt holes. Measured center-to-center. Hole_Spacing_Y Vertical spacing between the upper and lower bolt holes. Measured center-to-center. Back Nut Pocket Parameters Nut_Pockets Enables or disables hexagonal nut pockets in the back part. Options : true Adds hex nut pockets to the back part. false Creates normal through-holes only. Nut_Pocket_Clearance Adds extra clearance to the automatic nut pocket size. Increase this value if your nuts are too tight. Decrease this value if your nuts are too loose. Manual_Nut_Flat_To_Flat Manual override for the hex nut pocket size. Measured flat-to-flat. Set this value to 0 to use automatic sizing based on Bolt_Size and Nut_Pocket_Clearance. Manual_Nut_Depth Manual override for the hex nut pocket depth. Set this value to 0 to use automatic depth based on Bolt_Size. Increase this value if your nuts sit proud of the surface. Advanced Parameters Preview_Cutaway Creates a cutaway preview to inspect the internal groove and holes. Options: false Normal printable model. true Cutaway preview mode. Use false before exporting for printing. Facet_Count Controls the smoothness of circular features such as the bar groove, bolt holes and nut pockets. Options : 32, 48, 64, 96, 128 Recommended value : 96 Higher values create smoother curves but may generate larger files. Print Settings Recommended material: PETG ASA ABS PETG-CF Suggested settings: 4–6 walls/perimeters 40–60% infill 0.2 mm layer height Print both parts with the groove facing upward Use supports only if your slicer requires them for the nut pockets For motorcycle use, avoid PLA because heat and sunlight can deform the part. Hardware Recommended hardware: 4x M4 bolts 4x M4 nuts or nyloc nuts Optional washer under bolt heads Optional thin rubber strip or double-sided tape around the bar for extra grip Disclaimer This is a DIY 3D printed motorcycle accessory. Use at your own risk. Check fitment and strength before riding. Re-check bolt tightness after the first ride and inspect the part regularly for cracks or wear. Credits Created as a customizable navigation bar holder for motorcycle GPS / DMD-style mounting setups.

description: ## Bumblebee Security Camera Housing – Tapo TC71 Compatible Bring the ultimate Autobot protector to your desk or shelf! This custom-designed, Bumblebee-inspired security camera housing is built specifically to fit the **Tapo TC71** camera. ### The Story Behind the Model This is my **first-ever 3D model**! After seeing an inspiring video online, I decided to take on the challenge. I used AI to generate the initial concept image, converted it into a 3D model, and then heavily modified and engineered the design from scratch to make sure it fits the Tapo TC71 perfectly. I poured a lot of energy, time, and hours of trial and error into this project. As a beginner, I learned so much along the way (and used quite a bit of filament to get it just right!). I would be incredibly happy to hear your feedback, advice, or suggestions—good or bad—to help me improve for my next designs! --- ### Key Features * **Perfect Fit:** Tailored specifically for the Tapo TC71 camera. * **Super Stable Base:** Designed with a heavy, massive torso and legs to ensure your camera stands rock-solid on your desk without tipping over. * **Lightweight Helmet:** The helmet section is optimized to be light and perfectly sized so it doesn't strain the camera rotation. * **Two Versions Included:** Choose between the **Pin-Joint Assembly** version or the **Fixed** version. --- ### Print Settings & Assembly Tips My test models (shown in the photos) were successfully printed with the following setups: * **Yellow Version:** Printed on a **Bambu Lab A1** using the **0.24mm Draft** profile. * **Gold Version:** Printed on a **Bambu X2D** using a **Standard Layout / Settings**. To save you some headaches, here are my highly recommended tips based on my test prints: * **The Golden Rule for the First Layer:** I highly recommend starting your print at **50% speed** until the first layer is perfectly laid down and has solid bed adhesion. Once the ground is good, you can safely bump the speed back up. * **A Warning on Multi-Color Printing (AMS/AMS Lite):** I strongly advise **against** printing this model in multiple colors directly from the slicer. I tested printing just a single leg in 2 colors, and the filament waste (purge) was equivalent to the weight of an entire extra leg! It is much more efficient and cost-effective to print it in a single color and post-process/paint it afterward (which is exactly what I did with my painted version!). * **If you choose the Pin-Joint Version:** * Scale the legs up by **1mm or 1.5mm on the X, Y, and Z axes** in your slicer. * Give the pins a quick, light sanding before assembly. This will make them fit smoothly. If they go in too tight, you risk breaking the pins when trying to disassemble them. * **If you want a hassle-free print (Fixed Version):** * Print the **Fixed version**. It takes a little longer to print, but you won't need to scale anything or worry about joint tolerances. Everything is pre-sized and ready to go! --- ### Feedback is Welcome! Since I am just starting my 3D design journey, please feel free to leave a comment, post your makes, or give me a Boost if you like my work! Your support and advice mean the world to me.

description: Flow Rate Calibration Cube | Micrometer Dieser einwandige, oben offene Kalibrierungswürfel dient zur präzisen Einstellung der Flussrate beziehungsweise des Flow Ratio eines Filaments. Die tatsächliche Wandstärke wird an mehreren Stellen mit einer Bügelmessschraube oder einem präzisen Mikrometer gemessen. Aus dem Mittelwert aller Messungen lässt sich anschließend der korrigierte Flussratenwert für das verwendete Filamentprofil berechnen. Der Würfel benötigt nur wenig Material, ist schnell gedruckt und eignet sich ideal zur Feinabstimmung neuer oder bereits vorhandener Filamentprofile. Benötigte Hilfsmittel Bügelmessschraube oder präzises Mikrometer Bambu Studio oder ein kompatibler Slicer Das zu kalibrierende Filament Aktueller Flussratenwert des Filamentprofils Eingestellte Linienbreite der Außenwand Durchführung 1. Würfel drucken Drucke den Würfel mit genau dem Filamentprofil, das kalibriert werden soll. Verändere für den anschließenden Kontrolltest möglichst keine anderen Einstellungen wie Temperatur, Geschwindigkeit oder Linienbreite. Lasse das Modell nach dem Druck vollständig abkühlen. 2. Wandstärke messen Miss jede der vier Würfelseiten an mehreren Stellen: mindestens 3 Messungen pro Seite empfohlen sind 5 Messungen pro Seite bei 5 Messungen pro Seite entstehen insgesamt 20 Messwerte Miss möglichst mittig auf den geraden Wandflächen. Vermeide dabei: die Ecken des Würfels die Z-Naht den oberen Rand die ersten Schichten sichtbar unregelmäßige Stellen Verwende bei jeder Messung einen gleichmäßigen und möglichst geringen Messdruck. Mittelwert berechnen Addiere alle gemessenen Wandstärken und teile die Summe durch die Anzahl der Messungen: Mittelwert = Summe aller Messwerte ÷ Anzahl der Messwerte Je mehr saubere Messungen verwendet werden, desto zuverlässiger ist das Ergebnis. Zielwert bestimmen Der Zielwert entspricht der in Bambu Studio eingestellten Linienbreite der Außenwand . Du findest den Wert unter: Qualität → Breite der Linien → Außenwand Beispiel: Außenwand-Linienbreite: 0,42 mm Wichtig: Verwende als Zielwert nicht automatisch den Düsendurchmesser, sondern immer die tatsächlich eingestellte Linienbreite der Außenwand. Aktuellen Flussratenwert ermitteln Öffne das verwendete Filamentprofil und notiere den dort eingestellten aktuellen Wert für die: Flussrate / Flow Ratio Beispiel: Bisheriger Flow Ratio: 0,988 Neuen Flow Ratio berechnen Verwende folgende Formel: Neuer Flow Ratio = Zielwert × bisheriger Flow Ratio ÷ gemessener Mittelwert Beispielrechnung Zielwert: 0,42 mm Bisheriger Flow Ratio: 0,988 Gemessener Mittelwert: 0,421 mm Rechnung: 0,42 × 0,988 ÷ 0,421 = 0,985653 Gerundet ergibt sich ein neuer Flow Ratio von: 0,986 Trage den neuen Wert anschließend in das Filamentprofil ein. Drucke den Würfel danach erneut und kontrolliere die Wandstärke mit einer weiteren Messung. Falls erforderlich, kann die Berechnung wiederholt werden. Excel-Formel Die Berechnung kann auch direkt in Excel oder einer anderen Tabellenkalkulation durchgeführt werden: =Zielwert*Bisheriger_Wert/Mittelwert Beispiel mit Zellbezügen: =I13*I6/D6 Dabei steht: I13 für den bisherigen Flow-Ratio-Wert I6 für den Zielwert D6 für den Mittelwert aller Messungen Ergebnis interpretieren Gemessene Wand ist dicker als der Zielwert: Der Flow Ratio wird reduziert. Gemessene Wand ist dünner als der Zielwert: Der Flow Ratio wird erhöht. Mittelwert entspricht dem Zielwert: Die Flussrate ist bereits passend eingestellt. Hinweise Die Kalibrierung sollte für jedes Filamentprofil separat durchgeführt werden. Hersteller, Material, Farbe, Drucktemperatur und weitere Einstellungen können das Ergebnis beeinflussen. Dieser Würfel dient ausschließlich zur Kalibrierung der Flussrate beziehungsweise des Flow Ratio . Er ist nicht für die Einstellung von Flow Dynamics, Pressure Advance oder K-Wert vorgesehen. Für reproduzierbare Ergebnisse sollten alle Messungen mit derselben Bügelmessschraube und mit möglichst gleichmäßigem Messdruck durchgeführt werden. Druckprofil Einwandiger, oben offener Kalibrierungswürfel Keine Stützstrukturen erforderlich Geringer Materialverbrauch Kurze Druckzeit Ideal für wiederholte Kontrollmessungen Druckzeit und Materialverbrauch können abhängig von Drucker, Filament und verwendeten Einstellungen abweichen.

Tired of ironing that comes out blobby, dragged, or just plain ugly? So was I. Most ironing calibration tests wastes filament printing giant plates covered in embossed numbers you only need to read once. This one lets you skip that entirely and just read the image in the documentation. Each square on the plate is set to a different combination of ironing flow percentage and ironing line spacing . Print it, find the square with the cleanest top surface, and plug those exact values into your slicer. Done. What's included: Ironing Test (No Numbers) .3mf — the clean version. Prints just the squares, saving you the filament and time of printing embossed labels. Use this one with the mapping image below. Ironing Test (With Numbers) .3mf — same plate, but with each square labeled if you'd rather have the values printed right on the model. Mapping image — shows which square corresponds to which flow % and line-spacing combo, so the no-numbers version tells you everything you need without the extra plastic. description: This is a fully custom window‑mounted vent system I designed for my Bambu H2C printer. My goals were simple: Airtight Secure Permanent installation Fast magnetic connection/disconnection of the exhaust hose Weatherproof cover for when the printer isn’t running I wasn’t satisfied with the existing MakerWorld options, and my window is only 521 mm wide , so I built something specifically for my setup — but I’m sharing the Fusion file, STEP file, and laser‑cut gasket files so you can adapt it to your own window if it’s similar. This design is meant for small windows, but the parametric model makes it possible to adjust dimensions if your window differs. Features 🔒 Airtight & Secure The duct and window frame use 2 mm EVA foam gaskets , recessed 1 mm into the mating surfaces for a tight seal. With magnets pulling the duct into place, the connection feels solid and leak‑free. 🧲 Magnetic Quick‑Connect The system uses 10 mm × 2 mm neodymium round magnets : 10 magnets in the window frame 10 magnets in the duct Optional: 10 magnets in the weather cover This lets you instantly attach the exhaust hose when printing, and swap it for the weather cover when not. 🌧️ Weatherproof Cover The optional cover seals the opening when the duct is removed. I printed mine in PETG, but any outdoor‑friendly filament works. 🪟 Permanent Window Fixture The window frame stays installed permanently. The two halves connect with a tight dovetail joint . I intentionally used small tolerances for a high‑quality feel — sanding the edges slightly helps if the fit is too snug. 🧰 Customizable CAD Files Included: Fusion 360 file with editable parameters STEP file for use in any CAD program .lac laser file for cutting EVA gaskets Printable gasket groove outlines if cutting by hand If your window is wider than ~520 mm, you may need to split the extension piece — Bambu Studio makes this easy with built in tools. 🧪 Material Recommendations ASA‑CF (my choice): weather‑resistant, rigid, great for outdoor use PETG : perfectly fine for most users Any other weather resistant material that has some temperature resistance (ABS, PET-CF, etc.) Parts & Materials Printed Parts Window Frame (2 pieces, dovetail connection) Duct Outside Vent Weather Cover (optional) Gasket inserts (optional if cutting by hand) Hardware 30 ea. - 10 mm × 2 mm neodymium magnets EVA foam sheets , minimum 9" × 12" , 2 mm thick Glue for gaskets (contact cement or similar adhesive works best, super glue not recommended as it's likely too rigid) Tools Bambu H2C laser module (optional, could cut gaskets by hand) Sandpaper (for dovetail tuning) Utility knife if cutting gaskets manually Assembly Notes Ensure magnet polarity is consistent across all parts. Install magnets on the duct and optional weather cover are opposite polarity of magents in the window frame so they attract and don't oppose. Test-fit the dovetail before final installation — light sanding may be needed. Laser Cutting Notes (H2C 10W) For 2 mm EVA foam gaskets, these settings work extremely well: Power: 35% Speed: 6 Air assistant: On Pass: 1 Cut Offset: 0.00 This produces crisp edges with minimal melt. Who This Is For This design is not universal — it was built specifically for my window dimensions and style. But if your window is similar, or you’re comfortable modifying CAD files, this can get you most of the way to a perfect custom vent. If your window is very different, you may still find the duct, magnet system, and gasket approach useful as a starting point. Feel free to download my files as a starting point for your project. IMPORTANT: Before committing to a full print, I strongly recommend slicing off a small test segment of the window frame to verify the fit in your window. In your slicer, cut a short 3–5 inch section from the model (left‑to‑right, as it sits in the frame) and print that first. This quick test ensures the final part will fit properly before you invest time and material into the full print. Included Files Fusion 360 file (with parameters) STEP file STL files for all parts .lac laser file for EVA gaskets Printable gasket outlines Assembly instructions (text) Final Thoughts This vent has been rock‑solid for me — airtight, secure, and incredibly convenient. I can leave the window fixture installed permanently, snap the duct on magnetically whenever I print, and seal it with the weather cover when I’m done. If you adapt it to your own window, I’d love to see your remix.

model_name: The Ultimate Wall Mounted TPU Spool Holder!
tags: bambu|BAMBU LAB|TPU|tpu spool|tpu spool holder|tpu spool mount|wallmounted tpu|tpu wallmount|tpu holder|tpu bearing|tpu 608|spool|spool holder|spool holder bearings
description: This is the ultimate, fully customizable, wall mounted spool holder which should be suitable for the softest of filaments. It has been tested with: Bambu 95A Bambu 90A Bambu 85A Bambu TPU for AMS Siraya tech flex TPU Of course it should work with all standard filaments too. It features a total of six “tool” holders. The central two (one on each main arm) below the hub are designed to take the flap brake. The flap brake will only work with these two. The other holders are used for the friction brakes. This is the third version of my wall mount and based on the original one which was super smooth but had little control, could run backwards and overrun. I did update it with some brakes which helped but they weren’t very adjustable at all and adding a flap brake just wasn’t practical. I am still in a testing phase but even without adjusting between filaments this version has worked flawlessly so far. I hope it does for you too! Upgrading? For people who already have that old version, this version can re-use at least some parts you already have printed: The original wall brackets will work (although they will be tighter than the new ones). The PTFE tube holder is unchanged. The rear joining bracket is unchanged The wall template is unchanged, no need to redrill anything! Printing Suggestions. The 3MF file contains the settings and support methods I used for this print. Filament: Bambu PLA Metal Iridium Bambu PLA Metal Iron Grey Sparse infill 25% (15% will work just fne) Sparse infill pattern Gyroid Place brim ears on all four parts the two piece arms. In Bambu slicer the brim ears tool set to auto does a great job. You will need to set the brim type to “painted”. Materials you will need: Plugs and screws. Check the screw heads will sit in the countersunk hole and clear the dovetail on the arm. Plugs – if required – I used Fischer 4no. 6x30, 6mm drill bit Screws – 4no. 4x35 – make sure the head will sit within the recess A small amount of PTFE tube. (This is not essential, you can bypass the PTFE holder in use if you choose) Two 608 bearings – these are pretty good: https://www.amazon.co.uk/dp/B08ZN94S5L?ref=ppx_yo2ov_dt_b_fed_asin_title but almost any 608 bearing should be fine. Fleece fabric Tessa tape,19- 20mm ideally 51608-00001-00 Or Cable tie Velcro with the soft side as the brake 10-20mm wide Super glue. Installation and assembly: This video should help you understand how it works when assembled, I’d recommend you have sound turned on whilst I’m fitting the brake. Sorry.. VERY boring video :( https://youtube.com/shorts/ZhJ1bJGjlVE?feature=share Choosing parts: Note that I have named all the parts in the 3MF file. I will refer to them here. There are two types of spool arms. One set is only printable on a large bed printer such as the H2D. The other set should be printable on most printer beds and offers a different aesthetic if you use two colours. Photos/videos are of the two part type. Choose how many tool arms to print and of which type (more on this later!). If in doubt just print one standard tool arm “ARM TYPE1 MEDIUM”, one flap brake arm “ARM TYPE 3 Flap Brake”. Note: Arms can be inserted upside down in the front arm holder. Choose which tool to print, again, if in doubt I would suggest “Brake Tool TYPE 1” which has the ridges around and no chamfer. Choose a cover plate type (you may not want cover plates at all!) Note that the large cover plate has a bambu logo which looks nice if printed in a different colour. Choose your axle cap design round or hex – photos are of the hex type. You can choose not to print the flanges. The hub does not require either of them but you won’t get the non-reverse function of course. There is a filament guide included “Flimanent Guide OPTIONAL”. This helped to stop filament loop drops in version 1. I still have it mounted in this version (in the photos) but I haven’t used it nor needed it so far. I would suggest you don’t print it unless you have problems and think it will help. Wall mounting: I would recommend printing the template and using that to position the drill holes. Accuracy IS important. Check that your screw heads will sit within the counter sunk holes. The wall brackets have a little vertical movement in them. Screw the brackets to the wall. Assembly: The two part version is very easy to put together but make sure you trim any access filament (the brim) off the joint on both sides! You can only push the two parts together from one side. Lay the main arm flat on a table and push the small arm on until the whole thing is flush. It may require some force, it’s designed to be tight. A light tap with a hammer can help. Join the parts of the PTFE tube holder together to match the photos. Attach the PTFE tube holder to one of the arms. Take the rear bracket and insert it, bevel edges forward onto the same arm. Now take the other arm and carefully seat it on both the rear bracket and the PTFE tube carrier. Now slide the whole assembly onto the wall brackets to check alignment. It should slide on easily. Assemble the hubs. Remove any support material, use snipe nose pliers to remove the support in the axel socket. Check the supported edge looks flat with no bits of support left and test fit the flanges (if you are using them) to make sure they are flat and flush when seated. Push an axel in each hub as far as it will go. Put a spacer sleeve on next, then your bearings which should be a fairly snug fit. Finally your choice of axel cap. The cap should take quite a bit of force to get on. If it is loose you might want to add some glue. Fitting the flanges Test fit the flanges again. They should be fairly loose fitting without glue. This is by design. Remove them, run a bead of superglue all the way around the edge of the hub, stick the flanges on and leave to dry. Check they are well stuck! Almost done! The hubs should fit together without any effort. Obviously they need to come apart to insert your spools so don’t glue them! Put them together and try dropping the hub into the wall mount. It should drop in and pull out with almost no effort. If it sticks or doesn’t seat correctly there may be some support materials in the arm sockets. If there isn’t try taking the hib in and our a few times. If it doesn’t and the arms didn’t slide into the the wall brackets with ease then you may have an alignment problem. Check your drilling template against the holes in the wall. How things work and Tuning: Flap Brake (s): The function of the flap brake is primarily to stop the spool from running backwards. You will need the smaller ARM TYPE3 (they aren’t handed) and one flap brake for the side you intend to use it on. Fit the brake to the arm (it should fit fairly tightly). When correctly aligned the outer ARM hex faces should line up with the Flap Brake male end hex faces but the most important part is that the flat end of the flap must line up perfectly with the deep flat edge of the scoops on the flange plate. Once fitted the arm can be adjusted by pulling it in and out. Insert it roughly into position so that the end just sits in a scoop The designed position is when it “ticks” fairly quietly in the forward direction and stops the spool turning in the reverse direction. Tuning the flap brake: “Turn” any other brakes off! Use your hand to manually turn the spool forwards and check that there is little to no resistance and you can hear the flap ticking on the disc. Then try to gently spin with spool in reverse. It should be stopped almost immediately as the flap connects with an edge. Note - If you want you can put flap brakes on both sides of the holder. Note – The flap brakes can actually be used as friction brakes too if you push the tool arm in further – it will just be more noisy! Main friction Brakes: Generally I would recommend installing just one or two but you can use up to four. NOTE: Why four? Partly – just in case and you might only have access to one side of the holder but you may like to have one on each side to keep the spool aligned or all four installed to keep everything aligned with a light pressure on all of them. There are two brake types, one is designed for Tessa tape or Velcro style cable ties to wrap around. The other can also take tape but can be used on it’s own – you can just angle the chamfered part against the spool. Tuning the main friction brakes: You can push and pull the arms and you can also angle the tool head on the arm which should allow to you to really fine tune the amount of friction you are applying perfectly to suit the filament type. My personal preference is to use Tessa tape, it sticks on and the surface is very smooth. Tool arms: The arms are handed for left and right There are three types. Short – This makes the tool easy to remove but doesn’t provide much resistance to stop the tool head from being moved when tilted. Medium – Recommended. Some give but plenty of resistance. However it is quite hard to pull the arm out without breaking it. Long – Loads of resistance, almost impossible to remove the arm. Basically a permanent position once you push the head all the way on. Happy Soft Filament printing! Minor update 14-7-2026: The flap stop could catch on the edge of a flange when a spool is dropped in to the arms. This version adds a chamfer to the flanges to make it smoother and less likely to catch and rotate the flap stops.
