tags: spear|bronze age spear|spear of king fuchai of wu|spearhead
description: This spearhead model is inspired by the famous Spear of King Fuchai of Wu (吴王夫差矛) . If you're interested in the history behind the original artifact, you can read about it on Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spear_of_Fuchai The spearhead is modeled at approximately the same size as the original artifact and is just over 300 mm long. Since it exceeds the printable height of many printers, it is split into two pieces that are joined with the included connector. I recommend printing one spearhead piece per build plate, even though it may be tempting to place both pieces on the same plate. There are two reasons for this: Print stability – The spearhead is very thin and tall. When both pieces are printed side by side, the nozzle may strike one of them while traveling between parts, causing a print failure. (I learned this the hard way.) If you decide to print both at once, place them end-to-end (like - -) rather than side-by-side (like =) to reduce the chance of collisions. Surface finish – I found that the surface texture is noticeably smoother when only a single part is printed on the build plate. Printing multiple parts at once produced a slightly different finish. This may depend on your filament or printer, but for the best-looking result, I recommend printing the pieces individually. The spearhead shown in the photos was printed using ERYONE Gold Silk PLA at a 0.16 mm layer height. The gold color is intentional —newly cast bronze weapons had a golden appearance.The greenish appearance of the surviving artifact is due to the patina formed during more than two thousand years of corrosion. The pole is designed as 25 mm in diameter and is divided into 150 mm (approximately 6 in) sections. Each section uses M20 × 1.5 threads, allowing you to print as many sections as needed and screw them together to create a spear of your desired length. I printed the pole sections with Fuzzy Skin enabled to create a nice visual contrast with the smooth, polished spearhead. The pommel completes the assembly. To avoid support, a threaded connector was included and the pommel can be threaded onto the end of the pole using that connector. Printing Notes Supports is required for the lower spearhead section only. The upper spearhead section, pole sections, connector, and pommel print without supports. For maximum strength, glue the two spearhead halves together after inserting the connector. Note: The cover image was created using AI.

description: A Project Hail Mary inspired glove. This is the “Weaver”, which is based of of Rocky's 3d printer thingies that he uses to make the little figurines and chains seen in the movie. The connection between these two pieces is designed to be a friction fit, so no glue is needed. On the finger clamp pieces, there are also two slots meant for “finger rings”. For each finger clamp, you should use one small finger ring on the tip and one regular finger ring on the back. description: Inspired by Homer's Iliad , this full-size modular spear is my own interpretation of Achilles' legendary weapon. Rather than recreating a movie or game prop, I wanted to design a display piece that captures the spirit of ancient Greek mythology while remaining practical to print and assemble on a standard FDM printer. Every decorative section tells part of Achilles' story through carefully chosen artwork: Greek key borders inspired by classical architecture Olive branches representing Greece A Corinthian helmet surrounded by laurel branches, symbolizing Achilles as a victorious warrior Mount Pelion with ash leaves, referencing the legendary origin of Achilles' spear The Greek inscription ΑΧΙΛΛΕΥΣ engraved into the shaft Realistic wood grain running throughout the spear The completed spear measures approximately 200 cm in length and is designed around a 150 cm wooden broomstick handle , creating a lightweight yet incredibly strong display piece. Modular Design This model has been designed to suit different building styles. For maximum strength and durability, I recommend using a 150 cm wooden broomstick handle as the internal core. This creates a rigid finished spear while keeping the printed parts lightweight. However, the spear can also be assembled without the wooden core if you prefer a fully 3D printed version. For builders wanting additional reinforcement, the spearhead and butt spike have also been designed to accept: Four 10 mm × 40 mm wooden dowels Two 40 mm screws (8 mm head) These reinforcement methods are completely optional . They are included for builders who want extra strength, but the model can also be assembled without them depending on your intended use. Please note: Wooden broomstick handles and wooden dowels can vary slightly in diameter depending on the manufacturer. You may need to lightly sand the broomstick handle or dowels to achieve the perfect fit. Test fit all parts before applying glue. Colour Options This model has been designed to give makers complete creative freedom. Option 1 – Paint Your Own Print everything in a single colour and paint the model yourself to achieve realistic wood, bronze and twine effects. Option 2 – Multi-Colour Printing If you own a printer with an AMS or another multi-material system, the decorative details can be printed in multiple colours straight from the printer, allowing you to create your own unique version without painting. Whether painted by hand or printed in multiple colours, every maker can create their own interpretation of Achilles' legendary spear. Print Settings Material PETG Layer Height 0.16 mm Walls 3 Nozzle 0.4 mm Supports Only where required Additional Materials 1 × 150 cm wooden broomstick handle (approximately 30 mm diameter) 4 × Wooden dowels (10 mm × 40 mm) 2 × Screws (40 mm long with an 8 mm head) Super glue or epoxy Twine for both grip sections Assembly Instructions Test fit all printed parts onto the wooden broomstick handle before gluing. If required, lightly sand the broomstick handle or wooden dowels to achieve a smooth fit. Assemble the spearhead: Screw the spearhead socket onto the broomstick handle. Insert the two 10 × 40 mm wooden dowels. Apply glue and slide the spearhead into place. Install the first grip section (the decorative brass-style rings are already part of this printed piece). Install the Achilles shaft section, ensuring the ΑΧΙΛΛΕΥΣ inscription faces the correct direction so it can be read when the spear is standing upright. Install the remaining decorative shaft sections in any order you prefer. Install the second grip section. Assemble the butt spike: Screw the butt spike socket onto the broomstick handle. Insert the remaining two 10 × 40 mm wooden dowels. Apply glue and attach the butt spike. Wrap both grip sections with twine. Lightly pass a flame from a lighter over the twine to remove any loose fibers and give the grips a cleaner, more authentic finish. Take care not to scorch the printed parts. Features Approximately 2 meters long when assembled Modular construction Designed for standard 250 × 250 mm FDM printers Optional wooden core for maximum strength Optional dowel and screw reinforcement Detailed engraved artwork inspired by Homer's Iliad Beginner-friendly assembly Easy to transport and store thanks to the modular design Suitable for display, collections and cosplay Painting Suggestions Wood Dark brown base coat Medium brown dry brush Light tan highlights Metal Aged bronze or brass Black wash for weathering Light metallic dry brushing on edges Grips Leave the twine natural for a rustic appearance Or apply a light brown wash for an aged look Designer's Note Rather than recreating an existing film or game prop, this spear is an original interpretation inspired by Homer's Iliad . Every engraved section was chosen to represent part of Achilles' legend—from the ash wood of Mount Pelion to the Greek inscription of his name—creating a display piece that tells a story while remaining practical for everyday 3D printing. Whether you choose to paint it by hand or print it in multiple colours using an AMS, I hope you enjoy building it as much as I enjoyed designing it. If you make one, I'd love to see your finished version!

description: 一、模型设计概述 本模型基于《我的世界》游戏内二维像素剑造型进行3D重构。区别于仅做平面拉伸的同类模型，该设计利用高低落差的阶梯式结构，塑造出三维立体的体素浮雕质感。在无需多色打印的条件下，依然可通过光影呈现丰富的层次感。 剑柄部分针对握持的人体工学进行了重新设计。参考游戏内官方3D化逻辑，将原二维扁平剑柄进行90度旋转并合并重组，消除冗余块面，使握把具备真实的立体体积和圆润的握持手感。剑柄底部设计有贯穿的镂空结构，可穿入挂绳，用于悬挂或作为背包挂饰。 二、打印与组装参数 文件拆分 ：剑身与剑柄已完成分体处理，默认分布在1-2两盘，可分开独立打印。 公差与组装 ：经多重精度测试，公差控制精准。装配预期为无胶水拼装（摩擦力卡合结构），无需额外使用粘合剂。 打印设置测试 ：内部已进行多组打印参数实测，以保障最佳打印质量。 三、耗材适配与操作提示 多色与单色适配 ：模型未预设固定配色，任何基础色彩耗材均可直接打印。纯色打印即可凸显像素浮雕质感；若配备多色打印系统（如AMS），或具备后期手涂上色能力，由于全模型皆为方块构造，表面涂装和分色操作非常简便，可根据游戏原作色彩自行调配。 耗材翘边预警 ：模型默认未在剑身部分添加辅助裙边（Brim）。若使用PETG或ABS等收缩率较高的材料，打印时 必须 在切片软件中手动开启裙边功能，否则极易发生翘边；若使用PLA材料，则无需额外处理。 打印尺寸限制 ：针对A1 mini 等较小打印平台的机器，无法直接打印原比例尺寸模型，可通过切片软件等比缩小后输出缩小版本。 四、文件开源与兼容性说明 本模型同步提供 STEP 格式开源文件，可在网页端下载。用户可将其导入任意CAD软件中进行结构修改，用于创作个人二次开发版本。 注意 ：此STEP文件暂无法在 Bambu Studio 切片软件中直接打开。如需在常见切片软件中预览和打印，请直接下载模型提供的 STL 格式文件。

根据很多伸缩剑，做的一个模型，和雪糕结合起来。需要使用502胶水和雪糕桶粘起来就能使用了.只用粘3个分片就行了。切记不要多粘。 看了下打印评论，尽量使用 pla basic 。 不要使用 lite 或者其他 哑光 的耗材， 会出现 卡顿 ，甚至 粘连 的情况。 展开后会存在尖锐的部分，给小朋友玩要小心，注意安全。 这个部位会藏有支撑，也要清理干净。 如果拆了支撑还很紧致，可以握着这个上半部分敲打几下（注意控制力道，别拍碎了。） 粘胶的话，需要贴紧这些位置，粘的更牢固。

description: 7月24日最后一次更新（小尺寸钥匙扣） 需要用到ams多色打印，雏菊配件用胶水粘合（风车雏菊在安装良好的情况下也能迎风转动） 7月15日更新（香薰底座） 当我完成风车雏菊的时候我就在想，它放在我的电脑桌前，风从它的背后吹到我的脸上，除了风车能转动，它还能带来什么？我觉得它应该有一种淡淡的香味！所以我制作了一个可以放置香薰的底座！你可以把你喜欢的香薰藏在底部。 你还可以打印一些雏菊装饰它，让它变得更加美观跟清新！（雏菊制作完后用打火机燎一下，然后让所有的叶片翘起来） _________________________________________________________ 为什么做这个模型？ 我是一直很喜欢《玩具总动员》里的所有角色，尤其是巴斯光年！但最近却被三眼仔彻底圈粉了——特别是GD主理的PEACEMINUSONE和迪士尼、Toy Story合作的特别版，那个雏菊元素真的太戳我了。可惜国内一直买不到，心里痒痒的，就干脆自己动手，用SolidWorks建模设计了一个还原度比较高的外观。 正好夏天到了，我在电脑前常开风扇，就突发奇想： 能不能让雏菊转起来？ 于是就有了这个“三眼仔 × 风车雏菊”的互动模型——它既是摆件，也是一个可以迎风转动的小风车，放在桌面特别有趣（我非常喜欢它转动时发出的声响）。 🛠 设计与结构 全程使用 SolidWorks 建模（不是AI生成，每一个曲面和卡扣都是手工调整的，花了很多心血）。 完全无胶水组装 （除了嘴巴那块薄片，我暂时搞不定，如果有大神有妙招，恳请指点！）。 零件可替换 ：如果某个部位坏了，或者你想换颜色，直接拆换对应零件就行，非常方便。 🌼 雏菊的两种形态 我做了两套雏菊配件： 还原版 — 尽量贴近原版PEACEMINUSONE的雏菊造型（静态装饰）。 风车版 — 保留雏菊元素，但优化了叶片角度，可以迎风旋转。 你可以根据心情随时替换，一个模型两种玩法。 📦 后续计划(0715已经更新) 我本来还打算设计一个专用底座，用来收纳多余的雏菊配件，也让三眼仔有个“家”，但比赛时间太紧，没来得及完善。后续我会陆续上传底座和更多配件，欢迎关注。 组装顺序请参考附图

Berserk: Dragon Slayer I created this model for my Advanced Manufacturing class where our final project required us to incorporate something we learned during the semester. I decided to combine 3D printing with carbon fiber skinning to create a functional, lightweight version of Guts' iconic Dragon Slayer . When designing this model, my main goals were strength, functionality, and minimizing material usage . Many of the Dragon Slayer models I've seen on here require an incredible amount of filament ( ~6kg ). By designing the sword around a structural core, I was able to reduce the total filament usage to roughly 2.5kg while still creating a sword sturdy enough to swing around. The model is designed to fit a 256mm³ build volume and is hollow throughout most of the blade. The center of the sword is designed to accept a 1-inch PVC pipe approximately 75 inches long , providing the primary structural support and preventing the blade from flexing during use. A few things to note: The tip of the blade is intentionally infilled for added durability. I included two versions of the base section : A hollow version to minimize filament usage and overall weight. An infilled version for those who prefer a heavier, more realistic feel. The hilt and chain are printed as a single piece . A modifier is included that automatically increases this section to 6 walls and 99% infill , since I consider these to be the most critical structural parts of the build. Recommended Print Settings These are the PLA settings I personally used: 3 walls 3% Gyroid infill Support for the hilt, chain, and tip only. These settings produced rigid parts that became significantly stronger after being reinforced with carbon fiber. If you don't plan on carbon fiber skinning the sword, I'd recommend printing with: 4 walls 6% Gyroid infill for some extra strength. Assembly To bond the pieces together, I used JB Weld Plastic Bonder , which is compatible with thermoplastics, carbon fiber composites, coated metals, and several other materials. After assembly, I filled all of the seams with wood filler before beginning the epoxy process. At the time of uploading this model, I'm currently applying the final layers of epoxy. After that, I'll sand everything smooth and paint the finished sword. I've been documenting the entire build process, so keep an eye out for a YouTube video showing the complete build from printing to the finished prop! If you end up printing one, I'd love to see your results. If you notice any fitment issues or have suggestions for improvements, please leave a comment and I'll do my best to update the model as quickly as possible. Happy printing!

description: When the tip of his finger brushed the gradient cold light on the blade, the prosthetic left hand of scavenger Kay suddenly got an uncontrollable electric tremor ⚡. Three months ago, he found this dagger in the wreckage of a fallen alien scientific research ship in the radioactive red gobi. Any mutated radioactive swarm will freeze instantly when it gets within three meters of this dagger, then all blood vessels burst and turn into a puddle of purple glowing pus ☣️. He originally thought it was just a biological weapon left by alien researchers, and planned to sell it to an arms broker in the lower city to exchange for a new non-leaking prosthetic. Until last midnight, that low-frequency hum seeped out from the skeleton pattern of the handle. His old radiation scar on the palm started to bleed blue glowing blood uncontrollably, the blood seeped in along the hollow pattern, and a line of twisted wriggling text slowly emerged in the hollow of the blade. The text crawled into his cerebral cortex along the nerve interface of his prosthetic, and he finally understood the murmur: this is not a weapon, it is a cage 🩸. The sandstorm in the far gobi has already pressed over with countless fine shrieks. Those things following the blood smell are the remnant souls released from the alien rift by this dagger. Kay clenched the heated handle, the gradient cold light reflected his face covered with blue blood vessels. He doesn't know if feeding himself to this blade can seal the rift again 🌪️

Thanos Cross 2: Modular Secret Necklace A redesigned version of my Thanos Cross necklace inspired by the Squid Game prop. This V2 was created in response to issues reported with the hinge and snap lock in the first version. The main mechanical parts were redesigned and are now printed separately, in orientations that improve their strength. They are also much easier to replace if needed. The original idea was to keep the model fully printable and hardware-free, so the Snap Lock version still uses only short pieces of filament for assembly. However, based on community requests, I also added optional magnetic closure variants. All versions use a filament pin for the hinge. The Snap Lock version also uses a filament pin for the latch. This version also includes a matching printable chain. What’s new in V2? Improved Snap Lock Stronger, replaceable latch Stronger Hinge Reinforced, replaceable design Magnetic Closure Optional magnet lock variant Printable Chain Matching 700 mm chain included Print profiles Several print profiles are available depending on the version you want to build. Split by Plate profiles These are the recommended basic profiles. Parts are split across plates for easier printing and assembly. Snap Lock version Magnetic Lock 3×1 mm Magnetic Lock 10×2×1 mm Printable Chain 700 mm Print by Object profiles Print-by-object profiles are also available for the three closure variants: Snap Lock Magnetic Lock 3×1 mm Magnetic Lock 10×2×1 mm Currently, print-by-object profiles are available for the H2 series . More printer profiles will be added later. Closure options You can choose one of three closure systems. Snap Lock Fully printable closure. Uses a small printed latch mounted with a short piece of filament. Glue is optional and should not be needed in most cases. Magnetic Lock 3×1 mm Uses 4 round magnets . Make sure the polarity is aligned correctly before gluing the magnets in place. Magnetic Lock 10×2×1 mm Uses 2 rectangular magnets . Make sure the polarity is aligned correctly before gluing the magnets in place. Assembly guide Follow the visual assembly guide below to build the hinge, install the selected closure option, and finish the necklace. Recommended material PLA is recommended for this model. The basic color combination shown in the photos is: Bambu PLA Basic Silver Bambu PLA Matte Charcoal The printable chain is slightly larger than the original prop-style chain due to normal FDM printing limitations, especially with a 0.4 mm nozzle. It still matches the cross well and works great as a wearable accessory. Notes For the hinge and snap lock assembly, use short pieces of filament as pins. Flush cutters are useful for trimming the pins after insertion. Needle-nose pliers may help if the pins fit tightly. For magnetic versions, a small amount of super glue is needed to secure the magnets. Have fun creating your own Thanos Cross 2 necklace. Just don’t use it to hide anything suspicious! 😉

description: UPDATE: I made a version that supports an aluminum rod! This version uses a ½" aluminum rod that is 56" long. I recommend taking a 6ft aluminum rod and cutting it down. The parts are all assembled the same way as the original with the same guide, but I recommend using epoxy instead of glue. I wanted the aluminum rod to go all the way into the spearhead, but a ½" rod is too thick to fit, and any rod thinner than ½" is not rigid enough. If anyone has a good idea for reinforcing the spearhead, let me know! Just created a Makerworld account! (Idk why I didn't do it earlier) This is just the same model that I originally posted on Printables. NOTE: The model is around 76 in (1.93 meters) long, but the real in-game spear is around 85 in (2.2 meters). I scaled it that way because I wanted a spear that would fit me, and I'm just not as tall as Kratos. Every single part of this spear, except the spearhead, is threaded, so you don't need an aluminum rod. For the spearhead, I just used PVA glue, and it worked pretty well, but you can use 3D gloop if you want a stronger bond. I'm still working on painting my spear. All of the parts need support, and I'd recommend a brim as well, just to be safe. I might consider making a version of this spear with an aluminum rod on the inside if anyone wants a stronger spear, so let me know in the comments if you would like that :) When printing, each piece is labeled with a number. Follow the image guide above for how to assemble it. Infill: 15% Material: PLA Supports: All parts need support Brim: Not technically required, but highly recommended (especially for the spearhead)
